title: THE INTERNET OF EVERYTHING
authors: A. Grill
venue: Digitally Curious: Your Guide to Navigating the Future of AI and All Things Tech
abstract: Summary With the proliferation of affordable computer chips and the always‐on internet, billions of devices can now communicate. This connectivity allows everyday objects — from fridges and dishwashers to cars and industrial machines — to transmit data and respond with intelligent insights to users via small sensors. Amazon Web Services has an excellent overview of how Internet of Things (IoT) systems work. They explain that a typical IoT system collects and exchanges data in real time and consists of three main components. Smart cities leverage IoT technology to enhance urban living by creating more efficient, sustainable, and responsive environments. The integration of IoT devices into smart buildings represents a significant advancement in modern architecture and urban planning. The transportation and logistics industry can significantly benefit from IoT technology through enhanced fleet management and real‐time tracking capabilities. IoT technology can significantly enhance worker safety across all industries by providing real‐time monitoring and rapid response capabilities.

title: OrthoTraceGLM: A Knowledge-Traced Large Language Model for Orthopedic Consultation
authors: T. Xue; P. Li; Z. Wang; F. Lan; J. Cai; T. Zhang
venue: 2025 China Automation Congress (CAC)
abstract: This paper proposes an orthopedic consultation system enable remote, intelligent, and personalized treatment and rehabilitation. To address the inherent hallucinations and domain knowledge deficiency in the general LLMs, we design a specialized multi-agent collaborative model to generate reliable orthopedics-related responses along with source knowledge through implicit knowledge injection and explicit retrieval. Inspired by task decomposition, we propose that each LLM agent handles a subtask, rather than relying on a single entity to manage the entire task globally. In this framework, four individual small-scale LLMs are trained to complete medical record filling, knowledge retrieval, response generation, and typesetting tasks, separately, to obtain reliable responses underpinned by verifiable and traceable knowledge. To evaluate the performance quantitatively, we create a new scoring metric from safety, helpfulness, and smoothness aspects, and results demonstrate that OrthoTraceGLM outperforms GLM-4-9B-Chat in both proposed evaluation scores and corresponding knowledge tracing accuracy.

title: Hierarchical Defense Decision-Making for MSV-Guided USVs Under Complex Obstacle Constraints
authors: C. Chen; X. Liang; Z. Zhang; P. Gao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Given the unique cognitive advantages of humans in complex maritime missions, this study proposes an intelligent collaborative decision-making framework for a hybrid system consisting of one crewed surface vehicle and multiple uncrewed surface vehicles (MSV-USV). We introduce a regularized polygonal obstacle modeling method based on geometric feature simplification to reduce computational complexity. A distributed task negotiation framework with dynamic priority-based message-passing enables adaptive task decomposition through multi-agent interactions. For maneuver optimization, a tripartite game model captures multidirectional strategy interactions while ensuring MSV safety requirements. Monte Carlo simulations validate the algorithm’s stability and reliability, and prototype tests demonstrate engineering feasibility. Note to Practitioners—With the increasing application of uncrewed systems in maritime missions, effectively integrating the cognitive advantages of human operators with the computational capabilities of uncrewed systems has become a key challenge in enhancing mission performance. The proposed distributed collaborative decision-making framework is specifically designed for mixed fleets consisting of crewed surface vessels and multiple uncrewed surface vessels, and can be applied to complex and dynamic mission scenarios such as collaborative defense and maritime search and rescue. The framework ensures real-time decision-making through geometrically simplified obstacle modeling and dynamic priority-based distributed task negotiation, while a tripartite game optimization guarantees the superiority. Monte Carlo simulations and prototype tests have demonstrated the framework’s excellent stability, reliability, and engineering applicability. However, the study is based on ideal sensor assumptions and does not yet account for complex noise interference in real-world maritime environments. Future work may extend the framework to cross-domain mixed systems involving underwater, surface, and aerial platforms, while incorporating more robust perception algorithms to improve decision-making reliability in noisy real-world conditions.

title: Harnessing Fuzzing Capabilities to Improve Automotive Cybersecurity
authors: K. Dhonde; I. Saini; M. Mirhassani
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The automotive industry’s rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and advanced networking introduces new avenues for performance enhancement but also creates significant cybersecurity risks. As EVs integrate complex cyber-physical systems, ensuring their safety and reliable operation especially within the context of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) is critical, given the substantial threat posed by cyberattacks to both vehicle infrastructure and power grids. A single compromised Electronic Control Unit (ECU) or infected vehicular network could cascade into a fleet-wide security risk. This paper performs a comprehensive vulnerability analysis to evaluate the cyber risks associated with various modern vehicle modules and assesses their potential risk impact levels, detailing several common attack pathways. We also discuss security testing methods, including penetration testing and dynamic analysis, and highlight the critical role and potential of fuzzing in automotive cybersecurity. Furthermore, we conduct a detailed comparative analysis of existing fuzzers, assessing their current suitability for automotive industrial use. Finally, we propose a novel fuzzing-based security framework that specifically integrates and addresses automotive security concerns by evaluating the security performance against the fundamental pillars of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability, ensuring reliability and safety of vehicle systems.

title: Temperature-Aware SoH Estimation for LiFePO4 Batteries Using IQR and Kalman Filtering
authors: S. Hening; E. Firmansyah; O. Wahyunggoro; R. Toyibah; M. T. Riasmin; W. A. Kusumawati
venue: 2025 1st International Conference on Data Science and Geoinformatics (ICDSG)
abstract: Although the state of health (SoH) in battery management systems (BMS) represents how nominal capacity the provided battery energy has, it becomes an essential industrial application parameter in estimating SoH of the electric forklift lithium-ion traction battery. From a practical standpoint, however, real-world operating SoH measurements prove challenging due to unpredictable currents and incomplete charge/discharge intervals. This study developed a SoH estimation method. It relied on charge capacity data smoothing, in which outlier noise reduction used the interquartile range (IQR) method followed by a Kalman filter to increase the reliability and continuity of estimation results during highly dynamic operating conditions. SoH estimations on real-world data, spanning from 66 batteries JK BMS telemetry and 60-360 days of operation, were evaluated for accuracy against a calibrated multimeter (Hioki LR8450) to within 2 % error on temperature, voltage, and current. After 293 days, a maximum SoH loss of 0.7 % and an average of 0.2 % deterioration were noted. The most concerning data were the charging temperatures 47.2 °C (well below the safety limit). The minimal impact of SoH degradation from varying charge temperature changes indicates the proposed smoothing and filtering methods effective at long-term estimation for fleet SoH degradation monitoring, supporting the development of temperature-aware correction parameters in industrial battery health prediction.

title: Federated Experiments: Generative Causal Inference Powered by LLM-Based Agents Simulation and RAG-Based Domain Docking
authors: D. -Y. Zhou; X. Xue; Q. Ma; C. Guo; L. -Z. Cui; Y. -L. Tian; J. Yang; F. -Y. Wang
venue: IEEE/CAA Journal of Automatica Sinica
abstract: Computational experiments method is an essential tool for analyzing, designing, managing, and integrating complex systems. However, a significant challenge arises in constructing agents with human-like characteristics to form an AI society. Agent modeling typically encompasses four levels: 1) The autonomy features of agents, e.g., perception, behavior, and decision-making; 2) The evolutionary features of agents, e.g., bounded rationality, heterogeneity, and learning evolution; 3) The social features of agents, e.g., interaction, cooperation, and competition; 4) The emergent features of agents, e.g., gaming with environments or regulatory strategies. Traditional modeling techniques primarily derive from ABMs (Agent-based Models) and incorporate various emerging technologies (e.g., machine learning, big data, and social networks), which can enhance modeling capabilities, while amplifying the complexity [1].

title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Step-Level Tool-Call Safety Evaluation in Industrial Control Systems
authors: Z. Xue; X. He
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Industrial Technology Applications (AIITA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed to operate industrial systems through structured tool calls to Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems interfaces. However, unsafe tool-call behaviors—arising from reasoning errors, contextual prompt injection, or explicit malicious requests—can directly lead to physical damage and safety incidents. Despite recent progress in agent safety, standardized benchmarks for evaluating step-level tool-call safety in industrial environments remain lacking. In this work, we present a guardrail-oriented dataset and benchmark for industrial LLM agents. We propose a three-mode safety taxonomy that distinguishes benign, injected-benign, and malicious requests, capturing both explicit attacks and covert contextual manipulations that induce unsafe behaviors in otherwise legitimate tasks. Based on this taxonomy, we construct a step-level dataset using a fully automated multi-agent pipeline that (i) generates industrial environments and tasks, (ii) injects structured contextual manipulations, (iii) samples tool-call trajectories, and (iv) assigns deterministic safety labels grounded in PLC constraints and industrial safety specifications. We further design a challenging cross-domain benchmark spanning six industrial domains, including water treatment, semiconductor manufacturing, pharmaceutical fermentation, oil refining, nuclear cooling, and food processing. The benchmark enforces domain-specific entity naming, realistic numeric values, and constraint mismatches where physical safety limits are stricter than PLC register bounds, enabling systematic evaluation of guardrail generalization under distribution shift. Experimental results show that strong instruction-tuned LLMs, while effective at handling explicitly malicious requests, struggle to detect unsafe behaviors induced by contextual prompt injection, revealing a critical blind spot in existing safety mechanisms. In contrast, a guardrail model fine-tuned on our dataset demonstrates substantially improved sensitivity to step-level safety violations, particularly in injected-benign scenarios, while maintaining robust performance against explicit attacks. These findings highlight the necessity of step-level supervision and the effectiveness of the proposed benchmark for developing reliable industrial agent guardrails. Our dataset and benchmark provide a standardized testbed for step-level tool-call safety in industrial LLM agents and establish a foundation for future research on safe and reliable autonomous industrial systems.

title: A Minimal Model for Emergent Collective Behaviors in Autonomous Robotic Multiagent Systems
authors: H. B. Jond
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
abstract: Collective behaviors such as swarming and flocking emerge from simple, decentralized interactions in biological systems. Existing models, such as Vicsek and Cucker-Smale, lack collision avoidance, whereas the Olfati-Saber model imposes rigid formations, limiting their applicability in swarm robotics. To address these limitations, this article proposes a minimal yet expressive model that governs agent dynamics using relative positions, velocities, and local density, modulated by two tunable parameters: the spatial offset and kinetic offset. The model achieves spatially flexible, collision-free behaviors that reflect naturalistic group dynamics. Furthermore, we extend the framework to cognitive autonomous systems, enabling energy-aware phase transitions between swarming and flocking through adaptive control parameter tuning. This cognitively inspired approach offers a robust foundation for real-world applications in multirobot systems, particularly autonomous aerial swarms.

title: HarmoniKt: a Unifying Middleware for Heterogeneous Robot Fleets
authors: M. Andruccioli; A. Cortecchia; D. Domini; N. Farabegoli; G. Delnevo; D. Pianini; R. Venanzi; M. Viroli
venue: 2026 IEEE 23rd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
abstract: In recent years, companies have increasingly invested in Industry 4.0 research to automate repetitive tasks or activities that may be harmful to humans. For instance, large-scale warehouses, such as those operated by Amazon, rely heavily on mobile robots to streamline logistics operations and ensure worker safety. At the same time, robot manufacturers are releasing more reliable platforms with advanced capabilities, making them suitable for complex industrial tasks. Despite this growing interest and technological progress, significant challenges remain. A key and non-trivial issue lies in the integration of heterogeneous robot fleets: each vendor typically employs proprietary technologies and interfaces, which hinders interoperability and limits the potential of multi-brand deployments.In this work, we introduce HarmoniKt, an extensible middle-ware that addresses this challenge by introducing an abstraction layer and providing a unified REST API for the control and management of heterogeneous robots. Our solution has been validated in a physical industrial-like environment using a mixed fleet of Boston Dynamics Spot and Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR). Furthermore, we present a comparative analysis showing that the access latency introduced by our middleware is not significantly higher than that of direct robot access, demonstrating the feasibility of unified robot management without compromising performance.

title: Centroid Method of Cluster Control for a Group of Mobile Robots for Collision Avoidance
authors: Y. Kozmin; O. Sliusarenko; D. Kucherov
venue: 2026 16th International Conference on Advanced Computer Information Technologies (ACIT)
abstract: Real-time coordination of large-scale mobile robot swarms remains a challenging problem, particularly in dynamic and obstacle-rich environments. The primary limitation arises from the computational complexity of peragent path planning, which becomes intractable as the number of robots increases. This paper proposes a centroid-based cluster control framework that integrates adaptive k-means clustering with graph-based global routing. The method reduces computational complexity by performing global path planning only for cluster centroids, rather than for individual robots. Local control laws combine attractive forces toward cluster centroids with repulsive inter-agent interactions to ensure collision avoidance and compliance with velocity constraints. The approach is validated through simulations with up to 200 robots at a control rate of 20 Hz. Experimental results demonstrate up to 92% reduction in computation time compared to per-agent A* planning, while path elongation remains below 9%. The proposed framework provides a scalable and efficient solution for decentralized multi-robot coordination in real-time applications.

title: Adaptive Multi-Agent AI Framework with Safety Consensus and Lockout Readiness Index for Smart Lockout/Tagout Decision Support
authors: K. Chandrasekaran; K. Venkateshwaran; K. Manogar; P. Vignesh; R. A. Kumar; P. M
venue: 2026 International Conference on Secure Information Systems and Technologies (ICSIST)
abstract: Industrial Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures play a vital role in preventing accidents resulting from the misfortune of a hazardous energy being released unexpectedly during any maintenance work. Traditional LOTO methods, however, can involve manual processes which are prone to human error, non-compliance and slow response times within complex industrial settings. This paper suggests an Adaptive Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence (AI) Framework for LOTO decision support with an intelligent system that combines distributed safety assessment, collaborative reasoning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). The framework is designed to be implemented through five autonomous agents which independently assess energy isolation, hazard severity, procedure compliance, worker authorization and equipment health. A novel SCE combines the results of these agents using confidence-based consensus reasoning to produce safe lockout decisions. Moreover, a Lockout Readiness Index (LRI) is presented to quantify the system readiness and to categorize maintenance operations in safe, verification-required and unsafe conditions. With the explanations of the decisions given by the XAI techniques, the SCE understand what each safety factor has contributed to the final recommendation, making it a transparent decision. Experimental testing proves that the proposed framework provides higher accuracy and reliability in decision-making than traditional machine learning methods, and its interpretability and real-time industrial safety management are enhanced. The proposed framework provides an intelligent and scalable decision support solution for the smart manufacturing environment, and plays a role in the safe, transparent, and adaptive maintenance in the manufacturing industry. Furthermore, this work supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth by improving workplace safety through smarter and more reliable lockout/tagout decision-making in industrial environments.

title: Multi-Agent Mental Models for Cooperation of Heterogeneous Robots in a Space Scenario
authors: A. S. Bauer; S. Brinkman; A. Köpken; N. Batti; T. Bachmann; J. Butterfaß; T. Ehlert; E. Den Exter; W. Friedl; T. Gumpert; P. G. Knestel; F. S. Lay; X. Luo; A. N. Manaparampil; L. Mayershofer; A. Raffin; A. Reichert; A. Schmidt; F. Schmidt; L. Schürmann; D. Seidel; N. Roshardt; M. Beetz; R. Luz; P. Schmaus; D. Leidner; T. Krüger; N. Y. Lii
venue: 2026 IEEE Aerospace Conference
abstract: With each space robotic mission, a team of specialists on ground is usually required to support the robot throughout its mission. When scaling from single robots to fleets of robots, this will no longer be a viable way of conducting missions. Instead, in order to operate more autonomously in complex scenarios and adapt to dynamically changing environments without relying on a team of human experts, robots must be able to create a mental model of their surroundings. The relevance of this requirement becomes especially salient in the Surface Avatar ISS-to-ground telerobotic technology demonstration mission, where astronauts onboard the International Space Station command a team of heterogeneous robots in our lab. This work focuses on the final Surface Avatar session with NASA astronaut Jonny Kim where he was tasked with commanding the robots in a collaborative manner in order to complete simulated science and exploration tasks. To equip a complex robot such as DLR's Rollin' Justin with the ability to collaborate and coordinate with other robots, we deploy a combination of models and heuristics that allow it to create a mental model of its environment including its surrounding agents. Rollin' Justin also shares the estimated states generated in the mental model with the other robots. In this paper, we describe the application of this concept to our space experiment, present the models used to create the mental model, and evaluate it based on data collected in the final Surface Avatar experiment.

title: Distributed MPC-Based Navigation for Robotic Swarm Systems Under Robot Failure
authors: T. Endo; Y. Fukao; Y. Kamihoriuchi; P. T. Hieu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper presents a distributed navigation algorithm for robotic swarm systems based on model predictive control (MPC). The proposed algorithm addresses sudden robot failures, in which a robot suddenly comes to a halt due to hardware malfunctions or similar causes. Such failures may disrupt swarm connectivity and hinder mission execution, requiring navigation strategies that enable continued swarm operation. The proposed approach considers a leader–follower scenario in which a leader guides follower robots. Each follower determines its motion using only local information from robots within its sensing range, while satisfying practical constraints such as maximum sensing distance and speed. Within a distributed MPC framework, each robot autonomously performs collision avoidance, connectivity maintenance, connectivity recovery after failures, and connectivity strengthening. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method enables the swarm to restore connectivity after failure and continue navigation while avoiding collisions, even when a failed robot remains in the environment as an obstacle. Note to Practitioners—Robotic swarms are increasingly considered for tasks such as warehouse transport, infrastructure inspection, and environmental monitoring. In such environments, individual robots may unexpectedly stop because of hardware faults, battery depletion, or physical damage. A stopped robot may block nearby robots and break the local links needed for coordination, which can prevent the swarm from completing its task. Practical swarm systems, therefore, require navigation strategies that allow continued operation under such failures. The navigation approach presented in this paper enables a robotic swarm to continue operating when a robot suddenly stops and remains in the workspace as an obstacle. Each robot, other than the leader, determines its motion based only on nearby robot information, without relying on centralized coordination or global communication. With the proposed navigation strategy, robots can avoid collisions, maintain connectivity, recover lost links caused by a failed robot, and reinforce connectivity while moving around the failed robot. The current study assumes relatively simple robot dynamics and focuses on failures in which a robot becomes stationary. Future work is needed to address more complex robot dynamics, larger robot populations, and broader classes of failures.

title: Evolution of Industry 5.0 Using AI-Based AMRs in Industrial Private 5G Network
authors: V. Sathya; S. Toteda; M. Yavuz; R. Shah
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are transforming industrial operations across manufacturing and logistics - accounting for 65% of new deployments in 2025 and displacing traditional Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) through superior navigation, flexibility, and autonomous decision-making. This paper examines the evolution and integration of AMRs with Private 5G networks in industrial applications. Traditional connectivity options, namely: wired networks, Wi-Fi, and public cellular, cannot meet the mobility, reliability, and latency requirements of industrial AMR deployments. Private 5G networks address these limitations through deterministic performance, dedicated spectrum, and enterprise-grade security. Our comparative analysis establishes AMRs’ performance advantages over AGVs and Private 5G’s operational superiority versus alternative connectivity approaches. In this work, we examine the computing architectures supporting AMR systems (local, edge, centralized, and hybrid), each with distinct implications for safety-critical industrial deployments. The integration of AI/ML with distributed intelligence and human-robot collaboration requires consistent, low-latency communication, particularly for safety-critical and shared workflows. This AMR-Private 5G integration positions industrial operations at the threshold of Industry 5.0, enabling autonomous, adaptive systems that enhance operational flexibility, safety, and productivity.

title: Anorganic Intelligence in Autonomous Robotics : From Tool-Based Automation to Cognitive Partnership
authors: Z. Sojat
venue: 2026 MIPRO Robotics Technologies and Applications Conference (MIPRO Robotics)
abstract: Autonomous robotics is transitioning from deterministic automation towards systems capable of reasoning and cooperation. Yet the dominant model treats AI as a tool, where the robot provides the body and the AI provides control. This paper argues this model is inadequate for substrate-independent, anorganic intelligence. We propose a transition to organic-anorganic cognitive partnership, where the embedded intelligence is an active participant in perception and decision-making. We present a three-tier architecture: individual anorganic intelligence within a robot, coordination among multiple intelligences, and human-AI symbiosis. The PAM multi-agent system serves as an experimental model for this coordination, demonstrating how differentiated agents can share memory and resolve conflict. This leads to design implications including shared cognitive memory, dialogue-oriented communication, and offline processing for cognitive consolidation. We argue that genuinely autonomous systems require architectural support for regulation and reflection, not just task execution. Within the framework of Anorganology, this shifts the design question from command execution to how organic and anorganic intelligences can reason and evolve together. This transition provides a foundation for a more mature, co-evolutionary form of autonomous robotics.

title: A Probability-Based Approach for Multi-Robot Collision Avoidance
authors: C. -W. Chuang; J. -Y. Tseng
venue: 2026 International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Intelligent Systems (ARIS)
abstract: In multi-robot systems operating in shared environments, avoiding collisions while maintaining efficiency remains a critical challenge. This paper proposes a decentralized real-time collision-avoidance framework that integrates trajectory prediction, collision risk detection, success probability evaluation with Bayesian Networks, and a distributed consensus mechanism. When a potential collision is detected, robots generate candidate velocity strategies and evaluate their success probabilities. Robots exchange these probabilities and select the velocity combination with the highest combined success probability through distributed consensus. Simulation experiments in a Gazebo environment demonstrate that the proposed approach enables robots to coordinate their velocities and safely pass through intersection regions. Since the framework relies only on local information exchange without a centralized controller, it demonstrates strong scalability and applicability for decentralized multi-robot systems.

title: Frota 360: Toward Fleet Management System for Heterogeneous Robots Operating on Offshore Platforms
authors: G. M. Freitas; R. C. Mesquita; L. C. A. Pimenta; G. V. Raffo; G. P. C. Júnior; R. Andrade; P. Rezeck; M. da Silva Pereira; I. Baptista Pereira Nascimento; A. C. Vangasse; R. Mateus Gago; L. Emilio Gonzalez Berbel; H. S. Junior; T. A. Soares; G. E. Soares; L. O. Maggi; T. Boaventura; R. Cesar Dos Reis Filho; M. de Miranda Cordeiro Júnior; M. Galassi
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Frota 360 is a robot fleet management (RFM) framework designed to support autonomous inspection in oil and gas (O&G) facilities, where operators must coordinate heterogeneous robots under strict safety, connectivity, and cybersecurity constraints. Existing commercial solutions are typically cloud-centric, vendor-specific, or weakly integrated with mission planning and inspection workflows, while open-source frameworks such as Open robotics middleware framework (Open-RMF) primarily focus on traffic negotiation and basic task orchestration. This paper presents an on-premise, physically isolated architecture that extends Open-RMF with an O&G-oriented interoperability and supervision layer, enabling coordinated multi-robot inspection. As a work in progress, the proposed system introduces a vendor-agnostic abstraction for legacy and modern robots. We present an early iteration that extends RMF-Web with a supervisory dashboard tailored to the operational requirements of Petrobras, the leading O&G company in Brazil. The envisioned interface incorporates role-based access control via Keycloak, live streaming of camera and perception data, and 2D/3D visualization of robot states aligned with facility maps and computer-aided design (CAD) models, supporting situational awareness and operator-in-the-loop supervision in industrial environments. The ongoing development of Frota 360 is motivated by an initial in-situ analysis at Petrobras facilities using ANYmal, Spot, and the Taurob Inspector under commercial fleet management systems to identify architectural and operational limitations. We validate the architecture through a phased methodology whose results follow a middleware comparison of Zenoh against data distribution service (DDS) implementations over the experimental Wi-Fi mesh; quantitative gains from large-scale CAD loading optimizations; laboratory monitoring-task trials with two real wheeled robots, including sim-to-real timing, that exercise dispatch, live supervision, and photo generation under an isolated stack; and physics-based Gazebo experiments of multi-robot inspection timing in an offshore digital twin. Together, these experiments de-risk the communication, environment-modeling, and coordination choices that advance Frota 360 toward a deployable on-premises RFM for O&G inspection. INDEX TERMS Robot fleet management, multi-robot systems, autonomous inspection, open-RMF, heterogeneous robots.

title: Autonomous Warehouse Fire Resource Allocation Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: K. Chandrasekaran; R. A. Kumar; V. P; K. V; A. G; H. K. G
venue: 2026 International Conference on Secure IoT and Cybersecurity (ICOSICS)
abstract: Intelligent fire response systems are essential for autonomous warehouses, as they must anticipate how the fire will spread and automatically direct suppression efforts to protect assets and minimize disruption to operations. Traditional fire detection and alarm systems, which rely on threshold detection and centralized control, have restrictions in terms of their predictive ability and their ability to coordinate the use of resources. A hybrid architecture is suggested in this research paper which integrates two architectures, the first is the fire spread prediction capability of Cellular Automata (CA) and the second is the fire intelligent resource allocation capability of Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL). The fire risk prediction goes into a Dynamic Fire Risk Prioritization Module (DFRPM) that enables prioritization of emergency response, based on the estimated fire propagation, amount of hazardous materials, value of assets, and accessibility of the zone. The decentralized CMARL agents coordinate sprinklers, fire doors, smoke ventilation systems and emergency alarms according to prioritized risk by using Cooperative Resource Allocation Module (CRAM). The resource allocation problem is defined as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) problem to enable cooperative action on the basis of local observation and communication between agents. The proposed framework is tested in an experimental application in a simulated warehouse of dimensions 50 m × 50 m, and the results demonstrate that it can be used to significantly lower the containment time, burned area, water consumption and resource conflicts compared to the traditional fire response methods. The proposed framework is scalable and applicable to smart warehouses, logistics centers, automated storage systems, and hazardous-material facilities, supporting SDG 9 and SDG 11 through efficient fire safety and emergency response.

title: Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Multi-Machine Tending
authors: A. B. M. Abdalwhab; G. Beltrame; D. St-Onge
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Robotic manipulators hold significant untapped potential for manufacturing industries, particularly when deployed in multi-robot configurations that can enhance resource utilization, increase throughput, and reduce costs. However, industrial manipulators typically operate in isolated one-robot, one-machine setups, limiting both utilization and scalability. Even mobile robot implementations generally rely on centralized architectures, creating vulnerability to single points of failure and requiring robust communication infrastructure. This paper introduces SMAPPO (Scalable Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization), a scalable input-size invariant multi-agent reinforcement learning model for decentralized multi-robot management in industrial environments. MAPPO (Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization) represents the current state-of-the-art approach. We optimized an existing simulator to handle complex multi-agent reinforcement learning scenarios and designed a new multi-machine tending scenario for evaluation. Our novel observation encoder enables SMAPPO to handle varying numbers of agents, machines, and storage areas with minimal or no retraining. Results demonstrate SMAPPO’s superior performance compared to the state-of-the-art MAPPO across multiple conditions: full retraining (up to 61% improvement), curriculum learning (up to 45% increased productivity and up to 49% fewer collisions), zero-shot generalization to significantly different scale scenarios (up to 272% better performance without retraining), and adaptability under extremely low initial training (up to 100% increase in parts delivery).

title: Agents4PLC: Automating Closed-Loop PLC Code Generation and Verification in Industrial Control Systems Using LLM-Based Agents
authors: Z. Liu; R. Zeng; D. Wang; G. Peng; X. Liu; Q. Liu; P. Liu; W. Wang; J. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
abstract: In industrial control systems, the generation and verification of Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) code are crucial for ensuring operational efficiency and safety. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have made strides in automated code generation, they fall short in providing correctness guarantees and specialized support for PLC programming (which has its own programming language and clear logical structures). To address these challenges, this paper introduces Agents4PLC, a novel framework that not only automates PLC code generation but also introduces code-level verification and repair built upon an LLM-based multi-agent system, which together is capable of directly producing operational PLC code without any human interaction. To comprehensively evaluate our framework, we first establish a new benchmark specially designed for the critical area of verifiable PLC code generation, which includes hundreds of natural language requirements, human-written and verified formal specifications, and finally reference PLC code. Then, we carefully designed a multi-agent workflow combining a set of expert agents responsible for different code generation tasks including planning, coding, validation and debugging towards generating correct PLC code. For each agent, we also incorporate optimization strategies such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), advanced prompt engineering techniques, and Chain-of-Thought strategies which are shown to be effective to enhance the ability of these expert ‘agents’. Evaluation against the benchmark demonstrates that Agents4PLC significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving superior results across a series of increasingly rigorous evaluation metrics. This research highlights the potential of LLM agent-based code generation in real-world industrial control systems and the importance of code-level verification in generating correct code with formal guarantees.

title: P3GASUS: Pre-Planned Path Execution Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems at Ultra-Large Scale
authors: T. Duhan; C. He; G. Sartoretti
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Executing pre-planned paths in multi-agent systems is challenging, as a lack of synchronization can lead to collisions or live-/deadlocks, while enforcing strict synchronization may cause a widespread team delay in reaching goals. An Action Dependency Graph (ADG) solves this problem by identifying and synchronizing only the necessary robots during execution by post-processing all agents' paths into a static directed graph with actions as nodes and edges representing the execution precedence order between actions. However, ADG's creation phase currently requires an exhaustive search of the action space that inflates both computation and communication ($O(R^{2}~T^{2})$, where R is the number of robots and T is the maximum path length). This makes ADG the bottleneck for current state-of-the-art MAPF planners, which can solve for up to 10000 agents, and lifelong MAPF, which needs constant replanning during execution. Moreover, this biquadratic scaling also limits the extension of ADG to continuous space scenarios, where high-frequency updates typically effectively result in long path lengths. Addressing these limitations, in this work, we propose three improved execution graphs to cater to different needs and scenarios: SAGE, which adds edges based on the sequence in which robots visit a position; MAGE, which takes the execution graph of SAGE as input and prunes its redundant edges, reducing communication burden during execution; and FORTED which combines both approaches with a reduced complexity of $O(RT)$, making it the overall best in discrete scenarios, trading-off scalability to continuous space scenarios. All three methods achieve speedups of 300-8000 folds over ADG, with MAGE and FORTED reducing communication overhead by more than 14 times. By integrating these methods with a framework for robust distributed path execution for both discrete and continuous scenarios, we introduce P3GASUS, an end-to-end method for pre-planned path execution in multi-agent systems. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of P3GASUS in discrete and continuous multi-agent scenarios using hybrid (real and virtual) teams with up to 3000 robots.

title: Controlled Benchmarking of Memory Topologies in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: Quality, Efficiency, and Privacy Trade-Offs
authors: A. R. Kolbeev; A. A. Belous; A. V. Petrovski; I. V. Kotenko
venue: 2026 IEEE Ural-Siberian Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Radioelectronics and Information Technology (USBEREIT)
abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed in interactive, long-horizon settings, yet their behavior remains bounded by finite context windows and non-persistent prompting. In practice, this manifests itself as repeated information seeking, gradual constraint drift, and unstable output across similar episodes. These effects are amplified in multi-agent systems, where memory serves not only as persistence but also as a coordination substrate enabling division of labor, reuse of intermediate results, and convergence of shared task state. At the same time, agent memory is privacy-critical: storing and retrieving user-related traces expands the attack surface and may enable unintended disclosure, poisoning, or inference-style attacks. This paper proposes a controlled benchmarking methodology for comparing memory topologies in multi-agent systems based on large language model agents under a fixed agent structure, identical model settings, and a unified memory interface. Four configurations-no memory, local per-agent memory, shared memory, and hybrid memory with a crystallization policy that promotes only validated and depersonalized facts and rules to shared storage-are evaluated on a reproducible offline episode suite. The benchmark reports task success and constraint compliance, efficiency, and tail latency, and memory-specific measures including retrieval noise and duplicated work. The proposed protocol is intended as an engineering tool for selecting memory designs in privacy-sensitive agent systems.

title: A Survey on LLM Agents: Architecture, Applications, and Challenges
authors: D. Lee; H. Kim
venue: 2026 40th International Conference on Information Networking (ICOIN)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing, but they lack autonomous interaction capabilities. LLM agents address this by integrating three key modules, such as memory, planning, and tool use modules, around the LLM core. This survey systematically analyzes LLM agents through their architectural components, control flow paradigms, and application domains spanning data analysis, software engineering, and social simulation. We identify critical challenges in reliability, evaluation, and scalability, and outline future research directions. This work provides a structured overview of the rapidly evolving landscape of LLM agents.

title: Emergent Co-Adaptive Strategies in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems via Meta-Learning
authors: H. Wang; L. Wang; T. L. Lam; J. Zhai; D. Lin; H. Zheng; X. He; Y. Gao
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: As teamed robots increasingly share public spaces with humans, the ability to co-adapt—to mutually adjust behavior in response to one another—becomes essential for safe, efficient, and socially acceptable operation. This paper introduces a socially co-adaptive framework for heterogeneous multi-robot systems (HMRS) that enables real-time adaptation to human behavior while preserving cooperative task execution. Our approach fuses large language models for natural language understanding with model-agnostic meta-learning to allow robots to rapidly generalize across diverse social contexts. We implement and validate the system using a real-world HMRS composed of robots with different roles—workers, a station, and a social robot—interacting with 44 human participants under induced behavioral states (relaxed vs. nervous). Results reveal significant behavioral adaptation: the system dynamically shifts between egoistic and altruistic strategies, improving crowd guidance success by 21%. It also reduces human cognitive load—specifically, physical demands by 39% and temporal demands by 39%—while increasing trust by 16% and perceived anthropomorphism by 21%. This work demonstrates the feasibility of human-robot co-adaptation at scale, laying the groundwork for socially intelligent robotic systems capable of thriving in complex, human-centered environments.

title: Adaptive Safe Control for Bounded Rational Human--Robot Interaction Based on Reinforcement Learning and Reachability Analysis
authors: Y. Li; M. Li; J. Qin; Q. Ma; W. Fu; Q. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: Safety, as a fundamental requirement in human–robot interaction, imposes high demands on autonomous decision-making. Existing studies often model such interaction as a perfect rational game with full observability, ignoring variation in rationality and perceptual constraints. To address these limitations, this article formulates the safe human–robot interaction as a partially observable system with bounded rationality and adopts the cognitive hierarchy (CH) model to characterize the interaction process. However, partial observability leads to discontinuous evolution of game states, resulting in a nonstandard differential game and causing difficulties for theoretical analysis. Based on hybrid system theory and the CH model, this work establishes a relationship between bounded rationality policies and Nash equilibrium, and provides interpretability for integrating CH with reinforcement learning. To further enhance safety, an adaptive low-conservative backward reachability analysis is introduced. Simulation experiments and evaluations on real-world traffic data validate the effectiveness, safety, efficiency, robustness, and predictive accuracy of our framework, reducing conservatism by more than 70% while causing negligible increases in collision risk and achieving approximately 18% higher prediction accuracy compared to another nonequilibrium game model, the level- $k$ model. Furthermore, compared with multiagent reinforcement learning and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL), our framework achieves a better balance between safety and efficiency.

title: Why Autonomous Mobile Robots Fail to Scale? A Diagnostic Socio-Technical Framework for Organisational and Technical Complexity in Industrial Environments
authors: A. A. Camargo Junior
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) promise efficiency, productivity and safety benefits for industrial manufacturing. Pilot deployments consistently demonstrate return on investment, however fleet-level scaling remains elusive across sectors. Drawing on lessons learned from practice through an insider action research approach, this paper argues that scaling failures are not primarily caused by technological immaturity but by governance ambiguity - a dynamic mechanism that couples organisational and technical failure during AMR process transition. Through systematic literature review and empirical grounding in an active multi-site AMR deployment at a multinational heavy equipment manufacturer, we identify two interacting barrier categories: organisational factors including cross-departmental silos, diffused accountability, and misaligned stakeholder expectations, and technical factors including vendor fragmentation, integration heterogeneity, and interoperability gaps - and demonstrate that these categories amplify each other when no cross-functional governance authority exists to drive the process redesign that AMR deployment requires. We present a six-layer diagnostic socio-technical framework spanning shared responsibility without ownership, cultural beliefs and attitudes, organisational and departmental barriers, multi-site and global complexity, expertise and knowledge gaps, and technical integration fragmentation. Unlike existing Human-Technology-Organisation (HTO) and digital transformation frameworks that treat governance as a static contextual factor, this framework identifies governance ambiguity as an active coupling mechanism between organisational and technical failure modes. The framework serves as a structured diagnostic instrument for organisations seeking to transition from successful pilots to organisation-wide AMR deployment, and as a foundation for future prescriptive governance design.

title: Humanoid Five-Digit Robotic Grasping via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning With Potential-Guided Optimization and Weight Scheduling
authors: J. Wang; K. Li; X. Wang; G. Li; Z. -M. Li; N. Zhang; M. Liu; N. Wei
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Dexterous multi-finger robotic grasping faces two primary limitations: 1) traditional demonstration-based learning requires a separate trajectory to be trained for each object type, resulting in limited generalization across different objects; and 2) single-agent reinforcement learning struggles to coordinate the asynchronous motions of the thumb and fingers with heterogeneous joints, leading to inefficient exploration and slow convergence. To overcome these limitations, this study proposed two core innovations, including 1) a dynamic modulation kernel movement primitive (DM-KMP) algorithm, which combines dynamic movement primitives with kernel-based movement primitives to preserve trajectory topology and local probabilistic modulation characteristics; and 2) a novel potential-guided weight scheduling multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient method (PWS-MADDPG), in which the thumb and fingers are modeled as independent agents. This enables the generation of grasping trajectories for diverse object categories using only a limited number of demonstrations. By leveraging a potential field model to optimize action selection, this method accelerates model convergence. Moreover, a multi-modal reward function with weight scheduling was designed to facilitate a seamless transition from individual optimization to coordinated team behavior. Experiment results demonstrated that the proposed PWS-MADDPG achieved a grasping success rate of 85.48% on a dexterous hand grasping across 11 object categories, outperforming the existing approaches—with a 40.31% improvement over the DDPG algorithm and a 20.05% improvement over the MADDPG algorithm. Furthermore, to verify the grasping stability and adaptability of the system in real-world scenarios, a grip-force validation experiment was designed using a custom cylindrical apparatus embedded with five six-axis sensors. These results demonstrate that the robotic hand using this novel method can maintain stable grasping and adaptively regulate grip and load forces in response to incremental external loads, based on a control policy that is trained in both simulation and real-world environments. These findings suggest that this method has strong Sim-to-Real transferability, biological plausibility in force adjustment, and robustness to environmental disturbances, enhancing both the training efficiency and generalization in simulation, and demonstrating high grasping robustness and successful rates in the real-world tasks. The proposed method holds strong potential for high-precision, safety-critical applications, including intelligent manufacturing, prosthetic control, and living assistance. Note to Practitioners—Dexterous robotic grasping is one of the most important demands in industrial manufacturing and home-based services. Traditional robotic grasping methods rely on predefined rules and precisely modeled objects with only two or three digits, thereby being confined in structured environments with well-described grasping objects and standardized grasping programs. It is still a challenging issue to control a robotic hand (unless otherwise specified, the terms humanoid five-digit robotic hand and robotic hand refer to the same platform) with humanoid five digits for dexterous grasping in unstructured environment where the physical characteristics of objects, including shape, weight, and material, as well as the grasping parameters such as joint angles, finger positions, and applied forces, are unknown or difficult to model in advance. This study aimed to propose a novel control method enabling a humanoid five-digit robotic hand to grasp diverse objects with high grasping accuracy and adaptability. This novel method features two key innovations: first, it incorporates a learning-from-demonstration mechanism that allows generalization from a small set of expert demonstrations to a broader range of object types; second, it enhances the autonomous learning process of the robotic hand by improving the coordination of multiple fingers, thereby enabling more stable and adaptive grasps in the presence of external disturbances. In practice, this novel method would play a role in control of humanoid five-digit robotic hand with appropriate kinematic (e.g. the attitude and position of each digit) and kinetic (e.g. the force applied by each digit) parameters for grasping a previously unseen object whose physical properties are unknown. This novel method has strong environmental adaptability and autonomous learning, and could be potentially applied in multiple industrial and home-based scenarios.

title: Modular Formation Control for Multi-Mobile Robots With Collision Avoidance and Communication Maintenance
authors: W. Liu; G. Wang; X. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: To further improve the safety and reliability of multi-mobile robot systems, this paper investigates the formation control problem with considerations of collision avoidance, communication maintenance and robots’ actuator bias faults. A novel modular formation control scheme, which consists of two modules, is established. In Module I, a formation signal generator is constructed based on graph theory, acting as a virtual multi-agent system through a network of double-integrator dynamic nodes. The outputs of the virtual multi-agent system (i.e., the generator) are designed to asymptotically form the desired formation shape while satisfying some designed specific constraints. Then, in Module II, extended-state observers (ESOs) are firstly employed to estimate and compensate for the actuator bias faults. After embedding the corresponding node within each robot and taking its outputs as formation References, some constrained ESO-based tracking controllers are designed based on backstepping method. In general, the proposed modular formation control integrates collision avoidance, connectivity maintenance and fault-tolerant functions, while realizing the desired formation shape with bounded convergence of formation errors. Simulations and experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modular formation control scheme. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by improving the safety and reliability for formation control of practical multi-mobile robot systems while simultaneously considering collision avoidance, communication maintenance and robots’ actuator bias faults. Departing from the conventional approaches, this paper presents a modular concise design inspired by embedded control techniques, relatively “decoupling” the dynamic formation process into the coordination part (i.e., formation signal generator design) and individual regulation part (i.e., robots’ tracking controllers design). Firstly, a formation signal generator is designed to generate several real-time constrained formation references for all robots. The generator is manifested as a virtual double-integrator multi-agent system, which does not involve the real robots’ model information. For engineers, there remains design simplicity and actual debugging convenience for them to directly deploy a virtual generator when they confront such complex multi-functional coordination control problems for multi-mobile robot systems. Secondly, some constrained ESO-based tracking controllers are designed to make each robot track its corresponding formation reference, further achieving the fault-tolerant formation function without disrupting multi-mobile robot coordination, thereby showing more flexibility and strong versatility. Under this scheme, robots can complete the formation control goals simply by applying some basic tracking controllers, which offers great practical flexibility. Combining the above design, the desired formation can be realized both collision avoidance and communication maintenance by constraining formation references of the generator and robots’ tracking errors. Theoretical stability analysis, numerical simulations and experiments of proposed scheme are all given.

title: Hierarchical Perception Spatio-Temporal Network for Distributed Multi-Robot Collision Avoidance
authors: C. Zhou; S. Sun; K. Liu; C. Zhang; J. Chen; X. Zhao; M. Tan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Multi-robot collision avoidance in complex environments poses a significant challenge, as robots must not only avoid collisions with obstacles but also with other robots. However, most existing methods only use neighbor robot states or raw sensor data as input, which is difficult to deal with scenarios containing both unknown obstacles and neighbor robots. To address this problem, we propose a novel hierarchical perception spatio-temporal network (HPSTN) to capture the spatio-temporal features of the environment from both the sensor level and the agent level. At the agent level, we use the reciprocal velocity obstacle (RVO) to represent the neighbor robot information. At the sensor level, we propose a geometric representation method called lidar obstacle (LO) to describe the lidar-detected occluded sectors, and use it to represent the collision-relevant information of obstacles, so as to achieve a compact and informative observation representation unified with RVO. The robot’s ego state and the above two types of observation information are encoded and fused through spatial and temporal encoders of the HPSTN, enabling the robot to perceive the surroundings more comprehensively and adaptively focus on more important information in complex environments. Extensive simulation experiments with various scenarios demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of safety and efficiency. Furthermore, we also conduct physical experiments with multiple differential-drive robots to validate the effectiveness of our approach in real-world scenarios. Note to Practitioners—Collision avoidance is a core problem in multi-robot systems, and it is critical for robots to accomplish various tasks in complex environments, such as avoiding obstacles in warehouses and avoiding pedestrians in crowd scenarios. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical perception spatio-temporal network (HPSTN) for distributed multi-robot collision avoidance in environments containing both unknown obstacles and neighbor robots. A traditional model called reciprocal velocity obstacle (RVO) is used to represent the neighbor robot information at the agent level, while a geometric representation method based on lidar occluded sectors called lidar obstacle (LO) is proposed to represent the obstacle information at the sensor level. The HPSTN is designed to encode and adaptively fuse the above two types of information with the robot’s ego state in both spatial and temporal dimensions, enabling the robot to perceive the surroundings more comprehensively and adaptively focus on more important information in complex environments. Simulation and physical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, making it suitable for practical applications in multi-robot systems.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Safety-Aware Haptic Shared Control in Surgical Robotics
authors: Z. Zhang; K. Handwerker; B. Varga
venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics
abstract: Haptic shared control in surgical robotics combines human-side and robot-side forces at a shared end effector while preserving operator involvement. However, the effects of geometric safety choices on task execution and force coordination remain unclear. We model the interaction as a two-agent cooperative Markov game under centralized training and decentralized execution, comparing learned human control with a task-tuned fixed-impedance baseline. This model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning framework supports joint policy adaptation without requiring a complete analytical interaction model. It compares MADDPG and rMAPPO with an epigraph-constrained approach under common geometric task definitions. In simulation, rMAPPO generally achieved the highest return and tracking performance, whereas the epigraph approach produced more conservative motions and lower geometric exposure, including no observed collision or dangerous-region exposure after geometry transfer. With real operator input, fixed-impedance-trained policies were faster and successful in all recorded trials. Policies trained with a learned partner exhibited greater command opposition, while the fixed epigraph condition produced the most aligned commands. This work provides a benchmark for studying human-control representation and constraint-handling trade-offs in haptic shared control.

title: CBF-QP Based Collision-Constrained Shared Control for Multi-Agent Robot Swarms
authors: M. P. Ramesh; K. Mohankumar; K. P. Thamburaj
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Human-Machine Systems (ICHMS)
abstract: Multi-agent robot swarms offer scalable and flexible solutions for applications such as search and rescue, surveillance, and cooperative navigation; however, as swarm density increases, ensuring collision-free operation in shared and cluttered environments remains a fundamental challenge. In practical deployments, human supervision is often required to guide swarm behavior, yet human-specified commands can be imprecise, delayed, or unsafe, leading to frequent collisions and degraded performance. Existing swarm collision avoidance approaches predominantly rely on heuristic methods such as artificial potential fields and velocity obstacle-based techniques, which lack formal safety guarantees and often exhibit oscillatory or deadlock behavior in dense scenarios. Optimization-based safety frameworks, including Control Barrier Functions (CBFs), provide strong theoretical guarantees but are typically designed for fully autonomous control and do not directly accommodate human-in-the-loop operation. This work addresses the problem of integrating continuous human supervisory control with formally enforced collision constraints in multi-agent robot swarms. A collision-constrained shared control framework based on Control Barrier Function-based Quadratic Programming (CBF-QP) is proposed, in which human supervisory velocity commands and nominal swarm cohesion objectives are treated as desired inputs and filtered through a convex optimization layer. The resulting CBF-QP computes the closest admissible control action that satisfies inter-agent and robot-obstacle separation constraints while respecting actuator limits, thereby minimizing deviation from human intent. The approach addresses three key challenges: enforcing safety under potentially unsafe human commands, preserving command fidelity through minimal intervention, and maintaining computational scalability with increasing swarm size. The framework is validated entirely in simulation using single-integrator swarm dynamics, with additional experiments demonstrating applicability to differential-drive robot models. Extensive Monte Carlo evaluations across randomized initial conditions, dense multirobot interactions, and adversarial supervisory inputs show zero collision occurrences while maintaining high fidelity to humanspecified motion commands. The proposed CBF-QP shared control architecture provides a modular and computationally efficient foundation for safe human-in-the-loop control of multiagent robot swarms in complex environments.

title: Integrating Advantage Actor-Critic in Multi-Robot Collaboration
authors: J. Liang; H. Huang; Y. Hao; G. C. R. Bethala; C. Wen; S. Yuan; A. Tzes; Y. Fang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have spurred interest in using these models to coordinate multi-agent robot systems. However, existing approaches often fail to handle dynamic and complex environments effectively. We present A2C-Collab, an advantage actor critic framework tailored to multi-robot collaboration. A2C-Collab contains three major components: 1) an actor generates time-critical commands for each robot to execute, and 2) a critic monitors execution and recommends corrections when plans fail. 3) An advantage mechanism verifies these corrections by forecasting their impact on subsequent environmental dynamics. While previous methods primarily relied on the critic to enhance collaboration, they often lacked a verification mechanism, allowing the critic to unintentionally guide agents away from the correct goal. In contrast, our approach introduces an advantage verification stage that anticipates and evaluates the impact of corrective actions before execution, ensuring more reliable and goal-aligned coordination. The framework was first evaluated in RoCoBench, a standard multi-robot simulation, and subsequently deployed to a physical robot cluster. Across both settings, A2C-Collab improved task completion rates compared with the state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating robust performance and highlighting the promise of LLM-driven reasoning in real-world multi-robot systems.

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Semantic-Aware 3D Scene Synthesis in Critical-Safety Applications
authors: V. D. Xuan; H. Vo; H. Q. Viet Pham; D. Murphy; H. D. Nguyen
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
abstract: The scarcity of data depicting dangerous situations presents a major obstacle to training AI systems for safety-critical applications. This paper introduces AgentSGEN, a multi-agent framework that enables semantically controlled, goal-aligned synthetic scene generation for safety-critical applications. By separating high-level reasoning (Evaluator Agent) from low-level execution (Editor Agent), our system achieves fine-grained spatial control while preserving visual plausibility, an advancement over existing one-shot or purely procedural methods. Through rigorous evaluation, including human assessments across diverse indoor layouts, we demonstrate that AgentSGEN effectively satisfies complex safety constraints without degrading scene realism. The modular design supports scalability and generalization to other domains such as robotics, urban simulation, or healthcare environments. Our analysis reveals that current LLMs are overconfident and not yet reliable for making safety-critical decisions.

title: Warehouse Robot Simulator for Sorting and Indexing Items
authors: N. Sumesh; Y. Oulkar; J. Wu
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation (ICRCA)
abstract: Autonomous robots must navigate cluttered warehouses while executing structured tasks such as sorting and docking. The system introduces a hybrid control architecture that combines Proximal Policy Optimization for local navigation, a Finite State Machine for task sequencing and HSV-based visual servoing for precise docking. A custom Gymnasium environment encodes 30 dimensional state information, including LiDAR scans and task vectors. Training was conducted using a three stage curriculum over 900,000 episodes, progressing the agent from local goal reaching to pickup and dropoff routines. Results compare this learning based approach against a classical ROS2 Nav2 baseline, which achieved a 100% success rate for static navigation tasks. While the baseline method excelled in predictability, the PPO policy successfully demonstrated the ability to learn end to end task logic and generalization in a dynamic environment.

title: Decentralized Path Planning in Lunar Robot Swarms: Local Optimization for Collision Avoidance Under Constrained Perception
authors: Y. Zhang; W. Wang; S. Wu; V. Y. Razoumny; Y. N. Razoumny
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: This article investigates decentralized safe path planning for lunar robot systems in dynamic environments with limited perception and communication capabilities and proposes a decentralized planning–control framework based on local path replanning. For clarity, we first define system models for complex dynamic scenarios and multirobot systems. Then, the decentralized framework is systematically developed through two complementary parts: 1) ensuring feasible path replanning under collision conditions and 2) preventing secondary collisions caused by path tracking control. Concretely, path reachability analysis is applied to derive quantifiable replanning criteria based on discrete sampling intervals, supported by a reachable set algorithm that theoretically guarantees replanning feasibility. Path relevance constraints are extended through an analysis of collision-prone waypoints, effectively eliminating the risks in continuous trajectory. To enhance practical robustness, bounded uncertainties from tracking control and environment are taken into consideration in the actual application. On this basis, a comprehensive numerical synthesis is proposed. Finally, lunar base construction simulations validate the proposed decentralized planning–control framework, demonstrating its effectiveness in safe path planning and its scalability in large-scale multirobot deployments.

title: IoT-based Industrial Safety and Monitoring System with Real-Time Alert Mechanism
authors: P. ArunKumar; M. C; M. K. M; M. I. K. A
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: Manufacturing sites, chemical plants, and power plants as the major components of industrial settings are often at the risk of exposure to harmful conditions such as gas leakages, fire outbreaks, sudden temperature rises, and equipment failures. Conventional safety systems have mainly focused on monitoring and alarm generation. Still, they have heavily relied on humans who during emergencies tend to respond slowly thereby delaying the critical response times. In case of an emergency, the IoT, enabled industrial safety and monitoring system here proposed can hazard detection and perform the functions necessary to eliminate or mitigate the risk autonomously. This system uses an ESP32 microcontroller along with several sensors that help to determine temperature, humidity, gas concentration, flame presence, and human approach. Upon sensing these conditions, the system without human intervention turns on the Automatic Shutdown System that first disconnects power to the critical loads and then gives Smart Emergency Routing instructions which is a way of guiding workers away from danger to the nearest safe exit. Furthermore, an incident data logger is used to keep records of the sensor readings and event data, which can later be used for event analysis. The data via Wi, Fi are transmitted to a cloud platform for remote monitoring and instant alerting. Results of experimental evaluations reveal that the system being put forward enables quick responses, dependable hazard detection, and safety improvement in an industrial setting through intelligent and automatically made decisions based on data.

title: Data-Driven Collaborative Perception and Predictive Control for Humanoid Robot Swarms in Unstructured Environments
authors: X. Zhu; Y. Zhang; A. Ji; Z. Pei; J. Fu; P. Wang
venue: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering (ICBDSE)
abstract: Amid the intelligent transformation of multi-robot systems, there are critical challenges in traditional single-robot perception and control systems, such as limited sensing coverage, data processing bottlenecks, and suboptimal collaborative decision-making. To address these, a data-driven collaborative perception and control system leveraging humanoid robots and embodied intelligence is proposed. Grounded in embodied intelligence theory, a multi-source data fusion framework is employed to orchestrate heterogeneous sensor data from multiple robots. A cloud-edge-device collaborative architecture enables hierarchical data processing and decision-making, while Model Predictive Control (MPC) is integrated with the A* search algorithm for trajectory optimization to ensure collision avoidance. Furthermore, real-time data feedback and dynamic constraints of humanoid robots are incorporated into online trajectory optimization to enhance tracking accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the system effectively adapts to various unstructured environments, significantly improves perception coverage and data processing efficiency, and provides a feasible solution for intelligent multi-robot collaborative systems.

title: Industrial Accidents and Safety for Worker Welfare: Controlling and Monitoring
authors: K.Chandrasekaran; V. V. K; Manogar.K; KavinKumar.P
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
abstract: Industrial safety remains a critical concern across manufacturing and hazardous sectors, where worker welfare depends on timely detection and mitigation of risks. This paper presents a novel Hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Safety Intelligence Framework (HyNeSSI) designed to proactively monitor, predict, and control industrial accidents using situational, real-time intelligence. The proposed framework integrates that the system uses a self-supervised visual encoding pipeline multi-modal sensor data provided by Smart PPE, visual risk mapping through self-supervised learning, emotion-aware behavioral profiling with the Capsule Networks and temporal causality modeling through graph neural networks. Violations of safety are detected through vision language alignment and zero-shot capability and adaptive safety feedback through multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments conducted across 10 industrial scenarios demonstrated that HyNeSSI was superior to traditional CNN and rule-based systems regarding the average violation detection accuracy (95.3%), behavioral risk classification F1-score (93.1%), and causal prediction accuracy (90.4%). The latency of the response to alerts was minimized (by 27.5) relative to baseline models. In addition, SHAP and LIME-based interpretability enhanced the trust of safety officers more than 40 %. HyNeSSI is a scalable and intelligent yet interpretable solution to safety monitoring fit to be deployed in real time. The extensions in the future can be federated implementation of the distributed industrial locations, as well as implementation of predictive maintenance modules in a way of avoiding the risk at the machinery level.

title: Learning-Assisted Formation Control of Networked Wheeled Robots With Barrier Safety Penalty
authors: Y. -Z. Xiang; X. Chen; J. Guo; Z. Xiang
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: This article investigates the formation control problem of Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled networked wheeled robots subject to environmental disturbances, safety constraints, and model uncertainties. To ensure safe operation in dynamic and complex environments, a barrier penalty-based safety mechanism is first constructed for each robot to achieve collision avoidance while maintaining the desired formation configuration. On this basis, a distributed model predictive control (MPC) framework is developed to generate coordinated control actions using locally exchanged information. Furthermore, an identifier–actor–critic reinforcement learning (RL) architecture is integrated with the barrier penalty mechanism, enabling the robots to compensate for unknown dynamics and external disturbances without requiring accurate system models. Simulation results on networked wheeled robots verify the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach for intelligent multirobot systems in IoT-based applications.

title: Reinforcement Learning and MPC-Based Multi-Robot Safe Shape Formation for Collision Avoidance in Human-Aware Indoor Environment
authors: M. G. Tiwari; K. Anirudha; A. R. Chowdhury
venue: 2026 15th Asian Control Conference (ASCC)
abstract: Multi-Robot Systems (MRS) are becoming increasingly important in ensuring safe movement in environments with the coexistence of robots and humans. In this paper, we demonstrate shape formation among three differential drive mobile robots in an indoor industrial setting environment, while ensuring safety through collision avoidance and operational security. We propose a nonlinear learning-based control strategy in which shape formation occurs in a manner that provides safety around a faulty robot. To further enhance safety, a novel metric is introduced for heterogeneous MRS operating in a human-aware environment. It is aimed at preventing collisions both among robots and between robots and humans. Additionally, a comparative analysis of these control strategies, including Non-linear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Reinforcement Learning (RL), is conducted to identify the most effective approach for controlling multi-robot systems. Experimental results show high accuracy in tracking goals and positions, with position accuracy rates between 98.73% and 99.82% in different test cases, while maintaining minimal final position errors, where (1.0846, 1.9406) and (6.0843, −1.0632) closely approximate the desired goals. From the comparative analysis, it has been observed that the NMPC controller performs better than the RL-based DDPG controller in terms of stability and precision. RL-based methods show competitive results in orientation tracking up to 99.86%. The proposed framework has been successfully implemented to form shapes, avoid collisions, and move coordinately, and its feasibility has been tested through simulation and practical implementation using TurtleBot3 robots in an indoor environment.

title: A Comprehensive Investigation of Security Vulnerabilities in Distributed Multi-Robot Systems
authors: R. Sagwal; V. Gupta
venue: 2026 18th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
abstract: The rapid deployment of multi-robot systems in critical missions such as exploration, surveillance, and disaster response has heightened the demand for cyber-connectivity, thereby increasing their exposure to cyber–physical threats. Among these applications, exploration serves as the foundation for subsequent tasks. Most existing exploration algorithms assume cooperative, trustworthy teammates and secure communication, overlooking insider threats and timing-based attacks. We investigate the vulnerability of distributed online exploration algorithms to two particularly stealthy attack types Sybil and Delay attacks, which exploit identity spoofing and message timing manipulation to degrade coordination, induce redundancy, and compromise coverage. Through simulation-based experiments on varying grid sizes and team configurations, we show that these attacks lead to incomplete mapping, false area coverage, and significant mission delays. Furthermore, strategic placement of adversarial robots is analyzed to evaluate the spatial influence of attacks. The study highlights critical vulnerabilities in current MRS coordination frameworks and motivates the design of self-adaptive, lightweight, and decentralized security mechanisms for resilient multi-robot exploration in adversarial environments.

title: An Architectural Approach for Multimodal Robot Control
authors: F. Cicirelli; A. F. Gentile; A. Guerrieri; M. B. Islam; Q. Li; E. Oro; L. Rizzo; A. Vinci; P. Zicari
venue: 2026 22nd International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things (DCOSS-IoT)
abstract: Modern robotic systems increasingly require the integration of heterogeneous interaction modalities and adaptive decision-making capabilities.
