Ablation results indicate that TAER and ASM each contribute to performance and provide additional gains when combined. These findings suggest that CBF interventions can serve as useful feedback for improving the safety and efficiency of MARL policies in the evaluated multi-robot setting.

title: Robust k-Maintained Multi Agent Path Replanning Under Fault Conditions
authors: X. Liu; Y. Hua; Y. Wang; Z. Ji
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper introduces Robust $k$ -Maintained Multi-Agent Path Replanning (R $k$ M-MAPR) algorithm, designed to address robustness in Multi-Agent Path Replanning (MAPR) when agents encounter faults. First, we introduce the temporary destination assignment strategy, which dynamically reassigns goals to agents when the primary destinations are inaccessible due to the failure of other agents. Then, we propose the R $k$ M-MAPR algorithm which replans paths and ensures safety while considering $k$ delays in MAPR under fault conditions. We delineate the replanned paths by giving the initial $k$ steps special consideration, using the Action Dependency Graph (ADG) to simulate and establish the simulated paths as the initial $k$ steps of the paths. Beyond this critical phase, the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) algorithm takes over, ensuring collision avoidance for the subsequent paths. Furthermore, we prove the collision-free nature and the $k$ -step robustness of the replanned paths. This analysis underpins the practical applicability of the R $k$ M-MAPR algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness through both simulations and real-world experiments.

title: Meta-Reinforcement-Learning-Based eVTOL Scheduling for Urban Logistics
authors: Y. Deng
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Technologies and Applications (ICAITA)
abstract: Urban low-altitude logistics requires eVTOL fleets to complete delivery tasks under dynamic demand, strict airspace constraints and multi-aircraft coordination. This paper proposes an $\mathbf{R L}^{\mathbf{2}}$-MAPPO scheduling method for rapid adaptation across different scenario configurations under the same task-generation mechanism. A grid-based urban airspace is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process, and a shared recurrent actor with memory attention is used to encode interaction history. A centralized critic and a scene-adaptive reward-weight module are introduced to improve training stability and dynamically balance completion, timeliness, safety and energy-related objectives. Experiments on independent emergency evaluation tasks show that the proposed method maintains high completion with low violation under unseen scenario configurations.

title: Integrated Task and Motion Planner Using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Robot Collaboration
authors: J. Zhang; C. Mu; K. Wang; L. Ren
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The task planning and motion planning problems in multi task and multi robot collaboration are usually considered as independent parts to be solved. However, in long-horizon, multi-step collaborative scenarios, this independent solution approach is difficult to effectively handle the coupling problem between task planning and motion planning, such as the inability to simultaneously consider robot motion collisions during task allocation. To address these limitations, we develop a unified hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that enables agents to learn effective policies in multi task and multi robot collaborative motion planning, supplemented by two techniques: 1) using a shared graph attention network and distributed police networks to assign target tasks to each robot at a high level, and 2) training decentralized motion planning policies for each robot at a low level to control the workspace state and target end actuator posture. The high-level and low-level policies are trained in parallel and stabilized through expert dataset guidance. To verify the effectiveness of the method, we conduct experiments on a general object placement platform and an engine hydraulic column assembly platform. The results indicate that this method can more efficiently complete multi task and multi robot collaborative work. Note to Practitioners—This study proposes an integrated task and motion planner for executing long-horizon, multi-step collaborative tasks in multi-robot systems. Traditional methods usually treat task planning and motion planning as two independent processes, which makes it difficult to fully consider the dynamic constraints of the robot’s actual motion during the task allocation stage, resulting in frequent collisions and other issues during execution. To address this challenge, this study constructs a unified framework based on hierarchical reinforcement learning, which achieves efficient collaboration of multi-robot systems through collaborative optimization of task planning and motion planning. Future work will focus on studying the adaptability of this method in dynamic task environments and further expanding its application potential in diverse industrial scenarios.

title: Predictive Flocking of an Omnidirectional Multi-Agent System for Lattice Formation: Sigma-Norm Design and Comparative Performance Assessment
authors: E. E. Hernández; H. Mirhajianmoghadam; E. S. Espinoza; L. R. G. Carrillo
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper presents a decentralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) flocking algorithm based on the sigma norm, designed to achieve coordinated motion among agents while ensuring collision avoidance and lattice formation. The proposed method is rigorously compared against a seminal classic flocking model and two advanced MPC-based strategies that incorporate lattice-structured cost functions. Through a series of statistical hypothesis tests, we demonstrate that the proposed approach reliably achieves the target lattice configuration, ensures convergence to a common velocity, and prevents collisions with both obstacles and neighboring agents. The results show that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches, offering superior performance and reliability for multi-agent systems modeled as omnidirectional four-wheeled robots.

title: GELATO: Multi-Instruction Trajectory Reshaping via Geometric-Aware Multiagent-Based Orchestration
authors: J. Huang; Y. Gong; C. Li; X. Duan; L. Figueredo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Language is one of the most intuitive ways for humans to communicate intent or corrections, however, translating high-level open-vocabulary instructions into reliable robot spatial motion adaptations is far from trivial. Language instructions are typically contextual, without the spatial precision required for robot execution, while the resulting motion must simultaneously respect geometric, kinematic, and environmental conditions. This becomes particularly challenging when several instructions interact or impose conflicting spatial requirements, spatial relationships that are not necessarily apparent to the user when expressing them. To bridge this gap, we present GELATO, a language-driven trajectory-reshaping framework that explicitly unifies semantic interpretation with geometric scene reasoning, connecting high-level user intent to verifiable robot-motion adaptations. GELATO automatically constructs a semantic–geometric representation of the environment by registering scene objects as 6D analytic primitives through a VLM-assisted multi-view pipeline. An LLM translates free-form instructions into explicit geometric and kinematic conditions tied to these representations, which are incorporated into a geometry-aware vector-field optimisation for trajectory reshaping. A multi-agent orchestration further explores such geometrically verifiable conditions together with complementary ways of resolving interacting instructions, while an Observer–Refinement loop verifies the resulting motion, checks constraint satisfaction, and adjusts failed candidates, increasing the success rate without retraining. Simulated, user studies, and real-world quantitative results demonstrate that our method achieves smoother, safer, and more reliable solutions compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with a high success rate on complex multi-instruction examples. Note to Practitioners—Robots are increasingly deployed near people in homes, care settings, and flexible workspaces, where users need intuitive ways to modify and correct their motion without reprogramming the system. In such scenarios, a practical challenge is to interpret multiple natural-language instructions, often conflicting, and convert them into reliable, context-aware, collision-free trajectory adaptations. GELATO addresses this problem through a modular, open-vocabulary framework for multi-instruction trajectory reshaping. Using off-the-shelf RGB-D cameras and vision models, it automatically registers scene objects as 6D analytic primitives, enabling more interpretable and predictable trajectory updates than point-based alternatives. It further introduces a multi-agent orchestration strategy that explores complementary ways of resolving interacting instructions, providing broader coverage of the solution space rather than a single strategy alone. By mapping language into explicit geometric constraints and reasoning over object pose and primitive shapes, GELATO generates, verifies, and refines multiple trajectory modifications, ensuring the users intent is satisfied while maintaining safe clearances. In practice, this provides a reliable way to deploy human-guided robots without retraining or requiring users to have programming expertise, offering a practical reference for more intuitive collaboration in industrial and service robotics.

title: Learning-Based Decentralized Control With Collision Avoidance for Multiagent Systems
authors: O. Y. Nieto; A. A. Simoes; J. I. Giribet; L. J. Colombo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
abstract: In this article, we present a learning-based tracking controller based on Gaussian processes (GP) for collision avoidance of multiagent systems where the agents evolve in the special Euclidean group in the space SE(3). In particular, we use GPs to estimate certain uncertainties that appear in the dynamics of the agents. The control algorithm is designed to learn and mitigate these uncertainties by using GPs as a learning-based model for the predictions. In particular, the presented approach guarantees that the tracking error remains bounded with high probability. We present some simulation results to show how the control algorithm is implemented.

title: CREST: Constraint-Release Execution for Multi-Robot Warehouse Shelf Rearrangement
authors: J. Tan; Y. Luo; S. Huang; Y. Yang; H. Ma
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Double-Deck Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (DD-MAPD) models the multi-robot shelf rearrangement problem in automated warehouses. MAPF-DECOMP is a recent framework that first computes collision-free shelf trajectories with a MAPF solver and then assigns agents to execute them. While efficient, it enforces strict trajectory dependencies, often leading to poor execution quality due to idle agents and unnecessary shelf switching. We introduce CREST, a new execution framework that achieves more continuous shelf carrying by proactively releasing trajectory constraints during execution. Experiments on diverse warehouse layouts show that CREST consistently outperforms MAPF-DECOMP, reducing metrics related to agent travel, makespan, and shelf switching by up to 40.5%, 33.3%, and 44.4%, respectively, with even greater benefits under lift/place overhead. These results underscore the importance of execution-aware constraint release for scalable warehouse rearrangement.

title: Collision-Free Leader-Follower Formation Control for Unicycle Robots Using Control Barrier Functions
authors: J. Liu; W. Zhang; P. Li; G. Zhang
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: This paper presents a leader-follower formation control method for unicycle robots in obstacle-rich environments. A backstepping-based nominal control protocol is firstly proposed to ensure asymptotic formation convergence. Building on it, a safety-guaranteed protocol that integrates distance-based control barrier functions is designed to resolve the relative degree mismatch via a quadratic program(QP). This method achieves formation control while ensuring collision avoidance among all agents as well as between agents and obstacles. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Llm-Based Multi-Agent Simulation System: Design and Quantitative Evaluationof Asymmetric Decision Protocols with Configurable Blocking Thresholds
authors: K. Liu; H. Li
venue: 2026 International Conference on Complex Systems, Intelligent Science and Computing Technology (CSITec)
abstract: The design of decision mechanisms significantly impacts consensus generation in multi-agent systems (MAS), yet few computational frameworks have systematically evaluated these protocols in complex, asymmetric environments where agents possess heterogeneous decision-making power. In this paper, we present a novel LLM-driven multi-agent simulation system designed to model and evaluate multilateral deliberation under configurable threshold-based decision protocols. We conduct a controlled computational experiment comparing two distinct algorithmic protocols: a baseline single-agent blocking rule (where any single privileged agent can block a proposal) and a relaxed blocking threshold (WV) mechanism requiring at least two concurrent negative judgments to block proposal adoption. Technically, our system introduces a complete generative pipeline comprising dynamic hidden goal generation, structured multi-dimensional text debate, power-weighted proposal synthesis via a Chair agent, and an independent LLM-as-a-judge Evaluator agent for post-hoc assessment. Deployed across 12 diverse thematic scenarios using DeepSeek-V3, our simulation reveals significant emergent behaviors governed by algorithmic constraints. Paradoxically, the relaxed blocking threshold regime decreases the overall proposal adoption rate to 71.3% (vs. 79.6% under the single-agent blocking baseline). This is driven by the alleviation of the "blocking chill" effect—an emergent phenomenon where removing the absolute single-agent blocking constraint encourages LLM agents to express dissent more freely. Furthermore, we demonstrate how this threshold shift forces the Chair agent's synthesis algorithm to adopt "lowest common denominator" language, computationally favoring agents with defensive profiles while diluting the influence of assertive agenda-setters. Our work contributes a robust computational testbed for evaluating decision protocol design in asymmetric multi-agent systems and demonstrates how algorithmic decision constraints alter LLM reasoning and negotiation dynamics.

title: A Hierarchical Nested Constraint Scheme for Finite-Time Formation Tracking Control of Disturbed Second-Order Multiagent Systems
authors: G. Wang; X. Wang; S. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: This article proposes a hierarchical nested constraint finite-time formation control scheme to solve the formation control problem of disturbed second-order multiagent systems with collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. The main idea of the proposed approach is to achieve agent collision avoidance and connectivity preservation goals in a nested manner by allocating the spatial distance constraints to the reference signals and the tracking control errors in the hierarchical formation control strategy, respectively. In general, the proposed method inherits the advantages of the hierarchical control scheme and integrates both collision avoidance and connectivity preservation functions, while realizing finite-time formation convergence and multichannel disturbance handling under agent spatial distance constraints. This combination of capabilities is not achieved in the existing reports. The proposed method is applied to an actual multi-mobile robot system to demonstrate its effectiveness.

title: Adaptive Target Trapping with Multirobot Systems via Distributed Probabilistic Inference
authors: M. Huang; D. Xiao; Y. Sun; H. Pu; J. Luo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: In the field of multiagent systems, the multirobot coordinated encirclement task in a dense environment is extremely challenging. However, existing methods often rely on pre-defined task assignments, limiting the system’s ability for self-organized encirclement, which undermines robustness, especially against agile targets in dense environments. To address this issue, a novel distributed probabilistic inference model for cooperative trapping is proposed, based on adaptive cooperative trapping factors. The model can propagate Gaussian messages in parallel using the incremental collaborative Gaussian belief propagation (ICGBP) algorithm, achieving self-organized encirclement, thereby enhancing capture efficiency and ensuring effective collision avoidance. Specifically, we derive the relationships between Gaussian messages under various constraints and provide theoretical proof to guarantee the asymptotic convergence of the algorithm. Moreover, we extensively investigate the relationships between several parameters of task configuration and trapping success rates, determining the optimal range of the adaptive shrinking radius. Finally, both simulations and real-world experiments with highly maneuverable and human-controlled targets are performed, validating the effectiveness and robustness of ICGBP for multirobot adaptive target trapping under high-randomness unknown evasion strategies.

title: Global Connectivity Maintenance-Based Formation Optimization Control for Multi-Agent Systems with Input Saturation
authors: L. Yang; Z. Yan; X. Ma
venue: 2026 5th Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (FASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a cooperative control strategy for multi-robot systems subject to input saturation constrains while executing multi-task formation control in complex environments, with a focus on global connectivity preservation and shortest-path tracking. A distributed Fiedler eigenvalue estimation algorithm is developed, enabling each robot to evaluate and maintain the algebraic connectivity of the system in real time using only local interactions, thereby preserving global connectivity of the communication topology. Under input saturation constrains, a shortest-path optimization method based on global connectivity preservation is proposed, achieving optimal dynamic target tracking and formation reconfiguration. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in terms of constraint satisfaction and task execution.

title: SLEI3D: Simultaneous Exploration and Inspection via Heterogeneous Fleets Under Limited Communication
authors: J. Chen; Y. Zhu; X. Zhang; B. Luo; M. Guo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Robotic fleets such as uncrewed aerial and ground vehicles have been widely used for routine inspections of static environments, where the areas of interest are known and planned in advance. However, in many applications, such areas of interest are unknown and should be identified online during exploration. Thus, this paper considers the problem of simultaneous exploration, inspection of unknown environments and then real-time communication to a mobile ground control station to report the findings. The heterogeneous robots are equipped with different sensors, e.g., long-range lidars for fast exploration and close-range cameras for detailed inspection. Furthermore, global communication is often unavailable in such environments, where the robots can only communicate with each other via ad-hoc wireless networks when they are in close proximity and free of obstruction. This work proposes a novel planning and coordination framework (SLEI3D) that integrates the online strategies for collaborative 3D exploration, adaptive inspection and timely communication (via the intermittent or proactive protocols). To account for uncertainties w.r.t. the number and location of features, a multi-layer and multi-rate planning mechanism is developed for inter-and-intra robot subgroups, to actively meet and coordinate their local plans. The proposed framework is validated extensively via high-fidelity simulations of numerous large-scale missions with up to 48 robots and 384 thousand cubic meters. Hardware experiments of 7 robots are also conducted. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by the challenges of coordinating large-scale heterogeneous fleets for the inspection of large buildings and infrastructure, where heterogeneous UAVs must collaborate to explore unknown environments, identify areas of interest, and more importantly, inspect specific features (such as cracks, leaks, and other anomalies). Furthermore, these features must be relayed back to a control station for further analyses. Existing methods predominantly focuses on exploration tasks and often overlooks the need for close-up inspection. Instead, a hierarchical and flexible framework is proposed to coordinate a group of heterogeneous UAVs online for efficient exploration, inspection and communication, subject to an unknown number and location of features. Instead of relying on an all-to-all communication network, limited communication range and bandwidth are addressed by leveraging intermittent and proactive communication protocols, i.e., to enable exchange of local plans, explored areas, and detected features during online execution. Via extensive simulations in a high-fidelity simulator, the proposed framework is shown to be efficient and reliable for large-scale simultaneous exploration and inspection tasks within various scenes. Robustness to robot failures and communication loss is also demonstrated. Hardware experiments over UGVs and UAVs validate the practical relevance.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Edge Caching for Industry 5.0: A Survey of Collaborative and Inference-Enabled Techniques
authors: R. Maiti; A. Madhukumar; T. Z. Hui Ernest
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
abstract: Industry 5.0 is transforming edge caching from a passive traffic offloading mechanism into an active enabler of distributed intelligence and real-time analytics. However, conventional caching strategies lack the collaborative adaptability, inference-awareness, and domain-specific customization required for dynamic Industry 5.0 workloads. This survey provides a comprehensive and systematic review of machine learning (ML)-driven edge caching organized around two fundamental pillars: collaborative caching (distributed, federated, and multi-agent reinforcement learning paradigms) and inference-enabled caching (content and model placement accelerating real-time edge analytics). We systematically examine how traditional ML, deep learning (DL), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and multi-agent RL (MARL) techniques address domain-specific challenges across five Industry 5.0 applications: robotics, manufacturing, logistics, immersive training, and healthcare. For each domain, we provide comparative assessments based on latency requirements, scalability targets, and collaboration needs. Our analysis reveals fundamental tradeoffs: MARL excels for distributed coordination with promising efficiency gains but requires higher computational resources, while DRL balances adaptation and complexity, and federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaboration across multiple sites. Each application section concludes with Key Insights synthesizing technique suitability, domain requirements, performance gains, and unresolved challenges. We identify five critical research directions: Bayesian optimization for sample-efficient learning, federated workflow-aware caching with sub-second staleness, resilient caching under intermittent connectivity, scalable multi-modal caching with low latency, and mission-critical prioritization meeting industry standards. This work provides a roadmap for designing adaptive, safe, and scalable ML-driven edge caching systems for intelligent industrial operations.

title: Towards Communication Efficient Multi-Agent Cooperations: Reinforcement Learning and LLM
authors: Y. Su; Y. Du; Y. Deng; M. Dohler
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) have gained popularity due to their effectiveness in diverse applications. Among these, decentralized approaches, which rely on inter-agent communication, have emerged as a promising alternative to centralized MAS coordination methods. However, existing communication protocols often learn abstract representations that are difficult for humans to interpret. Also, the limited wireless bandwidth in real-world applications imposes a significant challenge on efficient communication among agents. To address these issues, in this paper, we consider a multi-robot navigation scenario and propose a goal-oriented human-interpretable feature communication protocol, enabling robots to transmit only the most semantically important features. Building on this protocol, we first introduce a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO)-based Bandwidth-Adaptive Dual-Policy (MAPPO-BDP) framework, which employs a dual-policy architecture to jointly optimize feature selection and navigation under bandwidth constraints. However, as MAPPO-BDP requires retraining for different bandwidth constraints, we further propose a Large Language Model (LLM)-based Bandwidth-Adaptive Dual-Policy (LLM-BDP) framework. By leveraging LLM-based multi-agents, LLM-BDP can adapt to varying bandwidth constraints by simply modifying the input prompt, thereby eliminating the need for retraining. Experimental results show that both MAPPO-BDP and LLM-BDP frameworks successfully complete navigation tasks within a limited number of steps by effectively communicating the most important features under bandwidth constraints. We demonstrate that LLM-BDP achieves better reasoning adaptability by utilizing more advanced LLMs and engineering example prompts. Notably, with human-interpretable feature communication protocol, robots trained with the MAPPO-BDP framework can seamlessly collaborate with robots from the LLM-BDP framework to complete tasks, even without co-training, demonstrating the practical applicability of the proposed communication protocol in new scenarios.

title: C-CBF: Communication-Aware Control Barrier Functions for Resilient Multi-Robot Connectivity
authors: T. -S. Nguyen; H. -N. Cao; N. H. Thai; M. T. Pham
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Ensuring resilient operation in networked multi-robot systems is critical when both physical safety and wireless communication are challenged by environmental uncertainty or adversarial interference. This paper presents Communication-Aware Control Barrier Function (C-CBF), a scalable control framework that integrates probabilistic communication constraints into safety-critical control synthesis using Control Barrier Functions (CBFs). By modeling wireless degradation via Rician fading, we formulate a reception-aware constraint that is optimized jointly with inter-agent collision avoidance through local Quadratic Programs (QPs). Each robot computes its control input using only neighbor state information. A decoupled approximation of globally coupled constraints ensures real-time feasibility. Adaptive slack variables enable the system to remain feasible even under conflicting demands, enhancing robustness in complex environments. Simulation results demonstrate that C-CBF ensures safe and connected operation across large-scale, cluttered environments under severe fading conditions. A confidence-tightened variant guarantees forward invariance in probability under channel-model mismatch. This leads to graceful degradation of safety without additional runtime cost. This framework provides a scalable foundation for resilient multi-robot autonomy and can be integrated with distributed optimal control solvers in future work. Note to Practitioners—Multi-robot systems deployed in cluttered, uncertain, or communication-degraded environments often struggle to stay connected while avoiding collisions. This work introduces a distributed control framework that enables each robot to plan safe movements while dynamically accounting for variations in wireless link quality. Unlike conventional solutions that treat communication and motion as separate layers, this method integrates both into a unified, real-time controller. By adaptively adjusting the level of enforcement for safety and connectivity, the system remains functional even when signal strength fluctuates due to distance, interference, or fading. The approach requires only local sensing and communication, making it scalable and robust without relying on centralized coordination. It is particularly relevant for practical deployments in disaster response, warehouse automation, or remote monitoring, where resilience and autonomy are essential. For future research, the framework could be extended with explicit cyber-attack detection and adaptive countermeasures against jamming or spoofing, further improving its utility in security-critical environments.

title: Triggered Adaptive Safety-Critical Cooperative Control and Application to Multiple Mecanum Wheel Robots
authors: J. Shen; X. Yu; L. Zhu; Y. Liu; W. Wang; J. Yan
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive safety-critical cooperative control scheme for multi-agent systems. For each safety constraint, a Control Barrier Function (CBF) is developed to quantify the degree of safety. To implement decentralization, the CBF constraint is decomposed into several sub-CBF constraints. For each agent, a batch identifier is designed to update the parameter estimates before any one of its relevant safety constraints is violated. By integrating the reference inputs, sub-CBF constraints and batch identifiers, we construct a decentralized safety-triggered adaptive quadratic programming controller. It is demonstrated that the effects of uncertainties are eliminated after a finite number of updates and the safety constraints are rigorously ensured. The proposed control scheme is applied to cooperative transportation of multiple Mecanum wheel robots.

title: Autonomous Robot Navigation in Warehouses Leveraging LIDAR IoT Communication and Edge AI for Real-Time Adaptive Path Planning and Efficient Intelligent Motion Control
authors: B. P; A. M; A. P; A. A; A. V; K. V
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: These research study proposes an Adaptive MultiSensor Fusion and Path Optimization (AMSFPO) algorithm implies a novel artificial intelligence-based navigation and control process and proposes its implementation to improve the efficiency and reliability of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) in a complex warehouse setup. The traditional robotic systems are often faced with the problem of dealing with unpredictable layouts, sensor errors, and making decisions quickly in a crowded or dynamic environment. In order to cope with these concerns, AMSFPO uses a smart combination of LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) RGB-D (RGB: Red, Green, Blue) and depth (D) cameras and ultrasonic sensors whereby the weight of sensors is dynamically modified based on the sensed uncertainty of the environment. This system is based on a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) engine with a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) to keep the path straight, evade collisions, and navigate without any hassles. In contrast to the classical A* algorithm and the Dijkstra algorithm, AMSFPO is an iterative approach to energy optimization of the paths, in which numerous operating factors, such as the payload, traffic laws, and battery status, are taken into account in the adaptive feedback. Simulation experiments have shown that the proposed algorithm increases the accuracy of navigation by about 24 percent and minimizes the collisions by 31 percent in comparison to the SLAM-MPC (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping with Model Predictive Control) and LiDAR-only methods. It has a modular design that facilitates its smooth deployment on a variety of robotic platforms and it can be scaled in multi-agent warehouse systems. Altogether, AMSFPO represents a new benchmark of the intelligent warehouse automation, welding perception, path planning, and control into the safer, smarter, and more efficient warehouse logistics in the age of Industry 5.0

title: WinkTPG: An Execution Framework for Multi-Agent Path Finding Using Temporal Reasoning
authors: J. Yan; S. F. Smith; J. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Planning collision-free paths for a large group of agents is a challenging problem in many real-world applications. While recent advances in Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) have shown promising progress, standard MAPF planners continue to rely on simplified kinodynamic models, preventing agents from directly following the generated MAPF plan. To bridge this gap, we propose kinodynamic Temporal Plan Graph planning (kTPG), a multi-agent speed optimization algorithm that efficiently refines a MAPF plan into a set of kinodynamically feasible speed profiles. We further incorporate execution timing uncertainty models and provide deterministic guarantees under bounded uncertainty models and probabilistic guarantees under stochastic models. Building on kTPG, we propose Windowed kTPG (WinkTPG), a MAPF execution framework that incrementally refines MAPF plans using a window-based mechanism, dynamically incorporating agent information during execution to reduce uncertainty. Experiments show that WinkTPG can generate speed profiles for up to 1,000 agents within 1 second and improves solution quality by up to 51.7% over existing MAPF execution methods. We further validate WinkTPG in high-fidelity physics-based simulation and on real-world robots. Note to Practitioners—The motivation of this article originates from the need to execute large-scale multi-agent path-planning solutions reliably in practical applications such as warehouse logistics, industrial material transport, and factory or airport automation. Although discrete MAPF planners can generate conflict-free paths, their solutions are often not directly executable by real robots due to kinodynamic constraints and execution timing uncertainties. This article develops WinkTPG, a windowed execution framework that converts MAPF plans into safe and kinodynamically feasible speed profiles while maintaining precedence relations implied by the discrete plan. WinkTPG further employs receding-horizon replanning to correct timing deviations caused by disturbances or sensing noise, making it suitable for practitioners deploying multi-robot fleets in constrained, time-critical environments.

title: Adaptive Task Token Framework for Multi-Agent Logistics Operations
authors: K. Shah; A. Gupta; B. Ho; J. Kim; H. -i. Won; S. -K. Choi
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD) extends Multi-Agent Path Finding to long-horizon settings where pickup-and-delivery tasks arrive online and agents must be assigned and routed continuously, as in automated warehouses. Existing MAPD methods leave three gaps that limit real-world deployment. First, token-based methods such as Token Passing (TP) and TP with Task Swaps (TPTS) assign tasks sequentially, yielding greedy, globally suboptimal allocations and leaving idle agents parked where they obstruct active agents. Second, these methods assume disruption-free execution and provide no recovery from the delays and deadlocks common on real robots; k-TP adds delay tolerance but only conservatively and at high computational cost. Third, centralized optimal methods such as CENTRAL coordinate well but do not scale to real-time operation. To close these gaps, we propose the Adaptive Task Token Framework (ATTF), which (i) replaces sequential assignment with a global, proximity-based module that pairs all idle agents with all available tasks simultaneously by travel cost, and (ii) introduces a unified delay-and-deadlock-resilient mechanism that truncates and replans only affected paths and redirects idle agents to non-task endpoints to relieve congestion. Across diverse warehouse layouts, ATTF matches or improves on TP and TPTS in makespan and service time, and outperforms k-TP on all three metrics under delays – reducing service time by up to 49% and runtime by ${\sim }82\%$ – while sustaining sub-second per-timestep runtime for up to 500 agents, a scale at which k-TP fails to produce solutions.

title: Game-Theoretic Insights into Multi-Agent LLM Debate for Enhanced Clinical Question Answering
authors: S. Sudhakara; S. Sudhakara
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have advanced in medical question answering, yet ensuring reliability remains challenging. We study multi-agent debate (MAD), where multiple LLM agents critique and aggregate each other’s answers. Our game-theoretic analysis shows that majority voting improves accuracy, confidence-weighted aggregation (e.g., with an LLM judge) is optimal under calibration, and early stopping yields efficiency with little loss. We implement MAD for multiple-choice medical questions (MedQA) and evaluate it across five frontier language models, comparing single-shot prompting, chain-of-thought (CoT), and MAD with 2 or 3 agents. MAD with 3 agents consistently outperforms single-shot and CoT, reaching 90% accuracy on Claude Sonnet 3.7 (vs. 88% with CoT). Moreover, early consensus allows most debates to end in early rounds, reducing latency. These results align with theory and suggest MAD as a promising path toward more accurate and trustworthy medical QA systems.

title: Bézier Curve-Based Optimization Framework for Multirobot Motion Planning in Unknown Environments
authors: A. Mazen; M. Faied; M. Krishnan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
abstract: In recent years, multirobot systems (MRSs) have witnessed significant growth because of their capability of solving complex problems involving collaborative missions. A two-phase approach is typically employed in such applications, encompassing task planning and assignment among the robots, followed by motion planning to execute the assigned tasks. This work focuses on the motion planning phase, which facilitates the optimal navigation of multiple robots from their initial to desired goal configurations. A novel multirobot Bézier curve-based trajectory planner (MrBTP) is proposed. MrBTP generates optimal trajectories for multiple robots navigating in an unknown environment, including the polygonal characterization of the available open space. The optimization process is based on using a weighted objective function that combines the navigation time of each robot and the length of its trajectory, allowing for various path optimization strategies. The effectiveness of MrBTP has been evaluated in various scenarios, and its performance is compared with that of a selected trajectory planner based on three performance metrics. Over the three robots used in the test, MrBTP reduced the navigation time by 21%–49% and the trajectory length by 10%–18% compared to the selected benchmark trajectory planner. In addition, it ensures $C^{2}$ rather than just $C^{1}$ continuity.

title: hGCBF: Heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Functions for Safe Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Z. Yang; J. Liu; Z. Li; W. Zhang
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Provable safety remains a critical challenge for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs), where differences in dynamics, state/action spaces, and sensing capabilities compromise existing learning-based methods that assume system homogeneity. To address this gap, we propose the heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Function (hGCBF), the first neural control barrier function framework designed for heterogeneous MASs. Our approach introduces a novel extended system formulation via zero-padding to unify heterogeneous state-action spaces, upon which we formally define hGCBF and establish theoretical safety guarantees. We further design a heterogeneous graph neural network architecture with agent-type embeddings and a decoupled node/edge attention mechanism to jointly learn the hGCBF and a distributed controller, enhanced by type-specific loss weighting. Extensive experiments in large-scale 2D and 3D environments demonstrate that our approach achieves over 27% higher safety rates than homogeneous baselines at scale while maintaining strong performance under compositional shifts in agent-type ratios.

title: Environment-Aware Multi-Agent Framework for Self-Driving Laboratories
authors: H. Xue; W. Zheng; S. Lin; Y. Wang; L. Bao; X. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Most self-driving laboratories (SDLs) rely on the assumption of a static and fully known experimental environment prior to execution, neglecting potential pre-experimental deviations and human errors that may trigger cascading failures during operation.To address these limitations, this paper presents a multi-agent SDL framework incorporating pre-execution environment perception. The system is designed to emulate human-like manipulation intelligence, integrating natural language interaction, synthesis planning, dexterous environment perception, cognitive task planning, and adaptive robot execution into a closed-loop workflow. The system is coordinated through six specialized agents-task clarification, synthesis planning, environment perception, robot planning, robot execution, and feedback-collectively enabling end-to-end automation from user intent to experimental realization. Validation was conducted on a customized automation platform using hydrogel and silicone preparation tasks, supported by a dedicated dataset encompassing these processes and multiple types of potential anomalies inconsistent with predefined conditions. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in both synthesis planning and environment perception (with perception accuracy reaching 99.86%), along with significant improvements in task success rates: hydrogel preparation increased from 0.64 to 0.90, and silicone preparation from 0.60 to 0.92. These findings confirm that integrating environment perception with multi-agent collaboration effectively enhances system robustness, safety, and adaptability under unexpected anomalies, underscoring the framework’s potential for scalable deployment in real-world laboratory environments. Note to Practitioners—This work aims to develop an SDL capable of operating robustly under the imperfect conditions of real laboratory environments. We introduce a multi-agent framework that enables the SDL to perceive its surroundings before executing an experimental protocol. By integrating perception and planning agents, the system verifies whether the physical environment aligns with the operational requirements. It can also interact with users in natural language to clarify tasks and automatically identify anomalies that violate predefined conditions. We validated the effectiveness of this framework on a custom automated platform for hydrogel and silicone synthesis. The results show a substantial improvement in task success rate, translating directly into higher efficiency and reduced material consumption. Practically, embedding environmental perception and multi-agent verification into the experimental workflow enables the creation of autonomous systems that are not only more reliable and safer but also suitable for everyday research environments. The core architecture is platform-agnostic and can be applied to other laboratory automation and robotic manipulation tasks, particularly those where pre-execution validation is critical. In terms of system cost, based on our deployment experience, a setup equipped with basic pre-execution perception capabilities can be built for approximately USD 50,000-100,000. In terms of implementation effort, the deployment cycle from scratch to the first automated experiment typically ranges from 4 to 8 weeks, and can be even shorter for laboratories with existing automation infrastructure.

title: Adaptive Ant Colony Optimization With Dynamic Information Entropy for Multi-Robot Path Planning in Dynamic Environments
authors: S. Sun
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Control Engineering (ICAACE)
abstract: Traditional Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algori thms often suffer from slow convergence, local optima trapping, a nd poor adaptability in dynamic multi-robot path planning scena rios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Infor mation Entropy Ant Colony Optimization (DIEACO) algorithm, which integrates three core improvements: (1) an adaptive phero mone evaporation strategy based on population diversity; (2) a dy namic heuristic function that fuses obstacle density and path smo othness; (3) an information entropy-based termination criterion $\mathbf{t}$ o reduce redundant iterations. Experiments are conducted in $\mathbf{5 0} \boldsymbol{\times} \mathbf{5 0}$ grid environments with static/dynamic obstacles, comparing D IEACO with standard ACO and hybrid ACO-artificial potential f ield (APF) methods. Results show that DIEACO reduces average path length by 4.81 %, shortens convergence time by 56 %, and im proves collision avoidance success rate to 98 % in multi-robot syst ems. This work provides a robust path planning solution for dyna mic intelligent systems such as warehouse robots and search-andrescue drones.

title: Aerial Pursuit: Multi-Agent Swarm for Predator–Prey Games
authors: W. Zining; C. Haoran; Z. Jinqiu; P. Yifeng; S. Srigrarom; B. C. Khoo
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Control and Robotics (EECR)
abstract: This paper addresses the cold-start and convergence challenges of multi-agent adversarial reinforcement learning in physics-rich environments. The UAVs are modeled as predator-prey agents inspired by eagle-hen interactions. We propose a curriculum-based two-stage training scheme: Stage 1 trains the hens against a heuristic eagle, and Stage 2 freezes the learned hen policy while training the eagle. Using Box2D physics and Gymnasium interfaces, we build a reproducible engineering pipeline based on Stable-Baselines3 PPO, parallel sampling, and TensorBoard logging. Our main contributions include environment modeling (world construction, chain joints, boundary handling, and bounce dynamics), observation and reward design, parallel training with evaluation callbacks, and behavior visualization with metric analysis. The results show improved defensive behavior by the hens in Stage 1, reflected in increasing mean returns, explained variance approaching 1, and decreasing entropy loss. In Stage 2, the eagle learns effective approach and capture behaviors, producing positive potential-based rewards and sparse positive returns upon capture while maintaining smooth overall training curves. Remaining limitations include the empirical tuning of reward weights and physical parameters. Future work will explore joint fine-tuning, self-play, and more complex scenarios.

title: Undesired Equilibria-Free CLBF Safety Control for Multi-Robot Warehouse Systems
authors: A. S. Baswara; M. Z. Romdlony; H. Septanto; N. A. Wahab; M. A. Ismail
venue: 2026 15th Asian Control Conference (ASCC)
abstract: This paper proposes an undesired equilibria-free CLBF safety control via a Circulation CLBF (Circ-CLBF) for multi-robot navigation. CLBF offers a closed-form alternative to quadratic programming-based safety control, but suffers from saddle points where robots may become stuck despite active obstacle avoidance. We integrate a circulation CBF into the CLBF control via a hybrid automaton, detecting undesired equilibria using the angle between the CLF and CBF control vectors, and activating a smooth circulation input to deflect robots away from saddle points. We also incorporate a LiDAR-based CBF for online obstacle detection and a CBF-based conflict resolution (CBF-CR) for multi-robot priority handling. We validate Circ-CLBF in MATLAB across several scenarios: single-robot navigation around non-convex and circular obstacles, multi-robot opposing-goal cases, and a 12-robot two-room warehouse simulation. The results show that Circ-CLBF successfully escapes undesired equilibria in all tested cases while achieving safe navigation outside the safety distance throughout all tests.

title: AgentPay: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Autonomous Payment Orchestration with Formal Compliance Guarantees
authors: S. Upadhyay
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computing and Communication (ETCC)
abstract: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly taking over payment processing tasks, yet no existing framework combines multi-agent orchestration with formal regulatory compliance guarantees. We introduce AgentPay, a multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework for end-to-end payment orchestration. It deploys five specialized agents (Router, Reconciliation, Dispute, Compliance, and Orchestrator) communicating through typed message-passing protocols over shared transactional state. A central Compliance Verification Layer (CVL) pairs LLM-based intent classification with SMT-based symbolic rule checking. We prove a soundness property: any action the CVL permits satisfies every rule in the encoded PCI-DSS, PSD2, and AML ruleset, so legal compliance reduces to the faithfulness of that encoding rather than to model confidence. We also formalize a Safety-Bounded Autonomy Model (SBAM) as a constrained optimization that assigns per-agent autonomy levels, scores transaction risk, and derives escalation thresholds for human-in-the-loop intervention. An accompanying protocol, AgentPayBench, spans six payment workflow types at three complexity tiers. A 15,000transaction prototype runs the symbolic gate on the Z3 solver with a calibrated stand-in for the neural classifier. Here the gate reproduces the encoded rules exactly on the deterministic subset, an internal-consistency check (faithful realization of the encoding at scale) rather than a measure of real-world generalization; it escalates 31% of traffic, and the neuro-symbolic design dominates rule-only and single-classifier ablations on the same workload. To our knowledge, AgentPay is the first framework to integrate multi-agent payment orchestration with a verified symbolic compliance gate; production validation on real LLMs and expert-labeled data remains future work.

title: Metamorphic Testing of Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Trace-Based Behavioral Oracle Framework
authors: G. Marimuthu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Testing (AITest)
abstract: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for complex tasks requiring autonomous planning, tool use, and inter-agent coordination. However, the non-deterministic nature of LLM outputs and the emergent behavior arising from agent interactions render traditional test oracles ineffective, creating a critical gap in quality assurance for agentic AI. This work introduces MORPHAGENT, a framework designed to address the oracle problem in multi-agent LLM systems through trace-based behavioral analysis. Our contributions are threefold: (1) goal-preservation relations that verify consistent goal achievement under input perturbations, (2) coordination-consistency relations that validate inter-agent delegation and communication patterns under agent substitution and reordering, and (3) tool-use integrity relations that ensure semantic equivalence of tool invocation sequences under prompt paraphrasing. MorphAgent instruments agent execution to capture structured traces comprising planning steps, tool calls, message exchanges, and final outputs, then systematically applies metamorphic transformations and checks behavioral invariants without requiring ground-truth oracles. We evaluate the framework on four multi-agent benchmarks spanning code generation, research synthesis, customer service, and data analysis tasks, encompassing 2,840 source-followup execution pairs across three LLM backends. Results show that MORPHAGENT detects 82.0% of seeded behavioral faults, including 90.3% of coordination failures and 81.7% of goal-deviation faults, while maintaining a false positive rate of 6.1%. The framework uncovers 14 previously unreported behavioral anomalies in established multi-agent frameworks, demonstrating its practical utility for assuring agentic AI reliability. These results suggest that trace-based metamorphic testing can serve as a practical foundation for reliable validation of emerging agentic AI systems.

title: Agentic SOC: A Hierarchical Swarm-Orchestrated Multi-Agent LLM Architecture for Autonomous OT Cyber Defense
authors: M. A. Rahman; M. M. Rahman; S. U. Jamil; M. A. Paracha; M. S. Hossain
venue: 2026 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
abstract: The convergence of enterprise IT networks with operational technology (OT), industrial control systems (ICS), and 5G/6G wireless-enabled cyber-physical infrastructures has expanded the attack surface of critical environments, exposing limitations in traditional IT-centric Security Operations Centers (SOCs). IT–OT systems impose strict latency, safety, and availability constraints, while rule-based detection and human-driven triage lead to alert fatigue, delayed response, and fragmented visibility across wired and wireless domains. This paper presents Agentic SOC, a hierarchical swarm-orchestrated multi-agent LLM architecture for autonomous and adaptive cyber defense in IT–OT converged networks. The architecture decomposes SOC operations into three cooperative tiers: a perception layer of distributed agents performing real-time telemetry analysis across IT, OT, and wireless network domains; a reasoning layer executing cross-domain correlation, MITRE ATT&CK (including ICS) mapping, and coordinated mitigation; and a strategic leader agent conducting kill-chain reconstruction, RAG-grounded threat hunting, and adversarial simulation. We implement and evaluate Agentic SOC under a managed security service provider (MSSP) model across four safety-critical scenarios: 6G telecom infrastructure, a power generation plant, a railway control system, and a three-dimensional Security of Air–Ground–Space Integrated Networks (SAGIN) environment. Experimental benchmarking demonstrates broader threat coverage, improved cross-domain correlation, reduced false positives, and a lower mean time to detection and response compared to flat, multi-agent, and rule-based SOC baselines while preserving human-in-the-loop governance. Agentic SOC provides an experimentally validated blueprint for AI-native, self-protecting SOC architectures in next-generation IT–OT cyber-physical systems.

title: GridSCAPE: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Real-Time Intelligent Supply Chain Planning in Electric Power Enterprises
authors: H. He; Y. Gu
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
abstract: Supply chain planning is a core challenge in supply chain management, orchestrating heterogeneous item categories across multiple vendors, and Jointly optimizing end-to-end material flows, from sourcing and inbound logistics, through warehousing, to on-time delivery at demand locations. Electric power enterprises, as large and safety-critical consumers of engineering materials, require a comprehensive supply chain planning system, spanning demand planning, supplier and contract management, inventory control, to ensure reliable and cost-effective material availability. Moreover, recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), have opened new directions for supply chain management, enabling knowledge-grounded reasoning, tool-augmented integration with enterprise platforms, and multi-agent coordination for closed-loop, adaptive planning. Accordingly, we present GridSCAPE, an LLM-based multi-agent framework, built to orchestrate closed-loop, real-time, intelligent supply chain planning for electric power enterprises. GridSCAPE deploys coordinated LLM agents with tool support, covering the entire supply chain, from demand and sourcing to inventory, warehousing, and logistics. We present implementation details of GridSCAPE and validate its efficacy via controlled experiments, showing reduced end-to-end cycle time, higher plan accuracy, and an increased in-stock rate.

title: G-MAPP: GPU-Accelerated Multi-Agent Planning and Perception for Reactive Motion Generation
authors: T. Bishnoi; R. Laha; T. Löw; J. A. Chandy; L. F. C. Figueredo; S. Haddadin
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Reactive motion generation in unstructured environments remains an open challenge in robotics. Due to the computational complexity of collision-free motion generation, existing methods either generate global trajectories for static scenarios, or employ models that make conservative assumptions about the environment. This paper identifies the primary bottleneck as the runtime performance demand of planning on high-fidelity environments, and the temporal integration between the perception and planning modules. Therefore, we propose a framework that does not compromise on runtime performance and world representations for perception and planning by accelerating world modeling and vector-field based planning using the GPU. This allows us to achieve faster parallel state exploration for quasi-global trajectory planning, and tighter coupling of the perception-action loop in real-time for dynamic cluttered environments with off-the-shelf depth sensors. We quantitatively evaluate the computation-time and success rate differences for the CPU and GPU versions of our planner, and perform qualitative evaluations of our coupled framework using real-world experiments on a 7-DoF Franka Emika robot. Experimental results demonstrate that our GPU-based framework achieves up to a 5x speedup over the CPU in non-trivial scenes.

title: Distributed Safety-Filtered Optimal Formation Control With Executed-Input-Matched Disturbance Estimation
authors: Z. Chen; Z. Wang; B. Cheng; J. Sun; B. He
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper addresses the distributed optimal formation control problem for second-order multi-agent systems subject to external disturbances and collision-avoidance constraints. The desired formation is formulated as a convex optimization problem with time-varying specifications driven by rigid-motion scheduling. We develop a unified control architecture combining a primal-dual nominal law with an optimization-based safety filter. To estimate structured disturbances without acceleration measurements, an executed-input-matched filter constructs an online disturbance proxy whose dynamics are independent of the applied control input. A filter-assisted internal-model observer then provides exponential convergence under the exact exosystem model and an explicit ultimate bound under bounded model mismatch. Pairwise collision constraints are incorporated through a distributed safety-filtering QP. The closed-loop analysis provides an input-to-state practical-tracking bound that explicitly accounts for disturbance-estimation error, safety-filter corrections, and time variation of the selected optimal multiplier; asymptotic tracking is recovered when these inputs vanish. Under the stated observer-envelope initialization, safe-initialization, QP-feasibility, and regularity conditions, the protected-pair safe set is forward invariant along the corresponding closed-loop solutions. Note to Practitioners—Multi-robot teams used in inspection, monitoring, and logistics must maintain safe separation while executing coordinated motions under disturbances such as wind, uneven terrain, or payload variation. In a safety-filtered implementation, the applied input may differ sharply from the nominal command when collision constraints are active. This paper filters the applied input with the same dynamics used to construct the acceleration proxy, so that these control modifications cancel directly from the proxy dynamics at the signal-construction level. Under exact exosystem matching, the resulting internal-model observer converges exponentially to the modeled disturbance; under bounded model mismatch, it admits an explicit ultimate estimation bound. Practical implementation requires access to the input actually applied to the plant and an exosystem model that captures the dominant disturbance modes. Any downstream actuator modification must also be supplied to the matched filter.

title: Robust Robot Localization and Mapping in Challenging Spaces via Thermal-LiDAR Fusion
authors: A. Pandey; M. Mehta; U. Das; S. Pathak
venue: 2026 Third International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving retail landscape, the deployment of autonomous service robots faces significant hurdles in cluttered and dynamic environments. Traditional vision-based navigation systems frequently fail due to variable lighting conditions, narrow supermarket aisles, and the high density of moving obstacles. These limitations significantly compound the inaccuracies of existing single-sensor or shallow localization approaches.We propose and evaluate SmartAssist, a novel AI-Driven Thermal-LiDAR Fusion architecture that exploits LiDAR’s high-precision structural mapping alongside the thermal sensor’s ability to detect human presence in low-light or occluded scenarios. This integrates a React-based front-end—featuring an embedded simulation view from the robot’s perspective, a real-time 2D map of the shopping area, and a chat interface for user commands—with a Node.js backend utilizing WebSockets for real-time bidirectional communication. User commands are translated to navigation coordinates and integrated with the autonomous control logic powered by ROS2, where thermal and LiDAR sensors enable the system to locate users and avoid dynamic obstacles in low-light conditions.Experiments run in a high-fidelity Gazebo simulation of a complex supermarket store aisle feature show that the system can navigate accurately over 95% to the product requested. The hybrid approach maintains obstacle avoidance in dynamic, multi-agent environments and addresses the unsolved key issues of agility and safety robustness in current indoor navigation robotics systems.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first implemented hybrid Thermal-LiDAR fusion system optimized for complete autonomous retail escort with a WebSocket-enabled ROS2 integration, ready to outperform manual or vision-only smart shopping carts. This paper also discusses ethical considerations like user safety, data privacy, and algorithmic reliability in public spaces.

title: Resilient Formation Containment for Multi-UAV Systems With Hybrid Safety Constraints and Prescribed-Time Recovery
authors: H. Shi; T. Li; Z. Ma; P. Zhu; Y. Zhou; L. Shi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Barycentric multiagent formations rely on strict spatial coupling, which inherently contradicts the local spatial decoupling needed for dynamic obstacle avoidance. This creates a fundamental spatiotemporal conflict in complex environments, as essential safety interventions introduce spatial deviations that disrupt the cooperative structure. To address this issue, we propose a hierarchical resilient formation containment framework (Hi-RFC). Instead of treating planning and control as isolated modules, Hi-RFC explicitly links global containment with local safety. A high-level multiagent reinforcement learning planner generates global spatiotemporal trajectories within a reduced-order state space. At the execution layer, a control barrier function (CBF) safety filter is integrated with an event-triggered prescribed-time control (PTC) law. The CBF strictly enforces local safety limits, while the PTC acts as a time-bounded energy compensator. It eliminates the residual repulsive potential energy and spatial errors caused by CBF interventions, mathematically guaranteeing that the distorted formation recovers and resynchronizes within a strictly defined time horizon. Simulations confirm that this architecture successfully resolves the spatiotemporal conflict, avoiding the deadlocks typical of artificial potential fields and the feasibility failures common in pure CBF approaches.

title: Resilient Safety-Aware Control Framework for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems Under Cyberattacks
authors: Y. Wang; M. Rajabinezhad; D. Panagou; S. Zuo
venue: 2026 American Control Conference (ACC)
abstract: This paper formulates and solves the Safety-Aware and Attack-Resilient (SAAR) control problem for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs) under Exponentially Unbounded False Data Injection (EU-FDI) attacks on both the Observer Layer (OL) and Control Input Layer (CIL). A novel attack-resilient OL and CIL are designed. A SAAR controller is then obtained via a CBF-based QP that enforces collision avoidance without slack variables, where strict safety enforcement does not compromise stability. Rigorous Lyapunov analysis proves UUB containment with the safety layer active. 3-D simulations validate concurrent containment and collision avoidance.

title: A Time-Varying Diffeomorphic Approach for Drone Fleet Coordination in Structural Monitoring
authors: L. D’Alfonso; G. Fedele
venue: 2026 30th International Symposium on Distributed Simulation and Real Time Applications (DS-RT)
abstract: The deployment of stable multi-agent systems, particularly fleets of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), for the automated inspection of critical infrastructure presents complex challenges in geometric coordination and scalability. This paper proposes a highly scalable distributed control framework for a drone fleet operating in time-varying monitoring scenarios, such as pipeline patrolling, bridge inspection, and industrial perimeter surveillance. By applying a time-varying diffeomorphism, the geometric complexity arising from trajectory tracking and dynamic formation morphing is entirely decoupled from the underlying dynamic control design. The mathematical formulation enables multiple operational use cases—ranging from dynamic shape morphing to precise rotational surface scanning—simply by tuning the mapping parameters. The approach is numerically validated, ensuring swarm aggregation, intrinsic collision avoidance, and seamless adaptability to arbitrary structural geometries.

title: Autonomous Safety Systems for Smart Cities Using LLM Enabled Intelligent Multi-Agents
authors: S. Anand; A. M. A. Sai
venue: 2026 Fifth International Conference on Power, Control and Computing Technologies (ICPC2T)
abstract: The recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising in building Intelligent systems to address the needs of smart cities. The safety and security of citizens and visitors in cities are very crucial due to the rapid urbanisation and increasing safety threats. In this work, we explore the usability of LLM enabled Multi-Agent systems to enhance the security and safety of smart cities, making them safer and more intelligent environments. We designed an AIoT-enabled agentic framework in which multiple autonomous AI agents collaborate and communicate with each other to monitor, analyze, and respond to security-related events. This paper details the implementation of an agentic AI framework for automated public-safety monitoring using CrewAI and GPT-4o. The system integrates computer vision and multi-agent reasoning to detect and assess real-world incidents such as fires, traffic accidents, and crowd gatherings. The framework consists of a VisionReasoner Agent that performs visual analysis, while specialized agents such as Safety Analyst and a Decision Maker collaboratively interpret results and produce safety alerts to citizens and administrators.

title: Simulation-Grounded Multi-Agent Planning for Interrupt Recovery in Intralogistics
authors: J. Sigel; N. Wilhelm; N. Jazdi; M. Weyrich
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) in intralogistics are typically coordinated by rule-based control, which performs reliably for anticipated situations but falls back to a safe state when an unforeseen interrupt occurs, halting operation until a human intervenes. This work presents a work-in-progress LLM-based agentic network that recovers from such interrupts autonomously. Role-decomposed expert agents examine an interrupt from different perspectives and are coordinated by a moderator that steers an internal discussion toward a high-level recovery plan; a second agentic network then grounds this plan into concrete function calls for the individual AGVs, which are validated in a custom 2D warehouse simulator whose feedback can trigger replanning. In a preliminary evaluation on five interrupt scenarios, assessed by both a human and an LLM judge, the expert network was generally preferred over a single LLM on the planning task, whereas a single LLM appeared sufficient for simpler cases. These results suggest that the architecture's advantage may grow with task complexity, motivating the longer-term goal of extending the approach to real-world scenarios.

title: Bearing-Only Collision-Free Formation Tracking Control for Multiagent Systems: A Safety-Critical Control Approach
authors: Z. Song; H. Huang; G. Feng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article focuses on bearing-only formation control under communication-free conditions. The primary challenges are twofold: 1) tracking formations moving with time-varying velocities without interagent communication; and 2) ensuring collision avoidance based solely on bearing measurements. For the first challenge, we develop a bearing-only formation control law based on an orthogonal projection matrix and prove that the velocity tracking error converges to zero and the position tracking error is uniformly ultimately bounded while converging to a neighborhood of zero. For the second challenge, inspired by the elevation angle theory, we first propose an inter-agent distance estimation method using only bearing measurements. Based on these estimated distances, safety constraints for collision avoidance are constructed via an exponential control barrier function (ECBF). To address the state- and input-related uncertainties that simultaneously arise in this ECBF, we design a novel robust ECBF, in which robustness is endowed by a Gaussian process (GP) with an attention-modulated compound kernel. Collision avoidance is maintained under the considered conditions by solving a second-order cone program (SOCP). Simulation and experimental results validate the proposed control method.

title: How Do Automated Vehicles Influence Following Human Drivers? A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
authors: Q. Pu; K. Xie; H. Guo; Y. Zhu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Robotic and Sensors Environments (ROSE)
abstract: Understanding how automated vehicles (AVs) influence human driving behaviors in mixed traffic environments is critical for enhancing transportation safety. Utilizing high-resolution trajectory data from the U.S. Department of Transportation's Third Generation Simulation (TGSIM) dataset, this study developed a multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MA-DDPG) framework for modeling safety-critical car-following dynamics between AVs and human-driven vehicles (HDVs). The MA-DDPG framework, designed to learn sequential and interactive decision-making over continuous action spaces, effectively captured dynamic AV-HDV interactions in three- vehicle configurations. Compared to single-agent reinforcement learning and supervised learning approaches, it demonstrated superior performance in simulating realistic evasive behaviors, achieving velocity RMSE of 0.847 m/s for AVs and 1.212 m/s for HDVs. Trajectory reconstruction validated the framework's capability to replicate collision avoidance mechanisms. When time-to-collision dropped to 3.2 seconds, the model accurately reproduced the AV's deceleration response and coordinated speed adjustments across all vehicles, with strong alignment between predicted and observed trajectories. Counterfactual analysis revealed that drivers trained following AVs adopted significantly more conservative patterns when encountering human-driven lead vehicles (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: p < 0.1). Mean speeds decreased from 5.7 m/s to 4.8 m/s, acceleration shifted from positive to negative, and braking frequency increased. This study develops multi-agent simulations of AV-HDV interactions that can inform collision avoidance strategies in autonomous and robotic systems.

title: Adaptive Stiffness Formation Control of Differentially Driven Mobile Robots for Trajectory Tracking
authors: A. Joon; W. Kowalczyk
venue: 2026 34th Mediterranean Conference on Control and Automation (MED)
abstract: This paper presents a trajectory-tracking controller for mobile robot formations that integrates an Artificial Potential Function (APF)-based collision avoidance module with a novel adaptive mechanism for formation preservation. Each agent tracks a prescribed trajectory while locally generating repulsive potentials to ensure collision avoidance with neighboring agents. The proposed adaptive mechanism attenuates the impact of transient disturbances on the formation elements, thereby preventing undesired deviations when a new robot attempts to join the formation. As a result, the rigidity of the formation increases, which in turn reduces its susceptibility to deformation. A Lyapunov-based stability analysis is provided. Simulation studies conducted in ROS (Robot Operating System) using the Gazebo environment for planar multi-robot formations validate accurate trajectory tracking, robust collision avoidance, and the ability to accommodate joining agents without disrupting the ongoing formation.

title: The Internet of Humanoids: A Survey of Technologies, Applications, and Challenges
authors: A. W. Yu; A. Nayak
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Humanoid robots are increasingly capable of operating autonomously in human-centric environments, motivating the emergence of the Internet of Humanoids (IoH)—a paradigm that interconnects humanoid robots into collaborative, intelligent networks. Unlike traditional Internet of Things (IoT) systems that link passive or task-specific devices, IoH treats humanoids as embodied, autonomous, and safety-critical agents with tightly coupled perception, decision-making, communication, and actuation. Leveraging advances in large multimodal models (LMMs), cloud–edge computing, and next-generation wireless connectivity, IoH enables real-time coordination, collective learning, and scalable fleet deployment across domains such as healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, and disaster response. This article synthesizes the IoH landscape, proposes a layered architectural reference model to unify heterogeneous subsystems, and critically analyzes challenges in security, privacy, scalability, interoperability, and ethics. We further outline open research directions toward secure, trustworthy, and interoperable humanoid networks at scale.

title: α3-Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents Over 6G Networks
authors: M. A. Ferrag; A. Lakas; M. Debbah
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as high-level controllers for autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) missions. However, current evaluations rarely assess whether such agents remain safe, protocol-compliant, and effective under realistic constraints of next-generation networking. This paper introduces $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench, a benchmark for assessing LLM-driven UAV autonomy as a multi-turn conversational reasoning and control problem operating under dynamic 6G conditions. Each mission is modelled as a language-mediated control loop between an LLM-based UAV agent and a human operator, where decisions must satisfy strict schema validity, speaker alternation, mission policies, and safety bounds while adapting to fluctuating network slices (URLLC/eMBB/mMTC), latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, and edge-load variations. To reflect modern agentic workflows, $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench integrates a dual-action layer that supports both Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) coordination, enabling the evaluation of tool-use consistency and multi-agent interactions within UAV missions. We construct a large-scale corpus of 113k AI conversational episodes grounded in UAVBench scenarios and evaluate 17 state-of-the-art LLMs using a fixed subset of 50 episodes per scenario under deterministic decoding. We propose a composite $\alpha ^{3}$ metric that unifies six pillars—Task Outcome, Safety Policy, Tool Consistency, Interaction Quality, Network Robustness, and Communication Cost—with reliability- and efficiency-normalized scores per second and per thousand tokens. Experimental results show that several frontier models achieve near-perfect mission success and safety compliance (Task Outcome and Safety Policy $\geq 0.95$ ), yet their robustness and efficiency diverge substantially: under degraded 6G conditions, Network Robustness scores drop by up to 30–40%, while efficiency-normalized performance varies by more than a $2\times $ factor across models in both $\alpha ^{3}$ per-second and $\alpha ^{3}$ per-1k-tokens metrics, reflecting significant variance in inference latency and token consumption. $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench provides a reproducible, extensible foundation for benchmarking conversational UAV autonomy and guiding the development of safe, network-aware, and resource-efficient LLM agents in 6G-enabled aerial systems. To support open science and reproducibility, we release the $\alpha ^{3}$ -Bench dataset on GitHub: https://github.com/maferrag/AlphaBench

title: Acceptance–Rejection Sampling-Guided Discrete RRT for Multiagent Path Finding
authors: J. Xin; Y. Duan; H. Zhu; J. Liang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Discrete rapid-exploring random tree (dRRT) methods have been proposed but remain to be improved, showing great potential for efficiently solving multiagent path finding (MAPF) problems. This article proposes a new dRRT algorithm designed to tackle complex and challenging MAPF instances that current discrete RRT approaches struggle to solve efficiently. In particular, we introduce an acceptance–rejection sampling method that efficiently guides the search for feasible paths toward destinations.
