venue: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions (GTSS)
abstract: Overloading of agricultural commercial trucks, especially in the case of sugarcane transportation, is a major problem that has been compromising road safety, the lifespan of infrastructure, fuel consumption, and compliance with regulations. Usually, weighing processes at stationary weighbridges are slow, operators are exposed to errors and the location is vulnerable to illegal operations. In this article, we developed a combined on, board dynamic weighing and secure data communication system for commercial trucks based on IoT sensors, GPS, and blockchain technology. The load cells fixed to the vehicle suspension continuously follow the changes in the load during the trip, signal conditioning and amplification make possible accurate weight estimation in real, time. The results of the measurement accuracy tests in different road conditions vary within 1-2%, thus the intermediate weighbridge stops are rendered obsolete. By using encrypted communication protocols, the system sends the weight and location data to the recipients and stores it on a tamper, proof blockchain ledger, thus ensuring data integrity, auditability, and transparency for the regulatory authorities. Besides, GPS integration allows route optimization and real, time fleet monitoring which, in turn, brings about less idle time, better logistics efficiency, and reduced fuel consumption. The proposed system architecture is capable of automated compliance reporting, reducing the corruption risk and gaining the trust of the involved stakeholders within the agricultural supply chain. Thanks to its modular and scalable design, the system could be adapted to other commercial vehicle fleets and agricultural commodities, thus being a cost, effective and efficient solution.

title: Multi-Agent Perception-Action Causal Transformer for Offline Cooperative Pursuit-Evasion of USV Swarms
authors: Z. Li; B. Sun; Z. Su; S. Jiang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) swarms have shown significant potential for complex cooperative maritime missions. However, deploying online Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) directly in real-world environments remains highly challenging due to marine disturbances, the high cost of physical experiments, and inherent safety risks such as inter-vessel collisions. To address these challenges, this paper develops a task-tailored multi-agent offline sequence-modeling framework, termed the Multi-Agent Perception–Action Causal Transformer (MAPACT), by adapting Decision-Transformer-based offline decision making to distributed USV pursuit–evasion. Unlike conventional Temporal Difference (TD)-based methods, the multi-USV cooperative control problem is reformulated as a conditional sequence modeling task. MAPACT adopts a parameter-shared Transformer architecture with causal masked attention to model historical multi-agent trajectories. Cooperative actions are generated autoregressively by conditioning on agents' historical states, previous actions, and Returns-to-Go (RTG), enabling effective long-horizon decision-making without online interaction. Extensive experiments in a high-fidelity multi-USV maritime pursuit–evasion simulation environment demonstrate that MAPACT can extract efficient cooperative pursuit and surrounding strategies from offline datasets containing suboptimal demonstrations. In addition, real-world lake experiments using physical USVs validate the practical feasibility of the proposed framework within a hierarchical control architecture, and the results are consistent with those observed in simulation. Quantitative evaluations show that MAPACT consistently outperforms Behavioral Cloning (BC) and representative offline reinforcement learning baselines across varying data-quality scenarios, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness for real-world multi-USV cooperative control tasks.

title: Vision-Constrained Formation Control With Integrated Rigid-Geometric Structures for Obstacle Avoidance
authors: Z. Wang; Z. Liang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: This article presents a formation control strategy for nonholonomic wheeled mobile robots that integrates both rigid and flexible formations to achieve efficient exploration and robust obstacle avoidance. A two-layer constraint framework is introduced to ensure safe and coordinated formation control. Specifically, the outer layer maintains the perception-based topology by enforcing field-of-view constraints, while the inner layer constructs control barrier functions based on directional obstacle models defined in the robot's local frame, which prevent interrobot collisions and enable safe navigation in unknown environments. Furthermore, the proposed controller guarantees predefined-time convergence and maintains formation objectives even in the presence of unknown obstacles, by using a Lipschitz continuous projection operator to enable smooth transitions between rigid and flexible formations without violating FOV constraints. Finally, the presented framework is validated through a real-world experiment, which confirms its ability to achieve coordinated formation tracking and obstacle avoidance in a complex environment.

title: Disguise While Defense: Avoid Refusal Responses in LLM’s Defense via a Multi-Agent Attacker–Disguiser Game
authors: Q. Xu; Z. Tian; H. Wu; Z. Huang; D. Liang; Y. Song; Z. Pan; F. Liu; D. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
abstract: With the enhanced performance of large language models (LLMs) on natural language processing tasks, potential moral and ethical issues of LLMs arise in the Web service. Malicious attackers exist who induce LLMs to jailbreak and generate information containing illegal, privacy-invasive information through techniques such as prompt engineering. As a result, LLMs counter malicious attackers’ attacks using techniques such as safety alignment. However, the strong defense mechanism of the LLMs through rejection replies, which are typically unrelated to the attacker’s query, is easily identified by attackers and leaks information that strengthens their capabilities. We propose an LLM-driven defense task that generates safe and disguised responses which remain relevant to the attack request while concealing defensive intent and withholding any useful information from the attacker. To achieve this task, we construct an LLM-based multi-agent attacker-disguiser game that trains two LLM-based players to select in-context learning (ICL) examples and strategies, guiding them to better generation and approach to Nash equilibrium. To enhance the LLMs’ generation via ICL, we apply the Minimax Q-learning to optimize the players for choosing ICL examples. To further refine generation, we use policy gradient (PG) to train the strategy selectors to select prompt strategies for LLMs. To improve the ICL examples and prompts for LLMs’ generation, we iteratively train the players with ICL sample selection training and prompt strategy training. The goal of this game is to arrive at the Nash equilibrium. Through training, we obtain an LLM-based defender which can receive jailbreak prompts from malicious users and output safe and disguised responses. The experiments reveal that our method strengthens the LLM’s ability to disguise the defense intent compared to other methods. Our method also minimizes the attacker-perceived drop in attack success rate, while delivering the largest actual reduction. This effectively misleads the attacker’s evaluation and enhances practical defense utility.

title: Large-Scale Battery-Conscious Collision-Free Path-Finding for Sustainable and Autonomous Multi-AGV Mobility Control
authors: Y. Cho; S. Ahn; S. Park; J. Kim
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a novel battery-conscious collision-free sustainable path-finding (BCSP) algorithm for large-scale multi-agent systems (MAS). The framework rigorously integrates battery management with reservation-based collision avoidance with local observation. Agent states, charging station availability, and spatiotemporal reservations are explicitly formulated to ensure safe navigation. An octile distance-based heuristic search strategy minimizes redundant node expansions and reduces computational overhead, utilizing adaptive waiting and local reservation updates. Furthermore, performance evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in terms of battery efficiency and collision avoidance, outperforming existing benchmark algorithms. Moreover, extensive experiments in highly congested and dynamic environments even reveal marked improvements compared to benchmarks. The performance and robustness of the algorithm underscore its potential for real-world applications in autonomous navigation, smart factories, and urban mobility.

title: Agents Trainer: Automatically Training Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Models for Drone Swarm Using Language Model-Based Agents
authors: J. Lou; R. Shi; H. Wang; M. -M. Yu; Y. Wang; Q. Wang; W. Wu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel at high-level reasoning and task decomposition but remain insufficiently reliable for fine-grained, low-level control, where reinforcement learning (RL) is more suitable. However, effective RL still relies heavily on expert-intensive environment configuration, reward design, and hyperparameter tuning–challenges that are amplified in multi-agent scenarios. To this end, we propose Agents Trainer, an LLM-assisted framework that automates the end-to-end multi-agent RL (MARL) pipeline with minimal expert intervention. The system decomposes MARL responsibilities across specialized agents and instantiates a generate-reflect-evolve iteration loop to produce executable, interpretable, and progressively densified reward signals aligned with task goals and safety constraints, while preserving diversity to avoid mode collapse. Experiments across two simulators of differing fidelity and a diverse set of tasks show that Agents Trainer outperforms classical MARL methods and automated reward-design baselines in success rate, episode return, robustness, and sample efficiency, and shifts the safety–efficiency Pareto frontier toward fewer collisions and lower energy consumption. Ablation studies demonstrate that removing any component degrades reliability or stability. A multi-granularity Sim2Real pipeline further validates that our method achieves lower trajectory error and jerk on physical quadrotors, enabling smoother and more precise transfer. These gains are reproducible across different underlying LLM backends, indicating that the performance improvements stem primarily from the framework design rather than any specific model choice. Note to Practitioners—This paper presents a practical approach to automating MARL in real-world robotics and automation systems by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to reduce expert effort in reward design and training protocols—tasks that are traditionally time-consuming and expertise-dependent. The implementation requires only minimal initial setup (e.g., specifying a high-level objective such as “achieve collision-free drone formation”) and is compatible with existing RL environments and simulators (e.g., OpenAI Gym, AirSim) through API-level integration. Currently, a single workstation can comfortably handle swarms of roughly 20–30 entities; larger teams typically require distributed or cloud execution. Caching rollouts and intermediate metrics can substantially reduce the overhead on the Eval and Evolution agents. The framework enables engineers to rapidly prototype MARL solutions for dynamic environments while maintaining alignment with operational goals via intuitive feedback. We recommend keeping reward functions modular and separating task rewards from safety penalties in both logging systems and dashboards. Future extensions will support ROS-based deployment to physical robots.

title: Architectures, Learning Loops, and Emergence in Agentic Services Computing
authors: S. Shafi; M. Bidollahkhani; J. M. Kunkel
venue: 2026 IEEE 50th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are evolving from isolated task executors into interconnected societies of autonomous services capable of coordination, adaptation, and collective intelligence. This paper surveys and synthesizes recent advances in agentic services computing, LLM-based multiagent systems, and language-augmented reinforcement learning to analyze how feedback-driven learning loops enable emergent behaviors at system scale. We organize the design space along four dimensions: perception and context modeling, autonomous decision-making, multi-agent collaboration, and evaluation with alignment and trustworthiness. Building on this analysis, we propose a reference architecture for feedback-driven LLM-agent societies that integrates reinforcement learning, verbal feedback, episodic memory, coordination, and governance layers. We further define sociocognitive execution metrics for coordination density, goal agreement, role specialization, recovery, strategy diversity, throughput, behavioral variance, and failure tolerance, and illustrate their use through case studies and a localized ASC Micro-Testbed prototype. The prototype results show how critic feedback, episodic memory, and macro-level safety filtering support bounded recovery and constraint preservation. Finally, we identify open challenges, including cumulative learning without knowledge entropy, scalable coordination, trustworthy evolution, and standardized evaluation for reliable emergent agentic systems.

title: Multi-Agent System for Building a Shared Obstacle Map for Autonomous Transport on Enterprise Territories
authors: V. Mikhailov; R. Zhitkov; K. Svyatov
venue: 2026 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article considers a subsystem for collaborative obstacle mapping for a group of unmanned motor vehicles operating on restricted enterprise territories. Such territories are characterized by repeated routes, technological passages, temporary obstacles, warehouse infrastructure and areas with limited visibility. The proposed approach combines local dynamic maps formed by each agent from LiDAR data and external odometry with a shared persistent obstacle map in the world coordinate system. Local maps are used for operational planning, while the shared map preserves information obtained by different agents and makes it available for subsequent movement along enterprise routes. The approach takes into account safety requirements for driverless industrial trucks and the general classification of driving automation. Practical verification was performed in ROS 2 and Webots for a convoy movement scenario with two vehicles.

title: Robust Geospatial Coordination of Multi-Agent Communications Networks Under Attrition
authors: J. S. Kent; E. Stefani; B. Plancher
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Coordinating emergency responses in extreme environments, such as wildfires, requires resilient and high-bandwidth communication backbones. While autonomous aerial swarms can establish ad-hoc networks to provide this connectivity, the high risk of individual node attrition in these settings often leads to network fragmentation and mission-critical downtime. To overcome this challenge, we introduce and formalize the problem of Robust Task Networking Under Attrition (RTNUA), which extends connectivity maintenance in multi-robot systems to explicitly address proactive redundancy and attrition recovery. We then introduce Physics-Informed Robust Employment of Multi-Agent Networks ($\Phi$IREMAN), a topological algorithm leveraging physics-inspired potential fields to solve this problem. In our evaluations, $\Phi$IREMAN consistently outperforms baselines, and is able to maintain greater than 99.9% task uptime despite substantial attrition in simulations with up to 100 tasks and 500 drones, demonstrating both effectiveness and scalability.

title: Distributed Formation Obstacle Avoidance for Multiagent Systems Based on Point-Cloud Fusion and p-Norm Obstacle Functions
authors: W. Wang; Y. Xie; S. Fan; C. Deng; B. Wang; V. Vyatkin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: This article addresses the problem of distributed formation and collision avoidance for a class of nonlinear multiagent systems (MASs) in cluttered environments. Unlike traditional collision avoidance methods that constrain the feasible workspace by relying on simplified geometric obstacle models, this article achieves a more precise representation of irregular obstacles to improve space utilization. To achieve these improvements, a hierarchical perception-control method consisting of a point-cloud fusion algorithm in the perception layer, distributed command governors in the navigation layer, and adaptive controllers in the control layer is proposed. Specifically, the point-cloud fusion algorithm is designed to extract closed obstacle boundaries by integrating data from LiDAR and RGB-D cameras to ensure that all obstacles are detected and their boundaries are identified with high precision. Based on the extracted boundary information, distributed command governors utilizing a $p$ -norm-based metric to construct a smooth and differentiable obstacle model are designed to generate a collision-free reference signal for each agent to follow. Furthermore, adaptive controllers are proposed by using the backstepping method. It is shown that collision avoidance and the preservation of the prescribed formation shape can be achieved by means of the developed method. Numerical simulations and experimental results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical control method.

title: Energy-Efficient Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative UAV Swarms
authors: P. S. V. Rao; E. V. Reddy; A. K. Srivastava
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Interdisciplinary Approaches in Technology and Management for Social Innovation (IATMSI)
abstract: Swarm robotic systems operating in large-scale agricultural monitoring and dynamic damage reduction must function under strict energy constraints and high safety requirements. Most existing multi agent reinforcement learning (MARL) assumes static environments and limits real-world applicability. This study presents an energy-aware, guidanceregularized deep reinforcement learning framework for multiagent damage treatment in dynamically evolving environments. A Guided Deep Q-Network (Guided DQN) is proposed which integrates domain-specific guidance into value-based action selection to stabilize the learning and improve task-focused coordination. The environment models collision-aware swarm motion, finite energy for each agent, and dynamic infection spreading. The proposed approach is evaluated against greedy, random, tabular Q-learning and DQN baselines under multiseed experimentation. It is analyzed in terms of energy consumption, infection suppression success and convergence behavior.

title: Toward 6G ISAC-Enabled Low-Altitude Economy Networking: A Multi-Agent DRL Perspective
authors: V. K. Quy; V. H. Nam; A. Chehri; T. N. Nguyen; D. -T. Tran; L. B. Le
venue: IEEE Network
abstract: Thanks to Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles’ (UAVs) breakthrough capabilities, the low-altitude economy concept is rapidly emerging as a new frontier for intelligent transportation, logistics, public safety, and urban aerial services. To support these applications, future networks must provide not only reliable wireless connectivity but also real-time sensing and adaptive intelligence. In this context, 6G integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) offers a promising foundation for low-altitude economy networking by enabling communication and environmental awareness within a unified framework. However, the high mobility of aerial nodes, dynamic network topology, and tightly coupled sensing-communication tasks make efficient coordination highly challenging. This article presents a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) perspective for 6G ISAC-enabled low-altitude economy networking. We discuss key challenges, outline a cooperative intelligent framework, and highlight representative application scenarios and open research issues. The goal is to show how multi-agent DRL can help enable adaptive, efficient, and safe networking for future low-altitude ecosystems.

title: Hierarchical Learning-Based Control for Multiagent Shepherding of Stochastic Autonomous Agents
authors: I. Napolitano; S. Covone; A. Lama; F. De Lellis; M. di Bernardo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
abstract: Multiagent shepherding represents a challenging distributed control problem where herder agents must coordinate to guide autonomously moving targets to desired spatial configurations. Most existing control strategies assume cohesive target behavior, which frequently fails in practical applications where targets exhibit stochastic autonomous behavior. This article presents a hierarchical learning-based control architecture that decomposes the shepherding problem into a high-level decision-making module and a low-level motion control component. The proposed distributed control system synthesizes effective control policies directly from closed-loop experience without requiring explicit interagent communication or prior knowledge of target dynamics. The decentralized architecture achieves cooperative control behaviors through emergent coordination without centralized supervision. Experimental validation demonstrates superior closed-loop performance compared to state-of-the-art heuristic control methods. Additionally, the control architecture scales beyond its design conditions, adapts to time-varying goal regions, and demonstrates real-time feasibility.

title: Short-Term Operational Coordination of China’s Water-Energy-Food Nexus via Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
authors: M. Lyu; A. H. P. Tan; S. -H. Chen; W. El-Bouri
venue: IEEE Systems Journal
abstract: The water-energy-food (WEF) nexus is an indivisible system in which isolated analyses fail to capture its complex interdependencies. While existing research acknowledges WEF synergies, few studies quantitatively evaluate short-term operational coordination under extreme resource stress. This study proposes a multiagent reinforcement learning framework comprising water, energy, food, and household agents to optimize dynamic resource allocation and system-wide stress responses as a unified whole. Crucially, the reward function internalizes the cross-regional transportation costs and policy safety baselines of WEF resources in China. Comparative experiments with independent proximal policy optimization reveal that multi-agent proximal policy optimization achieves 74.4% higher cumulative rewards, proving that joint optimization of WEF subsystems captures critical cross-sector dependencies. Sensitivity analysis shows that, relative to the baseline converged reward, mild and severe droughts reduce the reward by 17.6% and 29.4%, respectively, while the energy agent modestly increases the reward. Conversely, 20% and 80% energy shortages cut system rewards by 20% and 54.1%, triggering cascading losses across the water and food agents. Finally, action heatmap interprets the underlying microbehavioral mechanisms, revealing that agents autonomously execute strategic sacrifices to safeguard systemic lifelines. This highlights a critical tradeoff between overall efficiency and sector-level equity, suggesting that cross-sectoral compensation mechanisms may be needed to address unequal sectoral burdens.

title: Multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Practical Prescribed-Time Formation Tracking Control With Collision-Free Constraints
authors: X. -H. Liu; G. -H. Yang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: This paper studies the practical prescribed-time collision-free formation tracking (PPT-CFT) control problem for multi-AUV (autonomous underwater vehicle) systems. A dual-layer collision avoidance framework is proposed. Specifically, a distributed state observer with a collision avoidance mechanism is designed first to generate collision-free command signals. Then, based on a zeroing control barrier function (ZCBF), a controller is designed to achieve PPT-CFT control. Compared with the existing works, the proposed method offers a simpler structure but provides stronger safety guarantees. Finally, simulation results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the developed approach. This study lays the foundation for future extensions to systems with model uncertainties.

title: Learning Visuomotor Policy for Multi-Robot Laser Tag Game
authors: K. Li; S. Zhao
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: In this paper, we study multi-robot laser tag, a simplified yet practical shooting-game-style task. Classic modular approaches on these tasks face challenges such as limited observability and reliance on depth mapping and inter-robot communication. To overcome these issues, we present an end-to-end visuomotor policy that maps images directly to robot actions. We train a high-performing teacher policy with multi-agent reinforcement learning and distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy. Technical designs, including a permutation-invariant feature extractor and depth–heatmap input, improve performance over standard architectures. Our policy outperforms classic methods by 16.7% in hitting accuracy and 6% in collision avoidance, and is successfully deployed on real robots. Code will be released publicly1.

title: Greedy Priority Inheritance With Backtracking for Multi-Agent Pathfinding Problem
authors: M. Tang; Y. Li; L. Gan; C. Zhang; Y. Sun; J. Wu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Some real-world transportation systems require moving robots from their start points to goal points without collision, which can be formalized as the multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) problem. The Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT) algorithm is an efficient approach for MAPF with low-degree polynomial time complexity and proven completeness. PIBT employs a dynamic prioritization scheme to determine the order of sequential agent planning. However, this scheme may lead to low solution quality, which is measured by the sum of time steps each agent takes to reach its goal for the first time. In this work, we propose two greedy variants of the PIBT algorithm that improve solution quality while preserving completeness: Backflow-based Greedy PIBT (GPIBT-B) and Reduction-based Greedy PIBT (GPIBT-R). GPIBT-B introduces a backflow mechanism that allows a determined agent to adjust its plan during the planning of another agent, achieving higher solution quality while maintaining the same low time complexity as PIBT. GPIBT-R formulates the planning problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), enabling the use of efficient MILP solvers to find high-quality solutions. Experimental results show that GPIBT-B substantially improves solution quality with minimal additional computation time, while GPIBT-R achieves even better solution quality at the cost of increased computational time. Note to Practitioners—This paper addresses the challenge of inefficient multi-robot coordination in logistics and automation systems. While solvers like PIBT can quickly generate feasible paths, their solutions often suffer from low quality, leading to diminished system throughput and longer task completion times. To address this, we propose two greedy variants that significantly enhance solution quality. GPIBT-B uses a lightweight backflow mechanism, allowing robots to dynamically adjust their moves to avoid blocking each other. This achieves markedly faster goal attainment with minimal computational overhead. GPIBT-R employs an MILP model for higher-quality, globally optimized single-step plans, while more planning time is required. Experiments show GPIBT-B delivers superior solutions with negligible speed loss, making it ideal for real-time systems. GPIBT-R offers the highest quality for less time-sensitive applications. It should be noted that the solution quality of GPIBT-B, while significantly improved, may still be further optimized, and the computational efficiency of GPIBT-R remains an area for future enhancement. These algorithms can be directly applied to improve efficiency in warehouse logistics, automated sorting systems, and multi-robot assembly lines. Both algorithms assume a centralized coordination scheme where a server collects global information and distributes commands to robots. GPIBT-B is well-suited for real-time deployment due to its low overhead, while GPIBT-R is recommended for applications where path quality is prioritized over computation time.

title: SafeFlow: Attribution-Driven Adaptive Security Defense for Large Language Model Agents
authors: S. Gao; Z. Zhao; S. Zhang; F. Wang; Y. Zhang; X. Mi
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA)
abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in healthcare, finance, education, and other high-risk domains, their multi-turn interactions become more complex. When facing emerging threats such as context poisoning, memory injection, and tool manipulation, conventional binary filtering models struggle to provide effective protection. Although existing security frameworks establish layered defense architectures, they still rely on static thresholds and opaque binary decisions, making it difficult to trace attack sources or dynamically adjust defensive responses. This paper presents SafeFlow, a full-chain protection architecture that integrates three-dimensional security signals, namely risk category, confidence score, and attribution source, to enable end-to-end risk tracing and adaptive defense along the agent execution path. SafeFlow dynamically adjusts interception strength through a confidence-aware response mechanism and constructs collaborative cross-layer feedback based on aggregated attribution sources. While preserving task completion, SafeFlow effectively suppresses unsafe and adversarial behaviors. Experiments on Agent-SafetyBench show that SafeFlow reduces the unsafe behavior rate to 18.56%, lowers the attack success rate to 16.20%, and achieves an attribution accuracy of 86.4% under the ReAct execution paradigm. The results indicate that coordinated three-dimensional security signals improve safety judgment accuracy, and that attribution-driven defense can precisely identify memory pollution attacks in multi-agent scenarios, providing a new paradigm for interpretable and trustworthy LLM agent security.

title: Probabilistic Modeling and Control for Multi-UAV Search Over Uneven Terrain
authors: L. Lanča; K. Jakac; S. Ivić
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
abstract: This article addresses survey missions involving multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) over complex, varying terrain. The methodology integrates a probabilistic model of target’s position uncertainty with UAV flight dynamics, camera properties, and a machine learning-based detection system. It estimates undetected target probability and overall search performance, feeding into a feedback loop that combines 2-D ergodic search with model predictive control (MPC) of UAV altitude and velocity. Trial trajectory optimization accounts for sensing characteristics and operational constraints, producing terrain-aware, collision-free trajectories that balance area coverage with target detection. Simulations demonstrate the integration of MPC and ergodic search, enabling dynamic altitude adjustments to enhance the search performance. The control algorithm operates in real time and performs reliably under uncertainty. Field experiments provided training data, validated the method, and confirmed compliance with motion constraints. Detection rates closely match model predictions, demonstrating stable performance even under significant deviations from ideal conditions. The framework, thus, offers a reliable solution for autonomous multi-UAV search operations in real-world environments.

title: Lazy-DaSH: A Lazy Approach for Hypergraph-Based Multirobot Task and Motion Planning
authors: S. Lee; J. D. Motes; I. Ngui; M. M. Aguirre; N. M. Amato
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
abstract: In this article, we introduce lazy-decomposable state-space hypergraph (Lazy-DaSH), an improvement over the recent state-of-the-art multirobot task and motion planning method decomposable state-space hypergraph (DaSH), which scales to more than twice as many robots and objects while achieving more than an order of magnitude faster planning when applied to a multimanipulator object rearrangement problem. We achieve this improvement through a hierarchical approach, where a high-level task planning layer identifies planning spaces required for task completion, and motion feasibility is validated lazily only within these spaces. In contrast, DaSH precomputes the motion feasibility of all possible actions, resulting in higher costs for constructing state-space representations. Lazy-DaSH ensures efficient query performance by utilizing a hierarchical constraint feedback mechanism, effectively conveying motion feasibility to the query process while incrementally expanding the task and motion space representations when failures are detected, so the search space grows only as needed. By maintaining smaller state-space representations, our method significantly reduces both representation construction time and query time. We evaluate Lazy-DaSH in five scenarios, demonstrating its scalability with increasing numbers of robots and objects, as well as its adaptability in resolving conflicts through the constraint feedback mechanism.

title: Meanshift Shape Formation Control Using Discrete Mass Distribution
authors: Y. Cai; Y. Gao; P. Li; W. Wang; G. Sun; J. Lü
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: The density-distribution method has recently become a promising paradigm owing to its adaptability to variations in swarm size. However, existing studies face practical challenges in achieving complex shape representation and decentralized implementation. This motivates us to develop a fully decentralized, distribution-based control strategy with the dual capability of forming complex shapes and adapting to swarm-size variations. Specifically, we first propose a discrete mass-distribution function defined over a set of sample points to model swarm formation. In contrast to the continuous density-distribution method, our model eliminates the requirement for defining continuous density functions—a task that is difficult for complex shapes. Second, we design a decentralized meanshift control law to coordinate the swarm’s global distribution to fit the sample-point distribution by feeding back mass estimates. The mass estimates for all sample points are achieved by the robots in a decentralized manner via the designed mass estimator. It is shown that the mass estimates of the sample points can asymptotically converge to the true global values. To validate the proposed strategy, we conduct comprehensive simulations and real-world experiments to evaluate the efficiency of complex shape formation and adaptability to swarm-size variations.

title: Safe Optimal Formation of Continuous-Time Multiagent Systems via Maximum Entropy Adaptive Dynamic Programming
authors: L. Zhang; H. Zhang; T. Wang; J. Ma
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: This article addresses the problem of formation control for multiagent systems operating in partially unknown dynamic environments. A safe optimal control method is proposed by employing maximum entropy adaptive dynamic programming (MEADP) in continuous-time systems, alongside high-order control barrier functions (HoCBFs). First, an MEADP algorithm for continuous-time systems is developed to encourage exploration and prevent convergence to suboptimal solutions under partially unknown system dynamics, with a comprehensive convergence proof of the algorithm provided. Then, safety constraints are formulated using HoCBFs, which are capable of handling safety constraints with higher relative degrees. These constraints are incorporated via quadratic programming to modify the maximum entropy optimal control policy, ensuring that the system states remain within a predefined safe set and effectively avoid collisions with obstacles. Moreover, the MEADP method utilizes a critic neural network to approximate the entropy-regularized Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation, leading to a maximum entropy optimal control policy. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, making it suitable for safe formation control tasks in complex dynamic environments.

title: Data-Driven Safety-Critical Flocking Control for Multi-Agent Systems With Unknown Dynamics Under Uncertain Environments
authors: S. Yan; L. Shi; X. Bu; P. Zhu; Y. Zhou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The rapid development of consumer electronics, including consumer drones, smart home robots, and Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks, has spurred the deployment of multi-agent systems (MASs) in increasingly complex and uncertain real-world environments. A critical challenge in these applications is to ensure safe and coordinated operation when the system dynamics are unavailable and the environmental conditions are unknown a priori. This paper proposes a data-driven learning control barrier function (DDLCBF) framework to address the safety-critical flocking control problem for MASs with unknown nonlinear dynamics operating in uncertain environments. First, a distributed flocking controller is constructed using pseudo partial derivatives (PPD) that relies exclusively on input-output (I/O) data, eliminating the requirement of an explicit system model. The controller is further extended to cooperative-competitive networks on signed directed graphs, where bipartite flocking convergence is guaranteed under a structural balance condition via gauge transformation. Second, a Gaussian process (GP) regression-based learning scheme is developed to approximate stochastic control barrier functions (CBFs) from real-time sensor measurements, thereby enabling probabilistic safety guarantees without prior environmental knowledge. Third, the DDLCBF scheme is formulated by integrating the PPD-based data model into the CBF constraints, yielding a quadratic programming (QP) controller that simultaneously ensures safety and low environmental uncertainty. Rigorous theoretical analyses are provided, including convergence guarantees for the PPD estimator and probabilistic safety bounds. The effectiveness and practicality of the proposed approach are validated through numerical simulations and physical experiments on an indoor multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform equipped with a motion capture system.

title: Multi-Robot Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Persistent Monitoring
authors: F. Pagano; S. Marcellini; M. Selvaggio; V. Lippiello; F. Ruggiero
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
abstract: We present an approach to address a multirobot persistent monitoring problem, where a team of agents must repeatedly survey specific points of interest (POIs) within a 2-D area. Our approach models the interest value of each POI with a heat-like dynamics. Each agent then solves online a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem to determine feasible trajectories that minimize the cumulative heat across all POIs. The trajectories are parameterized with Bézier curves, whose control points are used as optimization variables; this parametrization enables agents to efficiently communicate their optimized motions. An additional quadratic optimization layer adds safety guarantees while a central unit updates the global POIs’ map. The method has been validated in simulation and real experiments, demonstrating that the algorithm can run online and on computationally limited hardware platforms. In addition, an extensive simulation campaign compares our NMPC against a state-of-the-art baseline across 90 randomly generated scenarios with different numbers of POIs. Our NMPC outperforms the baseline along the considered metrics, attaining lower robot velocities.

title: Modeling and Analysis of Bursty Delay Attacks in Cooperative Multi-Robot Systems
authors: R. Sagwal; V. Gupta
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
abstract: Autonomous Multi-Robot Systems (MRS) are widely deployed in time-critical applications such as defense, disaster response, precision agriculture, and search-and-rescue. However, their distributed operation exposes them to internal cyberphysical threats. This paper investigates the Bursty Delay Attack (BDA), a stealthy insider attack in which a compromised robot withholds messages and releases them in bursts, disrupting synchronization without altering data or violating communication protocols. We formally model BDA within a cooperative exploration framework and analyze its impact on coverage efficiency, synchronization stability, and exploration time across different team sizes. Results show that even a single adversarial robot can induce disproportionate coordination degradation, leading to redundant coverage, collisions, incomplete exploration, and noticeable increases in mission completion time. We further evaluate a lightweight self-adaptive backtracking mechanism that mitigates delay-induced stagnation, though without guaranteeing completeness. These findings highlight critical timing vulnerabilities in cooperative MRS and motivate the need for delay-aware and synchronization-resilient coordination mechanisms.

title: Agentic AI Frameworks: Orchestration Architectures and Autonomous LLM-Based Reasoning Systems
authors: Y. L; S. Rishwanth; S. R. M
venue: 2026 3rd International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: Agentic AI systems shift from static generative models to autonomous agents capable of reasoning and action. However, research remains fragmented across definitions, architectures, and evaluation practices, limiting informed adoption. Methods: 20 publications were reviewed (2021-2025) analyzing reasoning paradigms (CoT, ReAct, ToT), orchestration models (single-agent to multi-agent), memory designs, and evaluation methodologies using a five-dimensional analytical framework. Results: ReAct-based loops dominate (68 % adoption). Only 32% report safety mechanisms; evaluation is largely qualitative. Multi-agent architectures improve robustness but introduce 2-5x latency; hierarchical hallucination mitigation reduces errors by $\mathbf{4 0 - 5 0 \%}$. Conclusion: The proposed research provide practitioners a structured framework for selecting reasoning, orchestration, and guardrail strategies. Key gaps remain in standardized benchmarks, safety governance, and interoperability, outlining opportunities for production-grade agentic systems.tonomous Reasoning, Multi-Agent Systems, Tool-Augmented Intelligence

title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Multi-Agent Motion Planning and Encirclement of Moving Targets in 3D Space
authors: R. Long; Y. Wang; H. Fan; Y. Shen; Z. Ren; S. Srigrarom
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Control and Robotics (EECR)
abstract: This paper considers a Moving-Target Multi-Agent Motion Planning (MT-MAMP) problem that seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents to collectively encircle a few moving targets along straight lines, and each target has a requirement on the minimum number of agents for encirclement. MT-MAMP is challenging as it involves not only inter-agent collision avoidance, a fundamental challenge in MAMP, but also encirclement of moving targets that involves task allocation in a dynamic environment. While various approaches have been developed for MAMP and its variants, we are not aware of any prior research on MAMP that considers encirclement of moving targets. To address MT-MAMP, we formulate the problem as a mixed-integer program (MIP) by leveraging several existing techniques in the field of MIP for motion planning, and introduce a notion of shrinking encirclement, which allows the agents to tighten their encirclement as time evolves. We verify our MIP with up to 15 agents and 4 targets in various cases, which verifies the correctness and effectiveness of our approach for MT-MAMP.

title: A Multi-Agent LLM-Based System for Goal-Oriented Investment Guidance
authors: A. T; H. A. V; S. T
venue: 2026 IEEE 18th International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks (CICN)
abstract: Retail investors face difficulties in financial planning because they need to handle complicated market data and they do not receive personalized solutions through inaccessible advisory systems. The traditional investment recommendation platforms function as black boxes because they share only minimal details about their decision-making processes. The AI-based FinFlow project serves as a goal-oriented investment planning assistant which delivers educational investment assistance through natural language interfaces to users. Users provide their financial objectives and risk tolerance levels and investment periods through free-form text which FinFlow processes using its multi-agent system. The system identifies the goals of the user and uses appropriate financial knowledge to provide personalized investment strategies that are accompanied by comprehensive explanations. The system uses interpretability features to accomplish its goals which help retail investors to build trust and gain financial knowledge and make better choices. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of a large language model (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instant via Groq API) for transparent financial guidance while adhering to ethical and risk-aware constraints.

title: Risk-Aware Co-Optimization for Multi-Robot Control Under Execution Uncertainty
authors: Z. Gao; A. Marino; A. Prorok
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: While multi-robot motion control often treats the environment as a static constraint and assumes near-perfect execution, real-world uncertainty poses significant challenges. In poorly structured or densely populated spaces, these unpredictable variables frequently lead to collision risks and degraded performance. We address this issue by proposing a risk-aware framework that co-optimizes robot actions and environment configurations to mitigate execution uncertainty. To handle the complex relationships among the environment, robots, and uncertainty impact, we develop a bi-level approach using neural surrogate optimization, effectively bridging nonlinear programming with model-free learning for joint optimization. Supported by theoretical robustness guarantees, numerical simulations, and physical experiments, our co-optimization strategy creates “multi-robot-friendly” environments that mitigate the impact of execution uncertainty and facilitate superior multi-robot coordination.

title: Graph Connectivity Maintenance for Multi-Robots Systems under Visual Occlusion Constraints via CBFs
authors: V. Sá; A. Vangasse; D. G. Macharet; L. Pimenta; V. Gonçalves; G. Freitas
venue: 2026 Brazilian Conference on Robotics (CROS)
abstract: Maintaining network connectivity is a fundamental challenge in the deployment of Multi-Robot Systems, particularly during exploration or navigation tasks. This paper presents a centralized control framework for coordinating differential-drive robots within a mesh topology, ensuring connectivity maintenance regardless of individual goal assignments by separating the robots into task and connectivity roles. We address navigation in known environments by modeling connectivity through both inter-agent distance and Line-of-Sight (LoS) constraints. The proposed approach leverages Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) to formally guarantee that the algebraic connectivity (Fiedler value, λ2) of the graph Laplacian remains positive throughout the operation. This formulation allows the system to satisfy connectivity constraints while minimally deviating from the task robots’ nominal path-planning objectives. Furthermore, we integrate this framework into the standard ROS 2 Navigation Stack (Nav2), demonstrating the viability of the proposed method in realistic simulation scenarios. Results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness in guaranteeing connectivity, despite susceptibility to local minima in specific scenarios.

title: Research on Cooperative Path Planning for Multi-Agent Systems Based on an Improved Wild Horse Optimization Algorithm
authors: H. Que; X. Liu; Y. Zhang; J. Zhang; D. Ma; W. Wu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Artificial Intelligence (PRMVAI)
abstract: This study focuses on solving the issues of search-accuracy bottleneck and premature local convergence that frequently occur in cooperative path planning for multi-agent systems (MAS). By analyzing the diversity loss of the standard WHO algorithm during its final stages, we develop an Improved Wild Horse Optimization algorithm (IWHO). Specifically, we design a nonlinear adaptive inertia-weight mechanism to balance global exploration and local exploitation more effectively. Furthermore, a Cauchy mutation operator is applied to perturb subgroup leaders, strengthening the search engine's ability to escape local extrema. Simulation results in complex 3D multi-obstacle scenarios verify that IWHO delivers better path-cost optimization, trajectory smoothness, and stability than PSO and standard WHO.

title: Denoising Multirobot Trajectories
authors: Y. Zhang; K. Okumura; A. Shankar; A. Prorok
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
abstract: Multirobot trajectory planning is a fundamental problem in multirobot coordination but remains computationally challenging due to its nonconvex, multimodal, and high-dimensional nature. This work builds upon D4orm, a dynamics-aware diffusion-denoising framework, and develops a family of planning architectures for diverse operational requirements. Unlike conventional numerical optimization methods, D4orm employs sampling-based optimization to generate solution trajectories through massively parallel sampling, leveraging modern computing architectures, such as GPUs. Its diffusion-denoising structure iteratively optimizes deformations to candidate control trajectories, providing an efficient and versatile paradigm for generating kinodynamically feasible and conflict-free trajectories. Using D4orm as the building block for advanced planners, we present a decoupled planner for improved scalability, an online receding-horizon planner with feedback control, and a distributed planner for resource-constrained settings. Evaluations with differential-drive and holonomic robots in 2-D and 3-D environments demonstrate that D4orm-based approaches find high-quality solutions faster and more reliably than other sampling-based optimization methods, such as model predictive path integral control, as well as a learned diffusion-model-based method. We further demonstrate zero-shot deployment on ten real quadrotors with obstacles, large-scale deconfliction with 100 simulated robots, and fully onboard distributed “lifelong” operation with six ground robots. Overall, these results establish diffusion denoising as a scalable and reliable framework for multirobot coordination.

title: Symbiotic Multi-Agent Hybrid Intelligence for Emergent Socio-Cognitive Resilience in Human- Machine Manufacturing Ecosystems (Smahi-Er)
authors: F. K. Renu; J. S. George; G. N. Sundar; Narmadha
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Engineering and Next-Gen Healthcare Systems (IEHNS)
abstract: Manufacturing systems are transitioning from Industry 4.0 automation-centric paradigms to Industry 5.0 human-centric resilient ecosystems. This paper introduces SMAHI-ER, a comprehensive framework for modeling emergent socio-cognitive resilience through symbiotic human-machine collaboration. SMAHI-ER integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for emergent cognition, Generative Diffusion Reinforcement Learning (G-DRL) for adaptive strategy synthesis, Causal SHAP for ethical alignment, federated learning for privacy-preserving knowledge sharing, and Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) for real-time cognitive monitoring. The framework models manufacturing ecosystems as dynamic hypergraphs-the Symbiotic Intelligence Field (SIF)-where Human Digital Twins (HDTs), Machine Cognitive Twins (MCTs), and Ethical Meta-Agents (EMAs) continuously co-evolve through multi-relational edges encoding trust, empathy, dependency, communication, and ethical alignment. We propose four novel composite metrics: CAS++ (Collective Adaptability Score Plus), ASI (Affective Synchronization Index), ESQ (Ethical Stability Quotient), and EID (Emergent Intelligence Density). Preliminary simulations across 50+ disruption scenarios with 30 Monte Carlo runs per scenario demonstrate SMAHI-ER achieves 88.1% OEE, 1.2% defect rate during disruptions (35% improvement over Industry 4.0), 91.5% worker stress control (58% improvement), and 2.15× emergent intelligence multiplier compared to four baselines. The framework establishes both theoretical foundations and practical architectures for realizing human-centric, ethically-aligned, resilient manufacturing systems aligned with Industry 5.0 vision.

title: A Novel Convex Layers Strategy for Circular Formation in Multiagent Systems
authors: G. Kumar; A. Ratnoo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
abstract: This article considers the problem of conflict-free distribution of point-sized agents on a circular periphery encompassing all agents. The two key elements of the proposed policy include the construction of a set of convex layers (nested convex polygons) using the initial positions of the agents, and a novel search space region for each of the agents. The search space for an agent on a convex layer is defined as the region enclosed between the lines passing through the agent’s position and normal to its supporting edges. Guaranteeing collision-free paths, a goal assignment policy designates a unique goal position within the search space of an agent at the initial time itself, requiring no further computation thereafter. In contrast to the existing literature, this work presents a one-shot, collision-free solution to the circular distribution problem by utilizing only the initial positions of the agents. Illustrative examples and extensive Monte Carlo studies considering various practical attributes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Automated Power Dispatch Architecture Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
authors: J. Fan; H. Xiao; P. Tan; J. Zeng; J. Song; R. Xiang; K. Zheng; J. Song; G. He
venue: 2026 IEEE PES International Meeting (PES IM)
abstract: Traditional power dispatch struggles to adapt to the uncertainty of renewable energy. Here we propose a Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaborative Architecture for Power Dispatch (DMAC-PD). The architecture includes dynamically reasoning and invoking tools through the Main Agent while integrating domain knowledge by the Knowledge Agent, ensuring physical and power stability constraints through the Safety Agent, and integrating various power system computation tools. The architecture employs a power dispatch model context protocol to coordinate the invocation of heterogeneous power system computation tools, supporting end-to-end automated processes from task analysis to strategy generation. Case studies show that the system can comprehensively integrate the uncertainties of wind-solar power prediction and load fluctuations, generate power system scheduling plans that comply with physical constraints, and provide an automated solution for intelligent dispatch in power grids.

title: Design and Implementation of a Heterogeneous Edge-AI Drone Swarm for Autonomous Logistics: Cloud Connected Hybrid Architecture
authors: K. Satyam; A. Haldar; S. Mondal; S. Santra; C. Das; J. Budhiya; S. Ghosh; S. Dey; S. Pal; A. Mukherjee; M. Sinha
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computing, Electronics & Communications Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: A heterogeneous unmanned aerial system (UAS) is developed for autonomous logistics and surveillance, integrating edge artificial intelligence with secure global connectivity. The system combines two complementary aerial platforms, a high agility ‘Scout’ quadcopter for rapid reconnaissance and real time visual tracking, and a heavy lift ‘Mule’ coaxial octocopter for reliable payload delivery. A major contribution of the proposed architecture lies in the unified onboard edge computing framework based on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super, which enables real time computer vision, autonomous decision making, and closed loop control directly on each drone, removing dependence on centralized ground processing. Another distinctive contribution is the Beyond Line of Sight (BLoS) communication framework that leverages 4G LTE telemetry integrated with a Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel. This approach overcomes conventional radio range and network address translation limitations, providing secure, low latency command and control and high definition video streaming without a dedicated ground station. By combining heterogeneous airframes, decentralized edge AI intelligence, and cloud assisted global connectivity, the proposed system offers a scalable and cost effective solution for next generation autonomous aerial logistics and surveillance operations.

title: Privacy Risks in Retrieval Augmented and Multi-Agent LLM Architectures Handling PHI
authors: S. K. A. Koduri
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The rapid integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and multi-agent Large Language Models (LLM) is reshaping the healthcare sector, enhancing clinical decision support and patient triage. While these systems enhance reasoning through dynamic knowledge retrieval and agent collaboration, they introduce significant privacy vulnerabilities regarding Protected Health Information (PHI). This paper presents a systematic review and architectural risk analysis of centralized RAG, on-device RAG, and distributed multi-agent structures published between 2023 and 2025. Unlike prior surveys that focus primarily on single-agent chatbots, this work explores how agent cooperation, memory retention, and multi-hop retrieval create emergent PHI leakage vectors. We introduce a formal mathematical risk propagation model to quantify these vulnerabilities and instantiate it through a synthetic Monte Carlo simulation that characterizes how exposure scales across architectures, governance weightings, and multi-hop propagation paths. We further contextualize the model against recently published empirical benchmarks of multi-agent privacy leakage, showing that its qualitative prediction-that inter-agent channels are a substantial source of exposure-is consistent with directly measured leakage rates in independent studies. We conclude by proposing specific benchmarking metrics and privacy-by-architecture principles to support HIPAA-compliant agentic AI deployments.

title: CTS-PLL: A Robust and Anytime Framework for Collaborative Task Sequencing and Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: J. Jiang; Y. Xu; R. Li; S. Xu; J. Wang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: The Collaborative Task Sequencing and Multi-Agent Path Finding (CTS-MAPF) problem requires agents to accomplish sequences of tasks while avoiding collisions, posing significant challenges due to its combinatorial complexity. This work introduces CTS-PLL, a hierarchical framework that extends the configuration-based CTS-MAPF planning paradigm with two complementary mechanisms for improved robustness and anytime solution quality. First, when the configuration-based planner encounters prolonged stagnation, a lock detection and release module constructs an auxiliary MAPF instance from the current CTS state and invokes complete MAPF method for recovery. Second, after a feasible plan is obtained for a candidate joint task sequence, an intra-sequence refinement procedure is applied to further improve path quality. Extensive evaluations across sparse and dense benchmarks demonstrate that CTS-PLL achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of success rate and solution quality, while maintaining competitive runtime efficiency. Real-world robot experiments further demonstrate the feasibility of the approach in practice.

title: HalluChain: Measuring and Controlling Cascade Hallucination Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
authors: A. M. Nair; S. S. Jacob; A. P S; A. Jayakrishnan; A. Manoj; S. V. Nathan; A. D. T H; N. Pradeesh
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Innovations in Mechanical, Robotics, Computing and Biomedical Engineering (ICIMRBE)
abstract: Current are becoming more and more multi-agent systems where specialized agents collaborate for task solving. Such architectures provide enhanced reasoning abilities and performance but suffer from the important drawback – hallucination propagation. An erroneous agent's information is likely to be accepted by subsequent agents, resulting in propagating the error further and further down the pipeline. In this paper, we present HalluChain, a framework to measure and mitigate hallucination propagation in multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) pipelines. We evaluate hallucination error propagation in three pipeline architectures: Linear, Parallel and Hierarchical using the HaluEval benchmark dataset. To evaluate error propagation, we develop the Hallucination Propagation Metric (HPM Score). We also propose HalluFirewall – an inter-agent verification module based on confidence scoring, consistency checking, fact grounding and output sanitization. Experiments show that linear pipelines propagate hallucinations up to 5.5 times by the last agent stage, whereas parallel pipelines lower propagation up to 65%. HalluFirewall lowers HPM Scores up to 60-70% at the cost of 15% increase in runtime.

title: A Supervisor-Coordinated Multi-Agent Architecture with ReAct Reasoning and FHIR Integration, Achieving 41% Diagnostic Time Reduction in Telemedicine Workflows
authors: M. Chandrasekaran
venue: 2026 6th Middle East and North Africa Communications Conference (MENACOMM)
abstract: Telemedicine faces persistent challenges in terms of communication efficiency, triage accuracy, and documentation burden. This study presents MEDCOMM-AGENT, a novel multi-agent AI architecture that addresses critical communication bottlenecks through hierarchical coordination and specialized agent collaboration. The system comprises four domain-specific agents: the Triage Intelligence Agent (TIA), Diagnostic Support Agent (DSA), Communication Facilitation Agent (CFA), and Documentation Synthesis Agent (DOCSA), orchestrated by a Supervisor Agent (SA) with structured debate protocols. We integrated advanced reasoning mechanisms, including ReAct patterns, iterative $\mathbf{4}$-cycle self-refinement, and CoT prompting, within a FHIR R4-compliant framework. Simulation-based evaluation across $\mathbf{1, 5 0 0}$ synthetic encounters demonstrates significant improvements: $\mathbf{9 2. 4 \%}$ triage accuracy ($\mathbf{9 5 \%}$ CI: 90.1-94.3%, $p<0.001$) versus 34-68% baseline, 73% documentation time reduction (2.8 vs. 17.3 minutes), 41.1 % diagnostic time improvement ($\mathbf{1 0. 6}$ vs. $\mathbf{1 8}$ minutes, Cohen's $d=2.14$), and 33.9% reduction in 30-day readmissions ($\mathbf{R R = 0. 6 6, } p<0.001$). Ablation studies revealed catastrophic triage degradation ($-41.2 \%$) without TIA, substantial diagnostic loss ($-18.6 \%$) without DSA, and $5.7-7.9 \%$ degradation across metrics without a supervisor. The architecture demonstrated robust performance under adversarial conditions (maximum $<7 \%$ degradation under single stressors) with subadditive degradation under combined stressors. This study elevates patient communication to a status equal to diagnostic reasoning, providing a validated architectural framework and evaluation methodology for next-generation telemedicine. Computational analysis showed feasible deployment (23.0s latency, $0.70 cost, 11.8 GB memory) with linear scalability to 120 encounters/hour.

title: Safe Formation Control of Multi-Agent Systems via Control Barrier Function and Hybrid Disturbance Rejection
authors: Y. Liu; Y. Liu; J. Shen; W. Wang; J. Lü
venue: 2026 5th Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (FASTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid formation control framework for multi-agent systems to ensure hard safety constraints subject to unknown disturbances. While extended state observers (ESOs) actively compensate for lumped disturbances, their residual estimation errors often lead to constraint violations and compromise system safety. To address this, we propose a decoupled architecture, employing ESO-based reference control signals for formation tracking and distributed modified control barrier function (DMCBF) based safety filters. By integrating the DMCBF into a quadratic program (QP), it provides passive robustness against bounded estimation errors, strictly enforcing inter-agent and agent-obstacle collision avoidance. It demonstrates that the safety constraints and input-to-state stability (ISS) are guaranteed. Finally, experiments on a Crazyflie quadrotor swarm under wind disturbances validate the practical effectiveness of the proposed control framework.

title: A Meta-Learning and Physics-Informed Reinforcement Learning Framework for Multi-UGV Cooperative Defense
authors: D. Chen; J. Liu; F. Jin; J. Zhao; W. Wang; K. Sun
venue: 2026 IEEE 15th Data Driven Control and Learning Systems (DDCLS)
abstract: The widespread deployment of low-altitude, slow-speed, small unmanned aerial vehicles (LSS-UAVs) in battlefield reconnaissance and precision strike missions has made them a primary threat to force protection, and the efficient countermeasures against such targets have become a pressing challenge in modern warfare. In cooperative counter-UAV tasks involving multiple unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), multi-objective optimization must be achieved simultaneously for obstacle avoidance, accurate neutralization of intruding UAVs, and energy consumption control. However, conventional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) typically relies on fixed reward weights, which is difficult to adapt to dynamic battlefield environments, and it lacks explicit modeling of physical motion constraints, resulting in insufficient policy robustness and task adaptability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) framework that integrates meta-learning and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) into the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm, termed Meta Dynamic Reward Weight MADDPG-PINN (MetaDRW-MADDPG-PINN). A dynamic reward-weight predictor based on model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) outputs, in real time, the "mission - safety - energy" weights that match the current scenario. The PINN module converts physical constraints, including UGV kinematics and collision avoidance, into residual losses and incorporates them into the MADDPG optimization process. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared with MADDPG baselines, the proposed framework improves the obstacle-avoidance safety rate by 21.9% and the counter-UAV success rate by 31.1%, while reducing energy consumption by 34.1%, thereby effectively enhancing the coordination performance and robustness of multiple UGVs in dynamically complex battlefield settings.

title: Cyber-Physical GraphRAG: Safe, Real-Time, and Scalable Orchestration of Large-Scale Autonomous Fleets
authors: A. Ibrahim; F. Al Machot; K. Kyamakya
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Large-scale autonomous fleet orchestration requires both geometric reasoning for path planning and semantic reasoning for task allocation and policy compliance. Existing approaches either inject full robot state into Large Language Model (LLM) context windows, incurring prohibitive latency and token costs that scale linearly with fleet size, or rely on static Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that lack temporal awareness and cannot distinguish current state from stale history. Recent Temporal Graph-based RAG (GraphRAG) frameworks address temporal ambiguity for document retrieval but operate on discrete calendar-based time models unsuitable for the sub-second dynamics of cyber-physical systems. This paper introduces the paradigm of Cyber-Physical GraphRAG, a category of retrieval-augmented generation designed for real-time, safety-critical orchestration, and presents Hybrid State-Knowledge GraphRAG (HSK-GraphRAG) as its first realization. The framework contributes three innovations: (1) a Signal-Weighted Semantic Decay function that models physical freshness using continuous exponential decay incorporating wireless signal quality; (2) a Topological Safety Firewall that deterministically prevents invalid, stale, or non-compliant agents from reaching the LLM reasoning layer; and (3) stale-history-insensitive retrieval via validity-tier indexing, where query cost scales only with active agents. Experimental validation demonstrates sub-10 ms graph-query latency (excluding LLM inference), complete safety constraint compliance within the defined graph-based logical safety model, zero ghost-agent selection, and robustness under hardware-in-the-loop dataset replay with realistic sensor noise. These results establish Cyber-Physical GraphRAG as a viable foundation for deploying LLM-based reasoning in high-frequency autonomous fleet control.

title: Architectural Patterns for Scalable Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Software Engineering Perspective
authors: K. Savajiyani
venue: 2026 International Conference on Future and Intelligent Networking (FINE)
abstract: The proliferation of large language model (LLM)-based autonomous agents has created a new class of distributed system: the multi-agent LLM network. While significant research focuses on the intelligence of individual agents, comparatively little work addresses the software architectural concerns that govern how fleets of such agents are composed, orchestrated, and scaled. This paper identifies and formalizes four recurring architectural patterns (Hierarchical Orchestration, Event-Driven Agent Mesh, Capability-Indexed Agent Registry, and Stateless Execution with Persistent Memory Offload), drawing on well-established technologies including Apache Kafka, MongoDB, AWS, Spring Boot, and Docker. All experiments were conducted exclusively on synthetically generated data using a locally hosted reference implementation on a personal development machine. No enterprise, production, or personally identifiable data was involved in this work. We analyze each pattern with respect to throughput, fault tolerance, observability, and latency trade-offs using a fully controlled synthetic workload, ensuring complete reproducibility. Our evaluation demonstrates that no single pattern dominates across all dimensions, and that composition of patterns yields the strongest results. This work provides a foundation for treating multi-agent LLM system design as a first-class software engineering discipline. Note: The four patterns operate at complementary abstraction levels coordination (Patterns 1 and 2), discovery and routing (Pattern 3), and state management (Pattern 4) and are designed for deliberate composition rather than as parallel alternatives.

title: Dependency-Aware Online Computation Offloading for DAG Tasks in MEC-Enabled IIoT
authors: Y. Zhang; K. Peng; Y. Lin
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Communications and Computer Networks (ISCCN)
abstract: The rapid development of the Industrial Internet of Things drives the evolution of industrial systems to the interconnection and intelligent paradigm. The resulting largescale computationally intensive tasks with complex dependencies bring an unprecedented computational burden to the terminal. Mobile edge computing alleviates this pressure by offloading computing at the edge of the network. However, real industrial tasks usually show strict precedence constraints between subtasks. In addition, the fierce competition of multiple terminals for limited edge resources in a dynamic environment makes the learning process very vulnerable to instability and strategy performance degradation. Aiming at the above problems, a computational offloading method REMAPPO based on multiagent reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed. Specifically, we first use directed acyclic graphs to model complex dependent tasks. Then, multi-agent deep reinforcement learning is used to realize multi-terminal collaborative burden reduction decisionmaking, and experience playback and reservoir sampling mechanisms are introduced to preserve representative historical experience. Extensive experiments on real industrial datasets show that the REMAPPO method significantly reduces latency and energy consumption, improves edge resource utilization, and has better stability and robustness.

title: Input-to-State Safety for Reinforcement Learning
authors: M. S. Jha; S. Marthi; K. G. Vamvoudakis; S. Kanso; D. Theilliol
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
abstract: In this article, we present a novel off-policy, safe reinforcement learning (RL) approach for nonlinear dynamical systems under input saturation that guarantees safe initialization, safe exploration, as well as safe learning of optimal control laws. First, to encourage preferable exploration near safety boundaries, important for integrating system behavior near the safety limits, we formulate a safe exploration approach as a robust control problem by considering an enlarged safe set based on input-to-state safe control barrier functions (ISSf-CBFs). These constraints are then incorporated into a quadratic programming (QP) optimization. We propose a novel $\epsilon $ -tuning law that adaptively enforces stricter safety constraints near the boundaries of the safe set and relaxes constraints deeper within the safe set, encouraging safety boundary-proximal exploration while maintaining forward invariance of the safe set. The proposed $\epsilon $ -tuning law safely accommodates aggressive, high-magnitude exploration noise, enabling efficient state-space exploration without compromising safety. Next, safe learning under saturation limits is guaranteed through a safety-aware cost function. We establish safety, optimality, and stability properties (novel) in a mathematically rigorous manner. Furthermore, the safe RL problem is solved in an off-policy manner, and neural networks are used to approximate the value function and the control policy. To that end, we establish a novel off-policy equation under input saturation. Finally, simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed framework.

title: Web3-Driven Blockchain Multi-Agent Decentralized Supply Chain Decision Intelligence
authors: B. Sowan; A. Altarawneh; R. Almwari; E. Mallah; S. Swift; M. Arzoky
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Modern supply chains are becoming increasingly decentralized, requiring coordination mechanisms that can operate without centralized control or full bilateral trust. This paper introduces AGENTARA, an Autonomous Governance-Enabled Network Architecture for Distributed Decision Intelligence, as a blockchain-enabled multi-agent framework for autonomous and trustworthy supply chain decision-making. The proposed architecture integrates distributed ledger technology, smart contracts, decentralized oracles, reinforcement learning, and reputationweighted consensus to support transparent information sharing, adaptive disruption response, and auditable multi-stakeholder governance. AGENTARA was evaluated through an 18-month automotive supply chain simulation involving five production tiers and 47 participants. The results show a 68% reduction in decision-making latency, 89% disruption response effectiveness, 99.4% transaction verification success, and average consensus completion within 14.2 seconds. Economic analysis further indicates potential cost savings of 19-24% through reduced intermediation overhead and improved inventory coordination. These findings demonstrate that blockchain-enabled multi-agent architectures can provide a scalable foundation for low-trust supply chain governance, where autonomous agents coordinate decisions while preserving transparency, accountability, and operational resilience.

title: Joint Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Message-Passing for Resilient Multi-UAV Networks
authors: Y. Cho; S. Yi; S. Park
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
abstract: This paper introduces a novel resilient algorithm designed for distributed un-crewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) in dynamic and unreliable network environments. Initially, the UAVs should be trained via multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for autonomous mission-critical operations and are fundamentally grounded by centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) using a centralized MARL server. In this situation, it is crucial to consider the case where several UAVs cannot receive CTDE-based MARL learning parameters for resilient operations in unreliable network conditions. To tackle this issue, a communication graph is used where its edges are established when two UAVs/nodes are communicable. Then, the edge-connected UAVs can share their training data if one of the UAVs cannot be connected to the CTDE-based MARL server under unreliable network conditions. Additionally, the edge cost considers power efficiency. Based on this given communication graph, message-passing is used for electing the UAVs that can provide their MARL learning parameters to their edge-connected peers. Lastly, performance evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our proposed algorithm in terms of power efficiency and resilient UAV task management, outperforming existing benchmark algorithms.

title: OpenCDA-MARL: A Unified Benchmarking Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Intersection Management With Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: L. Guo; L. Liu; J. Tang; B. Liu; S. Cao
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Single-vehicle autonomy remains constrained by perception errors and uncoordinated maneuvers, resulting in avoidable collisions and throughput losses at intersections. Cooperative Driving Automation (CDA) offers substantial gains, yet fragmented toolchains hinder progress: industry develops closed systems, while academic studies rely on simplified simulators that lack realistic dynamics. We introduce OpenCDA-MARL, an open-source extension of OpenCDA that transforms the high-fidelity CARLA simulator into a unified benchmarking platform for autonomous intersection management (AIM).
