The framework provides a modular multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) API enabling reproducible training and comparison of cooperative policies under identical physical conditions. Building upon OpenCDA's integration and scenario managers, OpenCDA-MARL provides an additional MARL Adapter Interface layer, along with MARL scenario and environment managers for custom traffic conditions, performance tracking, baseline agents, and standard MARL algorithms, to support a comprehensive MARL evaluation suite in AIM. Key innovations include: (1) a 43-dimensional TTC-augmented observation model providing proactive collision awareness via physics-based trajectory prediction; (2) a cooperative yielding reward that incentivizes speed reduction when neighboring vehicles face collision risk; and (3) an LSTM-based multi-agent context encoder that captures spatiotemporal traffic interactions using distance-sorted agent sequences. OpenCDA-MARL includes rule-based, behavior, and vanilla agents, along with MARL baselines (MATD3, MADQN, MAPPO, MASAC) implemented under centralized training with decentralized execution. Evaluations using standardized metrics show that MASAC achieves perfect success at light traffic and maintains strong performance under heavy congestion (300 vph), substantially outperforming rule-based baselines. OpenCDA-MARL provides datasets, training scripts, and evaluation protocols to accelerate reproducible research toward safe and scalable CDA systems.

title: Mean-Field Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: L. Huo; J. Mao; H. San; R. Li; Z. Xuan
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Continuous-space multi-agent path finding (MAPF) presents severe challenges for deep reinforcement learning (DRL), as joint state–action spaces grow exponentially and fine-grained inter-agent coordination is required. Applying mean-field approximation can reduce input complexity from $\mathcal {O}(N^{2}~d)$ to $\mathcal {O}(Nd)$, but naively averaging neighbors may weaken critical local interactions, limiting planning success. To address this, we propose the Mean-Field Multi-Agent Reinforcement Pathfinding Framework (MAMFRPF), which integrates mean-field interaction compression, a dual-stream local mean-field critic, trust-region policy optimization, and a sparse-reward design. The dual-stream critic compensates for information loss caused by mean-field averaging, improving planning success by over 20 percentage points under partial observability, while training time is reduced by roughly 7%. Trust-region optimization ensures monotonic policy improvement, and the sparse-reward mechanism accelerates long-horizon credit assignment. Experiments on continuous MAPF benchmarks show that MAMFRPF outperforms strong baselines by 15% in success rate, scales with agent density, and generalizes across diverse spatial layouts.

title: Bearing Measurement-Based Adaptive Predefined-Time Enclosed Fault-Tolerant Control for Multiple Vehicle Systems
authors: H. Zhang; K. Li; Y. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: This article investigates the issue of dynamic event-triggered (DET) predefined-time cooperative formation target enclosed control for multiple vehicle systems, which subjects to infinite actuator faults and unknown dead-zones. The barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) is constructed to confine angular errors within predefined bounds, such that collision avoidance and inherent field-of-view restrictions of bearing sensors are ensured throughout the target enclosed control design. Meanwhile, considering the frequent updates of actual control signals, a DET mechanism is designed, which can significantly improve the utilization of communication resource. Combining the bearing measurement information and adaptive technique, a novel event-based robust adaptive cooperative formation target enclosed fault-tolerant control (FTC) algorithm is further developed. With the help of practical predefined-time stability theory, the developed enclosed control scheme can ensure that the multiple vehicle system is predefined-time stable and all signals are bounded. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the presented control algorithm can be verified by simulation results.

title: Edge-Cloud Collaborative USV-ROV System: Active Tether Control and Multi-Agent Navigation for Marine Pastures
authors: D. Song; W. Li; W. Song; W. Zheng; X. Liu; Y. Lv
venue: 2026 International Conference on Sensor-Cloud and Edge Computing System (SCECS)
abstract: To address the communication bottlenecks, severe tether-induced drag, and inadequate navigational autonomy of traditional Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs) in marine monitoring, this paper proposes an edge-cloud collaborative USV-ROV system. Utilizing the USV as a mobile edge relay, the architecture integrates a force-feedback smart winch to achieve Autonomous Launch and Recovery (ALARS) and active tether tension control. For autonomous navigation, we construct a multi-agent framework combining 2D cross-product-based reactive obstacle avoidance with global dynamic target allocation, ensuring collision-free operations in constrained waters. Furthermore, an asymmetric hierarchical perception mechanism is developed: a lightweight YOLO model is executed at the edge (ROV) to ensure ultra-low latency for real-time tracking and reactive control, while a high-precision YOLO model—integrated with Vision-Language Models (VLMs)—is deployed in the cloud for complex semantic parsing and high-fidelity obstacle classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the system effectively suppresses tether tension, enhances navigational safety, and achieves robust visual perception, providing a highly reliable solution for autonomous marine monitoring.

title: Resilient Event-Triggered Flocking Control of Multiagent Systems With Malicious Nodes
authors: Z. Liu; X. Luo; X. Li; D. Chen; W. Qi
venue: 2026 5th Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (FASTA)
abstract: This paper studies resilient flocking control for second-order multi-agent systems in the presence of non-cooperative agents and limited communication. Each cooperative agent only measures its own state, exchanges information with neighbors at asynchronously triggered instants, and runs a local estimator of the algebraic connectivity and its gradient. A switched distributed control architecture is proposed: when the estimated connectivity is low, a connectivity-enhancement mode is activated to increase the Fiedler eigenvalue of the cooperative subgraph. Once a connectivity margin is recovered, the system switches to a flocking mode that combines a repulsive-attractive potential with a WMSR-based velocity alignment term. An event-triggering mechanism with time-varying thresholds is designed to reduce communication while avoiding Zeno behavior. Under mild robustness and time-scale separation assumptions, it is shown that cooperative velocities remain uniformly ultimately bounded, the system switches to the flocking mode in finite time, and all cooperative agents asymptotically achieve resilient flocking: their velocities converge to a common value and all inter-agent distances stay within a prescribed safety interval. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and demonstrate significant communication savings compared with continuous-feedback schemes.

title: Cooperative Decision-making Optimization of Underwater Robots Based on Knowledge Graph and Reinforcement Learning
authors: B. Miao; Y. You; Y. Tang
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Mechatronics, Robotics, and Artificial Intelligence (MRAI)
abstract: In response to the technical bottlenecks faced by existing underwater robots when performing tasks in complex and dynamic unknown sea areas, such as the single-point failure risk of centralized planning systems in complex environments and the lack of global collaborative cognition in single-machine decision-making, this paper studies and proposes a collaborative task planning and decision-making optimization method based on the integration of distributed knowledge graphs and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), aiming to enhance the safety, robustness, and collaborative efficiency of underwater robot groups in real-time task allocation and obstacle avoidance. Firstly, this paper proposes a distributed knowledge graph construction method for underwater operation environments, integrating multi-source heterogeneous information. Secondly, a scene-aware communication topology strategy based on local perception is designed, which enables on-demand interaction of key knowledge according to the real-time relative situation of the robot group. Finally, the extracted structured collaborative knowledge is used as a prior constraint for the multi-agent reinforcement learning network, and through a distributed reward mechanism and action masking technology, the model is guided to generate safe, compliant, and globally optimal planning strategies. Ultimately, simulation experiments show that in typical exploration tasks, the communication cost of the proposed distributed collaborative decision-making framework is significantly reduced by approximately 90%, and the task completion rate is increased to 94.5%.

title: Evolution of the Swarm Test Arena for Resilient Systems: A System of Systems Case Study
authors: J. Kohlmeyer; B. Watson
venue: 2026 21st Annual System of Systems Engineering Conference (SoSE)
abstract: Systems of Systems are comprised of multiple autonomous systems, often developed in parallel. System architecture evolves as new constituent systems are added and removed from the System of Systems. As subsystem evolution occurs each system and associated interfaces are developed until the System of Systems reaches a usable configuration. Examination of the process of evolving new System of Systems can be difficult to conduct in real-world scenarios, due to evolution occurring ad-hoc over long periods of time. Thus, specific data on a System of System's development is difficult to obtain. In response to this gap, this article documents the development and evolution of a large research project: the Swarm Test Arena for Resilient Systems (STARS). The Swarm Test Arena for Resilient Systems is a System of Systems comprised of 8 interconnected systems (Rover agents, Charging Stations, Ground station, Computer vision positioning system, Automated charging sequencer, Telemetry system, Anti-collision system, and virtual sensor system) developed in parallel by six teams over the course of eight months. We view this as a case of System of System evolution as each sub-team was autonomous (pursuing various primary goals including research output or capstone course credit), the System of Systems evolved through multiple states with varying levels of functionality, and the System of Systems demonstrated emergent properties. This article outlines the methodology employed in developing STARS, some insights into studying System of Systems, insights for practitioners looking to utilize capstone teams to develop new capabilities in existing research platforms, and an overview of the stages of development of the project.

title: Safe Fuzzy-CBF: A Monitoring Approach for Deep Reinforcement Learning Navigation Agents
authors: M. Yang; G. Liu; Z. Zhou; G. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: In safety-critical reinforcement learning tasks such as robot navigation, autonomous driving, and industrial control, real-time monitoring of agent behavior is paramount to prevent unsafe actions from compromising system reliability. We introduce Safe Fuzzy Control Barrier Functions (Safe Fuzzy-CBF), a monitoring framework that continuously evaluates agent risk using a smooth control barrier function learned from data via Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy rules, rather than relying on a predefined model-based barrier. In the offline phase, we extract fuzzy rules from trajectory data and construct a continuously differentiable barrier that unifies state, action, and cost into a single risk metric. During online execution, we estimate the barrier’s time derivative using finite differences, apply Lipschitz-based corrections, and when the barrier condition is violated, we solve a small quadratic program in the normalized control space to compute a safe corrective action. Evaluated on three Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks and the MetaDrive autonomous driving environment, our framework detects emerging safety violations in real time and enforces runtime safety without degrading the underlying RL policy’s performance, achieving up to an 86.8% reduction in accumulated cost. Note to Practitioners—Real-world deployment of reinforcement learning controllers is challenged by model inaccuracies and high human monitoring costs, especially in safety-sensitive scenarios such as robotic navigation and autonomous driving. To this end, we propose an end-to-end, online differentiable safety fuzzy-CBF monitoring module that can be embedded in any reinforcement learning system. The module extracts a small number of trajectories offline before training, automatically generates differentiable fuzzy control barrier functions, evaluates barriers in real time during training or inference, and solves a quadratic program to generate safe corrective actions on potentially dangerous actions to generate safe actions to replace the original decisions. Experimental results show that the safety fuzzy-CBF monitoring module can reduce the cumulative cost of navigation tasks without degrading the performance of the original policy of the original policy, providing engineers with a real-time safety assurance method. Although our method has demonstrated strong safety monitoring performance in single-agent scenarios with unknown dynamics, to extend it to multi-agent applications it is necessary to combine decentralized barrier function design with graph neural networks to cope with complex interactions between agents and real-time scalability.

title: Safety-Guaranteed Energy Management in Networked Multienergy Microgrids: A Multi-Actor Single-Critic Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
authors: H. Yang; H. Tian; F. Guo; R. Deng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Distributed energy systems are shifting from stand-alone microgrids to networked multienergy microgrids (N-MEMGs), where energy management must handle multienergy coupling, renewable uncertainty, and strict device/network safety under distributed operation. A safety-guaranteed framework that couples a multi-actor single-critic multiagent deep reinforcement learning method with randomized ensembled double $Q$-learning (REDQ) and a model-based safety layer is proposed. Actors run locally at nodes for decentralized operation; a centralized REDQ-based critic module reduces $Q$-value overestimation and reliably guides policy updates; and the safety layer analytically enforces device, power balance, and multitimescale constraints, explicitly capturing inertia-induced effects along hydrogen device chains. On a five-node N-MEMG, the proposed method coordinates energy trading, hydrogen storage, and peak shaving, achieves zero observed safety violations over 12 000 evaluation steps, and outperforms mainstream baselines (multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3), multiagent deep deterministic policy gradient, and multiagent soft actor critic) with an average daily adaptive normalized score of 98% across test days. The results point to a practical route to safe and scalable energy management in N-MEMGs.

title: Efficient Exploration in Large State-Action Space Through Structured Action Space for Learning Multirobots Motion Planning
authors: C. Mu; Z. Jiang; J. Zhang; K. Wang; X. Xu; J. Yi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
abstract: Multirobots tasks, such as collaborative motion planning or flexible parts assembly, are complex for autonomous robot operations. The robot system for such tasks would need a combination of multigoal motion control and collision avoidance in the shared workspace. For reinforcement learning (RL)-based methods with enhanced flexibility and broader applicability, these methods struggle to effectively handle intricate tasks that require collision-free motion planning and control across long time horizons. Current RL systems cannot achieve efficiently motion planning due to high degrees-of-freedom (DoF), large-scale continuous action space, and tightly coupled workspaces of multirobot system. Additionally, the exploration efficiency for multigoal tasks is typically low, particularly in scenarios where rewards are scarce. To tackle these issues, we propose a new method to decompose the large-scale continuous action space into the combination of discrete action space that enhances exploration and small-scale continuous action space that enhances accuracy of structured hybrid action space (SHAS). To train the model with SHAS efficiently, we develop a task-conditioned hierarchical RL (TC-HRL) framework to train both high-level (HL) policy and low-level (LL) policy in parallel. Comparative experiments from different perspectives demonstrate that our model can learn multirobots manipulation tasks more efficiently and stably, and with considerably less time consumption. Finally, our work is verified by the pick-grasp tasks and real manipulators experiments.

title: The Trust Paradox in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: When Collaboration Becomes a Security Vulnerability
authors: Z. Xu; M. Qi; S. Wu; L. Zhang; Q. Wei; H. He; N. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) are advancing rapidly, yet the security implications of trust-mediated collaboration remain insufficiently understood. We introduce and empirically validate the trust–vulnerability paradox (TVP): increasing inter-agent trust to improve coordination can simultaneously amplify risks of over-exposure and authorization drift (AD). To study this phenomenon under controlled and reproducible conditions, we operationalize trust as a system-level control parameter governing authorization strictness and information disclosure, rather than as a cognitive or social construct. We construct a purpose-built scenario-game dataset spanning three macro-scenes and nineteen sub-scenes, and conduct extensive closed-loop agent-to-agent (A2A) interactions with explicit trust parameterization. Using minimum necessary information (MNI) as the safety baseline, we propose two unified metrics: over-exposure rate (OER) to quantify boundary violations, and AD to capture the sensitivity of disclosure behavior to trust variation. Experiments across multiple model backends and orchestration frameworks reveal consistent trends: higher trust improves task success but also increases over-exposure risk, with substantial heterogeneity in risk sensitivity to trust across systems. We further evaluate mitigation strategies, including Sensitive Information Repartitioning and guardian-agent (GA-Agent) enablement, which effectively reduce OER and attenuate AD under elevated trust. Overall, this work formalizes TVP as a systemic security property, establishes reproducible experimental baselines with unified metrics, and demonstrates that trust must be modelled, calibrated, and managed as a first-class security variable in the design of LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS).

title: A Study of Fully Autonomous UAV Based on Singleagent and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: W. -T. Lee; Z. -Q. Ying; H. -W. Wei; H. Hsu; C. -J. Chuang
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Consumer Technology (ICCT-Pacific)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous control technologies, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have been widely utilized in applications such as agricultural inspection, reconnaissance, environmental monitoring, and mountain rescue. This study aims to develop an autonomous UAV system designed for mountain search missions, utilizing a reinforcement learning framework for training. The single-agent Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is employed to achieve stable flight control and obstacle avoidance, while the Multi-Agent Posthumous Credit Assignment (MA-POCA) algorithm enables cooperative exploration and collision prevention among multiple drones. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed observation and reward design, based on the reinforcement learning framework, enables drones to perform autonomous and highly efficient cooperative search missions in complex terrains.

title: Game-Theoretic Safe Multiagent Motion Planning With Reachability Analysis for Dynamic and Uncertain Environments
authors: W. Mai; M. Liwang; X. Yi; X. Xia; S. Hosseinalipour; X. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Ensuring safe, robust, and scalable motion planning for multiagent systems in dynamic and uncertain environments is a persistent challenge, driven by complex interagent interactions, stochastic disturbances, and model uncertainties. To overcome these challenges, particularly the computational complexity of coupled decision-making and the need for proactive safety guarantees, we propose a reachability-enhanced dynamic potential game (RE-DPG) framework, which integrates game-theoretic coordination into reachability analysis. This approach formulates multiagent coordination as a dynamic potential game, where the Nash equilibrium (NE) defines optimal control strategies across agents. To enable scalability and decentralized execution, we develop a neighborhood-dominated iterative best response scheme, built upon an iterated $\varepsilon$-BR process that guarantees finite-step convergence to an $\varepsilon$-NE. This allows agents to compute strategies based on local interactions while ensuring theoretical convergence guarantees. Furthermore, to ensure safety under uncertainty, we integrate a multiagent forward reachable set mechanism into the cost function, explicitly modeling uncertainty propagation and enforcing collision avoidance constraints. Through both simulations and real-world experiments in 2-D and 3-D environments, we validate the effectiveness of RE-DPG across diverse operational scenarios.

title: Learning to Debate: Optimal Stopping Strategies for Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
authors: X. Zhang; D. Hu
venue: 2026 International Conference on Generative Artificial Intelligence and Information Security (GAIIS)
abstract: Multi-agent debate has emerged as a promising paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, the relationship between debate duration and output quality remains poorly understood. In this paper, we introduce the debate fatigue hypothesis: the notion that debate quality follows a non-monotonic trajectory, initially improving with additional rounds before eventually degrading. We propose a scaling law that models debate quality as a function of rounds: Q(T) = a • log(T + c) − b • T, where the fatigue coefficient b> 0 captures diminishing returns. Through extensive experiments with GPT-4o across 108+ debates spanning five task categories (Mathematics, Code, Logic, Science, and Finance), we validate this hypothesis with 100% confirmation rate. We further develop an adaptive stopping strategy that achieves 98.7% of oracle performance while reducing computational costs by up to 50%. Additionally, our security evaluation demonstrates that multi-agent debate reduces hallucination indicators by 61.6% and corrects 50.6% of single-agent errors, providing significant safety improvements for LLM deployment. Our findings provide both theoretical foundations and practical guidelines for deploying multi-agent debate systems efficiently in industrial applications.

title: I Spawn with My Little Eye: Low-Bandwidth Situational Awareness for CBRNE Response via Sparse Geometric Digital Twin of the Environment
authors: M. Kozlik; E. Wachtler; K. G. Alamdar; K. Cirkvencic; F. Petric; M. Orsag
venue: 2026 IEEE 35th International Conference on Robot and Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN)
abstract: This paper presents a bandwidth-efficient teleoperation system that enables effective environmental perception and object manipulation in CBRNe (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosive) environments under constrained communication conditions. The proposed framework combines a mobile robotic platform equipped with a manipulator and perception sensors with a virtual reality operator interface developed in Unity. Instead of streaming raw video, the system transmits compact spatial and semantic information to reconstruct a simplified yet informative scene representation. Object size and pose are estimated using 6D pose estimation to support reliable manipulation of potentially contaminated objects. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains operational awareness while reducing bandwidth requirements by up to 15 times compared to standard RGB video streaming. Video: https://youtu.be/zVY83z6yGzM?si=AE450Ayvx71J1NXt.

title: Hallucination-Aware Collaborative Task Scheduling in Multiplex Industrial Networks With LLM-Driven Agents
authors: P. Li; T. -Y. Zuo; M. Liu; Y. Jiang; K. Di; J. Lin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
abstract: LLM agents in an industrial workflow exchange plans, observations, and intermediate results. A wrong output from one agent can enter another agent's context and spread through the workflow. We model this process as a feedback-amplified cascade on a multiplex network that represents task dependencies, communication links, physical proximity, and shared LLM services. The model reveals a connectivity–vulnerability trade-off. Extra cross-layer links can improve collaboration while making hallucination outbreaks easier. We then formulate the Hallucination-Aware Collaborative Task Scheduling (HACTS) problem and prove its $\mathcal {NP}$-hardness. Our Cross-Layer Hallucination-Aware Scheduling algorithm (CLHAS) places verifiers, selects agents, and routes messages according to cascade risk. Under fixed propagation scenarios, verifier placement has a provable approximation guarantee, while the complete scheduler is a practical polynomial-time heuristic. Simulations and controlled API-driven case studies show that CLHAS improves the safety–utility trade-off over networked schedulers. Ablations show that verification and risk-aware routing suppress error propagation, while assignment gains depend on the model backbone and task structure. A strong single-agent baseline further shows that collaborative scheduling is most useful when the workflow requires information exchange across agents.

title: Scalable Task Allocation for Multi-Robot Systems Using Vision-Informed Graph Decomposition
authors: H. Byeon; M. Soni; V. Sharma; K. Prasad; F. A. Reegu; P. G. G. Lagrazon
venue: 2026 IEEE World Skills Conference on Universal Data Analytics and Sciences (WorldSUAS)
abstract: In the domain of computer vision and robotics, efficient deployment of autonomous mobile robots is critical for tasks such as surveillance, exploration, and environmental mapping. This paper addresses the challenge of multi-robot task allocation for full area coverage, formulated as a graph-based optimization problem. We propose a Vision-Guided Multi-Level Graph Partitioning (VG-MLGP) framework that leverages environmental data, possibly derived from vision-based sensing, to construct a weighted graph representing the operational area. The method comprises two key stages: a coarse task allocation algorithm that uses hierarchical graph coarsening and a fine-grained refinement algorithm employing a Lazy & Lock boundary node exchange strategy. This dual-stage heuristic approach enables balanced and collision-free task assignment while preserving spatial connectivity essential for real-time robotic navigation. Extensive simulations on vision-derived real-world maps and synthetic large-scale graphs demonstrate that VG-MLGP significantly improves computational efficiency and task distribution quality. The framework scales to graphs with up to 1,000,000 nodes, achieving near-optimal coverage allocation in under 60 seconds—making it suitable for vision-driven robotic operations in complex, large-scale environments.

title: Safe Human-Centric Shared Control for Consumer Service Robots in Smart Home Environments via Observer-Based ADP
authors: L. Meng; Y. Hao; Q. Yuan; Y. Zhan; D. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Human-in-the-loop coordination has been widely applied in consumer electronics, including smart home service robots. Deploying such algorithms on consumer-grade hardware faces significant challenges, including constrained residential Wi-Fi bandwidth, unmeasurable states due to low-cost sensors, and the unpredictable behavior of non-expert users who may issue kinematically unsafe commands. To address these conflicts, this paper proposes a human-centric unified dynamic event-triggered safe shared control architecture. First, a neural network observer reconstructs unmeasurable system states. Second, to rigorously model real-world human interventions, a state-dependent bounded rationality framework is established. To prevent user-induced mechanical damage, a control barrier function is mathematically coupled with adaptive dynamic programming. This creates an asymmetric authority shield that actively filters unsafe commands without inducing algorithmic singularities. Additionally, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism integrated with experience replay guarantees asymptotic consensus while drastically conserving communication resources without requiring persistent excitation. Theoretical analysis rigorously proves the coupling mechanism among observer errors, safety projections, and optimal approximations, ensuring that all closed-loop signals are uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulations confirm that the system remains forward invariant under severe human panic inputs, while achieving high bandwidth efficiency and reliable collision avoidance in consumer multi-robot networks.

title: Multi-Agent Deep Learning Framework for Supply Chain Resilience
authors: S. Guram; S. Pahune
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Computing Technology (I3CTCON)
abstract: Contemporary supply chains function in a highly dynamic and unpredictable environment that is typified by demand volatility, geopolitics, climate events and cyber risks, as well as infrastructure collapse. Conventional centralized methods of optimization are not always flexible and cannot respond in real-time to such a complex condition to achieve resilience. This paper will present a Multi- Agent Deep Learning Framework Supply Chain Resilience (MADL-SCR), that combines distributed smart agents, deep neural structures, and cooperative learning algorithms to improve resilience, adaptability, and recovery in supply chain networks. The suggested framework represents the most important entities of the supply chain, i.e., suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and logistics hubs, as independent learning agents that can make local decisions based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and graph neural networks (GNNs). Each agent is informed about the best policies to use in inventory management, demand prediction, risk avoidance, and dynamic routing in the presence of stochastic disruptions. A federalized learning layer facilitates inter-agent interaction by allowing federation of aggregation and attention-driven exchange of information, maintaining the privacy of data, and enhancing worldwide resilience maximization. To measure the performance, the framework is tested based on simulated disruption conditions such as demand peaks, transportation delays, supplier failures and cyber-physical disturbances. Experimental outcomes show that the service level stability, time of disruption recovery, cost-effectiveness, and robustness of the network have greatly improved when using experimental results as opposed to the conventional centralized and single-agent deep learning models. This suggested MADL-SCR architecture will offer scalable, adaptable, and private next-generation resilient supply chain ecosystems.

title: Vulcan: Vision-Language-Model Enhanced Multi-Agent Cooperative Navigation for Indoor Fire-Disaster Response
authors: S. Liu; Q. Yan
venue: IEEE INFOCOM 2026 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications
abstract: Indoor fire disasters pose severe challenges to autonomous search and rescue due to dense smoke, high temperatures, and dynamically evolving indoor environments. In such time-critical scenarios, multi-agent cooperative navigation is particularly useful, as it enables faster and broader exploration than single-agent approaches. However, existing multi-agent navigation systems are primarily vision-based and designed for benign indoor settings, leading to significant performance degradation under fire-driven dynamic conditions. In this paper, we present Vulcan, a multi-agent cooperative navigation framework based on multi-modal perception and vision-language models (VLMs), tailored for indoor fire disaster response. We extend the HabitatMatterport3D benchmark by simulating physically realistic fire scenarios, including smoke diffusion, thermal hazards, and sensor degradation. We evaluate representative multi-agent cooperative navigation baselines under both normal and fire-driven environments. Our results reveal critical failure modes of existing methods in fire scenarios and underscore the necessity of robust perception and hazard-aware planning for reliable multi-agent search and rescue.

title: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Optimized Supply Chain Management Using Edge-Enabled Digital Twins
authors: D. P. Sahu; B. Rathore; R. S. Iqbal; W. Jiang; S. Prakash; V. K. Singh
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
abstract: In order to cope with the growing complexity and dynamism of contemporary supply chain management (SCM), this paper suggests a hybrid optimization model that combines Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in an Edge-Enabled Digital Twin (EEDT) setting. The framework uses GA to optimize strategic decisions globally, and MARL to adapt to changes at supply chain nodes in a decentralized manner, with the help of constant feedback provided by digital twins deployed at the edge. Experimental analysis with real-world and synthetic SCM data shows that the performance is greatly improved compared to the baseline algorithms, such as standalone GA, MARL, PSO, and ACO. In particular, the proposed model enhances fill rate by about 91%-96.5%, inventory turnover ratio by about 20% (improved by about 4.7 to 5.78), and stockout rates by as much as 4.3% (compared to higher baseline levels of more than 5.5%). Also, the transportation costs are decreased by approximately 10-15%, and the average delivery time is decreased in high traffic conditions (e.g., 78 minutes versus 83-85 minutes with the baseline methods). The framework also converges more quickly and more steadily, with a convergence rate of up to 99.8% and a better prediction accuracy with MAPE of 3.5% and a value of $R^{2}$ of nearly 0.98. These findings indicate that the suggested GA-MARL-EEDT framework offers a scalable, adaptive, and cost-effective solution to next-generation intelligent supply chain optimization.

title: CLOT: Multi-robot Motion Planning via Collaborative Optimal Transport under Signal Temporal Logic Tasks
authors: Y. Zhang; Y. Zhang; A. T. Le; M. Guo
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Multi-robot systems often need to navigate cluttered environments while performing complex tasks. To ensure collision-free trajectories among the robots and with the obstacles is essential for the overall safety, along with additional requirements such as dynamic feasibility, relative formation, connectivity maintenance and temporal tasks. Existing work mostly focuses on the design of analytical controllers that encapsulate all these constraints, which often suffer from undesired local minima due to conflicting non-convex objectives. This work proposes a novel motion planning scheme for multi-robot systems under various safety and high-level tasks, specified as signal temporal logic (STL) formulas over collective states such as collision avoidance, relative formation and connectivity maintenance. A gradient-free method called collaborative optimal transport (CLOT) is proposed that optimizes batches of system-wide smooth trajectories over highly nonlinear costs handled through the zero-order Sinkhorn Step. Via parallel computation on GPUs, the method achieves a planning time of few seconds for small teams and maintains tractability for over 100 robots. Lastly, its applicability is extensively demonstrated both in simulation and hardware, over complex environments and high-level temporal tasks.

title: XAI-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Swarm USV Continuous Multi-Target Hunting
authors: N. Hamid; H. Saleh; S. E. Ferik
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Swarm unmanned surface vehicle (USV) has become a promising solution for maritime security and defense activities. However, the complexity of continuous multi-target hunting presents significant challenges for multi-agent coordination in water environments. This study proposes an XAI-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for swarm USVs to perform continuous multi-target hunting. The framework integrates multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (basic MAPPO and MAPPO-LSTM) for cooperative hunting policies with explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms to provide interpretable insights into swarm behaviors and decision strategies. Experimental results in a 3D simulation platform environment demonstrate that MAPPO-LSTM achieves superior interception performance, reducing mean time-to-capture and improving trajectory smoothness compared to the baseline MAPPO. Furthermore, the proposed XAI pipeline combines distance-based importance attribution, influence graph analysis, strategic clustering, and temporal dynamics evaluation to explain agent contributions, inter-agent dependencies, emergent strategies, and efficiency patterns. By providing multi-level interpretability, the framework enhances transparency, trust, and deployment readiness of swarm USVs in dynamic maritime defense scenarios.

title: Enhanced Cooperative A* for Multi-Order Picking in a Multi-Agent Warehouse
authors: D. Alfiani; A. A. Nursultan; R. Mariel; I. P. D. Wibawa; A. Rusdinar; A. Z. Fuadi
venue: 2026 13th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In warehouse order picking, concurrent operation of multiple agents in shared aisles and cross-aisle junctions can introduce node and edge conflicts that compromise safety and degrade throughput. While Cooperative A⋆ (CA⋆) supports multi-agent path coordination, warehouse picking operations additionally require managing multiple concurrent orders under continuous agent traffic, a requirement not explicitly addressed by the standard formulation. This paper investigates whether a multi-agent path-finding algorithm can be extended to handle multi-order picking without sacrificing collision-awareness. A Multi-Order CA⋆ is proposed that sequentially processes an order queue with dynamic agent-order assignment and resolves conflicts through a reservation table combined with a two-stage re-planning strategy: waiting time followed by spatial rerouting through Alternative Horizontal Line (AHL). The warehouse is modeled as a costed graph where edges represent travel time under a constant agent speed of $\nu \approx 1.20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. Experiments were executed on a compact grid-based layout of 18 nodes and 27 edges, using 30 picking orders executed by three agents in a BASE-to-STAGE scenario. During the simulation, 97 potential collision events were detected and successfully resolved through reservation-based re-planning. Results show that the proposed Multi-Order CA⋆ reduces total travel distance from 814 m (A⋆) to 788 m, a 3.19% improvement, at the cost of a modest increase in median per-order runtime from 0.09 ms to 0.32 ms that remains in the millisecond range and therefore practical for multi-order execution.

title: Online-Tuning Control Barrier Function Approach for Signal Temporal Logic Tasks and Prior-Unknown Obstacle Avoidance
authors: Z. Huang; B. Zhao; X. Yin; X. Yu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
abstract: This article investigates the control problem of making an autonomous system modeled by a nonlinear input-affine system achieve signal temporal logic (STL) goal-reaching tasks and avoid prior-unknown obstacles. A novel controller is proposed, including two components: one synthesized using control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure the satisfaction of STL goal-reaching tasks, and the other derived from artificial potential fields (APFs) to avoid obstacles. Departing from the existing predesigned CBF methods, an online-tuning CBF approach is proposed to ensure the system remains within its invariant set built for achieving STL goal-reaching tasks, even when the system is navigating around prior-unknown obstacles. Moreover, the approach is demonstrated to be effective for temporal logic control synthesis in systems with input constraints. As a result, the performance of achieving the STL goal-reaching tasks is improved by the proposed CBF online-tuning algorithm, making the controller well-suited for STL control synthesis in prior-unknown environments. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated by simulations and is also demonstrated by a physical experiment on an autonomous drone.

title: Large Language Model Agents in Dynamic Mine Planning: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
authors: R. Nunes; N. Risso; M. Momayez
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The increasing availability of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven agents has introduced a new class of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems capable of processing, organizing, and interacting with heterogeneous data sources using natural language. Although these systems are being adopted across various industries, their application in mining, particularly within Dynamic Mine Planning (DMP), remains nascent. A key research gap is the limited understanding of how LLM-driven agents can support multisource data integration across geological, operational, and safety domains in DMP to support adaptive decision-making. Traditional planning pipelines are typically too static to accommodate operational variability and real-time responsiveness. To address this gap, the review is structured around five research questions: agent applications in mining, transferable architectures from related domains, adoption barriers, multi-agent opportunities for real-time decision support, and future deployment priorities. Through a PRISMA-based synthesis of 33 peer-reviewed studies across mining and adjacent engineered sectors, the review examines LLM agents within the broader landscape of AI-embedded decision-making systems, from dispatch automation and predictive maintenance to Mining 5.0 frameworks, identifying current capabilities, performance benchmarks, and methodological gaps. The analysis proposes an incremental maturity pathway, advancing from bounded advisory systems to fully integrated planning frameworks tailored to mining’s operational requirements. As mining-specific LLM-agent implementations are largely conceptual, the pathway serves as a theoretically grounded framework to guide future empirical validation in mining. The proposed pathway offers a structured, conceptual reference for phasing in LLM-driven decision support toward greater autonomy. The findings advance both academic research and industry practice by clarifying the necessary data infrastructure, hybrid architectures, safety validation mechanisms, and governance conditions for deployment in mining operations.

title: Multi-Robot Collaborative Interactive Obstacle Avoidance via Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Networks and Model Predictive Control
authors: Z. Zhang; R. Chen; H. Zhang; W. Sun; Z. Jiang
venue: 2026 18th International Conference on Advanced Computational Intelligence (ICACI)
abstract: Multi-robot interactive navigation in highly constrained and unstructured environments faces the dual challenges of high-dimensional computation and physical safety. To address the lack of strict safety guarantees in pure learning methods and the curse of dimensionality in centralized planning, this paper proposes a novel Imitation Learning-guided Hierarchical Interactive Navigation framework that decouples macroscopic scheduling from microscopic execution. The architecture consists of three layers: the top layer generates safe macroscopic preview trajectories via a cascaded planner; the mid-layer utilizes a Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Network (GNN), pre-trained offline via Expert Imitation Learning, as a distributed inference engine to output yield offsets and resolve spatial deadlocks; the bottom layer employs an optimization-based MPC controller to track the GNN-modulated reference while reducing constraint violations and improving local execution safety. Experiments in Habitat-Sim show that the proposed framework achieves an 80.0% task success rate and reduces the deadlock rate to 13.0% over 100 randomized constrained-navigation episodes, while still exhibiting a 7.0% collision rate in highly constrained cases.

title: Smart Logistic System: A Multidisciplinary Integrated System for Driving Safety and Transportation Management
authors: H. S. Mogahed; A. H. Mohamed; M. A. Ali
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: The logistics and transportation industry faces several critical challenges, including the absence of real-time vehicle data, inadequate safety measures, and inefficient resource management. This paper presents the Smart Logistic System (SLS), a unified intelligent transportation architecture that integrates embedded systems, Augmented Reality (AR), Machine Learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), and digital-twin technology within a single operational framework, rather than as independent subsystems. The system continuously monitors key vehicle parameters — location, speed, fuel consumption, and engine performance — to support proactive maintenance and minimize downtime. An edge-deployable driver-behavior-monitoring module employs computer vision and a lightweight MobileNetV3-Small classifier to detect drowsiness, distraction, and other hazardous behaviors in real time. Special-needs support includes seizure detection, GPS-based wandering alerts, and AR-guided vehicle-operation assistance. A route-optimization module formulates logistics planning as a constrained, multi-objective vehicle routing problem that jointly considers transportation cost, travel time, and estimated carbon emissions, while a digital-twin layer maintains a continuously synchronized virtual representation of fleet state to support fleet-manager decision-making. A mobile application delivers real-time data, alerts, and navigation to drivers; a desktop application allows managers to decode raw Controller Area Network (CAN) data; and a cloud platform provides secure storage, synchronization, and visualization. On a held-out benchmark, the driver-behavior-monitoring module achieves accuracy and inference-latency performance competitive with, and in several respects exceeding, recent state-of-the-art driver-monitoring methods; the route-optimization, predictive-maintenance, and digital-twin modules are validated through architectural and feasibility analysis rather than large-scale benchmarking. Taken together, these results indicate that SLS’s principal contribution is the integration of safety monitoring, logistics optimization, predictive maintenance, digital-twin synchronization, and accessibility features within a single operational architecture — a step toward more secure, efficient, and inclusive logistics and transportation systems.

title: Decentralized End-to-End Multi-AAV Pursuit Using Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation via Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Y. Li; Z. Zhou; H. Li; Y. Sun; Y. Wu; Y. Lai; Y. Wang; Y. Gong; J. Mei
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Decentralized cooperative pursuit in cluttered environments is challenging for autonomous aerial swarms, especially under partial and noisy perception. Existing methods often rely on abstracted geometric features or privileged ground-truth states, and therefore sidestep perceptual uncertainty in real-world settings. We propose a decentralized end-to-end multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that maps raw LiDAR observations directly to continuous control commands. Central to the framework is the Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation (PSTO), an egocentric grid representation that aligns obstacle geometry with predictive adversarial intent and teammate motion in a unified, fixed-resolution projection. Built on PSTO, a single decentralized policy enables agents to navigate static obstacles, intercept dynamic targets, and maintain cooperative encirclement. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior capture efficiency and competitive success rates compared to state-of-the-art learning-based approaches relying on privileged obstacle information. Furthermore, the unified policy scales seamlessly across different team sizes without retraining. Finally, fully autonomous outdoor experiments validate the framework on a quadrotor swarm relying on only onboard sensing and computing.

title: Multi-Robot Communication and Surveillance System Using Raspberry Pi and MQTT
authors: M. Thombare; P. Jadhav
venue: 2026 IEEE Global Symposium on Emerging and Communication Technologies (GSEACT)
abstract: This paper presents an IoT-based multi-robot hazard detection and surveillance system built on Raspberry Pi 4 single-board computers and the MQTT publish-subscribe messaging protocol. Three autonomous robotic units collaborate to monitor environmental hazards, elect a coordinating leader upon detection, and execute a synchronized response that includes audible alerting, photographic documentation, GPS geo-tagging, and SMTP email notification. Each robot integrates an MQ-2 combustible gas sensor, an inductive metal detector module, a NEO-6M GPS receiver, and a Pi Camera v2. Interrobot coordination is achieved through a Mosquito MQTT broker using a First-Come-First-Serve leader election algorithm that assigns incident command to whichever robot first exceeds a detection threshold. Non-leader robots acknowledge the event and autonomously navigate toward the reported coordinates to establish a multi-point monitoring perimeter. Experimental evaluation in a controlled $5 ~\mathrm{m} \times 5 ~\mathrm{m}$ environment conducted over 30 repeated trials confirms hazard detection response times below 2 seconds, QoS 1 MQTT latency of 41 ms mean, gas detection accuracy of 97%, metal detection accuracy of 99%, and uninterrupted operation over a 72-hour continuous reliability trial. The proposed decentralized architecture demonstrably outperforms conventional single-robot and centralized multirobot platforms in coverage, fault tolerance, scalability, and alert richness, while the per-robot bill of materials of approximately INR 7,755 makes it economically viable for industrial safety, military surveillance, and disaster response deployments.

title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning for Dynamic Target Search: An LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
authors: Y. Liu; X. Li; X. Jiang; H. Liu; J. Yang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
abstract: Deploying Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for dynamic target search in disaster response scenarios can reduce losses. This paper investigates multi-UAV cooperative trajectory planning for dynamic target search in a three-dimensional environment with static obstacles, aiming to maximize the number of searched targets and minimize the average uncertainty of the search area, while ensuring collision avoidance between UAVs and obstacles. Existing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) based methods face the sparse reward problem in dynamic target search, which hinders planning feasible multi-UAV trajectories. Notably, Large Language Models (LLMs), with extensive pre-trained knowledge and powerful semantic reasoning capabilities, exhibit potential for designing high-quality reward functions to alleviate the sparse reward problem. Therefore, we propose an LLM-guided Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (LLM-MAPPO) algorithm, which leverages LLMs’ reasoning capabilities to guide MARL policy learning and plans multi-UAV trajectories for efficient dynamic target search. Specifically, we design an offline LLM reward shaping scheme that generates dense reward signals to mitigate the sparse reward problem. Moreover, we propose a dual-mode pheromone-based search mechanism to guide UAVs to respond promptly to changes in target positions. Experimental results demonstrate that LLM-MAPPO significantly outperforms compared algorithms in terms of the number of searched targets and average area uncertainty, while successfully avoiding collisions. In particular, LLM-MAPPO reduces the target search time by 71.4%.

title: Expert Guided Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Scheduling of Warehouse AGVS
authors: X. Liu; J. Zhang; H. Li; T. Sui
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Algorithms (CAIBDA)
abstract: Coordinated AGV scheduling in RMFS strictly requires balancing collision-free navigation with low computational latency. While expert-planning ensures safety but suffers severe delays, standard MARL enables fast inference but lacks low-level safety guarantees and struggles with early convergence. To address this, we propose AG-MAPPO, an expert-guided multi-agent framework. During training, a Virtual Serial A* (VSP-A*) algorithm serves as an expert to generate safe path demonstrations via hybrid action sampling. This mitigates the cold-start problem without extensive parameter tuning and significantly accelerates convergence. At runtime, our system adopts stepwise planning. This eliminates the prohibitive cost of planning complete paths for all robots upfront, decomposing the problem into simple single-step local decisions. By dynamically updating robot decision order at each step, the method prevents deadlocks and maintains per-step latency of only a few milliseconds. Our work presents a practical distributed scheduling approach that balances training ease, fast response, and safety guarantees.

title: UAVBench: An Open Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous and Agentic AI UAV Systems via LLM-Generated Flight Scenarios
authors: M. A. Ferrag; A. Lakas; M. Debbah
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
abstract: Autonomous aerial systems increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) for mission planning, perception, and decision-making; yet, the lack of standardized, physically grounded benchmarks limits systematic evaluation of their reasoning capabilities. To address this gap, we introduce UAVBench, an open benchmark dataset comprising 50,000 validated UAV flight scenarios generated through taxonomy-guided LLM prompting and multi-stage safety validation. Each scenario is encoded in a structured JSON schema encompassing mission objectives, vehicle configuration, environmental conditions, and quantitative risk labels, providing a unified representation of UAV operations across diverse domains. Building on this foundation, we present UAVBench_MCQ, a reasoning-oriented extension containing 50,000 multiple-choice questions spanning ten cognitive and ethical reasoning styles—from aerodynamics and navigation to multi-agent coordination and hybrid integrated reasoning. This framework enables interpretable, machine-checkable assessment of UAV-specific cognition under realistic operational contexts. We evaluate 32 state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-5, ChatGPT 4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, DeepSeek V3, Qwen3 235B, and ERNIE 4.5 300B, and find strong performance in perception and policy reasoning but persistent challenges in ethics-aware and resource-constrained decision-making. UAVBench establishes a reproducible, physically grounded foundation for benchmarking agentic AI in autonomous aerial systems and advancing next-generation UAV reasoning intelligence.

title: A Joint Flow Scheduling Scheme for the Uplink of 5G-TSN in Industrial Internet of Things Systems
authors: J. Zhao; T. Wang; H. Tong; N. Yang; C. Yin; D. Niyato
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
abstract: As a crucial enabler for the wireless upgrade of the industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the integration of fifth-generation (5G) wireless network and the wired time-sensitive networking (TSN), i.e., 5G-TSN, is expected to support the deterministic transmission of massive data flows in IIoT systems. Therefore, we focus on the design of a joint flow scheduling scheme for the uplink of 5G-TSN. Specifically, in the 5G part, we propose a novel multiple configured grant (MCG) subframe structure to efficiently exploit the available spectrum resources. Meanwhile, in the TSN part, the age of synchronization (AoS) indicator, which measures the freshness of each flow arriving at the transparent bridge connecting 5G and TSN, determines which flow should be injected into the TSN. Then, to support massive device access, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the number of successfully transmitted flows while satisfying the quality of service requirements. To solve the non-stationary and non-convex problem, we propose a cooperative multi-agent proximal policy optimization (CMA-PPO) based flow scheduling scheme to determine the MCG configuration with cognitive information of flows. The scheme can improve the number of successfully transmitted flows within the deadline constraints. Extensive numerical simulations demonstrate that, compared with benchmarks, the proposed scheme improves the number of successfully transmitted flows by up to 24.02% and about two times compared with the benchmarks in the 5G-TSN network.

title: Distributed Robust Dispatch for Networked Microgrids With Coalition Game-Guided Multiagent Adversarial Safe Reinforcement Learning
authors: T. Pu; S. Du; L. Dong; J. Qiao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: The integration of distributed energy resources introduces demand-side flexibility and uncertainty, challenging dispatch of networked microgrids (MGs). This article proposes a coalition game-guided multiagent adversarial safe reinforcement learning (SRL) method to achieve distributed robust dispatch under privacy protection. Leveraging SRL for rapid decision-making with safety guarantees, we further overcome the reliance on predefined source-load distributions inherent in existing SRL approaches. Specifically, we employ the Wasserstein generative adversarial network to assume additional distributional information on source and load transition probabilities. This unique design for MG dispatch enhances decision robustness under source-load fluctuations compared to existing adversarial training, which gives adversary the same action space as the protagonist. To ensure privacy-preserving multiagent training, we construct a coalition game-guided training framework. This framework adjusts protagonists’ rewards based on game theory to ensure global convergence only with MGs’ boundary power, and uses Hash-based message authentication code to guarantee data integrity. Unlike existing multiagent reinforcement learning methods relying on global critic, our method avoids sharing privacy-sensitive local states and actions. Simulations on a modified IEEE-123 bus system and an actual power grid-derived test system validate the effectiveness.

title: Human Factors in Freight Transport: A Mixed-Methods Approach to Driver Risk Identification
authors: P. A. Fernando; D. Kosgoda; P. T. R. S. Sugathadasa
venue: 2026 Moratuwa Engineering Research Conference (MERCon)
abstract: This study investigates hazardous driving behaviours among commercial truck drivers, the associated behavioural drivers, and their relative influence on driving risk. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining structured literature review, expert interviews, and structured surveys administered to commercial truck drivers. The dataset comprised responses from 62 truck drivers and 24 industry professionals. The collected data were analysed to evaluate the influence of behavioural drivers, the likelihood and severity of risky driving behaviours, the availability of threshold values and technological add-ons, and the key challenges faced by truck drivers. Based on these findings, conceptual frameworks were developed to support the identification and mitigation of transport-related hazards from both organizational and individual perspectives. The results indicate that driving experience, organizational safety guidelines, and prior accident involvement exert the strongest influence. Among the identified behaviours, distracted driving, slow driving in inappropriate lanes, and fatigued driving were found to be the most frequently reported.

title: Multi-agent risk-aware constrained learning for network parameter optimization
authors: A. L. Forsberg; A. Nikou; A. Vulgarakis; J. Tumova
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: Mobile networks face increasing demands for throughput in highly dynamic and stochastic environments, posing significant challenges for effective parameter optimization. Traditional methods relying on precise dynamics models struggle to adapt to uncertainties, while existing reinforcement learning approaches often fail to balance safety and performance under constraints. In this work, we introduce a novel risk-aware constrained multi-agent RL framework, specifically applied to the Remote Electrical Tilt problem in mobile networks. Our method leverages a risk-aware critic based on risk metrics, enabling a dynamic trade-off between worst-case and expectation-based constraint satisfaction. By allowing fine-grained control over risk tolerance, the framework addresses the practical need to adapt policies to varying operational conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves robust network optimization, ensuring safety through action filtering while maintaining high performance. This work provides a scalable foundation for constrained RL in dynamic, multi-agent environments, with potential applications beyond mobile networks, such as autonomous systems and energy grids. Additionally, we present an ablation study illustrating how action filtering enhances safety in uncertain scenarios.

title: CoLMIN: LLM-based Multi-Decision Path Negotiation for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
authors: Z. Huang; Z. Fan; S. Wang; W. Wu; X. Zhao; M. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
abstract: Multi-vehicle cooperative autonomous driving enhances the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems through information sharing among connected vehicles, demonstrating significant potential for improving traffic safety. LLM-based approaches leverage strong reasoning capabilities of LLMs to enable effective inter-vehicle negotiation and improve cooperative driving performance. However, driving decisions in complex traffic scenarios are inherently multi-solution in nature. As a result, existing negotiation-based methods often converge prematurely to suboptimal solutions, hindering consensus formation and limiting the practical deployment of cooperative autonomous driving systems. To address this challenge, we propose CoLMIN, the LLM-based multi-decision path negotiation framework for cooperative autonomous driving, achieving stable decision consensus through multi-decision path negotiation and reflective reasoning. To achieve stable and high-quality consensus in cooperative autonomous driving, CoLMIN consists of three key components: (i) an LLM-based Multi-Intent Negotiation module (LMin), which adopts a Negotiator-Evaluator paradigm and generates multiple candidate driving intentions for joint evaluation, (ii) an Evaluation-based Shallow Reflection Module (ESRM), which analyzes negotiation outcomes and provides feedback to guide subsequent negotiations, thereby accelerating consensus formation; and (iii) an LLM-based Deep Reflection Module (LDRM) that performs long-term reflection over negotiation histories to mitigate cognitive fixation and prevent the system from converging to suboptimal solutions. Experimental results in CARLA simulation environment demonstrate that CoLMIN significantly outperforms existing methods in challenging interactive driving scenarios.

title: Multimodal Generative AI in the Enterprise: From Pixels to Profit: A Practitioner's Guide to Building Image, Audio, and Video Generation Applications
authors: M. Tschochohei; F. Schenker
venue: Multimodal Generative AI in the Enterprise: From Pixels to Profit: A Practitioner's Guide to Building Image, Audio, and Video Generation Applications
abstract: Build and deploy enterprise-grade multimodal AI systems using generative models for text, image, audio, and video.Key FeaturesDesign end-to-end multimodal AI systems for enterprise workloadsBuild scalable pipelines using Gemini, Veo, Imagen, Airflow, and KubeflowImplement governance, safety, and compliance for AI-generated contentPurchase of the print or Kindle book includes a free PDF eBookBook DescriptionThe Multimodal AI Playbook equips enterprise developers and ML engineers with the practical skills needed to build real-world generative systems using text, image, audio, and video models. This book offers a complete stack approach—starting from theory and progressing through tooling, orchestration, governance, and full-scale deployment. Beginning with the foundations of multimodal learning and generative AI models, you’ll explore how to generate modality-specific content while navigating key trade-offs in model selection, scalability, and orchestration. With a dedicated focus on enterprise use cases like automated marketing campaigns, the book shows how to manage model outputs responsibly covering bias detection, IP risk, and content safety. You'll implement a full pipeline using enterprise-ready models such as Gemini, Veo, and Imagen. With forward-looking chapters on real-time generation, 3D assets, and multimodal agents, this book bridges the gap between technical mastery and business impact- preparing you to lead in the AI-first future. title: Accommodation of Severe Faults During Multi-Robot Transportation
authors: C. Wang; D. Constantinescu
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA)
abstract: This paper proposes a planning and control framework that aims to ensure that a multi-robot system supporting an object from below carries it to a target destination despite several robots severely malfunctioning during task execution. The framework proposes a measure of balance stability for the object which serves to identify optimal formations for the healthy robots initially and when some robots suffer severe faults. It then assigns the healthy robots to positions in the new formation based on the Hungarian algorithm. Controls derived from an Improved Artificial Potential Field (IAPF) drive the robots to their positions in the new formation and a strategy for selecting temporary targets helps them escape the local minima of the IAPF during repositioning. Treating the entire system as a rigid body whose steering wheels are the healthy robots lets the IAPF and the temporary target selection strategies steer the system towards the target destination while avoiding collisions with the severely faulty robots. A MATLAB simulation illustrates the feasibility of the proposed framework.

title: LLM-Driven Heterogeneous Multi-Agent for Automatic Generation of Railway CTC Test Cases
authors: Y. Jiao; Z. Li; F. Gao; W. Xu
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The Centralized Traffic Control (CTC) system is an important part of railway operations. The testing of CTC is critical to ensuring safety and stability. High-quality test cases are key to testing. Currently, CTC test cases are mainly written manually, resulting in low efficiency, long development cycles and incomplete coverage. This fails to meet the needs of complex testing. To address these issues, this paper presents an automatic CTC test case generation approach based on an LLM-driven heterogeneous multi-agent system. The testing process is allocated to four agents: Demand Analysis, Test Strategy, Case Generation and Quality Assessment. An AI programming agent acts as the leader, and all subordinate agents are connected to large language models (LLMs) to perform respective tasks. This work also developed an AI dialogue tool for test case generation. Experiments show that the tool based on the proposed method can generate standard and complete test cases. Compared with manual work, this method enhances efficiency and the accuracy of test cases, reduces costs and improves testing capacity for the engineering application of railway CTC systems.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Pathfinding for Multiple UAVs Facing Abrupt Hazardous Areas
authors: Q. Wu; L. Chen; K. Liu; J. Lü
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Planning feasible paths for multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) amidst abrupt hazardous areas is a critical safety challenge, where existing methods often lack safety guarantees and uncertainty handling. To address this, we propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach for the UAV pathfinding problem. Our method ensures rapid responsiveness and adherence to safety constraints through the integration of a control barrier function, guaranteeing safe replanning even during sudden route changes. To overcome the potential inefficiency of purely reactive safety, we introduce a probabilistic neural network that quantifies hazard uncertainty, enhancing the anticipation of sudden dangers. Finally, to utilize swarm intelligence for mutual risk avoidance, the approach incorporates neighbors’ observations using a proximity-weighted mean-field mechanism, allowing each UAV to consider the impact of this aggregated information in its planning. Extensive simulations show that our method achieves a planning success rate surpassing 90% in transient environments, outperforming traditional planners and other MARL baselines. Real-world experiments further validate the approach’s adaptability, demonstrating its practical value for safety-critical missions. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by the safety-critical challenge of navigating UAV swarms through environments with abrupt, unpredictable hazards. Traditional planners often suffer from high computational latency during sudden changes, while standard learning-based methods typically lack rigorous safety guarantees. To address this, we present a decentralized pathfinding framework that integrates probabilistic uncertainty handling with a control barrier function. For implementation, the proposed system is lightweight enough for standard onboard embedded computers, enabling autonomous execution without centralized control. Experimental results indicate that the average computation time per step is less than 5 ms, leaving ample computational resources for other onboard tasks like state estimation and visual processing. This approach is particularly applicable to time-sensitive missions like disaster response, offering a solution that remains robust even under conditions of communication instability or sensor noise.

title: Containing the Cascade: A Benchmark and Reference Mediator for Failure Propagation in Tool-Using LLM Multi-Agent Systems
authors: V. R. Divi; S. Gullapalli; B. A. Brahmandam
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Electronics Representation and Algorithm (ICERA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MAS) increasingly automate multi-step, tool-using workflows, yet they fail far more often than their single-agent counterparts. Recent diagnostic studies attribute these failures to cascades: a single agent’s hallucination, malformed tool call, or role drift propagates through the agent graph and corrupts the final output. The community has so far concentrated on diagnosing such failures after the fact; there is no standard, reproducible benchmark for measuring whether a system can contain a cascade as it unfolds. We address this gap with three contributions. First, we introduce a taxonomy of six recurring cascading-failure modes and a suite of containment metrics—containment rate, cascade depth, blast radius, and mean time-to-detection—that quantify propagation rather than only end-task success. Second, we present Cascade-Bench, a controlled fault-injection testbed of 1080 scenarios across six task domains, instantiated on a discrete-event simulation of agent message passing that is calibrated to reported MAS failure statistics. Third, we propose Sentinel, a lightweight reference mediator that combines typed inter-agent message contracts, a semantic anomaly gate, a circuit breaker, and checkpoint-based recovery. Across 48 system configurations and over 590000 simulated task executions, Sentinel raises task success from 31.3% to 83.7% and containment from 46.2% to 99.4%, while holding cascade depth nearly constant as the system scales from 3 to 12 agents—where the unguarded depth nearly doubles. An ablation cleanly separates a fail-safe role (the circuit breaker, which governs containment) from a fail-operational role (checkpoint rollback, which governs task completion). We release Cascade-Bench and Sentinel as an open baseline for reliability research on tool-using MAS.

title: Behavioural Analysis of Heterogeneous Agents in Decentralized Multi-Agent Route Optimization
authors: P. D; D. K V; P. V; S. S. B A; L. Kandasamy
venue: 2026 Third International Conference on Innovations in Cybersecurity and Data Science (ICICDS)
abstract: Recent advances in reinforcement learning enable automated agents to improve their decision-making strategies through interaction with dynamic environments. Nonetheless independent learners in decentralized multi-agent systems operating within the same environment often grapple with issues, that includes non-stationary learning dynamics, volatility, partial observability, and communication overhead. These challenges undermine learning efficiency and reliability, especially in route optimization. Multiple existing multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches rely on centralized or cooperative learning configurations. Although these methods are effective in controlled environments, they are often unsuitable for decentralized and resourceconstrained systems because of high computational requirements and substantial inter-agent communication requirements. This highlights the need to investigate independent learning approaches and to better understand how heterogeneous agent behaviours affect learning stability under decentralized environment. This paper presents a behavioural analysis of heterogeneous independent reinforcement learning agents operating in a shared grid-based environment. Three independent agents with distinct behavioural characteristics are analysed over more than 300 training episodes under different circumstances of partial observability, full observability, and shared reward settings. The agents consist of a random-exploration agent (Speed), a deterministic-policy agent (Safe), and a stochastic-policy agent (Efficient). They are assessed based on cumulative reward patterns, learning fluctuations, convergence behaviour, and collision frequencies. The empirical findings indicate that the stochastic-policy agent demonstrates superior learning stability and lower reward variance compared with both the random-exploration and deterministic-policy agents. These findings highlights that stochastic-policy agents achieve superior learning stability and lower reward variance than the other agents in decentralized multi-agent learning environment, underscoring the critical role of behavioural heterogeneity in route optimization.

title: Cross Layer Resilient Control of 5G-Enabled Mobile Robots
authors: J. Huang; Z. Yan; J. He; H. Zheng; Y. Wang
venue: 2026 41st Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Industrial warehouses present hostile radio environments for dense AGV fleets, where metallic racking causes severe multipath fading and shadowing. These conditions frequently destabilize coordination, driving systems into stagnation when control logic ignores channel volatility. To bridge communication reliability and motion planning, this work formulates fleet coordination as a channel-aware Networked Control System. Central to this framework is a composite link-quality metric, Q, which fuses RSSI, latency, and packet reliability. We implement a hierarchical architecture where a primary layer performs preemptive adaptation by dynamically scaling update frequencies and safety margins based on Q, while a supervisory module acts as a fail-safe for persistent deadlocks. Validation on a private 5G testbed confirms Q accurately tracks spatial volatility. Furthermore, large-scale trace-driven stress tests reveal that while fixed-rate baselines succumb to gridlocks under high load, our channel-aware approach sustains liveness. Results show it improves throughput by approximately 60% and reduces stagnation duration by 57% compared to reservation-based baselines by aligning agent dynamics with instantaneous network capacity.

title: Behaviour-Aware Adaptive Path Planning With Q-Learning Weight Adaptation
authors: J. Zhang; M. Yang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: This article proposes a dynamic path cost modelling framework that integrates fuzzy C-means clustering, association rule mining, and a Q-learning-based weight adaptation mechanism to achieve multi-objective collaborative path planning based on active perception of obstacle behaviour patterns. The method constructs an obstacle behaviour pattern library from multimodal perception, mines context-dependent mappings between environment features and the weights of three cost terms, namely energy, safety margin, and path smoothness, and uses Q-learning to adjust these weights online. The planner is embedded in a two-layer navigation scheme, where an improved artificial potential field, APF, generates a global reference path and a dynamic window approach, DWA, local planner executes it under dynamic obstacles. Experiments on the ROS/Gazebo platform with TurtleBot3 in environments containing up to 25 obstacles per 100 m2 show that the proposed adaptive planner maintains a success rate of about 80% in high-density scenes, improving over classical APF by 30% and DWA by 55%, and remaining comparable to the deep reinforcement learning baseline TD3 at 82%.
