Following CADRE’s upcoming deployment on the Lunar surface, CRESCENT will be the first nonlinear optimization-based trajectory optimization approach used on another celestial body.

title: AIDR-Cloud: An Agentic AI—Driven Incident Response Framework for Cloud Failures
authors: A. Pratinav; A. Kataria
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: Modern cloud-native systems comprise hundreds of microservices, multi-region deployments, and streaming data pipelines. This complexity has dramatically increased the frequency, impact, and opacity of operational failures. Traditional incident response, which is built around manual troubleshooting, static rules, and prewritten runbooks, struggles to meet today's latency and reliability requirements. This paper presents AIDR-Cloud, an agentic AI-driven incident detection and response framework that combines real-time telemetry, a domain-specific cloud knowledge graph, and multi-agent large language model (LLM) reasoning to autonomously diagnose [11] and remediate failures in cloud environments. AIDR-Cloud introduces a three-layer architecture: a Perception Layer that continuously ingests metrics, logs and traces; a Cognition Layer composed of specialized LLM agents that perform hypothesis generation, validation and remediation planning over a knowledge graph of cloud resources and dependencies; and an Action Layer that executes guarded remediation operations via Kubernetes and cloud-provider APIs under a safety and governance framework. We evaluate AIDR-Cloud along three complementary axes. First, in controlled fault-injection experiments on multi-region Kubernetes and Kafka workloads, we compare AIDR-Cloud against experienced human operators using standard observability and runbook tooling. Second, we analyze the cost and latency overheads of AIDR-Cloud by decomposing end-to-end response time into perception, cognition and action components, and by estimating LLM token usage, control-plane calls and infrastructure cost as a function of incident rate. Third, we report outcomes from a multi-week deployment of AIDR-Cloud on real production incidents, including changes in MTTR and escalation behavior, as well as qualitative improvements in postmortem quality and runbook evolution. Across both synthetic and real incidents, AIDR-Cloud reduces MTTR relative to the human baseline, achieves faster root-cause analysis, reduces the rate of human escalation, and selects correct remediation actions in a large fraction of cases, while adding only a small amount of reasoning latency and no unsafe actions due to strict guardrails. These results show that agentic AI can act as a statistically well-characterized and cost-conscious SRE co-pilot, significantly improving reliability and operational efficiency in complex cloud systems.

title: Guardrailing LLM and Agentic Decisions for 6G AI-RAN
authors: Y. Tang; M. Zou; W. Guo; S. A. R. Zaidi
venue: 2026 IEEE 23rd Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are envisioned as cornerstones for autonomous, zero-touch 6G AI-RAN operations. Numerous frameworks adopt LLM-based agents as decision-makers to optimize network configurations, orchestrate resources, and interact with users and connected use cases. However, intrinsic limitations (hallucinations, misaligned human values) and extrinsic adversarial threats (jail-breaks, prompt injections) pose critical risks to network safety, reliability, and privacy—challenges largely overlooked in existing literature. This paper addresses this gap by reviewing state-of-the-art guardrail techniques for 6G AI-RAN. We categorize guardrails across model-level and agent-level layers and map them to common agent application patterns in 6G networks, providing practical foundations for designing trustworthy agentic decision-making frameworks in future 6G AI-RAN systems.

title: Integrated Decision Making and Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Driving Under Multimodal Uncertainties: A Bayesian Game Approach
authors: Z. Huang; T. Li; S. Shen; J. Ma
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: Modeling the interaction between traffic agents is a key issue in designing safe and non-conservative maneuvers in autonomous driving. This problem can be challenging when multi-modality and behavioral uncertainties are engaged. Existing methods either fail to plan interactively or consider unimodal behaviors that could lead to catastrophic results. In this paper, we introduce an integrated decision-making and trajectory planning framework based on a Bayesian game (i.e., a game of incomplete information). Human decisions inherently exhibit discrete characteristics and, therefore, are modeled as types of players in the game. A general solver based on no-regret learning is introduced to obtain a corresponding Bayesian Coarse Correlated Equilibrium, which captures the interaction between traffic agents in the multimodal context. With the attained equilibrium, decision-making and trajectory planning are performed simultaneously, and the resulting interactive strategy is shown to be optimal over the expectation of rivals' driving intentions. Closed-loop simulations on different traffic scenarios are performed to illustrate the generalizability and the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Multi-Agent Path Planning in Complex Multi-Obstacle Environment: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Formation Containment Method
authors: T. Li; H. Shi; P. Zhu; Z. Ma; Y. Zhou; L. Shi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper addresses the multi-agent path planning (MAPP) problem for heterogeneous systems where only a subset of agents, termed leaders, can perceive obstacles. A novel hierarchical framework is proposed, which decouples high-level path planning from low-level path execution. At the high level, a Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic (MASAC) algorithm trains the leaders to collectively navigate and dynamically shape an obstacle-free “safe mobile corridor”. At the low level, a distributed consensus-based controller guides the sensor-less followers to remain within this moving corridor, effectively tracking the path planned by the leaders. This architecture significantly enhances sample efficiency and scalability while naturally supporting low-cost, heterogeneous agents. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and experiments on a physical multi-UAV platform. Note to Practitioners—For industrial applications such as autonomous logistics, warehouse automation, and aerial surveillance, deploying large-scale robot swarms faces significant challenges regarding hardware costs and real-time communication latency. This paper addresses these practical constraints by demonstrating a scalable hierarchical control strategy. The results suggest that for complex obstacle environments, it is feasible and cost-effective to deploy a heterogeneous team where only a few “leader” agents possess expensive sensing and computing capabilities, while the majority are low-cost, sensor-less units. Furthermore, the work provides a practical solution for compensating for system delays during agile maneuvers. This approach offers engineers a viable path to scale up multi-robot fleets without linearly increasing hardware costs or sacrificing safety.

title: Quantum-Neuromorphic Hybrid Architecture for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination in Distributed Healthcare Networks
authors: M. Chandrasekaran
venue: 2026 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference Workshops (WCNCW)
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid quantum-neuromorphic computing architecture for multi-agent wireless healthcare networks that must meet strict energy, latency, and reliability requirements. My approach separates global optimization from real-time execution by combining Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) for system-wide coordination with Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) running on neuromorphic hardware for ultra-low-power local decision making. To reduce communication overhead, I propose a Quantum-inspired Spike-Timing Protocol (QSTP), which converts a quantum-derived correlation structure into spike-timing patterns that enable event-driven coordination with minimal beaconing. I implemented a VQC-based multi-agent resource allocation method (QC-MARA) and deployed policy execution using STDP-enabled spiking agents. Across a 12-agent Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) under interference and mobility, the proposed system achieves a 78% energy reduction compared with classical deep reinforcement learning while maintaining sub-50 ms end-toend latency and $99.9 {\%}+$ packet delivery reliability, supporting safety-critical medical monitoring and long-term operation.

title: Guaranteed-Performance Formation Control for Multi-USV Systems with Collision Avoidance and Connectivity Preservation
authors: J. Guo; G. Liu; H. Liang; P. Du
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: With the rapid development of unmanned surface vessel (USV) technology, multi-USV systems are increasingly deployed across various domains. However, in complex marine environments, ensuring connectivity maintenance, collision avoidance, and transient-steady state performance poses critical challenges for USVs formation control. To address these challenges, an artificial potential field-based approach is developed to guarantee that neighboring USVs maintain communication connectivity and avoid collisions. Additionally, an improved predefined-time prescribed performance control (PTPPC) approach is proposed to satisfy the prescribed transient-steady state performance. It automatically adjusts the initial value of the performance function according to the initial value of the formation error to eliminate the feasibility condition and avoid the invalidation of the performance function when the initial error is zero. Subsequently, a novel error transformation mechanism is introduced into the PTPPC approach to enhance the error convergence precision. With the help of Lyapunov stability theory, the control objective is achieved. Finally, a simulation example is provided to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Continuous Symbol Emergence via Decentralized Bayesian Inference With Gaussian Processes
authors: Z. You; I. Saito; M. Nagano; T. Nakamura; A. Taniguchi; T. Taniguchi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
abstract: Real-world communicative signals—such as gestures, vocalizations, and facial expressions—are inherently continuous and subtle. Research on emergent communication has been advanced as a constructive approach to elucidate the emergence of symbol systems enabling communication among agents through interactions mediated by physical signals, namely, signs. However, research on emergent communication using decentralized Bayesian inference has predominantly relied on discrete symbolic representations, struggling to capture inherent subtleties. To address this limitation, we propose a probabilistic framework called multimodal Gaussian process (GP) emergent communication (MGPEmCom), which enables the emergence of continuous symbols among decentralized agents. This framework integrates GP latent variable models (GPLVMs) to describe multimodal sensory observations and employs the Metropolis–Hastings naming game (MHNG) for decentralized inference, allowing agents to jointly infer shared continuous signs without accessing one another’s internal states. We validate our approach with a referential game task in which a speaker uses an emergent continuous symbol to communicate a target object to a listener. Experimental results demonstrate that MGPEmCom outperforms existing methods, including Inter-MDM and VAE + REINFORCE, particularly in scenarios that require fine-grained distinctions and generalization to unknown objects. These results indicate that our method enables more expressive and generalizable symbol emergence. This work establishes a principled Bayesian approach to decentralized symbol emergence using continuous latent representations, offering a foundation for modeling communication applicable to unknown objects.

title: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Security
authors: X. Zhang; X. Lu; Y. Bu; L. Fang
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Computer and Communication Systems (ICCCS)
abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been widely used in wireless security such as data encryption and authentication, in which each wireless device shares its observed network security status as observations to improve the security policy optimization efficiency. However, the shared observation information during transmission may be wiretapped by inference attackers that can infer the observation from which specific devices, resulting in privacy leakage. In this paper, we propose a privacy-preserving MARL framework for wireless security against a designed attacker who can tamper observations and impersonate legitimate devices to broadcast falsified observations, with a stronger attack ability than typical inference attackers. Therefore, we design an optimized unary encoding (OUE)-based lightweight privacy mechanism for each wireless device to perturb observations before being transmitted to neighboring devices to balance data utility and privacy protection. By incorporating the underlying network status and the perturbed observations shared by other devices, each device owns a policy network that determines the privacy budget used in OUE and the corresponding security policies to maintain security performance as well as prevent privacy leakage against inference attacks. A case study in a multi-agent cargo transportation secure transmission scenario is performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the framework against a decision tree-based inference attacker. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces the attack success rate compared with existing benchmarks.

title: Adaptive Swarm Intelligence with Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Drone-Robot Coordination in Large-Scale Regenerative Agriculture
authors: K. R. Chaganti; P. Rajyalakshmi; K. R. Goud; N. Vasudha; N. Yadagiri; P. Kulkarni
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: To enable regenerative agriculture at scale, we need intelligent, sustainable and autonomous field management systems for monitoring crop conditions, maintaining soil health, reducing chemical dependency and IMPROVING resource efficiency. Traditional precision agriculture solutions rely on stand-alone drones, fixed sensors or manually supervised ground robots, which limit scalability and flexibility in changing farm conditions. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes an Adaptive Swarm Intelligence with Deep Reinforcement Learning (ASI-DRL) framework for the autonomous drone-robot coordination in large-scale regenerative agriculture. The proposed framework comprises unmanned aerial vehicles for aerial sensing and crop-risk mapping, unmanned ground vehicles for localized field intervention, adaptive swarm intelligence for cooperative movement and task allocation, and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making. We adopt a centralized-training, decentralized-execution approach where agents learn cooperative policies using global farm information in training, but operate independently using local observations in execution. The components of the regenerative reward function are derived considering the field coverage, crop-health improvement, soil health preservation, weed density reduction, energy efficiency, collision avoidance, communication cost, and soil-compaction minimization. The simulation results show that the proposed ASI-DRL framework outperforms rule-based coordination, PSO-based swarm coordination, single-agent DRL, and MADDPG. The proposed model achieved 94.6% field coverage, 29.8 kWh energy usage, 94.1% intervention accuracy, 1.2% collision rate and 91.3 regenerative sustainability score. These results show that the proposed ASI-DRL framework is capable of providing an effective, scalable and sustainability-driven solution for the next-generation autonomous regenerative agriculture.

title: Distributed Safety Critical Control among Uncontrollable Agents Using Reconstructed Control Barrier Functions
authors: Y. Peng; W. Wang; J. Yan; M. Yu
venue: 2026 European Control Conference (ECC)
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed safety critical control for multi-agent systems (MASs) in the presence of uncontrollable agents with uncertain behaviors. To ensure system safety, the control barrier function (CBF) is employed in this paper. However, a key challenge is that the CBF constraints are coupled when MASs perform collaborative tasks, which depend on information from multiple agents and impede the design of a fully distributed safe control scheme. To overcome this, a novel reconstructed CBF approach is proposed. In this method, the coupled CBF is reconstructed by leveraging state estimates of other agents obtained from a distributed adaptive observer. Furthermore, a prescribed performance adaptive parameter is designed to modify this reconstruction, ensuring that satisfying the reconstructed CBF constraint is sufficient to meet the original coupled one. Based on the reconstructed CBF, we design a safety-critical quadratic programming (QP) controller and prove that the proposed distributed control scheme rigorously guarantees the safety of the MAS, even in the uncertain dynamic environments involving uncontrollable agents. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated through a simulation.

title: Guardrail-First Architecture for Multi-Agent Systems: Typed Rails as First-Class Connectors
authors: V. Ragupathy
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI)
abstract: This paper introduces the Guardrail-First Architecture (GFA), a unique paradigm for multi-agent system safety, compliance, and governance. GFA uses Design-Science Research to enforce semantic, policy, and capability restrictions on inter-agent and agent–tool interactions with Typed Rails as first-class architectural connectors. Agent, Tool Interface, Typed Rails, and Policy Engine/Evidence Store layers ensure verifiable, policy-compliant activities with traceable evidence. GFA maintains operational performance while enhancing governance, as shown by a 47% decrease in dangerous activities, a 31% increase in policy adherence, and little latency overhead in a controlled MAS environment. Quality feedback emphasises openness, auditability, and minimised manual monitoring. GFA provides a solid foundation for trustworthy and responsible MAS implementation by architecturally formalising safety and compliance semantics. Automated Typed Rail synthesis, dynamic policy adaption, and heterogeneous, enterprise-level MAS scalability will be studied.

title: Adaptive Resource Management for Multi-AGV Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Systems
authors: G. Chen; Y. Zhou; Y. Geng; H. Liu; Z. Wei
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Computer Communication and Artificial Intelligence (CCAI)
abstract: To address the challenges of intense resource competition among communication, sensing, and control in industrial wireless networks, where communication congestion in largescale intelligent clusters thus limits production throughput, this paper proposes a Two-stage Adaptive Resource Management (TARM) method for integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) systems. In the first stage, focusing on automated guided vehicle (AGV) material transportation within automotive assembly workshops, a safety-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) adaptive closed-loop interaction cycle method is proposed. The base station (BS) proactively harvests sensing data to dynamically reconstruct AGV kinematic states. By dynamically modulating the closed-loop interaction cycles of multiple AGVs, the system shifts from traditional fixed-period communication to an active on-demand paradigm, this transition significantly reduces the underlying communication load, thereby effectively elevating the upper bound of the controllable AGV cluster capacity. In the second stage, leveraging the expanded upper bound of the controllable cluster scale from the first stage, this paper derives a cooperative scheduling algorithm for multiple AGVs. By incorporating AGV kinematic characteristics and cluster expansion capabilities with production efficiency, the algorithm dynamically adjusts task allocation logic to achieve a precise matching between logistical supply efficiency and multi-line demands, thereby enhancing workshop throughput. Simulation results demonstrate that TARM substantially outperforms the traditional algorithm with nmax outage tolerance (TANOT), classic ISAC algorithm (CISACA), and traditional algorithm (TA) benchmarks, achieving a 56% reduction in global communication load and a throughput enhancement of at least 30.73%.

title: Adaptive Patrol Routing in Smart Cities: A Systematic Survey and Hybrid Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
authors: S. Majumdar; A. Awasthi; L. A. Szolga
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Intelligent police patrol routing has advanced through artificial intelligence, optimization, geospatial analytics, and smart city sensing. However, the transition from algorithmic patrol-routing models to real-time, accountable, and field-deployable systems remains limited. This paper presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review of intelligent patrol-routing literature from 2005 to 2025. From 327 initially identified records, 64 studies were assessed as eligible and 32 core studies were coded for in-depth analysis. Unlike purely descriptive surveys, this review introduces a structured coding scheme covering algorithmic approach, optimization objectives, data-source integration, validation environment, real-time capability, implementation maturity, scalability, and ethical safeguards. The synthesis shows that multi-agent coordination and evolutionary optimization dominate the literature, whereas real-time closed-loop routing, CAD/911 integration, IoT-enabled sensing, fairness-aware allocation, and field validation remain comparatively underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the paper proposes a hybrid multi-agent reinforcement learning, genetic optimization, and digital twin framework for adaptive patrol routing. The framework formalizes patrol routing as a multi-objective optimization problem balancing coverage, response time, deterrence, unpredictability, travel cost, workload, and fairness. An illustrative cross-city open-data analysis, validation protocol, and evaluation metrics are also provided to support future simulation-based and field-based assessment. The study contributes a reproducible evidence synthesis and a system-level pathway for moving intelligent patrol routing from simulation-focused research toward responsible smart city public safety deployment.

title: Performance, Adaptability, and Security in AI-Driven IIoT: A Survey
authors: U. M. Borhan; A. Raza; T. Uddin; M. Islam; A. K. M. M. Islam; J. Chen
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) integrates cyber–physical systems (CPSs), edge–cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced connectivity to enable intelligent, data-driven operations across manufacturing, energy, transportation, and healthcare. The convergence of operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT), together with pervasive AI-driven automation, complicates meeting the joint requirements of performance, adaptability, and security (PAS). This survey adopts an explicitly AI-centric view of PAS and reviews IIoT research spanning deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL), digital twins (DTs), federated learning (FL) and collaborative learning, graph neural networks (GNNs), blockchain-assisted analytics, and lightweight and post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The reviewed approaches are analyzed across device, edge, fog, cloud, and application layers under industrial constraints, such as latency, reliability, resource limits, safety requirements, and regulatory compliance. A PAS-centric taxonomy is introduced that links technique families to deployment layers and application domains, and recurring tradeoffs among PAS dimensions are summarized. Open challenges are identified in multiobjective optimization, semantic interoperability, lifecycle validation, and governance, with directions outlined toward secure and sustainable Industry 5.0 IIoT ecosystems.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Risk-modulated Multi-Agent Cooperation (UAR-MAC)
authors: S. Liu; K. Han
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Transportation Systems (RAITS)
abstract: Uncertainty-Aware Risk-modulated Multi-Agent Cooperation (UAR-MAC) explicitly incorporates environmental dynamics and uncertainty into cooperative decision-making. Dynamic obstacles, perception noise, and communication disturbances are modeled using a unified uncertainty representation and a soft-computing-based adaptive risk assessment mechanism guides decision modulation. UAR-MAC balances robustness and efficiency via adaptive replanning and uncertainty-aware cost adjustment, improving decision stability and safety under varying uncertainty intensities.

title: Convex Parameter Matrix-Based Topology Reconfiguration Algorithm for Collision-Free Containment Control of MSVs
authors: P. Ye; Q. Shan; J. Sui; T. Li; C. L. P. Chen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: Aimed at mitigating the potential conflict between cooperative objectives and collision avoidance safety requirements in the containment control design, a convex parameter matrix (CPM)-based topology reconfiguration algorithm for collision-free containment control by dynamically adjusting the communication topology among multiple marine surface vehicles (MSVs) is devised. First, a topology reconfiguration algorithm is designed based on the proposed CPM characters that the convex parameter equals the average of its neighbors’. Second, under the well-structured topology, the repulsive potential function-based containment control protocols are thereby presented to steer all follower MSVs to strictly converge into the leaders’ interior convex hull, especially those initially driven outside the boundary. Furthermore, the stability of the closed-loop collision-free systems for MSVs is theoretically be proven via designing two Lyapunov functions. Finally, both numerical simulation and experimental results using Cybership II MSVs are reported to substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in a port environment.

title: AreaSafe MARL: Projection-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Overload Mitigation in Transmission Systems
authors: X. Zhu; Y. Zhao; H. Ye; J. Shao; Z. Guo; J. Wu
venue: 2026 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: To alleviate and mitigate the online computational burden of centralized security control in power systems with high penetration of renewable energy, this paper proposes a projection-guided area-based safe multi-agent reinforcement learning framework. The transmission network is decomposed into multiple control areas, where each area agent generates active-power redispatch commands for local controllable generators based on regional operating states, enabling coordinated area-level mitigation of system overloads. To ensure physical feasibility, a line-flow-sensitivity-based safety projection layer is embedded to map the raw actions produced by the agents onto a feasible set defined by generator regulation limits and transmission-line capacity constraints. Moreover, a projection-consistency regularization term is incorporated into the training objective to guide the agents toward policies that are intrinsically closer to the safe feasible region, thereby reducing their dependence on post-processing corrections. The proposed framework enables fast, scalable, and physically secure real-time overload mitigation for renewable-rich transmission networks.

title: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication for ISAC-Enabled Robotic Obstacle Avoidance
authors: W. Liu; Y. Deng; H. Wymeersch
venue: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications
abstract: Obstacle avoidance is a fundamental task in mobile robotics and has been extensively studied over the past decades. However, existing studies are fundamentally limited by an exclusive reliance on robot’s onboard sensors, which restricts the field of view and lacks the global understanding of dynamic environments. How to leverage the base station (BS) to enable sensing and control of mobile robots for reliable obstacle avoidance remains largely underexplored. To fill this gap, we investigate an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC)-enabled BS for the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) obstacle avoidance task, and propose a goal-oriented semantic communication (GOSC) framework for the BS to transmit sensing and command and control (C&C) signals efficiently and effectively. Our GOSC framework establishes a closed loop for sensing–C&C generation–sensing and C&C transmission: For sensing, a Kalman filter (KF) is applied to continuously predict UAV positions, mitigating the reliance of UAV position acquisition on continuous sensing signal transmission, and enhancing position estimation accuracy through sensing–prediction fusion. Based on the refined estimation position provided by the KF, we develop a Mahalanobis distance-based dynamic window approach (MD-DWA) to generate precise C&C signals under uncertainty, in which we derive the mathematical expression of the minimum Mahalanobis distance required to guarantee collision avoidance. Finally, for efficient sensing and C&C signal transmission, we propose an effectiveness-aware deep Q-network (E-DQN) to determine the transmission of sensing and C&C signals based on their value of information (VoI). The VoI of sensing signals is quantified by the reduction in uncertainty entropy of UAV’s position estimation, while the VoI of C&C signals is measured by their contribution to UAV navigation improvement. Extensive simulations validate the effectiveness of our proposed GOSC framework. Compared to the conventional ISAC transmission framework that transmits sensing and C&C signals at every time slot, GOSC achieves the same 100% task success rate while reducing the number of transmitted sensing and C&C signals by 92.4% and the number of transmission time slots by 85.5%.

title: Distributed Reinforcement Learning for Formation Task Planning in Communication-Constrained Environments
authors: N. Cao; C. Xue; X. Shao; C. Cai
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Mechatronics, Robotics, and Artificial Intelligence (MRAI)
abstract: For multi-agent systems, formation control and obstacle avoidance navigation are the two most critical research topics. Many classical methods require problem-specific modeling, limiting their applicability to different scenarios. Learning-based methods often assume perfect communication to obtain global information, which is difficult to maintain in complex real-world environments. To address this challenge, we propose a distributed multi-agent reinforcement learning approach. This method incorporates the length of communication link in policy optimization to handle communication constraints. We also use scalable formation rewards to decouple topological position constraints from communication distance constraints, and simulate message passing using a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to prioritize the extraction of more important features. The experimental results validate the feasibility and scalability of our approach. Compared to baseline methods, our approach demonstrates superior performance in terms of convergence reward, success rate, and formation error. Ablation studies further highlight that the components we designed contribute to address multiple constraints in complex scenarios.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based Drone Trajectory Design for Fire Rescue
authors: N. Sun; Z. Han; X. Li
venue: 2026 20th International Symposium on Wireless Communication Systems (ISWCS)
abstract: As a critical application of the low-altitude economy, fire rescue requires drones to collect the dynamic wildfire information observed by distributed ground users and to deliver it to command centers for timely decisions. To this end, the trajectories of drones need to be designed with respect to the value of information (VoI), the age of information (AoI), as well as the safety and energy constraints over time-varying air-to-ground links. Conventional studies focused on perimeter tracking or connectivity, leaving user-centric VoI-AoI service under explicit fire condition unexplored. To bridge this gap, a physics-enriched simulation environment with a robot-operatingsystem-compatible interface is developed in this paper. A cooperative strategy based on multi-agent proximal policy optimization with parameter sharing is further proposed. Simulations are conducted to illustrate the performance gain of the proposed strategy compared with other baselines.

title: A Distributed Neural Linear Thompson Sampling Framework to Achieve URLLC in Industrial IoT
authors: F. Pase; M. Giordani; S. Cavallero; M. Schellmann; J. Eichinger; R. Verdone; M. Zorzi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications
abstract: One of the most prominent requirements of future Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks will be to provide Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) in support of critical physical processes underlying the production chains. However, standard protocols for allocating wireless resources may not be able to optimize the latency-reliability trade-off, especially for uplink communication. For example, centralized (e.g., grant-based) scheduling can ensure almost zero collisions, but introduces delays in the way resources are requested by the User Equipments (UEs) and then granted by the Next Generation Node B (gNB). On the other hand, distributed scheduling (e.g., based on random access), in which UEs autonomously choose the physical resources to transmit uplink data, may lead to potentially many collisions especially when the density of UEs (and so the traffic) increases. Along these lines, in this work we propose DIStributed combinatorial NEural linear Thompson Sampling (DISNETS), a novel scheduling framework that combines the best of the two worlds. By leveraging a feedback signal sent from the gNB and reinforcement learning, the UEs are trained to autonomously optimize their uplink transmissions by selecting the available physical resources so as to minimize the number of collisions, disaggregated from the network and without additional message exchange to/from the gNB. DISNETS is a distributed, multi-agent adaptation of the Neural Linear Thompson Sampling (NLTS) algorithm, which has been further extended to admit multiple actions in parallel. We apply DISNETS to the context of IIoT, and demonstrate by extensive simulations the superior performance of the proposed approach in addressing URLLC compared to other baselines.

title: Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 6G Communications: Fundamentals, Applications and Future Directions
authors: E. Eldeeb; H. Alves
venue: IEEE Wireless Communications
abstract: The next-generation wireless technologies, including beyond 5G and 6G networks, are paving the way for transformative applications such as vehicle platooning, smart cities, and remote surgery. These innovations are driven by a vast array of interconnected wireless entities, including IoT devices, access points, UAVs, and CAVs, which increase network complexity and demand more advanced decision-making algorithms. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), especially reinforcement learning (RL), are key enablers for such networks, providing solutions to high-dimensional and complex challenges. However, as networks expand to multi-agent environments, traditional online RL approaches face cost, safety, and scalability limitations. Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) offers a promising solution by utilizing pre-collected data, reducing the need for real-time interaction. This article introduces a novel offline MARL algorithm based on conservative Q-learning (CQL), ensuring safe and efficient training. We extend this with meta-learning to address dynamic environments and validate the approach through use cases in radio resource management and UAV networks. Our work highlights offline MARL’s advantages, limitations, and future directions in wireless applications.

title: ASPIRE: An Agentic Decision System for Early Equipment Failure Prediction and Intervention in Industrial IIoT
authors: S. Guha; A. Datta
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Early fault prediction in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT)-based predictive maintenance systems is typically framed as an end-to-end learning problem, where models map multivariate sensor windows directly to warning or failure labels. Although such approaches can achieve high recall, they often generate unstable alerts, excessive false alarms, and limited operational interpretability, which restricts their use in safety-critical settings. We introduce ASPIRE, a decision-centric multi-agent system that reframes early fault prediction as a structured decision problem under uncertainty. Instead of using model outputs as direct alert triggers, ASPIRE combines evidence from role-specialised agents that monitor local sensor anomalies, temporal regime shifts, and fault probabilities. This evidence is evaluated by a deterministic Decision Agent using explicit and auditable policies, including margin-based gating and contextual evidence. In doing so, ASPIRE separates prediction from operational decision-making without modifying or retraining the underlying predictive model. Evaluated on the MetroPT-3 dataset for two-hour-ahead early-warning prediction and fault detection, ASPIRE improves early-warning precision from 0.875 to 0.889, recall from 0.941 to 0.953, and F1-score from 0.906 to 0.920 over a strong Transformer baseline, while maintaining identical fault-detection performance. Agreement-bucket and ablation analyses indicate that these gains are driven by two decision-layer mechanisms: suppression of ambiguous boundary-adjacent warnings through margin-based gating, and recovery of near-miss cases using window-level temporal context evidence from the Adaptive Window Agent. A non-intervening LLM-based Expert Agent provides human-readable explanations and recommended operator actions without influencing automated decisions. Overall, the results show that treating decision-making as a core component of the system improves reliability, interpretability, and robustness under changing operating conditions. A cost-efficiency and cost-effectiveness analysis further shows that ASPIRE’s performance gains can translate into operational cost benefits, even when exact preventive intervention or breakdown costs are unknown.

title: Robust Cooperative Localization in Featureless Environments: A Comparative Study of DCL, StCL, CCL, CI, and Standard-CL
authors: N. Khosravi; R. Ventura; M. Basiri
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA)
abstract: Cooperative localization (CL) enables accurate position estimation in multi-robot systems operating in GPS-denied environments. This paper presents a comparative study of five CL approaches: Centralized Cooperative Localization (CCL), Decentralized Cooperative Localization (DCL), Sequential Co-operative Localization (StCL), Covariance Intersection (CI), and Standard Cooperative Localization (Standard-CL). All methods are implemented in ROS and evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations under two conditions: weak data association and robust detection. Our analysis reveals fundamental trade-offs among the methods. StCL and Standard-CL achieve the lowest position errors, but exhibit severe filter inconsistency, making them unsuitable for safety-critical applications. DCL demonstrates remarkable stability under challenging conditions due to its measurement stride mechanism, which provides implicit regularization against outliers. CI emerges as the most balanced approach, achieving near-optimal consistency while maintaining competitive accuracy. CCL provides theoretically optimal estimation, but shows sensitivity to measurement outliers. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting CL algorithms based on application requirements.

title: On AI Integrated Multi-Robot Autonomy Under Uncertainty
authors: N. Vasilyev
venue: 2026 IEEE 8th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, and Information Processing (AICSIP)
abstract: Intellectual robots' fleet is simulated by relational cooperative game for autonomous performing tasks in an uncertain spatial configuration and communications range. The agents are able to make rational decisions pursuing their own interests taking into account of their preferences and fitting relations. A joint balanced decision is to be found by them. Optimal networking structure of the system is formed by and for self-organization. The problem is reduced to optimization of the game resulting relation that is a composition of the given binary relations built on the basis of messaging among stable coalitions. Distributed method is proposed to solve this relational networking cooperative game. The approach is convenient for promotion.

title: SafeSeCA: Safe Action Decomposition for 3D Deformation of Large Soft-Linear Objects
authors: A. K. Guzman-Leguel; R. Aragüés; C. Sagüés
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: The manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is vital across applications like surgery, food processing, and manufacturing, despite the complexity of their deformation. This work introduces SafeSeCA, which ensures safe (via continuous action masking using zonotope-based ray masks) and viable (kinematically feasible with current configuration) actions through internal mechanisms, eliminating external constraints. The control uses two agents to manage gripper translation and rotation, simplifying the action space. By adapting Sequential Credit Assignment (SeCA) for continuous and off-policy learning, the credit assignment problem is addressed. A sequential agent architecture further improves policy coordination. Training and testing in PyBullet validate SafeSeCA's effectiveness.

title: Predefined-Time Event-Based Consensus Tracking Control for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems With Self-Regulating Constraints
authors: L. Shao; T. Chen; H. Liu; S. Zhao; J. Li; C. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper addresses distributed predefined-time adaptive tracking control for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) with unknown dynamics and external disturbances, subject to prescribed-performance constraints on coordination tracking errors. A smooth self-regulating prescribed-performance control framework is developed to mitigate the feasibility conflict between rapidly shrinking performance envelopes and fast convergence requirements. Specifically, a differentiable self-regulating performance boundary is constructed via hyperbolic tangent functions to relax the constraint near the boundary, thereby preventing transformation singularities and alleviating chattering. A practical predefined-time control law is then designed to drive the coordination tracking errors into a tunable residual set within a user-specified time, regardless of initial conditions. To compensate lumped uncertainties without requiring acceleration measurements, a predefined-time nonlinear disturbance observer (PTNDO) is introduced using only velocity information. In addition, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is incorporated to reduce inter-agent communications and controller updates while excluding Zeno behavior. Lyapunov-based analysis proves boundedness of all closed-loop signals and practical predefined-time stability under the proposed scheme. Simulation results demonstrate fast convergence, satisfaction of the proposed self-regulated performance bounds, and reduced triggering frequency. Note to Practitioners—This paper investigates distributed predefined-time consensus control for nonlinear multi-agent systems subject to performance constraints. In engineering applications such as UAV swarms, achieving rapid convergence within a strictly defined time is crucial. However, aggressive convergence requirements often conflict with rigid safety constraints, potentially leading to controller singularity or oscillation. To address this practical issue, a self-regulating constraint framework is developed to automatically adjust boundaries, thereby ensuring smooth control signals and avoiding singularities. Furthermore, considering the limited communication bandwidth and unknown disturbances in real-world networked environments, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism and a velocity-based disturbance observer are integrated. This approach effectively reduces the communication burden and compensates for disturbances without requiring acceleration measurements. However, practitioners should note that this approach currently relies on velocity measurements, and high-frequency noise could affect the observer’s accuracy. Future work will focus on validating this algorithm on physical hardware testbeds and extending it to scenarios with significant communication delays.

title: Multi-UAV Formation Control Method Merging 3-D Virtual Tube Framework
authors: Z. Liu; Z. Tang; S. Long; G. Li; Y. Wang; S. Sun
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: In this article, to traverse complex and narrow environments in formation configuration, a multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) control strategy is proposed with the aid of a 3-D virtual tube. First, an improved 3-D virtual tube without internal obstacles is presented. Under the constraints of such a tube, the controller includes a tube obstacle avoidance component, a collision avoidance component, and a consensus control component. The core input of the formation control is the local position information of the agents within the virtual tube. When UAVs traverse narrow channels, they can automatically adjust through local perception to achieve formation control. This strategy can ensure the real-time performance of formation transformation and improve passage efficiency. Some Lyapunov-like functions are designed to verify the system stability. Simulations and experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: An Agentic Framework for Aerial Swarms: Integrating LLMs with the Crazyswarm2
authors: V. B. S. Fernandes; A. C. Vangasse; L. C. A. Pimenta; G. M. Freitas
venue: 2026 Brazilian Conference on Robotics (CROS)
abstract: Enabling non expert users to control robotic systems through natural language represents an important step toward democratizing access to advanced automation. This paper presents a modular framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with multi robot control using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A central contribution of this work is the proposal of an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) architecture designed to bridge the gap between probabilistic semantic reasoning and deterministic robotic control. By assigning distinct responsibilities to specialized agents (specifically for planning, execution, and verification) the system decouples high level intent from real time kinematic constraints. Operating within an asynchronous event-driven loop, these agents coordinate to invoke safety aware tools (e.g., takeoff, waypoint navigation) via MCP, allowing users to issue intuitive commands like "form a line along the X-axis." Validated within a containerized ROS 2 and Crazyswarm2 simulation environment, our results highlight the potential of this distributed architecture to lower the barrier to entry in swarm robotics, enabling domain experts to focus on mission goals rather than implementation details.

title: In-Depth Cluster Conflict-Based Search for Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: J. Lee; J. Park; B. -M. Jeong; D. -S. Jang; H. -L. Choi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper addresses a variant of the conflict-based search (CBS) algorithm for multi-agent path finding, presenting an effective cluster reasoning heuristic that searches for and detects conflicts involving more than two agents. The proposed in-depth cluster reasoning technique systematically alters the reference agent when computing the heuristic cost-to-go, and this yields a tighter estimate. It then balances the complexity of expanding CBS nodes against that of locating clusters by systematically scheduling the associated parameters. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm successfully detects clusters that state-of-the-art algorithms cannot identify and produces solutions for various extreme scenarios that existing algorithms cannot solve. Note to Practitioners—Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) computes collision-free routes for many agents sharing a map, and underpins applications such as automated warehouses, vehicle routing, and other coordinated robotic fleets. In practice, the difficulty grows sharply with the number of agents and the complexity of the environment, so conventional optimal solvers frequently exceed acceptable time limits. This work targets exactly those hard instances, producing high-quality routes even where prior methods return no solution in time. For practitioners, the method extends the range of problems that can be solved with a guaranteed-optimal solution rather than an approximate one. It is also tunable on a per-instance basis: parameters can be matched to the characteristics of a given site—for example, agent density or graph layout—so that performance on a specific deployment exceeds what fixed, general-purpose settings achieve. This makes it suitable as a configurable planning component that operators can adapt to their own facility. The grid-based routes the algorithm produces are a practical foundation for real robotic systems. Holonomic robots that move directly on the grid can follow them without modification. Robots with kinematic constraints can treat each route as a reference and adapt it: as shown in our experiments, the discrete routes can be smoothed into dynamically feasible trajectories that remain collision-free under positional noise. A current limitation is that the approach addresses the initial planning stage only; online re-planning during execution and full hardware integration require further development before field deployment.

title: Reinforcement Learning for UAV Adaptive Conflict Detection and Resolution with VFR-dominated Aircraft
authors: M. Luo; T. Zeh; H. Braßel; M. Lindner; H. Fricke
venue: 2026 New Trends in Civil Aviation (NTCA)
abstract: Integrating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) into Visual Flight Rules (VFR) airspace requires Conflict Detection and Resolution (CDR) mechanisms capable of tolerating uncertainty in pilot behavior. This paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which learns how to avoid collisions with other crewed aircraft by interacting with the surrounding environmental information. We model the CDR problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) in which a highly agile UAV must generate efficient actions and safety-prioritized maneuvers against stochastic VFR-dominated aircraft. The UAV is modeled as a quaternion-based 6-degree-of-freedom rigid body model to capture its attitude and trajectory, and the VFR-dominated aircraft is a 3-degree-of-freedom point mass model with envelopeconsistent speed. Observations encompass the flight performance of the UAV and VFR-dominated aircraft (such as position, distance, heading, etc.) along with contextual clues (i.e, risk warning indicators and recent avoidance maneuvers). Using PPO, the agent learns a policy that balances hard safety constraints with stable avoidance control. A safety-prioritized reward function severely penalizes violations of separation and stays in risk zone. The trained agent produces consistent, collision-free trajectories and effectively responds to sudden intrusions without manual reprogramming. Findings demonstrate RL’s applicability for CDR in mixed airspace: the technique adjusts to VFR-dominated aircraft uncertainties and reliably clears collisions, suggesting that low-altitude airspace operations can be automated.

title: Frequency-Shaped Primal-Dual Optimization for Distributed Model Predictive Control of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
authors: H. Dan; D. Kurabayashi
venue: IEEE Control Systems Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a distributed model predictive control (DMPC) method for multi-agent systems with smooth nonlinear dynamics and constraints, including pairwise distance constraints for collision avoidance. We cast the finite-horizon DMPC problem as a coupled optimization and apply a fully distributed generalized primal-dual gradient method that requires only neighbor-to-neighbor communication to solve the optimization problem. The update law for the optimization is built from diagonal transfer-function blocks that enable frequency-domain shaping of the iteration dynamics to mitigate oscillations and improve convergence. We show that any equilibrium satisfies the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the original DMPC problem and prove local convergence under a strong monotonicity assumption around a KKT-point. In a four-robot example, frequency-shaped tuning reduces KKT residuals by one to two orders of magnitude and yields collision-free trajectories comparable to a centralized MPC benchmark.

title: ACF-MATD3 Formation Control for Multi-Agent Wheeled Mobile Robot Systems
authors: Z. Hu; J. Gou
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Control Engineering (ICAACE)
abstract: Multi-agent wheeled mobile robot systems have been widely applied in tasks such as cooperative operations, environmental monitoring, and formation transportation. As such, formation control becomes an important topic to study for the area of unmanned systems. However, conventional formation control is based upon graph theory and consensus theory, requiring accurate modeling and complex mathematical analysis that restricts its flexibility in handling dynamic and high-dimensional settings. In this paper, the formation control problem is formulated as a multiagent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) problem, and an Action Consistency-Formation Multi-Agent Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ACF-MATD3) algorithm is developed to address formation control in an obstacle-free environment. Based on a leader-follower scheme, the algorithm introduces the action consistency loss and the formation maintenance loss to improve the coordination between agents as well as the robustness of their formations. In the square formation task, compared to the original MATD3 algorithm, the proposed approach reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by approximately 28.9 % and the standard deviation by 81.6 %. In the formation transformation task, a multi-branch input fusion architecture achieves an overall 47.4 % reduction in collision rate with $\mathbf{4 2. 4 \%}$ drop in global MSE. Additionally, when combined with Adaptive B-Spline Network (ABSN), the collision rate drops to zero while the global MSE decreases by another 20.7 %. Simulation and real-world experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing deep reinforcement learning methods in terms of accuracy, stability, and robustness, indicating strong potential for practical engineering applications.

title: HyperCortex: Adaptive Enterprise AI Runtime for Policy-Governed Multi-Agent Workflow Execution
authors: A. Panwar; S. Saini; N. Chauhan; R. Gupta; J. S. Makkar; S. Singh
venue: 2026 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICACT)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) systems that coordinate agents and tasks across enterprise workflows are becoming more dynamic and adaptable, changing their workflow execution at runtime due to ongoing failure rates, substituting agents, inserting steps, or escalating to humans, and external effects of workflow steps are already irreversible. Much is known about how this can be achieved: bounded plan repair over a partially-executed plan; and compensating actions, similar to saga transactions. The question remains, however, on how to assess the effectiveness of these systems. Reported evaluations typically involve comparing a system with baselines that are subject to failures sampled independently, simulated agents but do not necessarily include tests to verify that results apply to real models, and make safety claims rather than measuring safety. This paper provides an experimental methodology to overcome all three of those deficiencies and an implementation, HyperCortex, which is not claimed as a novel mechanism but rather as an evaluation vehicle. The methodology involves condition-independent failure scheduling, a protocol behind the back of the LLM that fixes the failure process and replaces a local LLM with a simulated agent, reporting safety invariants as measured quantities, and defining a safety oracle that is independent of the policy engine that it grades. The methodology gives the results not available in a demonstration-style evaluation: The benefit of non-local plan mutation over local repair is statistically indistinguishable from zero, given benign conditions, and grows to +0.153 (p = 1.7*10~41) with heavy failure injection; one repair operator is measurably counter-productive on the failure class it targets; organizational memory and replanning can replace repair; and replanning is a substitute for organizational memory. No violation of the invariant was detected for any execution.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Hospital Supply Chain Optimization: A Systematic Review
authors: S. Louah; H. Sarir; M. Tahiri
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Digital Applications (ISDA)
abstract: This research paper provides a systematic review of the literature relating to the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in supply chains for hospitals (HSC). It is currently limited in the literature regarding the ways AI is being researched and utilized within supply chains in hospitals, even though this area is a critical influence on healthcare outcomes, minimizing costs, and ensuring patient safety. This complexity is compounded by the fact that hospitals experience uncertainty in their businesses and demand varies at different levels, while at the same time maintaining compliance with federal regulations and having the need to make real-time decisions. AI techniques such as: machine learning; deep learning; natural language processing; expert systems; fuzzy logic; multi agent systems; neural networks; support vector machines; optimization algorithms; robotics; and computer vision, have all shown promise in improving inventory control, purchasing, shipping and receiving, forecasting demands for products, and allocating personnel and physical resources to be used in managing hospital supplies. The results of the literature review provided a classification of a total of 41 peer-reviewed research articles, published from 2002 to February 2026 and currently indexed in the SCOPUS database, with respect to the two major dimensions of AI technique and HSC function or activity. The results will guide the reader in realizing the current research focus, the prevailing AI methods, the lack of research in certain areas, and ideas for future research in developing intelligent and resilient HSCs.

title: Reward-Centering Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multiagent Coordinated Interception in Orbital Pursuit-Evasion Game
authors: C. Qin; Y. Liu; J. Qiu; W. Ji
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Maneuverable threat poses significant risks to the operational safety of spacecraft in orbit, thereby jeopardizing mission success in the contested space environment. To address the coordinated orbital game between multiple pursuers (spacecraft) and one evader (threat), this article proposes a reward-centering multiagent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm, which has twofold. First, a relative dynamical model considering $J_{2}$ perturbation is established to characterize orbital interactions among multiple players, laying a physics-based foundation for decision-making. Second, an improved multiagent reinforcement learning (RL) framework is constructed with two components. For individual spacecraft of multiple pursuers, a state-driven exploration–exploitation tradeoff mechanism is incorporated to avoid suboptimal strategy convergence. For the spacecraft group (namely, multiple pursuers), reward functions are designed to align individual behaviors with collective objectives. Furthermore, a reward-centering mechanism along with theoretical analysis is introduced to dynamically calibrate the reward baseline, which stabilizes policy update via reducing gradient variance. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm enables spacecraft to autonomously develop coordinated strategies, ultimately confining the threat within a predefined interception threshold.

title: Handling Stability Control for FWID-EVs Under Tire Blowout: An Online Off-Policy Multiagent Cooperative Approach
authors: Z. Gao; P. K. Wong; J. Zhao; L. Hu; J. Zhao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: The abrupt variation in lateral force and the resultant unbalance of inertial forces induced by tire blowout (TB) are recognized as significant threats to handling stability and driving safety. However, the modeling of vehicles under post-TB conditions is complicated by inherent nonlinearity, which degrades the effectiveness of the model-based control strategies. To address this issue, this work proposes an online off-policy multiagent cooperative method based on adaptive dynamic event-triggered schemes (ADET-OIMC) to improve the handling stability of the four-wheel independent drive electric vehicle (FWID-EV) under TB conditions, thereby improving driving safety. First, the dynamic behaviors of the FWID-EV under TB are described based on the UniTire model. Subsequently, an online off-policy multiagent cooperative framework is established by separately adjusting four brake torques and front-wheel steering. Furthermore, an adaptive dynamic event-triggered mechanism is proposed to adjust computational resources among multiple agents. Finally, the proposed ADET-OIMC method is validated via rapid control prototyping experiments.

title: GRACE: A Unified 2D Multi-Robot Path Planning Simulator & Benchmark for Grid, Roadmap, And Continuous Environments
authors: C. Zang; A. Mannucci; I. Barz; P. Schillinger; F. Lier; W. Hönig
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Advancing Multi-Agent Pathfinding (MAPF) and Multi-Robot Motion Planning (MRMP) requires platforms that enable transparent, reproducible comparisons across modeling choices. Existing tools either scale under simplifying assumptions (grids, homogeneous agents) or offer higher fidelity with less comparable instrumentation. We present GRACE, a unified 2D simulator+benchmark that instantiates the same task at multiple abstraction levels (grid, roadmap, continuous) via explicit, reproducible operators and a common evaluation protocol. Our empirical results on public maps and representative planners enable commensurate comparisons on a shared instance set. Furthermore, we quantify the expected representation–fidelity trade-offs (MRMP solves instances at higher fidelity but lower speed, while grid/roadmap planners scale farther). By consolidating representation, execution, and evaluation, GRACE thereby aims to make cross-representation studies more comparable and provides a means to advance multi-robot planning research and its translation to practice.

title: Planax: A JAX-Accelerated High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Large-Scale Fixed-Wing Aerial Swarms
authors: C. Xue; Q. Dong; Q. Liu; Y. Qi; X. Qin; J. Ren; Z. Zhou; B. Liang; J. Yang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for fixed-wing aerial robots requires both aerodynamic fidelity and high-throughput simulation, yet existing platforms typically provide either simplified kinematics or CPU-bound high-fidelity models. We present Planax, a JAX/XLA-accelerated, GPU-resident benchmark framework that combines nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) dynamics with wind-tunnel-derived F-16 aerodynamic lookup tables using tensorized interpolation. On a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, Planax achieves $2.33 \times 10^{7}$ environment steps per second for independent heading/pitch/velocity rollouts and supports batch sizes of up to $2 \times 10^{7}$ independent 6-DOF instances. These figures characterize independent rollouts; interacting formation and pursuit-evasion tasks additionally incur relative-geometry costs. Under matched model, interpolation, and rollout settings, the XLA-compiled JAX Tensor-LUT backend achieves lower steady-state latency than the evaluated same-model PyTorch baseline across the tested components and batch sizes. Cross-fidelity multi-agent ablations, with all policies evaluated in the high-fidelity environment, show that high-fidelity training improves both task performance and safety. Across three seeds, the pursuit-evasion win rate increases from $0.534\pm 0.097$ to $1.000\pm 0.000$, while formation slot RMSE decreases from $1493\pm 130$ m to $445\pm 211$ m and overload incidence decreases from $0.480\pm 0.049$ to $0.067\pm 0.071$.

title: Multi-Objective Computing Offloading in Satellite Edge Computing: A Preference-Aware Hybrid Latent Action Multi-Agent DRL
authors: J. Chen; W. Zhao; Z. Wu; J. Li; C. Huang; Q. Liang; Z. Han
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Satellite networks can provide global connectivity and full geographical coverage without constraints. This paper investigates a dynamic multi-objective computation offloading problem (MOCOP) in satellite edge computing (SEC) systems for remote Internet of Things terminal devices (ITDs), which aims to simultaneously minimize task completion delay and ITD energy consumption with dynamically changing user preferences. The two objectives are inherently conflicting, and the real-time shift of user preference weights poses severe challenges to adaptive decision-making. Moreover, computation offloading in SEC involves discrete-continuous hybrid actions including task offloading selection, local CPU allocation, and transmission power control, further complicating collaborative optimization. To address these challenges, we propose a preference-aware hybrid latent action multi-agent proximal policy optimization (PH_MAPPO) algorithm. Specifically, a preference-aware state fusion is designed to fuse real-time user preferences and environmental states for adaptive decision-making. A conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) is then adopted to construct a decodable latent action space, which converts hybrid action learning into stable continuous policy learning. Furthermore, a preference guided trajectory buffer (PGTB) and a centralized critic network are developed to enhance sample efficiency, alleviate training bias, and stabilize multi-agent policy learning. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that PH MAPPO reduces total task completion delay by 23.5%–41.2% and ITD energy consumption by 23.5%–41.2%, lowers the inverted generational distance (IGD) by 53.58%, and improves the hypervolume (HV) and average comprehensive objective indicator (ACOI) by 3.43% and approximately 4.00% on average, respectively.

title: Target Search and Cost-Optimal Navigation in Unknown Environments for Multi-Robot Systems
authors: G. Pan; C. Deng; S. Fan; Y. Xie; C. Shang; S. Hui; Q. -Y. Fan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: This paper investigates the target search and cost-optimal navigation problem for multi-robot systems (MRSs) in unknown environments to achieve efficient exploration, accurate recognition, and safe navigation. Different from the existing works on target search and path planning, this paper addresses target search and cost-optimal navigation for MRSs in completely unknown environments with persistently missing target signals. To overcome the challenges of the considered problem, a hierarchical control framework is developed for MRSs, which consists of real-time exploration and recognition, target allocation based on unknown region cost, and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based navigation algorithm. Specifically, a dynamic Voronoi-based exploration strategy is integrated with a You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based RGB-D perception module to enable fast detection and localization of potential targets. Then, an unknown region hazard coefficient is designed based on obstacle density, and real-time target allocation is achieved through the Hungarian algorithm. Based on this allocation, a global-local collaborative planning strategy is adopted for global path generation and effective dynamic obstacle avoidance, which integrates an improved Dijkstra algorithm with a DRL-based method. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through simulations and real-world experiments.

title: TopoEvo: A Topology-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices
authors: J. Wang; R. Chen; Y. Wang; X. Liao; Z. Fan; X. Wu; W. Wu; X. Liu; J. Zhao
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) in microservices is challenging due to (i) noisy and heterogeneous multimodal observability (metrics, logs, traces), (ii) cascading failure propagation that amplifies downstream symptoms, and (iii) non-stationary topology drift induced by autoscaling and rolling updates. Recent LLM-based RCA agents can generate tool-grounded explanations, yet they often remain topology-agnostic and suffer from symptom-amplification bias, misattributing the root cause to salient downstream victims. We propose TopoEvo, a topologyaware self-evolving multi-agent framework that couples graph representation learning with structured, topology-constrained reasoning. TopoEvo first introduces Metric-orthogonal Multimodal Alignment (MOMA), which decomposes metric embeddings into complementary subspaces and contrastively aligns logs and traces to reduce modality redundancy and sparsity, yielding stable node representations for graph encoding. It then applies Vector Quantization (VQ) to discretize topology-enhanced states into auditable symptom tokens with a symptom lexicon, enabling reliable retrieval and token-level evidence grounding. On top of these discrete topology cues, TopoEvo performs a multiagent Hypothesis-Evidence-Test (HET) workflow to explicitly verify propagation-consistent explanations and separate initiating anomalies from amplified downstream symptoms. Finally, a Self-Evolving Mechanism refreshes hierarchical incident memory and performs conservative test-time adaptation with high-confidence pseudo-labels to maintain robustness under drift. We evaluate TopoEvo on both a public AIOps benchmark and a real-world production incident dataset. Compared to the stateof-the-art baselines, TopoEvo achieves absolute improvements of up to 3.44% in root cause localization accuracy, while remarkably boosting fault-type classification performance by 4.39% to 16.81% across diverse datasets.

title: LYCO: Learning to Yield for Decentralized Multi-Agent Path Finding in Congested Environments
authors: H. Makino; K. Noshiro; K. Hasebe; S. Ito
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Leveraging its flexibility and scalability, decentralized reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely applied to multi-agent path finding (MAPF). However, existing methods often exhibit a decline in success rate as agent density increases. For example, agents that reach their goals early may remain there and block other agents. To maintain a high success rate as the number of agents grows, we propose Learning to Yield for Decentralized MAPF in Congested Environments (LYCO), a decentralized policy that explicitly learns localized yielding behaviors. LYCO is trained by imitation learning from Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT), a lightweight heuristic solver, and adds two components that promote yielding: (i) an observation channel encoding the estimated next positions of higher-priority neighboring agents, and (ii) a local cooperative reward that discourages waiting at a goal unless nearby agents have also reached theirs. Crucially, PIBT serves only as a source of imitation targets during training; during both RL training and inference, each agent selects actions solely from its local observations using the learned policy. LYCO thus maintains decentralized action selection without performing priority inheritance or backtracking at inference time. In grid-world settings, LYCO consistently outperformed representative decentralized RL baselines in high-density environments, achieving a success rate above 0.7 at an agent density of 0.3 on a $20\times 20$ map with obstacle density 0.1 while maintaining a competitive makespan. These findings show that LYCO is an effective decentralized approach for congested MAPF.

title: Learning-Based Prescribed-Time Cluster Lag Consensus Control for Six-Rotor UAVs: A Novel Congestion Avoidance Strategy
authors: L. Cao; Y. Zhou; Y. Lei; L. Chen; H. Liang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: As the low-altitude economy thrives, six-rotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) face increasingly complex missions and higher operational density, resulting in airspace congestion that poses challenges to flight safety and mission timeliness. This paper investigates the prescribed-time lag consensus optimized control with an adaptive dynamic surface control (ADSC) strategy for six-rotor UAVs. Concretely, a novel congestion avoidance strategy is devised for six-rotor UAVs by integrating cluster lag consensus into an optimized backstepping framework. This approach not only allocates distinct time lags to different UAV clusters to resolve the spatiotemporal coordination issue but also ensures robustness against unknown dynamic parameters and external disturbances. Meanwhile, to address the explosion of complexity, an improved prescribed-time filter is developed that guarantees filter errors converge within prescribed time by incorporating a prescribed-time adjustment function. Building upon the filter, an ADSC scheme is further constructed by embedding dominate functions, effectively solving the difficulty of parameter selection and enhancing the control performance. Moreover, a prescribed-time actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed to accelerate the convergence rate and minimize energy consumption for six-rotor UAVs. Lastly, two experimental scenarios are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

title: A Comprehensive Review on Control Barrier Functions: Uncertainty Handling, Design Optimization, and Feasibility Analysis
authors: S. Zhao; Z. Yan; T. Huang; S. Wen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide a rigorous framework for enforcing safety in control-affine systems by ensuring system states remain within predefined safe sets. However, practical deployment faces fundamental challenges that limit real-world applicability. This review analyzes recent progress in CBF methodologies across three interconnected domains: uncertainty handling, structural optimization, and feasibility assurance. For uncertainty, we distinguish strategies tailored to unknown dynamics, modeling discrepancies, and dynamic environments, spanning robust theoretical methods and learning-based approaches. For structural design, we examine class- $\mathcal {K}$ function selection, parameter tuning, and advanced modifications that jointly address conservatism and feasibility. For feasibility, we identify the root causes of CBF-QP infeasibility and survey solution strategies, including constraint relaxation, structural redesign, and mathematical guarantees. By synthesizing these directions into a unified framework, this review highlights key interdependencies and outlines future research opportunities for advancing CBF-based safety-critical control in robotics, autonomous systems, and beyond.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based Adaptive Navigation for Assistive Mobility in Simulated Indoor Environments
authors: P. M; R. Sudharsan; B. Swathy; Y. S. J
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: Assistive mobility technologies play a pivotal role in boosting the independence and overall well-being of people with physical disabilities. Nevertheless, the majority of smart wheelchairs available today operate based on pre-set navigation routes and are not adaptable to changing indoor environments. This research presents a smart wheelchair navigation system that adapts to the environment using a digital twin-based robot wheelchair optimized by Reinforcement Learning (RL) in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab. The digital twin is created through URDF and USD models of the wheelchair and the indoor environment, thereby allowing a realistic physics simulation. A multimodal sensor suite, which includes a 2D LiDAR, four IMU sensors attached to the wheels, and four directional RGB cameras, is installed to get complete spatial and motion perception. Sensor data are then encoded and merged into a single state representation, which is the input for the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent to learn the task of autonomous navigation. Safety measures in real-time, such as fall detection, collision detection, and emergency stop mechanisms, among other things, are what keep the robot safe during training and navigation. The outcome of the simulation shows increased reward progression and navigation success, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of RL-driven digital twins in creating intelligent, user-friendly assistive mobility systems.

title: Toward Empathetic Care: An LLM-Based Multi-Intention Recognition Framework for Mental Health and Complex Medical Queries
authors: D. Yang; J. Wei; M. Hu; J. Liu; L. Liu; Z. Chen; M. Li; J. He; W. Zhou; Y. Liu; L. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing
abstract: Mental health has become a critical global concern, and many individuals now turn to conversational agents for support when facing emotional distress and complex health problems. In these high-stakes and emotionally sensitive settings, patients' self-descriptions are often long, fragmented, and interweave medical facts with psychological needs, lifestyle concerns, and urgent safety questions.
