Large Language Model (LLM)–based assistants must therefore not only answer clinical questions, but also accurately uncover the multiple underlying intentions that drive a patient's request, as a prerequisite for empathetic and trustworthy interaction. In this work, we propose MIRA, a multi-intention recognition and planning framework designed to understand complex patient intentions in mental health–related consultations. MIRA first introduces a two-stage intention recognition module that decomposes verbose queries into clinically aligned sub-queries using semantic matching with medical intent prototypes, including intents such as medical psychological support and lifestyle guidance. Next, a Dynamic Intent Orchestration (DIO) agent leverages clinical dependency modeling to plan execution sequences that respect medical best practices and safety considerations. Based on this plan, a multi-agent collaboration system with a Hierarchical Progressive Decision-making (HPD) agent synthesizes evidence across sequential diagnostic stages to generate context-aware advice that is suitable for emotionally sensitive scenarios. We evaluate MIRA on several real-world medical dialogue benchmarks. Both automated metrics and expert physician evaluations show that MIRA consistently outperforms existing different baselines in intent comprehension, clinical planning, and overall response quality.

title: ADM-DP: Adaptive Dynamic Modality Diffusion Policy through Vision-Tactile-Graph Fusion for Multi-Agent Manipulation
authors: E. Wang; W. Fan; D. Zhang
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Multi-agent robotic manipulation remains challenging due to the combined demands of coordination, grasp stability, and collision avoidance in shared workspaces. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Dynamic Modality Diffusion Policy (ADM-DP), a framework that integrates vision, tactile, and graph-based (multi-agent pose) modalities for coordinated control. ADM-DP introduces four key innovations. First, an enhanced visual encoder merges RGB and point-cloud features via Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) modulation to enrich perception. Second, a tactile-guided grasping strategy uses Force-Sensitive Resistor (FSR) feedback to detect insufficient contact and trigger corrective grasp refinement, improving grasp stability. Third, a graph-based collision encoder leverages shared tool center point (TCP) positions of multiple agents as structured kinematic context to maintain spatial awareness and reduce inter-agent interference. Fourth, an Adaptive Modality Attention Mechanism (AMAM) dynamically re-weights modalities according to task context, enabling flexible fusion. For scalability and modularity, a decoupled training paradigm is employed in which agents learn independent policies while sharing spatial information. This maintains low interdependence between agents while retaining collective awareness. Across seven multi-agent tasks, ADM-DP achieves 12-25% performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation studies show the greatest improvements in tasks requiring multiple sensory modalities, validating our adaptive fusion strategy and demonstrating its robustness for diverse manipulation scenarios. https://Enyi-Bean.github.io/ADM-DP/

title: Efficient Cooperative Trajectory Planning Using Cognitive-Based Risk Models for Multi-Agent Systems in Non-Convex Environments
authors: Y. Guo; F. Bai; Z. Bai
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: This letter focuses on the multi-agent trajectory planning (MATP) problem for car-like intelligent agents operating in high-density unstructured environments and structured scenarios (e.g., urban roads) containing heterogeneous traffic participants. The primary challenge in addressing such problems is obtaining a globally optimal solution rapidly while ensuring safety. The nonlinear kinematic constraints of vehicles, along with the collision constraints that scale with scenario complexity, significantly increase the computational difficulty. Furthermore, the quality of homotopy solutions critically impacts the feasibility of the final solution. To tackle these issues, we propose a hierarchical search and centralized optimization (HSCO) method. Initially, a priority-based search algorithm is employed to rapidly generate an initial guess, enhanced by a time-priority collision pair selection strategy that significantly improves search efficiency. Subsequently, we introduce a novel higher-order warped Gaussian collision risk model integrated with a driver perception field model, effectively reduces the potential collision risk caused by tracking performance uncertainty. Finally, the original MATP problem is linearized into a coupled convex quadratic programming formulation. The proposed collision risk model is seamlessly integrated into the separation plane of potential collision pairs, enabling efficient iterative solution processes that ensure safety, feasibility, and optimality. Experimental results demonstrate that HSCO outperforms existing MATP algorithms in large-scale unstructured scenarios. Moreover, in structured scenarios involving heterogeneous traffic participants, HSCO rapidly generates safe and optimal cooperative trajectories.

title: The Agentic Control Framework: Integrating Knowledge Graph Retrieval and Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Learning for Robust Process Design
authors: R. Rodrigues; A. Abbasi; S. Hosseini; M. C. Nuno Da Costa; D. Fernandes
venue: 2026 IEEE 9th International Conference on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The realization of resilient autonomous systems is currently impeded by the difficulty of translating abstract design requirements into verifiable control policies that can withstand significant model uncertainty. Here we present the Agentic Control Framework, a full-stack neuro-symbolic architecture that unifies semantic reasoning with game-theoretic hardening to maximize robustness. The workflow initiates with a Large Language Model (LLM)-based agent that leverages a domainspecific Knowledge Graph to comprehend unstructured design specifications and retrieve optimal control constraints. These formal specifications characterize a high-fidelity Digital Twin, which incorporates a Reduced Order Model (ROM) integrated via Runge-Kutta (RK4) methods. Within this adaptive environment, we solve the robust control problem as a multi-agent zero-sum differential game using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), where a stabilizing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy competes against an adversary injecting worst-case stochastic disturbances. We benchmark this adversarial formulation against classical $H_{\infty}$ synthesis and standard Vanilla PPO, demonstrating that the system converges to an empirical Nash Equilibrium that rivals theoretical robust control baselines. Our results indicate that grounding agentic comprehension in rigorous game-theoretic training produces self-organizing controllers that maintain operational stability under severe uncertainty, bridging the gap between theoretical robust control and adaptive autonomy.

title: A Risk-Aware Distributional Reinforcement Learning Framework for Multiagent Motion Planning in Dynamic Environments
authors: H. -T. Zhao; H. -N. Wu; X. -Y. Jiang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
abstract: In dynamic and uncertain environments, existing multiagent motion planning methods often exhibit limited adaptability to disturbances and rely heavily on accurate global information. This setting requires a decision framework that can coordinate multiple agents using locally available information while accounting for environmental uncertainty and safety constraints. To address these limitations, this article formulates the obstacle-avoidance motion planning problem as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and proposes an actor–critic distributional reinforcement learning (AC-DRL) algorithm under a multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) paradigm. Each agent’s actor network generates real-time trajectory decisions based on its local observations and the recent action histories, while a centralized critic learns the full return distribution via a quantile representation rather than a scalar expectation. The critic further employs multistep $\lambda $ -returns to smooth the learning targets and improve training stability. In addition, a gated recurrent unit (GRU) is integrated into each actor to encode latent environmental features from partial observations. To improve risk awareness under uncertainty, an adaptive conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) mechanism is introduced, enabling each agent to dynamically adjust its risk level. Extensive simulations across multiple dynamic obstacle scenarios demonstrate that the proposed AC-DRL algorithm achieves higher success rates and improved safety margins than state-of-the-art baselines including the deep Q-network (DQN), artificial potential fields (APFs), and rapidly-exploring random trees (RRTs).

title: Language-Guided Safety-Critical Mixed-Traffic Scenario Generation for Closed-Loop Automated Driving Validation
authors: H. Yao; Z. Wang; C. Hou; J. Chen; G. Zhou; H. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Generating realistic, language-guided traffic scenarios remains a significant challenge, as existing methods struggle to balance high-level semantic controllability with the kinematic constraints of heterogeneous multi-agent interactions. To address this, we introduce language-guided traffic simulation (LangTS), a systematic generation framework featuring an agent-aligned language grounding mechanism that conditions class-specific motion-token representations on natural-language intents. Furthermore, we train a closed-loop autoregressive model with next-token and prompt-mask supervision, which supports language-conditioned rollout with responsive background traffic. To demonstrate its practical utility, we establish an engineering pipeline that mines safety-critical interactions via human-in-the-loop simulation to train a generative library for downstream safety validation. We assess rollout realism using metrics from the Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC) and instruction compliance using instruction-following accuracy (IFA). In downstream studies, LangTS-based policy adaptation lowers target-domain collision rates under both reported protocols, and the pedestrian hazard-trigger rate is 59% versus 41% for OpenSCENARIO. Overall, LangTS provides a framework for autonomous driving validation, bridging human semantic intent with dynamic physical realism in mixed traffic environments.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Finite-Time Fault-Tolerant Practical Tracking of Networked Robot Manipulators Subject to External Disturbances
authors: C. Han; W. Li; M. Shi; B. Lin; K. Qin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: Control timeliness, safety, and robustness are critical performance metrics in modern industrial and cooperative robotics, significantly impacting the effectiveness of cooperative tasks. However, external disturbances, actuator faults, and unknown reference input signals can significantly degrade the above critical performance metrics. To address these challenges, this article investigates the human-in-the-loop finite-time practical consensus tracking problem for networked robot manipulators in the presence of external disturbances and actuator faults. In the considered framework, the reference trajectory is generated by a human-in-the-loop system, where the human operator actively regulates the signal via an unknown control input that is inaccessible to all manipulators. To address this challenge, an extended state observer (ESO) is designed to simultaneously estimate the system states and the unknown human control input. Leveraging the observer estimates, an adaptive fault-tolerant control scheme is subsequently developed to guarantee that all manipulators achieve practical consensus tracking, with the tracking errors converging to prescribed residual sets. The proposed approach ensures that both the estimation and tracking errors converge within the finite time. Rigorous Lyapunov-based analysis is conducted to establish the finite-time stability of the closed-loop system. Simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control strategy.

title: MAPF-HD: Multi-Agent Path Finding in High-Density Environments
authors: H. Makino; S. Ito
venue: IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine
abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) involves planning efficient paths for multiple agents to move simultaneously while avoiding collisions. In typical warehouse environments, agents are often sparsely distributed along aisles; however, increasing the agent density can improve space efficiency. When the agent density is high, it becomes necessary to optimize the paths not only for goal-assigned agents but also for those obstructing them. This study proposes a novel MAPF framework for high-density environments (MAPF-HD). Several studies have explored MAPF in similar settings using integer linear programming (ILP). However, ILP-based methods require substantial computation time to optimize all agent paths simultaneously. Even in small grid-based environments with fewer than 100 cells, these computations can take tens to hundreds of seconds. Such high computational costs render these methods impractical for large-scale applications such as automated warehouses and valet parking. To address these limitations, we introduce the phased null-agent swapping (PHANS) method. PHANS employs a heuristic approach to incrementally swap positions between agents and empty vertices. This method solves the MAPF-HD problem within a few seconds, even in large environments containing more than 700 cells. The proposed method has the potential to improve efficiency in various real-world applications, such as warehouse logistics, traffic management, and crowd control.

title: A Survey of Reinforcement Learning Methods for UAV Path Planning: Safety, Scalability and Real-World Challenges
authors: D. Sharma; P. Naithani; S. Kaushal
venue: 2026 International Conference on Connected Intelligence for Industrial Applications (CI2A)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widespread tools in the modern world specially in surveillance, mapping, disaster management and communication support. Designing safe and efficient flight paths remains challenging, particularly in dynamic or uncertain environments. Various algorithms involving Rapidly-exploring Random Trees (RRT), A-star and potential field techniques struggle in partially known or dynamic environments. Adaptive responses to real-time conditions have driven the use of Reinforcement-Learning, especially Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) as a viable solution to the limitations. This paper is a systematic review of the recent studies on RL-based UAV path planning. The surveyed approaches are classified based on the nature of an RL framework (valuebased, policy-gradient, actor-critic, or multiagent), the nature of the environment (static/dynamic, discrete/ continuous) and the area of application (single UAV, multi-UAV coordination, communication-aware, or adversarial). The comparative analysis is made on the basis of the following aspects: reward function design, state and action representation, learning efficiency, safety constraints, scalability, and validation by simulation or real-world experiments. Key issues such as low sample efficiency, inability to ensure safety, low interpretability, and practical implementation issues are also identified in the paper. Lastly, possible research directions are outlined, focusing on safe RL, transfer learning, hybrid planning, and real-time adaptability. The purpose of this review is to systematically examine the current state of Reinforcement learning-based UAV path planning and to outline prospective research directions in this actively developing field.

title: Visual Safety Mapping for UAV Landings Using Ordinal Regression Networks
authors: S. Abdollahzadeh; M. S. Allili; A. Boulmerka; J. -F. Lapointe
venue: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: As uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) see growing use in civilian applications, reliably identifying safe landing zones (SLZs) in varied environments is essential for autonomous navigation and emergency response. Passive vision sensors offer a low cost, lightweight solution for real-time terrain analysis and 3D scene reconstruction, making them ideal for onboard systems. We introduce ordinal regression safe landing zones netwrok (OR-SLZNet), an original deep learning model based on ordinal regression to predict SLZs from UAV imagery. Unlike prior approaches, OR-SLZNet produces dense, multilevel safety maps by jointly leveraging photometric (e.g., color and texture) and geometric cues (e.g., flatness, slope, and depth), assigning each pixel an ordinal safety score that reflects landing suitability. With real-time inference ($\sim$0.02 s/frame), the model supports onboard deployment and rapid decision-making in time-critical situations. Extensive experiments on five diverse datasets demonstrate OR-SLZNet effectiveness and strong generalization across a wide range of structural complexities.

title: Toward Intent-Driven Autonomous UMEC: An LLM-Based Cognitive Agent for Closed-Loop Trajectory Orchestration
authors: M. Liu; H. Hou; H. -T. Cao; H. Zhao; S. Moussa; M. Alrashoud
venue: IEEE Network
abstract: The highly dynamic environment and heterogeneity inherent in uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (UMEC) networks pose severe challenges to the autonomous orchestration and computing resource scheduling of UAV edge nodes. Conventional optimization algorithms and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) approaches often struggle with poor environmental adaptability, difficulties in handling unstructured constraints, and a lack of physical safety guarantees. To address these limitations, a large language model (LLM)-based cognitive planning framework is designed to achieve intent-driven autonomous network management. This framework establishes an iterative perception-decision-reflection closed-loop mechanism, integrating three core components: Semantic Alignment, which transforms heterogeneous physical signals into structured network intent prompts; Role Injection and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which flexibly generates policies based on service level agreements (SLAs); and an Embodied Reflection Mechanism, which mitigates hallucination-induced risks and corrects physical risks within a simulation loop. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances the survivability and quality of service (QoS) of UAVs in complex and unknown environments. Compared to LLMs without framework support, our approach substantially improves the network service success rate in strongly constrained scenarios and generates highly efficient topological trajectories, validating its potential for the autonomous 6th generation mobile networks (6G).

title: Multi-Agent Systems for Distributed Decision-Making in Autonomous Vehicles
authors: V. Joshi; R. Kachhava; N. Paliwal; S. Madan; N. Singal; V. Sharma
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Technologies (CONIT)
abstract: This research paper aims at analyzing the use of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) in decision-making for self-governed vehicles in a distributed environment and the possibilities of enhancing efficiency and collaboration with reference to centralized systems. Using MAS for autonomous vehicles, traffic situations can be controlled, time can be saved, and accident rates can be minimized, with low communication overhead. This paper also reveals that the MAS algorithms can be very effective in improving the real-time decision making and dealing with the dynamic environments. Nevertheless, the following issues hinder the application of MAS for autonomous vehicles. A challenge that comes with the increase of the number of agents is scalability where there are increased computational and communication costs. Real time decision making is important in order to ensure safety and effective performance, but latency is a problem that can occur. Further, MAS is challenging to design for resilience to environmental variation and to incorporate with the latest technologies such as 5G networks and advanced sensors. As for the future work, it is essential to concentrate on the further advancement of scalable MAS frameworks that would employ distributed and, especially, cloud computing to handle complexity. Real-time processing may be improved by edge computing and to advance the MAS algorithms to make it suitable for various scenarios is also important. Hence, based on the concepts in MAS, there are potential solutions for the application in autonomous vehicle systems but there are some challenges that need to be solved including scalability, real-time performance, robustness, technology issue and ethical concern for it to be effective in its application. As a result, this paper aims at summarising these challenges and discussing possible avenues for future works to contribute to the development of the theory.

title: HiMAP: Hierarchical Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Path Planning
authors: Y. Xing; A. Verma; C. Liu; H. Pan; D. Ding; H. Qian; Y. Bao; W. Yao; C. Feddersen; C. Dean
venue: 2026 IEEE World AI IoT Congress (AIIoT)
abstract: This paper introduces HiMAP, a hierarchical framework for multi-robot path planning that integrates human-in-the-loop guidance with multi-agent reinforcement learning and classical planning. Decision-making is split into three layers: high-level task prioritization with human hints, mid-level assignment and coordination, and low-level motion planning using A* and DWA with conflict checks. Tasks arrive continuously via a Poisson process and require coordinated teams to reach goals within short time windows, modeling realistic collaborative missions. Priority dynamics, travel-time penalties, and confidence-based hints steer selection, while shared rewards encourage cooperation in learning baselines. The hierarchy reduces the joint action space, improves safety, and supports scalability through clear interfaces between layers. We evaluate HiMAP in a grid-world simulator with dynamic task streams and compare against DQN, PPO, DDPG, and tabular Q-learning. Results across baseline comparisons, training curves, agent scaling, and environment variations show that HiMAP achieves higher task throughput and substantially lower collision rates under comparable computational budgets. By separating ranking, assignment, and motion, it supports modular upgrades and tuning of safety and efficiency for diverse environments and mission profiles. This improves interpretability and simplifies integration with operators. The design also enables targeted debugging, facilitates transfer to new maps, and eases integration with operational constraints and mission policies. It also supports incremental deployment, enabling operators to adjust policies safely while preserving throughput under evolving mission requirements and realistic conditions.

title: LLM-based Reinforcement Learning for Controlling Robot Swarms
authors: C. daCunha; G. Giardini; M. Turqueti
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Control (AIRC)
abstract: Coordinating robot swarms is challenging due to the complexity of the system and the lack of systematic design methods. Existing approaches trade interpretability for performance: hand-designed controllers are transparent but don’t generalize, while learning methods require millions of samples and produce black-box policies. We propose an LLM-in-the-loop reinforcement learning framework where large language models iteratively design controllers using performance metrics as reward signals. We compare four LLMs (Grok, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT) on cohesive motion control using an extended Vicsek model. Grok achieves 94% of the theoretical maximum in one iteration; Claude converges in 9 iterations. However, ChatGPT’s performance collapses after iteration 6, revealing refinement failure modes. Our complexity analysis shows dynamical richness strongly correlates with performance (71%) while logical complexity does not (18%), suggesting effective swarm control requires continuous laws over discrete switching. Results demonstrate LLMs can accelerate controller design while maintaining interpretability, but demand rigorous validation for safety-critical applications.

title: NSF-HRPT: Neural Semantic Field meets Hierarchical Risk Perception Tree for Safety-Critical Scenario Assessment
authors: Y. Zhao; J. Pan; T. Hu; M. Yin; F. Yang; J. Liu; X. Liang
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: The ability to accurately assess and anticipate risks in safety-critical scenarios is crucial for autonomous driving systems. While existing research has made progress in collision prediction, accurately quantifying risk levels from monocular vision inputs remains challenging due to the complex dynamics of multi-agent interactions and the inherent uncertainty in real-world environments. To address these challenges, we present NSF-HRPT, a novel framework that combines learning-based perception with structured reasoning for quantitative risk assessment. Our approach features a Neural Semantic Field (NSF) that learns to model scene semantics, trajectory predictions, and probabilistic Time-to-Collision (TTC) distributions from simulation data. During inference, the pre-trained NSF serves as a prior for our Hierarchical Risk Perception Tree (HRPT), which enables efficient parallel computation and spatial reasoning about multi-agent risks. Additionally, we introduce a Sim2Real enhancement strategy that improves real-world applicability without retraining by incorporating priors from foundation models. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on synthetic benchmarks and delivers competitive, near-state-of-the-art results on real-world datasets for both TTC estimation accuracy and risk localization precision. The proposed method provides an effective solution for real-time risk awareness from monocular camera inputs.

title: Holonic Multi-Agent System to Develop Digital Twins Ecosystems
authors: V. Melo; F. de la Prieta; P. Leitao
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) is an emergent technology driven by the advances of Industry 4.0, being considered a significant component of the digital transformation. This approach relies on the integration of physical assets and their corresponding digital representations, ensuring the bidirectional synchronization and enabling the real-time monitoring and decision-support through, e.g., diagnosis, prediction, or optimization, based on advanced data analysis and simulation. The most common approach to design and implement DTs follows a centralized structure, considering the adoption of a digital representation that encompasses the entire asset under analysis. However, this centralized DT structure can be very monolithic, rigid, and inflexible to face the structural and behavioral complexity of the asset, as well as to properly address the assets life cycle. Insights from the Multi-Agent Systems and holonic principles can be used as inspiration to develop distributed organizational structures of DTs, taking advantage of their inherent characteristics of autonomy, cooperation and composition to build networks of interconnected DTs. Therefore, this paper proposes a holonic agent-based distributed DT architecture to face these requirements, framed with the ISO 23247 standard, and presents the design principles, dynamic behavior of individual DTs, and interaction patterns to enable interoperability between individual DTs as part of an ecosystem. A case study related to a modular conveyor transfer system is used to illustrate the application and validation of the proposed approach.

title: Conflict-Based Lazy Search for Fast Multimanipulator Planning
authors: D. Zheng; Z. Wang; S. Wang; Y. Lu; B. He; H. Wang; P. Tsiotras
venue: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: Employing multiple manipulators can boost efficiency and accomplish tasks that a single manipulator cannot do. However, real-time planning for multiple manipulators in a cluttered workspace still poses significant challenges for planning algorithms. This article proposes a new planning algorithm called Conflict-Based Lazy Search (CBLS) for multimanipulator planning. CBLS is built on Conflict-Based Search (CBS), an efficient multiagent pathfinding (MAPF) algorithm that has shown an order of magnitude speedup over previous approaches [1], [2]. CBS addresses MAPF by solving many single-agent pathfinding (SAPF) problems. Thus, its planning time directly depends on the efficiency of the SAPF algorithm adopted. Our CBLS algorithm enhances CBS with precomputation and lazy search. First, a lazily evaluated graph with controlled sparsity is precomputed for a single manipulator. Second, we propose the Lazy Edged-based A* (LEA*) for efficient SAPF. Since edge evaluation is the computational bottleneck of manipulator planning, LEA* uses lazy search and an edge queue to reduce the number of edge evaluations. We show that LEA* is optimally vertex efficient and has improved edge efficiency compared to A*. We apply the proposed CBLS to multimanipulator planning problems and show its superior performance by comparing it with CBS and a sampling-based algorithm, namely, RRT-Connect.

title: Resilient User-Centric UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing: Joint Task Offloading and Resource Allocation via Hierarchical Hybrid Sequential Optimization
authors: S. Pang; Y. Liu; J. J. P. C. Rodrigues; M. Wang; T. Ding
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
abstract: The user-centric network (UCN) paradigm provides a promising foundation for mobile edge computing (MEC) by mitigating severe cell-edge interference through multi-access point (AP) cooperation. However, most user-centric MEC schemes rely on ground APs, whose rigid deployment makes them vulnerable to post-disaster damage and severe blockage, delaying service recovery and restricting coverage. To address this issue, this paper develops a user-centric MEC architecture based on uncrewed aerial vehicle access points (UAV-APs), which leverage rapid deployment and flexible coverage to provide more reliable services in dynamic environments. Specifically, we formulate a multi-level delay-energy coupling optimization problem that jointly accounts for task offloading and resource allocation, thereby enabling more effective optimization of both communication performance and energy consumption. The problem is challenging because shared resource competition may cause policy oscillation in parallel updates, while existing action-modeling methods remain insufficient for capturing the coupling between discrete offloading and continuous power control in the access–fronthaul–edge computing process. To solve this problem, we propose HH-SEQUEL, a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework with level-wise hybrid discrete-continuous action parameterization and sequential cross-level updates, enabling end-to-end joint optimization of offloading and resource allocation under delay-energy coupling. Simulation results show that our method reduces latency by 21.39%–65.31% compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and lowers energy consumption by up to 93.89% against baseline approaches.

title: Safety Analysis of Over-the-Air Updates for CPS: A Contract-Driven Approach
authors: N. M. Bisceglia; A. F. Zanenga; M. Askarpour; S. Kokaly; S. Ramesh; M. Chechik; C. Menghi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) updates are becoming a standard practice for upgrading Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) software, allowing software systems to be modified through a wireless network. They are beneficial in several contexts. For example, in the automotive domain, OTA updates enable manufacturers to update vehicle software without physical access. However, the considerable number of products (e.g., vehicles within the fleet) and frequent changes and updates to software components can generate many software configurations that are impossible to analyze beforehand without any automated support. This problem hampers the verification of the system’s safety. This paper proposes a contract-driven framework for reasoning about the safety of OTA updates. Our framework supports (a) contract composition, which enables reasoning about the behavior composition of different software components, and (b) verification of component substitutability, which allows checking if the software component deployed by an OTA update can replace another component without generating any safety breach. We rigorously define our framework and formally prove that if the OTA update ensures the satisfaction of its contract, the system (safety) properties are preserved. We propose an instance of our solution that targets CPS designed with Simulink® System Composer, a widely used tool for modeling the different components of the system architecture and their interaction. We propose using Simulink® Requirements Tables to express the contracts of CPS components, as they enable engineers to model the system requirements using pre/post-conditions within their Simulink® models. We implemented our solution as a software prototype that extends Theano, a tool that enables engineers to verify the consistency and completeness of Requirements Tables. We evaluated our solution by considering the Ten Lockheed Martin Cyber-Physical Problems. We defined 20 OTA updates and effectively identified issues in 9 of them. We analyzed and fixed the problems, inspecting each unsafe OTA update to understand the causes of the safety breaches. After fixing the problems, Theano confirmed the safety of all OTA updates. Theano required less than a minute to analyze each OTA update, making it practical for industrial applications.

title: Safe Navigation and Formation Control for UAV Swarms Under Wind Disturbances
authors: V. Nikolakakis; A. Eqtami
venue: 2026 7th International Conference in Electronic Engineering & Information Technology (EEITE)
abstract: The deployment of autonomous multi-UAV swarms in complex, dynamic environments requires robust navigation strategies that ensure both formation integrity and collision avoidance. This paper presents a decentralized, reactive planning framework for multi-agent systems operating under continuous aerodynamic disturbances, such as wind gusts. Building upon existing CLF-CBF-QP-based control formulations, the proposed approach focuses on implementation-oriented aspects, emphasizing physical feasibility and real-time execution. Leveraging an optimization-based architecture, the framework utilizes Control Lyapunov Functions (CLFs) for trajectory generation and Robust Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) as a real-time safety filter against dynamic obstacles and inter-agent collisions. To account for unpredictable wind disturbances, a robustness margin is explicitly incorporated into the safety constraints, ensuring physically executable and safe avoidance maneuvers. The decentralized scheme is evaluated through simulation studies, demonstrating the swarm's ability to elastically reconfigure its formation to bypass dynamic threats while maintaining safety clearances. The results highlight the practical applicability of the framework for real-world robotic operations.

title: Combinatorial Control Barrier Functions: Nested Boolean and p-choose-r Compositions of Safety Constraints
authors: P. Ong; H. Lee; T. G. Molnar; D. Panagou; A. D. Ames
venue: 2026 American Control Conference (ACC)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of composing multiple control barrier functions (CBFs)—and matrix control barrier functions (MCBFs)—through logical and combinatorial operations. Standard CBF formulations naturally enable conjunctive (AND) combinations, but disjunctive (OR) and more general logical structures introduce nonsmoothness and possibly a combinatorial blow-up in the number of logical combinations. We introduce the framework of combinatorial CBFs that addresses p-choose-r safety specifications and their nested composition. The proposed framework ensures safety for the exact safe set in a scalable way, using the original number of primitive constraints. We establish theoretical guarantees on safety under these compositions, and we demonstrate their use on a patrolling problem in a multi-agent system.

title: Self-Triggered Connectivity Maintenance of a Teleoperated Multi-Agent System with Input Saturation
authors: L. Yang; X. Zhou; Z. Yan
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed collaborative control architecture to address the control issue of multi-agent bilateral teleoperation systems subject to input saturation constraints. This architecture incorporates two core mechanisms: dynamic saturation compensation and self-triggered communication, which effectively suppress tracking oscillations caused by input saturation and significantly reduce communication load while ensuring global connectivity. Ultimately, collision avoidance between agents and obstacles, asymptotic speed synchronisation, and maintenance of the desired interagent distances were achieved. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: Safe and Scalable Multi-Agent Optimization for Autonomous Electric Taxi Dispatching via a Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning Framework
authors: M. Zhao; Y. Zou; J. Wang; D. Li; Q. Yang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The widespread deployment of Autonomous Electric Taxis (AETs) in smart cities introduces critical challenges in large-scale dispatching and charging coordination under energy and operational constraints. Traditional Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) approaches often struggle to ensure both policy feasibility and system scalability in such complex, dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose a safe and scalable two-stage MARL framework for AET dispatching optimization. The proposed method, named Filter-to-Optimization Pipeline (FTOP), decouples constraint handling from reward maximization through a hierarchical architecture. In the first stage, an Action Classification-based Action Filter (ACAF) employs value decomposition to eliminate infeasible actions, enforcing energy and conflict constraints. In the second stage, a Utility-Prioritized Maximization Policy (UPMP) performs a model-based search within the filtered feasible space to optimize system-level utility. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FTOP achieves significant improvements in total fleet revenue, constraint satisfaction, and scalability across varying urban scenarios. These results highlight the potential of decomposed MARL strategies in solving large-scale, safety-critical optimization problems in autonomous transportation systems. Note to Practitioners—As autonomous electric taxis (AETs) continue to scale in urban environments, ensuring safe and efficient dispatch under energy limitations and coordination constraints becomes increasingly critical. This study proposes FTOP, a two-stage MARL framework that systematically addresses these challenges across three tightly integrated layers.At the safety estimation layer, FTOP incorporates the Action Classification-based Action Filter (ACAF) module, which encodes energy thresholds and action conflicts as constraints within a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). Leveraging feature-guided state stabilization, ACAF filters out 99.7% of infeasible actions and reduces energy violations to 0.4 per 10 hours—effectively mitigating high-risk behaviors such as battery depletion. At the coordination mechanism layer, FTOP introduces the Utility-Prioritized Multi-objective Planning (UPMP) strategy, which decouples long-term policy learning from short-term safety-critical decision-making. This hybrid planning approach enables support for heterogeneous actions (e.g., charging and dispatching) while ensuring constraint compliance. As a result, system-wide revenue increases by 23.8%, and the action conflict rate drops by 38.7%. At the system-level evaluation layer, extensive experiments involving 200 AETs and 15 charging stations confirm FTOP’s robustness under large-scale, dynamic urban scenarios. These results validate FTOP as a scalable, constraint-aware framework for safe and efficient multi-agent fleet dispatch.

title: Parallel Nursing: Enhancing Postoperative Nursing With LLM Agent Systems
authors: X. Qiao; J. Wang; M. Zhang; F. Lin; P. Ye; Q. Ni; F. -Y. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
abstract: Postoperative nursing plays a crucial role in healthcare by preventing complications such as infections and thrombosis through timely risk assessment and intervention. However, current nursing tools lack dynamic and personalized predictive capabilities, limiting their effectiveness. This article proposes the parallel nursing framework, which integrates large language models (LLMs) with the virtual-real synergy of parallel systems, leveraging the artificial systems, computational experiments, and parallel execution (ACP) approach. The framework utilizes LLM agents to enable proactive, precise, and personalized risk management within a closed-loop system. Building on this framework, we developed NursingGPT, a multiagent system with monitoring, prediction, simulation, decision, and communication agents that analyze patient data and predict risks. It provides real-time, tailored nursing interventions to address diverse needs. Its applications in infection risk management, complication prevention, personalized care, and cross-institutional knowledge sharing highlight its potential to enhance patient recovery, improve nursing quality, and reduce complications, offering a scalable, intelligent solution for postoperative nursing.

title: Traffic-Aware Emergency Vehicle Routing Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: T. Kaur; S. Mungara; V. Kolluru; R. Bhandari; K. R. Panwar; P. Krishnanjaneyulu
venue: 2026 Conference on Latest Innovations in Computing and Knowledge (CLICK)
abstract: The proposed system, overall, can be considered as a strong, extensible and context sensitive approach to the problem of navigation of emergency vehicles in smart cities. It bridges the gap between the learning-based routing and the real-world operational constraints, thus, making it very appropriate for the next generation intelligent transportation and emergency response systems. In SUMO, the training is carried out via consecutive simulation episodes where the agent: Observes the environment makes a decision by an, greedy or stochastic policy is awarded a reward based on routing outcome performs updates of network parameters through backpropagation to make the training process stable experienced replay and target networks are also part of it. For safety and legality, a route generated by an A* planner is used to validate each action selected by the RL system. Strictly enforce one-way streets and turn restrictions Avoid blocked or accident- prone road segments Generate collision free and feasible paths Follow maximum speed and lane constraints If an RL decision is found to violate constraints, the A* planner.

title: A Survey on Autonomous Compliance Enforcement using Agentic AI
authors: S. Soudagar; V. S. Rajpurohit; A. Shahapurkar; S. S. Sannakki
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Sustainable Computing and Smart Systems (ICSCSS)
abstract: Infrastructure compliance enforcement is increasingly considered for agentic AI systems that can plan, act and self-correct over many steps. A structured examination of the literature reveals several significant gaps. Multi-agent compliance pipelines have been architecturally proposed in several works but none report a functioning prototype with measurable compliance outcomes. Theoretical discussions extensively cover the safety hazards arising from the granting of autonomous control to an LLM agent over remediation of infrastructure. However, there are no documented real-world cases of an LLM agent outputting an operationally dangerous output in a compliance setting. The concept of utilising cross-run memory for compliance agents has been recognised but no lightweight implementation has yet been demonstrated to change the behaviour of agents. This paper surveys the field along seven dimensions: agentic architectures, compliance automation, LLM output safety, anomaly detection, multi-agent coordination, statefulness, and cloud-native deployment drawing on 46 representative works. Six specific gaps are identified through structured analysis. A hybrid architecture is then proposed that integrates the Isolation Forest anomaly detection with a four-agent LLM pipeline consisting of an Analyser that interprets system state and prior run history, a Planner that generates remediation strategies, a Verifier that applies LLM safety constraints, and an Explainer that produces human-readable audit reports. The architecture further incorporates deterministic value-level validation and persistent SQLite-based cross-run memory. In controlled experiments, the system improved compliance scores from 60% to 100%. Notably, a concrete instance of LLM overreach was observed during testing: the Planner agent generated a remediation plan that would have locked out SSH access by closing all network ports, a failure mode not previously reported in empirical literature. The paper concludes with a feature-by-feature comparison across twelve prominent works, a discussion of open challenges, and a proposed hybrid cloud extension.

title: Safe Neurosymbolic Learning and Control
authors: S. Bansal; J. F. Fisac
venue: Neurosymbolic AI: Foundations and Applications
abstract: Machine learning has enabled intelligent systems to perceive, adapt, and make decisions in new situations with remarkable efficiency. However, as these systems are increasingly deployed in high‐stakes applications – such as autonomous driving, robotics, and healthcare – the need to ensure their safety has become paramount. This chapter explores the emerging field of safe neurosymbolic learning and control, which combines the strengths of machine learning with symbolic reasoning to design controllers that are both data‐driven and provably safe. We focus on self‐supervised and neurosymbolic reinforcement learning approaches that enable safe control by leveraging structured knowledge from formal verification approaches, such as Hamilton – Jacobi reachability analysis. By integrating safety considerations directly into the learning and control process, these methods offer a pathway toward learning safe controllers directly from data, leading to a reliable deployment of intelligent systems in real‐world scenarios. We also discuss mechanisms to provide statistical and worst‐case safety assurances for the learned controllers. The chapter concludes by highlighting key research frontiers at the intersection of safe neurosymbolic learning and control.

title: Flexible Performance Function-Based Time-Varying Formation Control for Second-Order Systems Under Safety Constraints
authors: Y. Chen; J. Huang; X. Nian; W. Zhong; X. Dai; J. J. Liu
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: This article investigates the time-varying formation control problem of second-order multiagent systems with collision avoidance and connectivity preservation capabilities. To guarantee persistent connectivity of the communication topology during the formation process, a performance function-based method is employed to impose constraints on the formation error norms between agents with communication links. Meanwhile, an improved potential function is introduced to enable effective obstacle avoidance between agents and obstacles. To achieve a balance between performance constraints and collision avoidance requirements, an auxiliary system is designed to adjust the boundaries of the performance function adaptively. In addition, to handle unknown disturbances in the system, a disturbance observer featuring convergence within a predefined time is developed. The effectiveness of the proposed control method is demonstrated through simulation and UAV experiments.

title: Guide Policy-Enabled Safe Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Frequency Control in Low-Inertia Grids With Inverter Interface Resources
authors: J. Hu; Q. Xu; Z. Dong
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Frequency stability in inverter-based power systems is increasingly challenged due to the reduction of mechanical inertia and damping. Although several learning-based frequency control methods have been developed for low-inertia grids, they still exhibit limitations in action safety, learning efficiency, and policy coordination. This article proposes a guide policy-enabled multiagent reinforcement learning method for coordinated and safe frequency control. Specifically, a guide policy-based action filter corrects improper actions and forms a safe curriculum for the training policy. Moreover, a surrogate model-enabled planning process promotes safe exploration and policy coordination by refining potentially unsafe actions through temporary simulated experiences, without applying those actions directly to the environment. In addition, a behavior-cloning mechanism mitigates environmental nonstationarity and stabilizes multiagent learning. Electromagnetic transient simulations on a modified IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed method reduces the maximum frequency deviation of VSG5 from −0.2556 to −0.0709 Hz and its maximum rate of change of frequency from −4.9268 to −0.7575 Hz/s while improving action safety, learning efficiency, and policy coordination over existing methods.

title: MIPA: Multi-Agent Interval Analysis via Value-Flow and LLM-Solver Co-Reasoning
authors: X. Yang; G. Yue; G. Liu
venue: 2026 6th International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science (ISCTIS)
abstract: Interval information is essential for program optimization, safety checking, and bug diagnosis. Current interval analysis pipelines face two persistent limitations: (1) graph-only static propagation loses precision on complex control flow and cross-procedural reasoning, and (2) large language model (LLM)-only inference lacks numerical guarantees and can become unstable with long-context inputs. We propose MIPA, a multi-agent architecture that strengthens interval analysis through persistent value-flow graphs (PVFG), LLM-based intention and constraint inference, and SMT-based numerical validation (with Z3). MIPA decomposes the task into specialized agents for retrieval, semantic inference, solving, and verification, and performs dual-channel reasoning: (1) graph tracing for structural evidence and (2) semantic completion for latent constraints. A verification-aware fusion stage then resolves conflicts and outputs interval bounds, confidence scores, and evidence chains.We evaluate MIPA on two benchmark sources (Juliet Test Suite and DaCapo) using a selected 500-query subset, and we further evaluate it on six external open-source projects. On the selected 500-query subset, MIPA achieves 83.61% precision, 83.86% coverage, and 83.73% F1, indicating a balanced precision–coverage profile among the compared methods. External evaluation reports three publicly assigned CVEs, suggesting practical security relevance.

title: Adaptive-Horizon Conflict-Based Search for Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: J. Li; F. Pecora; R. Zhang; G. Zardini
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) is a core coordination problem for large robot fleets in automated warehouses and logistics. Existing approaches are typically either open-loop planners, which must compute complete trajectories before execution and therefore may incur substantial planning latency before actions can be taken, or closed-loop heuristics without reliable performance guarantees, limiting their use in safety-critical deployments. This paper presents Anytime Closed-Loop Conflict-Based Search (ACCBS), a closed-loop algorithm built on a finite-horizon variant of Conflict-Based Search (CBS) with a horizon-changing mechanism inspired by iterative horizon-deepening in Model Predictive Control (MPC). ACCBS dynamically adjusts the planning horizon based on the available computational budget, and reuses a single constraint tree to enable seamless transitions between horizons. As a result, it produces high-quality feasible solutions quickly while being asymptotically optimal as the budget increases, exhibiting anytime behavior. Extensive case studies demonstrate that ACCBS achieves a favorable balance between computational efficiency, solution quality, and execution flexibility, while naturally accommodating online disturbances through its closed-loop formulation.

title: Multi-UAV Cooperative Interception Planning in Obstacle Environments Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: J. Fang; H. Jia; W. Meng; B. Wang; X. Wang; J. Zhang
venue: 2026 6th International Symposium on Intelligent Robotics and Systems (ISoIRS)
abstract: To address the security challenge of intercepting Low-Slow-Small (LSS) aerial vehicles in dense urban building environments, where traditional interception methods are hindered by severe occlusion, this paper proposes a multi-UAV cooperative dynamic interception planning algorithm based on multi-agent reinforcement learning. The goal is to achieve reliable and safe interception of intruders through intelligent coordination of multiple high-speed fixed-wing UAVs. Building upon the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) framework, the proposed method introduces a composite state representation that explicitly incorporates repulsive perception from an artificial potential field, enabling agents to quantitatively sense the direction and magnitude of obstacle threats from local observations. A priority experience replay (PER) mechanism combined with cosine-annealing learning-rate scheduling is adopted to enhance policy convergence through prioritized sampling and dynamic learning-rate adjustment. Furthermore, a multi-objective reward function is designed to harmonize target approaching, obstacle avoidance, and formation maintenance. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves an interception success rate of $\mathbf{9 8. 0 8 \%}$ with a zero collision rate over 1,200 randomly generated dense-obstacle test scenarios. The results validate the effectiveness, robustness, and safety of the framework for intelligent cooperative interception in complex urban settings, providing a technical reference for the development of intelligent UAV countermeasure systems in urban security.

title: Research and Implementation of a Bearing Fault Diagnosis Large Model Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration and Multi-RAG Fusion
authors: J. Jia; M. Chen; L. Zhang; Y. Zhang; J. Qiu; H. Ji
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Mechatronics Technology and Intelligent Manufacturing (ICMTIM)
abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis is critical for rotating machinery safety, yet existing methods are inefficient, poorly generalizable, and lack interpretability. Large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-agent technologies offer new solutions, but a systematic framework for trustworthy, interpretable, and fully automated diagnosis remains lacking. This study proposes a bearing fault diagnosis large model based on multi-agent collaboration and multi-RAG fusion. A diagnosis rule knowledge base is constructed, and a three-agent collaborative architecture is designed to suppress LLM hallucinations via specialized division of labor. A prototype system is developed and validated through a case study, achieving full-process closed-loop operation. This study provides a reusable technical paradigm for next-generation industrial intelligent diagnosis systems.

title: On the Development of Collaborative Turtlebots
authors: E. Hansson; C. -H. Min; H. Salamy
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The concept of automating repetitive tasks by employing robots persists at the forefront of the modern age. Many applications involve a single robot designed for a specific purpose; however, ongoing research into Multi-Robot Systems offers an alternative: using a fleet of robots to coordinate on tasks. This paper presents a project for multi-robot communication under the ROS2 Humble framework. The goal of this paper is to establish a unique Collaborative TurtleBots (CTB) framework for reliable communication between multiple TurtleBot3 robots.

title: Attention-Enhanced Feedback Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network for Multi-Agent Formation State Prediction
authors: L. Fan; J. Gu; X. Wang; Y. Zhai; S. Ma
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: Multi-agent formation state prediction provides reliable perception support for cooperative control and decisionmaking of unmanned systems, which is crucial for improving formation control accuracy and adaptability in complex environments. Existing methods struggle to capture spatiotemporal dependencies and correct prediction errors caused by dynamic disturbances. This paper presents an AttentionEnhanced Feedback Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (AF-STGNN), which integrates dual attention modules and a feedback mechanism to achieve high-precision multi-agent state prediction. The attention modules adaptively focus on important agents and temporal segments, while the feedback mechanism dynamically adjusts inputs using prediction residuals. A UAV formation navigating an urban canyon environment is used as a case study, with a three-dimensional dataset containing noise and obstacles generated via MATLAB simulation for model training and evaluation. Experimental results show that AFSTGNN significantly outperforms baseline models in prediction accuracy and stability.

title: Distributed Time-Varying Formation Control With Obstacle Avoidance of Multiagent Systems Under Switching Topologies
authors: Y. Su; Y. Sun; X. Yang; W. Yu; X. Yang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics
abstract: Distributed formation tracking control with obstacle avoidance of multiagent systems (MASs) under random switching topologies and external disturbances is considered in this article. To achieve the complex objective, an effective control strategy is developed in three steps. First, under the transition probability (TP)-based mode-dependent average dwell-time (MDADT) switching topologies, a distributed objective trajectory achieves almost sure global exponential tracking of the desired formation trajectory. Second, a safe objective trajectory approach is designed by geometrically projecting the unsafe parts of the existing formation trajectory onto the boundary of the obstacle region. Finally, an integral-multiplicative barrier Lyapunov function (IMBLF) is proposed to allow agents to track the safe objective trajectory, where the IMBLF can further guarantee the safety of the MASs. One of the interesting merits of our results is that the impulsive increasing of Lyapunov function at switching instants which is necessary for classical analysis methods has been removed. The feasibility of the proposed formation control method with obstacle avoidance is verified by simulations.

title: Hybrid Aerial–Ground Wireless Power Transfer via UAVs: Dynamic Charging Scheduling for AGVs in Smart Factories
authors: Z. -Y. A. Chen; C. -C. Lin; S. -Y. Zhang; Y. -T. Chou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles
abstract: Continuous operation of automated guided vehicles (AGVs) in intelligent factories is often interrupted by battery depletion and additional travel to fixed charging stations. Although wireless power transfer (WPT) can reduce physical connector wear and enable flexible charging, its use for AGV energy support must account for charging efficiency loss, uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) hovering consumption, propulsion energy, and operational safety constraints. This work develops a physically parameterized hybrid aerial-ground energy-management framework in which UAVs equipped with WPT modules (UWs) provide supplementary and on-demand charging support to AGV fleets. The coupled UW-AGV charging mission is formulated as an episodic Markov decision process. To support real-time decision-making, a feature-based expected SARSA (FES) algorithm is developed to compress the state-action space through five problem-specific feature functions associated with energy cost, downtime penalty, charging efficiency, spatial proximity, and battery-safety margin. The proposed model explicitly incorporates WPT efficiency, UAV hovering energy, and propulsion-related energy consumption. Simulation experiments compare the proposed FES algorithm with feature-based SARSA, rule-based, and random baselines, and further analyze convergence behavior, computational scalability, UW deployment density, and the sensitivity of system performance to WPT efficiency, UW hovering or docking-maintenance power, and propulsion energy. The results show that FES provides computationally efficient and interpretable scheduling for hybrid AGV-UAV energy coordination, while limitations of large-scale UAV-assisted WPT deployment are explicitly discussed.

title: Proactive Multi-Agent Systems for Autonomous Code Generation and Software Maintenance
authors: S. Elsayed; S. Abubaker; M. Ali; M. Elbtity
venue: 2026 IEEE 50th Annual Computers, Software, and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: The evolution from reactive to proactive AI systems represents a paradigm shift in software engineering, enabling autonomous agents to anticipate requirements, plan complex workflows, and execute multi-step development tasks without human intervention. This paper presents a novel multi-agent architecture for autonomous code generation and software maintenance in enterprise environments. Our framework integrates specialized AI agents for requirements analysis, code synthesis, testing, and deployment, coordinated through a hierarchical planning system with adaptive decision-making capabilities. The system employs reinforcement learning to optimize task allocation, learn from code review feedback, and improve over time. Experimental evaluation on real-world enterprise codebases demonstrates that our proactive agent system achieves 87.3% automated issue resolution, reduces bug fix latency by 62%, and maintains code quality metrics comparable to human developers. The framework successfully handles complex refactoring tasks, security vulnerability remediation, and feature implementation with minimal human oversight, representing a significant advancement toward fully autonomous software engineering workflows.

title: Role-Structured Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Airship-Guided UAV Pursuit Tracking
authors: K. Yang; Y. Zhou; M. Zhu; Y. Zhang
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robot Perception and Intelligent Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper investigates heterogeneous aerial pursuit tracking with one high-endurance airship, multiple UAV pursuers, and evasive targets. The task is formulated as a partially observed mixed cooperative-adversarial game under centralized training and decentralized execution. A role-difference-potential multi-agent reinforcement learning framework is proposed, in which each agent maintains an individual actor and critics are shared at the role level with identity conditioning. To improve cooperative credit assignment, pursuer optimization combines potential-based shaping with counterfactual one-step difference rewards. The potential function integrates coverage guidance, approach pressure, capture-neighborhood entry, encirclement quality, and safety regularization; actions are parameterized by bounded speed and yaw rate for kinematic consistency. Simulation results show stable coordinated closure and reliable capture, indicating that role-structured entropy-regularized learning with difference-potential rewards is a practical baseline for heterogeneous pursuit tasks.

title: A Comparative Study of Environmental Sensing for Ambient Intelligence with Distributed Sensor Networks and Mobile Robots
authors: M. Radović; I. Šenk
venue: 2026 25th International Symposium INFOTEH-JAHORINA (INFOTEH)
abstract: Ambient Intelligence (AmI) systems depend on reliable environmental sensing to support comfort, safety, and energy efficiency in indoor spaces. This paper reviews three sensing paradigms for monitoring indoor environmental conditions: distributed wireless sensor networks (WSN), mobile robots employed as sensing platforms, and hybrid architectures that integrate static and mobile sensing. Typical system architectures and operational characteristics are examined, with emphasis on the trade-offs between continuous temporal monitoring at fixed locations and adaptive spatial mapping enabled by mobility. Based on this analysis, a decision framework is introduced that defines practical selection criteria including spatial and temporal requirements, cost (CAPEX/OPEX), reliability, safety, privacy, scalability, and infrastructure constraints, and illustrates how these criteria guide the choice between WSN-based, robot-based, and hybrid solutions. Finally, directions for future research are outlined, focusing on quantitative validation and software-supported methods for automated sensing architecture selection in AmI systems.

title: ChatAgents: Enhancing Autonomous Decision-Making in Multi-Agent Conversations via Intrinsic Motivation
authors: T. Huang; J. Zhang; P. Yan; R. Yang; X. Li
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Materials (ICAIM)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit advanced language capabilities, yet current agents lack genuine behavioral autonomy, operating on predefined logic rather than dynamically deciding when and how to participate in conversations. This paper proposes ChatAgents, a framework that endows agents with intrinsic motivation for autonomous decision-making in multi-agent group discussions. The framework introduces two key mechanisms: a context-driven module activator enabling dynamic memory retrieval and goal analysis based on real-time dialogue, and a preemptive speaking mechanism where agents autonomously compete for turn-taking based on internal willingness and simulated reaction times. In simulated team-building scenarios, agents exhibited emergent social behaviors-including spontaneous leadership, conflict mediation, and innovative proposal generation-without external intervention, while maintaining consistent personality traits throughout interactions. This work demonstrates a pathway toward more authentic autonomous systems by enabling LLM agents to replicate the complexity of human conversational dynamics.

title: Fuzzing Large Language Model Agents: A Taxonomy, Engineering Framework, and Evaluation Protocol
authors: Y. Cao
venue: Artificial Intelligence Science and Engineering
abstract: Agents powered by large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate as closed-loop decision systems that retrieve external context and memory, plan actions, invoke tools, and alter environment state. This autonomy creates trajectory-level risks, including indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, unsafe tool invocation, authorization violations, and erroneous environment-conditioned actions, which cannot be assessed adequately by prompt-level testing alone. This paper presents a taxonomy and engineering framework for fuzz-testing LLM-based agents. We formulate agent fuzzing as structured perturbation over user instructions, retrieved context, memory states, tool parameters, and environment feedback, and organize the design space by interaction surface, mutation strategy, execution environment, behavioral safety evaluator, and behavioral coverage objective. The framework integrates seed construction, semantics-aware mutation, trajectory-guided exploration, sandboxed execution, runtime monitoring, behavioral coverage feedback, risk scoring, and failure reproduction. A controlled study with 900 sandboxed trajectories across file-management, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), email, and database scenarios illustrates the workflow. It shows that semantics-aware and state-guided mutation strategies uncover more testbed failures than rule-based mutation. We further discuss evaluator reliability, long-horizon testing, memory safety, multi-agent interactions, scalability, and external validity.

title: Mutual-Rendezvous Control and Feature-Compatible Landing Optimization for Heterogeneous UAV–USV Fleets
authors: J. Ding; H. -T. Zhang; B. -B. Hu; W. Jiang; X. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: In this article, we propose a mutual-rendezvous controller to guide the heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) to approach close enough such that the states of the USVs become available for the UAVs through limited-range communication and observation. By this means, we design a coordinated landing algorithm for UAVs to land on feature-compatible USVs according to optimal pairwise heterogeneous feature matching. Significantly, a minimum-energy operation execution framework is developed by formulating control barrier function (CBF) constraints that encode subgroup formation, leader rendezvous, collision avoidance, and connectivity maintenance. This framework enables the UAVs and USVs to independently achieve their designated circular formations and coordinate rendezvous, relying solely on communication between the leading UAV and USV. Subsequently, a landing optimization strategy is devised for the UAVs, incorporating heterogeneous feature compatibility, allocation requirements, and collision-free landing convergence through additional CBF constraints. The sufficient conditions for the asymptotic convergence of the resulting closed-loop systems are derived. Finally, extensive simulations are performed to verify the effectiveness and robustness of the present design.

title: Quality or Quantity? Error-Informed Selective Online Learning with Gaussian Processes in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Z. Yang; X. Dai; J. Cheng; Y. Huang; P. Shi
venue: IEEE/CAA Journal of Automatica Sinica
abstract: Effective cooperation is pivotal in distributed learning for multi-agent systems, where the interplay between the quantity and quality of the machine learning models is crucial. This paper reveals the irrationality of indiscriminate inclusion of all models on agents for joint prediction, highlighting the imperative to prioritize quality over quantity in cooperative learning. Specifically, we present the first selective online learning framework for distributed Gaussian process (GP) regression, namely distributed error-informed GP (EIGP), that enables each agent to assess its neighboring collaborators, using the proposed selection function to choose the higher quality GP models with less prediction errors. Moreover, algorithmic enhancements are embedded within the EIGP, including a greedy algorithm (gEIGP) for accelerating prediction and an adaptive algorithm (aEIGP) for improving prediction accuracy. In addition, approaches for fast prediction and model update are introduced in conjunction with the error-informed quantification term iteration and a data deletion strategy to achieve real-time learning operations. Numerical simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed methodology, showcasing its superiority over the state-of-the-art distributed GP methods with different benchmarks.

title: Multi-Robot Cooperative Transport via Rigid Formation Control With Convex-Hull Planning
authors: Y. Bai; Z. Luo; Q. Wang; Z. Sun; Q. Wang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: This letter investigates the cooperative control problem for networked mobile manipulators (NMMs) in cooperative transport tasks. Our approach enables independent design of the end-effector controller and base motion planner through dynamic decoupling. For end-effector position control, we propose a novel rigid formation control method to regulate the relative distances and directions of end effectors, which are constrained to be aligned with the payload’s geometry. For mobile base coordination, we develop a convex hull-based motion planner guaranteeing collision-free navigation with homotopy-preserving trajectories in cluttered environments. This decoupled architecture allows for parallel optimization of manipulator positioning and base mobility while ensuring system-level coordination. Extensive validation through comparative simulations and real-world experiments demonstrates the framework’s effectiveness.

title: Safe-CTDE-MACE: QMIX-Based Cooperative Multi-UAV Coverage Exploration with Empirical Safety Filtering
authors: X. Zhang; Y. Jiao; Y. Guo
venue: 2026 3rd International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Robotics (CISR)
abstract: Cooperative multi-UAV coverage exploration requires multiple UAVs to cover unknown 3D environments under partial observability, obstacle constraints, and limited coordination bandwidth. This paper presents Safe-CTDE-MACE, a centralized-training/decentralized-execution framework that couples QMIX-based cooperative target selection with frontiercandidate action abstraction, residual-coverage global state, empirical safety filtering, and B-spline trajectory optimization. The decision layer maps each UAV's 3D target-selection problem to a compact set of frontier candidates, while the planning layer rejects unreachable or conflicting targets and converts accepted targets into smooth executable trajectories. In experiments on a 20×20×8 voxel environment with three UAVs, Safe-CTDE-MACE reaches an average success rate of 85.0%±7.1% over two training seeds and 20 evaluation episodes, compared with 46.7% ± 28.9% for Value-Decomposition Networks (VDN) under the same frontier-candidate interface. A direct QMIX+A* comparison under the 100-step setting reaches a final coverage of 0.853 and does not reach the 90% coverage target in the reported evaluation. These results suggest that QMIX-based coordination and continuous trajectory optimization can improve cooperative 3D coverage exploration under the evaluated simulation setting, while the safety shield serves as an empirical feasibility filter rather than a formal safety guarantee. Code and training artifacts are available at https://github.com/Jude-robotic/Safe-CTDE-MACE.git.

title: Context-Triggered Contingency Games for Strategic Multi-Agent Interaction
authors: K. Schweppe; A. -K. Schmuck
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: We address the challenge of reliable and efficient interaction in autonomous multi-agent systems, where agents must balance long-term strategic objectives with short-term dynamic adaptation. We propose context-triggered contingency games, a novel integration of strategic games derived from temporal logic specifications with dynamic contingency games solved in real-time. Our two-layered architecture leverages strategy templates to guarantee satisfaction of high-level objectives, while a new factor-graph–based solver enables scalable, real-time model predictive control of dynamic interactions. The resulting framework ensures both safety and progress in uncertain, interactive environments. We validate our approach through simulations and hardware experiments in autonomous driving and robotic navigation, demonstrating efficient, reliable, and adaptive multi-agent interaction.

title: BioRepairMARL: Multi-Agent-Assisted Biological Repair of Histological Systems
authors: M. A. -Z. Khan; J. Al-Karaki; M. Omar
venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics
abstract: Tissue repair at the cellular level presents a formidable challenge due to the dynamic and stochastic nature of biological environments. Traditional therapeutic approaches, such as systemic drug delivery or surgical intervention, often lack precision and adaptability. In this work, we introduce a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for orchestrating autonomous micro-scale agents–synthetic nanorobots or engineered cells–to perform targeted tissue repair. Our approach integrates a biologically grounded model of agent dynamics, combining chemical diffusion, electrochemical signaling, and stochastic noise to enable decentralized coordination. Through in silico experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed MARL framework achieves stable repair performance, emergent coordination, and energy-efficient operation. The results highlight the potential of AI-driven biological agents to outperform traditional methods in precision and adaptability, paving the way for future clinical applications.

title: A Sustainable AI-Enabled Predictive Maintenance Framework for Smart Industrial Systems Using Industrial IoT Data
authors: V. K. B. Parasaram; V. T. Bathini; S. K. Nalluri; A. H. Sannidhanam
venue: 2026 Third International Conference on Innovations in Cybersecurity and Data Science (ICICDS)
abstract: Predictive maintenance and operational dependability depend on an accurate estimate of the remaining useful life (RUL) of aircraft engines. It helps airlines to schedule maintenance procedures, preventing unplanned downtime and unanticipated malfunctions. Through the use of sensor signals and complex DL models, RUL estimation ensures safety, maximizes engine utilization, and saves on maintenance costs. This paper proposes an AI-powered predictive maintenance system that leverages NASA C-MAPSS data to function as a full-fleet engine (turbofan) system. The process of data preprocessing involves Remaining Useful Life (RUL) generation, Health Index (HI) generation, feature selection, normalization, and sliding window generation. Three deep learning models are designed and tested LSTM with SelfAttention, BiLSTM with Multi-Scale Attention, and Transformer with Squeeze-Excitation on the basis of RMSE, MAE, and $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$. Alternatively, experimental findings show that Transformer + SE model works best with a $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0. 8 5 3 0}$ and RMSE $=15.93$ which is superior to the previously employed methods. Moreover, the framework incorporates Explainable AI (XAI), uncertainty-driven risk evaluation, monitoring with a digital twin, and cost-benefit analysis to make decisions and their interpretation more interpretable.

title: Decentralized Swarm Control Via SO(3) Embeddings for 3D Trajectories
authors: D. Silveria; K. Cabral; P. T. Jardine; S. Givigi
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel decentralized approach for achieving emergent behavior in multi-agent systems with minimal information sharing. Based on prior work in simple orbits, our method produces a broad class of stable, periodic trajectories by stabilizing the system around a Lie group-based geometric embedding.
