Employing the Lie group SO(3), we generate a wider range of periodic curves than existing quaternion-based methods. Furthermore, we exploit SO(3) properties to eliminate the need for velocity inputs, allowing agents to receive only position inputs. We also propose a novel phase controller that ensures uniform agent separation, along with a formal stability proof. Validation through simulations and experiments showcases the method's adaptability to complex low-level dynamics and disturbances.

title: A Multi-Agent Digital Twin Framework for LLM-Driven Building Energy and Indoor Air Quality Co-Simulation
authors: Y. Huang; Y. Li; X. Chen; B. M. Chen
venue: 2026 IEEE 20th International Conference on Control and Automation (ICCA)
abstract: Simulation-based building thermal and indoor air quality analysis requires coupling building energy simulation (BES) with computational fluid dynamics (CFD), yet the associated multi-software configuration workflow remains fragmented, expertise-demanding, and error-prone. This paper presents a multi-agent co-simulation framework that transforms natural-language building-analysis requests into controlled BES-CFD workflows within a digital twin environment. The framework organizes an analysis chain comprising objective-profile extraction, case-bundle planning, shared research memory, domain-specific artifact generation with context-isolated sub-agents, guarded runtime execution with policy-constrained overrides, and evidence reporting. Retrievalaugmented generation supports each sub-agent, while a humanin-the-loop approval gate and a two-layer artifact management scheme separate candidate outputs from the validated runtime baseline to improve traceability, reproducibility, and execution safety. A sports hall occupancy-driven thermal and air quality analysis task is used to evaluate the framework, with a cross-backbone assessment across six frontier LLMs. All backbones complete the workflow and produce identical physical outputs under the guarded execution policy, while exhibiting substantial planning-level diversity in artifact expressiveness and scenario design.

title: Behavioral Verification of Fault and Delay Prone Multirobot System for Sim-to-Real Applications
authors: R. Bhardwaj; K. K. Singh; D. Malyshev; L. Rybak; N. K. Dhar
venue: IEEE Systems Journal
abstract: This article formally verifies behavioral attributes in a multirobot system (MRS) prone to potential faults and delays for sim-to-real deployments. It employs linear temporal logic to formally specify component- and system-level behavior, ensuring the correctness of the MRS operation. Despite the presence of faults and delays, the approach verifies the state and control consistency among the different components. Each component is verified in isolation to ensure that it meets specific requirements while preventing the state-explosion problem, overall system convergence is established using the composition principle. To evaluate the system safety, several potential violations are assessed across the system, including breaches of the intersafe distance, fault recovery, and tolerable delays. A case study involving simulation and real-time experiment is presented to demonstrate the verification of MRS operation, detecting whether the specified behaviors are satisfied or violated under fault and delay conditions, where satisfaction of all behaviors serves as strong evidence of correctness.

title: Many-to-Many Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
authors: E. Schneider; J. Chen; T. Gu; K. Lian; S. Hutchinson; S. Chernova
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Multi-robot systems in automated warehouses must manage continuous streams of pickup-and-delivery tasks while ensuring efficiency and safety. Prior work on Multi-Agent Pickup-and-Delivery (MAPD) has largely focused on the one-to-one variant, where each task has a fixed pickup and delivery location. In contrast, real warehouses often present many-to-many MAPD scenarios, where items, tracked by stock keeping unit (SKU) identifiers, can be retrieved from or stored at multiple locations, resulting in an NP-hard four-dimensional assignment problem. To solve the many-to-many MAPD problem, we contribute our algorithm: Many-to-Many Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (M2M). We experiment with two variants of our algorithm: one that minimizes estimated task durations (M2M), and one which incorporates SKU distribution into the objective function (M2M-wSKU). Simulation results over 8-hour warehouse operations show that our method consistently matches or outperforms prior state of the art, with M2M completing up to 22,000 more tasks on average across different environments and warehouse inventory densities.

title: KITNet: A Region-Attention-Activated Trajectory Predictor With Hierarchical Graph Neural Network in Dynamic-Mutant Multi-Agent System
authors: Z. Zhou; S. Wang; A. Huang; J. Lou; W. Tang; D. Navarro-Alarcon
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Safe and efficient operation of Autonomous Delivery Vehicles (ADVs) in dynamic multi-agent environments, such as university campuses and industrial parks, necessitates accurate trajectory prediction of interacting agents. Conventional autonomous navigation systems, however, rely heavily on reactive real-time perception and often fail to predict complex spatio-temporal interactions among heterogeneous agents. This limitation frequently leads to suboptimal motion planning outcomes and operational inefficiencies, including deadlock situations, in congested scenarios. This paper introduces Knowledge-Interaction-Temporal Network (KITNet), a novel trajectory prediction framework specifically designed for ADVs operating in such complex, dynamic settings. KITNet employs a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture to model intricate interaction dynamics, incorporating a novel attention mechanism based on set theory for enhanced spatio-temporal feature extraction and prediction of diverse behavior patterns. We evaluate KITNet on several trajectory prediction benchmarks according to the different tailored behavior modes under the defined mode space, including the ETH/UCY pedestrian dataset, the NGSIM highway driving dataset, and the Argoverse 2 urban driving dataset. Our results demonstrate state-of-the-art prediction accuracy, outperforming or matching existing graph-based and recurrent approaches. Furthermore, we discuss the integration of KITNet’s predictive outputs into local motion planning modules, showing potential for significantly reducing conflict scenarios and optimizing trajectory execution for ADVs. These findings establish KITNet as a highly effective trajectory predictor for autonomous transport systems, critically advancing predictive navigation and bridging the gap between perception and robust intelligent decision-making in complex urban and campus environments.

title: Suppressing Hallucinations in Anti-Fraud LLM Agents: The Robust Dual-Verification (RDV) Architecture
authors: M. Huo; Z. Xue; K. Lu; W. Yan
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed in financial anti-fraud systems are susceptible to hallucinations that manifest as numerical drift, fabricated entity relations, and logic overstepping of compliance rules. These errors carry severe regulatory and financial consequences. This paper proposes the Robust Dual-Verification (RDV) architecture, a multi-layered framework designed to suppress hallucinations in anti-fraud LLM agents. RDV integrates four synergistic components: a Structured-Semantic Retrieval-Augmented Generation mechanism (S2-RAG) enforcing Text-to-SQL anchoring and row-level citation tracing; a LoRA fine-tuning strategy targeting JSON schema compliance; a Dual-Agent Debate Protocol governed by a logistic calibration model for log-odds fusion; and deterministic guardrails providing a final hard-verification layer for explicit numerical claims. We introduce a domain-specific hallucination taxonomy and the Financial Adversarial Trap (FAT-1200) benchmark to rigorously evaluate the proposed architecture. Experiments demonstrate substantial reductions across all hallucination categories, with transparent evaluation methodology and honest discussion of practical limitations in real-world deployments.

title: LASER: Level-based Asynchronous Scheduling and Execution Regime for Spatiotemporally Constrained Multi-Robot Timber Manufacturing
authors: Z. Huang; L. Skoury; T. Stark; A. Wagner; H. J. Wagner; T. Wortmann; A. Menges
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Automating large-scale manufacturing in domains like timber construction requires multi-robot systems to manage tightly coupled spatiotemporal constraints, such as collision avoidance and process-driven deadlines. This paper introduces LASER (Level-based Asynchronous Scheduling and Execution Regime), a complete framework for scheduling and executing complex assembly tasks, demonstrated on a screw-press gluing application for timber slab manufacturing. Our central contribution is to integrate a barrier-based mechanism into a constraint programming (CP) scheduling formulation that partitions tasks into spatiotemporally disjoint sets, which we define as "levels." This structure enables robots to execute tasks in parallel and asynchronously within a level, synchronizing only at level barriers, which guarantees collision-free operation by construction and provides robustness to timing uncertainties. To solve this formulation for large problems, we propose two specialized algorithms: an iterative temporal-relaxation approach for heterogeneous task sequences and a bi-level decomposition for homogeneous tasks that balances workload. We validate the LASER framework by fabricating a full-scale 2.4 m × 6 m timber slab (Fig. 1) with a two-robot system mounted on parallel linear tracks, successfully coordinating 108 subroutines and 352 screws under tight adhesive time windows. Computational studies show our method scales steadily with size compared to a monolithic approach.

title: Multi-Partner Project: Enhancing Resilience, Efficiency, and Trustworthiness of Edge AI in Safety-Critical Systems (GuardAI)
authors: A. Savva; M. Demirel; Y. K. Adimoolam; R. Elia; A. Gkillas; C. Anagnostopoulos; E. -V. Pikoulis; A. Damianou; C. Barker; D. Bethell; A. S. Tawfik Ibrahim; F. Cugini; F. Paolucci; K. Vlachos; S. Gerasimou; A. Lalas; K. Votis; A. Lalos; C. Kyrkou; T. Theocharides
venue: 2026 Design, Automation & Test in Europe Conference (DATE)
abstract: AI at the network edge promises real-time perception and decision-making in safety-critical domains such as aerial robotics, autonomous vehicles, and 5G-enabled infrastructures. Yet, operating under resource constraints, dynamic, and adversarial conditions exposes edge AI systems to fragility, inefficiency, and security risks that threaten their safe operation. GuardAI, a Horizon Europe project, introduces a framework for resilient and trustworthy edge AI that unites three pillars: adversarial robustness, context-enhanced inference, and security-by-design. Initial project results include a diffusion-based adversarial purification framework optimized for real-time operation, lightweight deep unrolling architectures for LiDAR super-resolution with built-in outlier removal, and robust uncertainty quantification modules to improve confidence calibration. It further develops a context-enhanced inference engine that integrates visual, spatial, and operational context across multi-agent systems, and a risk-aware defense recommender that autonomously selects mitigation strategies based on evolving threat landscapes. Through representative Use Cases, covering monitoring with Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, decentralized 5G network analytics, and secure perception in connected autonomous vehicles, GuardAI demonstrates how robust and adaptive AI can be achieved within stringent edge constraints. Together, these technologies lay the groundwork for a new generation of secure, context-aware, and certifiable AI systems that can be trusted to operate autonomously in the physical world.

title: ZERO Swarm: Distributed Collective Intelligence for Autonomous Planetary Space Exploration
authors: D. K; B. T. G; K. V
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
abstract: Autonomous planetary exploration demands multi- agent intelligence resilient to radiation, communication black- outs, and extreme hardware heterogeneity. We present ZERO Swarm; a distributed collective intelligence architecture extendsing the ZERO Mind dual-core framework— Lifelong Multi- modal Memory Core (LMMC) and Self-Evolution Cognition Core (SECC)—to planetary-scale networks of heterogeneous autonomous agents. ZERO Swarm introduces three novel con- tributions: Swarm Episodic Memory Consensus (SEMC) for radiation-resilient probabilistic memory propagation, Federated Co-Evolution Protocol (FCEP) for zeroshot architectural mutation sharing across heterogeneous hardware, and Emergent Goal Alignment (EGA) for fully decentralized neuro-symbolic negoti- ation of swarm-wide objectives. Preliminary ROS2 and NVIDIA Isaac Sim experiments with 32 heterogeneous agents—rovers, drones, orbiters, and habitat AIs—on Mars-analog terrain demonstrate greater than $2 \times$ collective reward improvement over QMIX baselines, greater than 75% recovery from simulated radiationinduced memory corruption, and greater than 30% faster adaptation to novel dust-storm conditions. Full 256-agent validation is ongoing. ZERO Swarm establishes the architectural foundation for autonomous planetary digital twin constellations targeting Mars colony operations by 2028.

title: Safety-Critical Interactive Scenario Generation for Autonomous Vehicles Testing Using Diffusion-Based Method
authors: G. Zhou; Z. Wang; J. Chen; H. Yao; H. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: Safety-critical scenario generation is essential for evaluating autonomous vehicles (AVs) algorithms under rare but hazardous interactions. This article proposes a diffusion-based framework for generating specified interactive 2-D traffic scenarios from a single initial kinematic snapshot, including vehicle position, velocity, acceleration, and heading angle. The generated output is from the future traffic-interaction layer, represented by multiagent kinematic pose trajectories, while sensor and environment rendering are handled by downstream simulators. The framework integrates interaction encoding, staged trajectory generation, and residual diffusion refinement. The interaction encoder captures agent–agent relations and global dependencies; the preliminary generator provides an initial interaction-aware rollout; and the residual diffusion network refines the trajectory in residual space to improve fidelity and interaction consistency. The framework also supports multimodal generation and time-to-collision-based risk selection. Experiments on HighD show that the proposed method outperforms representative learning-based and rule-based baselines in avgADE, avgFDE, and avgMR. Scenario-centric statistics demonstrate the framework’s ability to generate diverse hazardous interactions for AV stress testing, and ExiD experiments further indicate cross-scenario generalizability. Hardware-in-the-loop experiment confirms trajectory fidelity, while reinforcement learning augmentation reduces the deep Q network (DQN) collision rate from 0.261 to 0.229 in HighwayEnv and from 0.457 to 0.389 on the 51Sim safety-critical test set. The model generates one scenario in 1.2 ms and 100 000 scenarios in about 2 min on a RTX 2080Ti GPU.

title: Teryaq: An IoT-Enabled System for the Smart Delivery of Temperature-Sensitive Medications
authors: D. Aloulah; F. Alqudayri; M. Alzunidi; F. Alsubaheen; S. Aldhawi; A. Aljohani
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI)
abstract: Temperature-sensitive medications transportation faces significant challenges, especially in maintaining the needed environmental conditions to guarantee safety and efficacy. Preserving the quality of the medication is critical, and many factors play a major role in the medication safe to be used. Temperature stability is a critical factor that needs to be monitored and controlled, especially during hospital-to-patient deliveries of temperature-sensitive medications. However, traditional transportation methods show limitations in this regard, increasing the risk of temperature excursions that can compromise patient safety. This paper presents a smart system called Teryaq which is designed to enhance the transportation of temperature-sensitive medications by ensuring optimal delivery conditions. The system integrates real-time environmental monitoring with intelligent routing algorithms to minimize risk and improve efficiency. Leveraged with wireless communication and embedded sensors, the system continuously monitors temperature and automatically transmits reports and alerts. The system identifies the safest and most efficient routes by analyzing data such as delivery time and traffic patterns. It combines hardware and intelligent software to ensure reliable performance, even under rapidly changing conditions. This work aims to ensure safe, reliable, efficient, patient-centered delivery of temperature-sensitive medications while minimizing medication waste.

title: Comparison of nuclear safety regulatory requirements for advanced modular reactors in the UK and US
authors: Y. Yan; E. Lee; K. Katsamangas
venue: IET Powering Net Zero (PNZ 2025)
abstract: Advanced Nuclear Technologies (ANTs), which includes Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and Advanced Modular Reactors (AMRs), have the potential to support countries in transitioning away from fossil fuels and achieving greater energy security . Their deployment, however, requires regulatory regimes that can accommodate novel designs and passive safety features. This paper uses a comparison of the regulatory regimes in the United Kingdom (UK) and the United States (US), two countries with mature but distinct approaches to nuclear regulation, to discuss the implications for regulatory harmonisation. Focusing on four key aspects of the regulations, category of Licensing Basis Events (LBEs), classification of Structure, System and Component (SSC), Defence-in-Depth (DiD) philosophy and probabilistic safety assessments, the paper highlights both where there are convergences and divergences. Both the UK and US regulatory frameworks share core safety principles and emphasize robust safety assessments for licensing ANTs. While this offers potential for harmonising AMR licensing, differences in regulatory approaches, such as SSC classification and the use of probabilistic safety assessments, mean that additional justifications or methodological adjustments may be needed for cross-border deployment. Leveraging the collaboration between regulators is expected to allow for further harmonisation and minimise additional justifications or methodological adjustments.

title: Synergetic Adaptive Orchestration and Governance: A Unified Framework for Production-Grade Multi-Agent Systems
authors: K. Bhatia
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: The field of artificial intelligence is transitioning from isolated Large Language Models (LLMs) to agentic collectives, autonomous networked systems essential for missioncritical deployments. This fundamental shift introduces core challenges of orchestration (dynamic coordination) and governance (oversight of autonomous behaviors), which determine system safety, reliability, and economic value. This paper proposes the Synergetic Adaptive Orchestration and Governance (SAOG) framework, a unified architecture designed to bridge the gap between performance optimization and safety-critical oversight. The Orchestration Layer utilizes a modular, self-optimizing, cellstructured design where agents minimize Variational Free Energy (VFE). The Governance Layer establishes a zero-trust communication environment using Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) to prevent impersonation and Sybil attacks. All inter-agent interactions are mediated through a Security Gateway, which applies a multi-perspective risk score covering content, privacy, and behavioral risk before authorization. This framework aligns with enterprise requirements for data lineage verification and ethical policy embedding. The framework provides a rigorous technical foundation for collective intelligence, emphasizing that the adoption of standardized protocols, such as Agent2Agent (A2A) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), and adaptive accountability mechanisms will be defining factors for institutional stability as the agentic market expands.

title: IMPACT-Agent: Intelligent Multimodal Prompt-Driven Agent for Collaborative Teaming
authors: T. Cho; H. You; A. J. Choi
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The future of disaster response, search and rescue (SAR) technology is rapidly evolving with the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and intelligent unmanned platforms. Manned-Unmanned Teaming (MUM-T) is revolutionizing on-site disaster structure and emergency rescue strategies by synchronizing manned and unmanned vehicles to support operations. This paper investigates the potential applications of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in intelligent MUM-T systems. We present a system capable of using aerial imagery to identify and locate survivors and hazards/risks, and to generate safe path plans for unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). The main contributions are: 1) the implementation of a Few-Shot In-Context Learning (ICL) method for MLLMs, which eliminates the need for fine-tuning or re-training the AI model, and 2) the application of the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting technique. The ICL method reduces the time required for data gathering and model training, while the CoT reasoning technique improves the path planning generated by MLLMs. Our experiments, using aerial imagery, demonstrate that the proposed system achieves up to 86% mean Average Precision (mAP) in survivor and hazard identification through 5-shot ICL. Furthermore, applying the CoT technique doubled the UGV’s path generation success rate from 20% to 40%. The proposed MLLM-based system effectively performed open-vocabulary object detection without additional training. This research highlights the potential of MLLMs for diverse and complex disaster relief missions in intelligent MUM-T systems, presenting an innovative approach to enhance capabilities and mission success while reducing human risk and operational costs. A demonstration video of our system is available at https://youtu.be/vReaSMDWu8o?si=RluQsqS4O_j5lVcS

title: Digital Transformation Through a Rail OEM Data Hub: Integrating Telematic Control Units and the Internet of Equipment
authors: P. Saha
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology & Management (ICETM)
abstract: Railway original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) operate within distributed ecosystems where operational, engineering, manufacturing, and service data are scattered across heterogeneous platforms and organizational boundaries. This fragmentation constrains the reliability improvements, predictive maintenance programs, warranty reduction initiatives, quality traceability, and customer transparency that modern digital transformation demands. This paper presents an integrated Rail OEM Data Hub anchored by a Telematic Control Unit (TCU)-enabled Internet of Equipment (IOE) architecture, combining edge computing, streaming ingestion, Lakehouse storage, asset identity resolution, semantic governance, and secure over-the-air (OTA) lifecycle management. Empirical validation across 340 field assets over 18 months demonstrates measurable outcomes: mean time-to-root-cause reduced by 31%, unplanned downtime by 23%, and OTA compliance increased by 28 percentage points. Use cases examined include closed-loop reliability engineering, predictive maintenance, fleet benchmarking, V2V/V2P autonomy enablement, and sustainability analytics. A staged implementation roadmap, governance operating model, and future research directions in federated learning, rail ontology standardization, and causal reliability modeling are provided.

title: MARS: A Machine Learning-Based Flight Condition Recognition and Maneuver Reporting Framework for Helicopter Predictive Maintenance
authors: I. B. San; O. H. Gulsoy; S. Solak; O. Okumus
venue: 2026 2nd International Symposium on AI-Driven Engineering Systems (ISADES)
abstract: Helicopter Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS) play a vital role in enhancing flight safety and supporting maintenance planning. However, many operational implementations still rely on event-based or rule-driven Flight Condition Recognition (FCR) methods. While these approaches effectively identify threshold exceedances, hard landings, and high-load events, they may inadequately capture unsteady maneuvers and recurrent sub-threshold aggressive operations that contribute to cumulative fatigue damage. To address this limitation, this paper presents MARS, a software-oriented Maneuver Analysis and Reporting System designed to recognize helicopter flight conditions from multivariate time-series sensor data and transform maneuver classifications into maintenance-oriented analytical insights. The proposed framework integrates robust preprocessing, sensor synchronization, sliding-window segmentation, time-series data augmentation, supervised time-series classification, a backend data management layer, and web-based reporting capabilities. Random Forest, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) models are employed as comparative classifiers for maneuver recognition. The system is designed to enhance existing Flight Data Recorder (FDR) and HUMS data streams without requiring modifications to onboard hardware, thereby supporting usage-based maintenance strategies and providing a foundation for future Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation.

title: Multi-Robot Trajectory Planning via Constrained Bayesian Optimization and Local Cost Map Learning with STL-Based Conflict Resolution
authors: S. Raxit; A. A. Redwan Newaz; J. Fuentes; P. Padrao; A. Cavalcanti; L. Bobadilla
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: We address multi-robot motion planning under Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications with kinodynamic constraints. Exact approaches face scalability bottlenecks and limited adaptability, while conventional sampling-based methods require excessive samples to construct optimal trajectories. We propose a two-stage framework integrating sampling-based online learning with formal STL reasoning. At the single-robot level, our constrained Bayesian Optimization-based Tree search (cBOT) planner uses a Gaussian process as a surrogate model to learn local cost maps and feasibility constraints, generating shorter collision-free trajectories with fewer samples. At the multi-robot level, our STL-enhanced Kinodynamic Conflict-Based Search (STL-KCBS) algorithm incorporates STL monitoring into conflict detection and resolution, ensuring specification satisfaction while maintaining scalability and probabilistic completeness. Benchmarking demonstrates improved trajectory efficiency and safety over existing methods. Real-world experiments with autonomous surface vehicles validate robustness and practical applicability in uncertain environments. The STLcBOT Planner will be released as an open-source package, and videos of real-world and simulated experiments are available at https://stlbot.github.io/.

title: Fuzzy Adaptive Formation Control for Nonholonomic Mobile Robots under Jointly Connected Switching Networks
authors: K. Wang; W. Wu; H. Ma; H. Ren
venue: 2026 International Annual Conference on Complex Systems and Intelligent Science (CSIS-IAC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the fuzzy adaptive formation control problem for nonholonomic mobile robots (NMR) under the conditions of joint connection switching network and full state constraints. A distributed reference generator is constructed to estimate the state information of the leader, thereby solving the problem of unknown leader state in discontinuous network topology. Based on the backstepping control method, a barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) is designed to ensure that all system states are confined within the safety boundary. Using the fuzzy logic system (FLS), the unknown nonlinear functions in the robot dynamics model are approximated and a fuzzy adaptive formation control algorithm is proposed. It is proved that all closed-loop signals of the system are semi-global uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB), and the formation tracking error converges to a small neighborhood close to zero. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Logic-Adaptive Discrete Neural Dynamics for Distributed Cooperative Control of Multirobot Systems via Minimum Infinity Norm Optimization
authors: D. Ma; J. Lv; C. Xu; L. Jin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
abstract: In pursuit of safe and efficient distributed cooperative control of multirobot systems (MRSs), a logic-adaptive discrete neural dynamics (LADND)-based minimum infinity norm (MIN) strategy is introduced in this article. The MIN strategy is employed to address critical safety concerns caused by excessively high velocity in the individual joint. To further improve the adaptivity of the neural dynamics solver, a fuzzy system is integrated to enable adaptive parameter adjustment based on the real-time behavior of MRSs. Specifically, the cooperative control problem is formulated as a linear program incorporating the MIN along with constraints associated with distributed network topology and orientation maintenance, thereby enhancing the safety and effectiveness of MRSs. To efficiently solve the proposed linear program, an LADND solver is developed, which adaptively adjusts its parameter in real time according to the trajectory tracking error and its derivative. Furthermore, theoretical analyses confirm the convergence and robustness of the proposed LADND solver. Simulative and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed LADND-based MIN strategy in cooperative trajectory tracking tasks.

title: Joint Energy-Efficient and Throughput Optimization in Large-Scale Mobile Networks via Safe Hierarchical MARL
authors: H. Liu; T. Li; W. Huang; D. Niyato; Y. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications
abstract: The rapid advancement of 5G networks has significantly increased the demand for high throughput and low latency, particularly for enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) services. Optimizing user rates in large-scale base station (BS) collaborative scenarios is crucial, ensuring high throughput and low energy consumption while meeting the needs of users. The optimization process faces two key challenges: how to efficiently explore and utilize the vast action space for collaborative decision-making in large-scale networks with numerous BSs, and how to ensure optimal decision-making across numerous parameters while satisfying constraints. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel solution that integrates a generative AI-powered Digital Twin platform with a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) decision algorithm. An important tool is the high-fidelity DT-SimNet platform, enabling seamless integration with AI optimizers. Moreover, we propose a novel algorithm called Safe Hierarchical Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization with Adaptive Prediction mechanism (Safe HMAPPO-AP). This algorithm integrates Safe MARL to ensure decision-making remains within constraint boundaries and incorporates a hierarchical structure to decompose the action space. Moreover, it leverages Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for efficient feature extraction and employs the Adaptive Prediction mechanism to accelerate learning and improve network performance. Comprehensive experiments using the DT-SimNet platform demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm compared to competing methods. Within the target area, Safe HMAPPO-AP achieved a 6.73% improvement in average throughput for regular users and an 11.48% increase in system utility, while meeting demands of newly added eMBB users.

title: Distributed Hierarchical Control for Collaborative Signal Temporal Logic Tasks via Reconstructed Control Barrier Functions
authors: Y. Peng; W. Wang; J. Yan; M. Yu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper investigates distributed cooperative control for multi-agent systems (MASs) subject to signal temporal logic (STL) specifications. We begin by encoding the STL formulas into control barrier functions (CBFs) to connect high-level task specifications with low-level system constraints. A key challenge is that collaborative tasks generate coupled CBF constraints, which depend on the states of multiple agents and prevent a distributed control solution. To overcome this, we introduce a novel method that reconstructs these coupled CBFs into decoupled, local constraints. This is achieved using distributed adaptive observers to estimate the states of other agents. We further modify the reconstructed CBFs with a prescribed performance adaptive parameter, which guarantees that satisfying the local constraint ensures the satisfaction of the original, global one. This framework is particularly robust as it remains effective even when collaborative tasks involve uncontrollable agents with uncertain behaviors. Furthermore, to manage multiple STL tasks with a predefined priority hierarchy, we develop a two-step quadratic programming (QP) controller. This controller uses a half-space projection method based on the reconstructed CBFs to ensure that the execution of lower-priority tasks never interferes with higher-priority ones. We demonstrate that our proposed distributed control scheme enables MASs to achieve complex collaborative STL tasks, as supported by physical simulations. Note to Practitioners—The tasks faced by robotic systems, such as cooperative transportation for warehouse robots and cooperative navigation for autonomous vehicles, are growing in complexity. Traditional control objectives, like trajectory tracking and stabilization, are often insufficient to capture these complex tasks. Consequently, temporal logic, as a formal language, is employed to specify these complex tasks. In this work, we begin by using signal temporal logic (STL) specifications to precisely define these complex tasks. These specifications are then translated into system constraints using control barrier function (CBF) techniques. When multiple autonomous systems are required to collaborate on a task, it results in “coupled” CBF constraints, which impede the implementation of a distributed control scheme. To solve this, our main contribution is a novel method to reconstruct these coupled constraints into local ones that each system can follow on its own. Furthermore, since these systems usually need to handle multiple tasks simultaneously, we developed a hierarchical task control scheme. This allows the system to handle tasks according to a predefined priority hierarchy. The proposed distributed control scheme is robust enough to function reliably even in uncertain dynamic environments. The proposed method is applicable to solving complex collaborative tasks for multiple autonomous systems and its efficacy is demonstrated through physical simulations.

title: TP-POCA: A MARL Algorithm for Target Defense Control of Non-Suicidal USVs in TAD Games
authors: H. Hu; Y. Wang; K. Gao; N. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: How to achieve collision-avoiding cooperative target defense with multiple underactuated uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) under partial observability is a challenging problem. This paper considers a Target–Attacker–Defender (TAD) scenario with a two-stage mission in which defenders escort the target to its destination and then continue guarding after arrival. Unlike suicidal defense that intercepts by collision once attackers enter the protection region, our defenders block and repel attackers outside the capture zone while maintaining safe separation from all vessels. To address partial observability and crowded engagements, we propose TP-POCA, a prediction- and history-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that integrates an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for short-horizon attacker state prediction and combines residual self-attention (RSA) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) module for relation modeling and temporal memory. Unity3D-based USV simulations demonstrate the practicality of the proposed method for cooperative target defense while satisfying non-suicidal collision-avoidance constraints. In the TAD scenario, TP-POCA achieves a success rate of 92.5% over 160 repeated experiments. Note to Practitioners—The motivation of this paper is to guide USV teams in learning how to collaboratively escort and defend a target vessel in a TAD scenario through MARL. This paper presents a method that combines the TP-POCA learning framework with an RSA-driven encoder to strengthen teamwork and credit assignment for non-suicidal USV defenders under partial observability. In addition, we design a bio-inspired reward that drives defenders toward advantageous interception positions, while preventing collisions and encouraging safety-aware behaviors. With this method, multiple USVs can reliably intercept attackers and safeguard the target via decentralized execution from local observations, aided by real-time attacker-state forecasting. To validate the proposed method, we built a Unity3D multi-USV simulator and ran repeated trials and baseline comparisons in the TAD scenario. Meanwhile, the same approach transfers to other competitive multi-USV coordination tasks, including pursuit–evasion and cooperative hunting missions. Furthermore, decentralized execution with safety-aware behaviors makes it well suited for integration into real-time USV control stacks and future on-water validation in practical navigation and control tasks.

title: Distributed State-Dependent Connectivity-Preserving Trajectory Generation for Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Y. M. Al-Rawashdeh; S. A. Aldalahmeh; S. El Ferik
venue: 2026 IEEE Jordan Conference on Applied Electrical Engineering and Computing Technologies (AEECT)
abstract: In this study, we present a guideline to test and design linear-like, state-dependent and connectivity-preserving behavioral protocols serving as distributed trajectory generators over undirected graphs. The concept of nonlinear eigenvalues is used to find the conditions needed to maintain the first smallest eigenvalue equal to zero and the second smallest one positive. This will ensure both invariance and connectivity of the trajectory generator systems over mainly undirected graphs. Also we present a collision-free, deployment and formation protocols that can also be used to achieve arithmetic, harmonics, geometric and mean-of-order-p consensus under state-dependent weighting functions. Working at the edge-level, the needed conditions for the previous protocols to accommodate state-dependent parameterization are presented. Numeric Simulation reveals the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Dynamics-Aware Critical Neighbor Selection for Distributed Connectivity Maintenance in Multi-Agent Systems*
authors: W. Tan; X. Chen
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Maintaining connectivity in multi-agent systems often compromises task performance. Current strategies are frequently hampered by heavy communication loads and overly restrictive motion constraints. Furthermore, their local decision-making relies on static geometric information, neglecting agent dynamics. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes a scalable, distributed framework centered on a novel dynamics-aware connection cost metric. This metric enables agents to prospectively select dynamically stable, task-compatible links, which are then enforced using control barrier functions (CBFs) within a cooperative optimization scheme. In multi-agent target-reaching tasks, simulations show our dynamics-aware metric reduces the final average goal distance by up to 26.1% compared to a static distance-based selection heuristic. Furthermore, our framework maintains persistent connectivity in highly dynamic scenarios, whereas a state-of-the-art algebraic connectivity-based method fails under limited communication bandwidth.

title: Emergency Response Integrated Drill Platform for Sudden Fire Accidents in New Energy Power Battery Workshops Based on AnyLogic*
authors: P. Liang; Y. Zhang; Y. Liu; X. Cu; L. Xu; X. He
venue: 2026 7th International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Information Technology (AINIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of the new energy industry, fire accidents in power battery workshops are characterized by strong suddenness, fast spread speed, and high disposal difficulty, posing severe challenges to emergency response capabilities. To address the deficiencies of traditional emergency drills, including insufficient authenticity, single training modes, lack of collaborative simulation, and low coupling between fire evolution and workshop processes, this paper proposes an integrated emergency drill platform for sudden fire accidents in new energy power battery workshops, which integrates big data, industrial internet, mixed reality (MR), and AnyLogic simulation. Taking the AnyLogic-based power battery workshop simulation model as the core, it couples personnel behavior with dynamic fire evolution to accurately reproduce the entire process of thermal runaway propagation, fire spread, and emergency dispatch. By collecting and analyzing key operational parameters such as temperature, voltage, and gas concentration in power battery workshops, the platform drives real-time iteration of the AnyLogic model, constructing a high-precision dynamic fire spread model with a prediction accuracy of 94.7%. Immersive interaction based on MR realizes workshop environment simulation, while the GIS communication module enables real-time information sharing among multiple departments. Experimental results show that compared with traditional training methods, this platform can reduce emergency response time by 37% and improve collaborative disposal efficiency by 40%, providing a new technical path for emergency drill training in the new energy field and promoting the engineering application of digital simulation technology in disaster prevention and mitigation.

title: Reinforcement Learning Based AGV Path Planning
authors: Y. Zhou; R. Yin; X. Chen; Z. Zhou; C. Wu; Y. Tian
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The multi-Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) system is an important component of intelligent manufacturing, but currently faces the challenge of dynamic path planning. This paper proposes a multi-AGV path planning methodology based on a two-tier architecture that integrates Petri nets and Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO). Specifically, the Petri net employs place and token mechanisms to preemptively prevent AGV conflicts, thereby furnishing safety constraints for the path planning process. Within this framework, MAPPO undertakes the dynamic path planning task, adopting a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) architecture. By modeling intersection nodes as individual agents, the approach decouples the complexity of the state space from the number of AGVs. Furthermore, a novel reward function is devised that incorporates inter-node travel time, balancing instantaneous congestion avoidance with goal-oriented guidance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method yields higher task completion efficiency within the system, showing relatively better performance particularly in scenarios with higher AGV densities. These preliminary simulation results suggest its potential scalability and indicate possible value for future industrial applications.

title: A Hierarchical LLM-MARL Framework for Market-Oriented Cooperative Scheduling of Multiple Virtual Power Plants
authors: L. Wang; N. Yang; M. Yang; L. Liu; Y. Ma
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Technologies and Applications (ICAITA)
abstract: The increasing participation of distributed energy resources in electricity markets requires independently operated virtual power plants (VPPs) to coordinate scheduled power delivery and flexibility provision while preserving private operational information and satisfying network constraints. However, existing MARL-based methods usually rely on fixed communication structures and direct state sharing, limiting their adaptability to dynamic market-oriented cooperation. This paper proposes an LLM-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning (LLM-MARL) framework for market-oriented cooperative scheduling of multiple VPPs. The proposed method employs LLM agents to conduct privacy-preserving semantic negotiation and generate structured market-oriented coalition contracts, which are further transformed into guidance information for MARL-based real-time control. A safety projection layer is introduced to ensure the feasibility of control actions, and a trust evolution mechanism is developed to enable adaptive coalition reconfiguration. Simulation results on an IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that the proposed framework improves economic performance, contract fulfillment, and operational safety compared with conventional MARL methods.

title: Distributed Task Allocation and Collaborative Obstacle Avoidance in Multi-AGV Systems
authors: Y. Liu; Z. Zhang; L. Song; J. Liu; Q. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper addresses real-time task allocation and path conflict resolution for heterogeneous agents in large-scale automated guided vehicle (AGV) systems within smart manufacturing. To overcome limitations of existing methods in dynamic and high-density environments, we propose a distributed market-based task allocation algorithm integrated with a cooperative multi-AGV obstacle avoidance strategy to ensure coordinated motion planning. A dynamic task buffer pool suppress system oscillations caused by frequent task arrivals. In addition, an incremental path caching mechanism is developed to reduce redundant computations during the 2-opt optimization process. The proposed Two-level priority mechanism effectively resolves multi-AGV collaborative obstacle avoidance and path conflict issues. Compared with existing approaches, the proposed method maintains robust conflict resolution among multiple AGVs while reducing task replanning frequency and computational cost. A standardized task allocation comparison framework is constructed to evaluate system performance under varying task scales. Simulation results based on real manufacturing layouts validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed hybrid algorithm. The results provide practical guidance for efficient task scheduling and collaborative obstacle avoidance in industrial AGV systems.

title: VISTA: A Vision and Intent-Aware Social Attention Framework for Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction
authors: S. Da Silva Martins; E. Aldea; S. Le Hégarat-Mascle
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
abstract: Multi-agent trajectory prediction is a key task in computer vision for autonomous systems, particularly in dense and interactive environments. Existing methods often struggle to jointly model goal-driven behavior and complex social dynamics, which leads to unrealistic predictions. In this paper, we introduce VISTA, a recursive goal-conditioned transformer architecture that features (1) a cross-attention fusion mechanism to integrate long-term goals with past trajectories, (2) a social-token attention module enabling fine-grained interaction modeling across agents, and (3) pairwise attention maps to show social influence patterns during inference. Our model enhances the single-agent goal-conditioned approach into a cohesive multi-agent forecasting framework. In addition to the standard evaluation metrics, we also consider trajectory collision rates, which capture the realism of the joint predictions. Evaluated on the high-density MADRAS benchmark and on SDD, VISTA achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with improved interaction modeling. On MADRAS, our approach reduces the average collision rate of strong baselines from 2.14% to 0.03%, and on SDD, it achieves a 0% collision rate while outperforming SOTA models in terms of ADE/FDE and minFDE. These results highlight the model’s ability to generate socially compliant, goal-aware, and interpretable trajectory predictions, making it well-suited for deployment in safety-critical autonomous systems.

title: Blockchain-Enabled Attribute-Based Access Control with Decentralized Revocation for Industrial IoT Edge Computing (D-ABAC)
authors: M. I. Mihailescu; S. L. Nita; V. Marascu; L. Zisu; L. B. Asalomia; M. Rogobete
venue: 2026 16th International Conference on Communications (COMM)
abstract: Suppliers, contractors, regulators, and other stakeholders all require secure, granular access to data in the complex ecosystems of contemporary industrial IoT deployments. For this scenario, the existing Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) solutions are inadequate. Centralized key authorities lead to unacceptable concentrations of trust and single points of failure. Additionally, current revocation mechanisms that necessitate complete ciphertext re-encryption are too costly for low-resource edge devices. D-ABAC, a blockchain-based ABE framework that tackles both issues at once, is presented in this paper. D-ABAC coordinates decentralized attribute authorities through smart contracts. This eliminates bottlenecks in central trust while maintaining policy uniformity across organizational boundaries. By using cryptographic accumulators to make verification complexity O(1), our lazy revocation system enables fast edge device authentication without requiring re-encryption. The hybrid architecture uses the unchangeability of the blockchain to attribute governance and enforcing economic incentives, while keeping encryption that requires a lot of processing power off chain. Formal analysis demonstrates the existence of IND-CPA security under the DLIN assumption. A 40% reduction in gas costs and a verification latency of less than 50 milliseconds are demonstrated by testing a prototype on Ethereum using ARM edge devices. Access control for more than 1,000 IoT devices across more than 50 stakeholders was successfully managed during a six-month smart manufacturing deployment, demonstrating its practicality.

title: A Proposed Unified Cloud-Native Framework for Intelligent Defect Triage and Resolution in Software-Defined Vehicles
authors: P. C. Sali
venue: IEEE Engineering Management Review
abstract: Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) rely on tightly coupled software ecosystems spanning in-vehicle controllers, edge platforms, cloud services, Over-the-air (OTA) infrastructure, cybersecurity services and supplier-managed components. This architectural shift has fundamentally altered defect characteristics, creating cross-domain failure modes that exceed the capabilities of traditional automotive defect triage and resolution processes. Technology managers must address fragmented incident management systems, component-centric analysis, and severity-based prioritization models that limit organizations' ability to rapidly identify, correlate, and resolve safety-critical defects at fleet scale. This article proposes a unified, cloud-native framework for intelligent defect triage and resolution tailored to SDV environments. The framework is designed to integrate signals from vehicle diagnostics, OTA update systems, cloud observability platforms, and supplier incidents that feed into a unified, normalized, safety-aware defect model. Machine learning–driven correlation, automotive safety classification, and fleet-level impact assessment enable automated prioritization and resolution orchestration while preserving regulatory traceability. Drawing on lessons from industrial implementations of automated incident management, observability, and bug triage systems, the framework outlines how organizations can modernize defect management practices while preserving human oversight and regulatory traceability. The article also discusses implementation considerations, governance requirements, anticipated business benefits, and adoption challenges relevant to technology managers responsibilities. The framework illustrates how cloud native architectures can support both operational scalability and safety assurance in modern automotive software ecosystems essentially benefitting and encouraging technology managers into its adoption.

title: Leader–Follower Formation Control of Underactuated USV With FOV Constraints and Obstacle Avoidance: A High-Order Control Barrier Function Approach
authors: C. Yu; X. Chen; Y. Wu; L. Chai
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
abstract: An improved leader–follower formation control framework is developed for underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) under field-of-view (FOV) constraints and obstacle avoidance. To address these constraints, a high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) method is introduced to ensure collision avoidance and FOV maintenance. The control design is formulated as a quadratic programming (QP) optimization problem, which guarantees the uniqueness and optimality of the control signals. In addition, a fixed-time extended state observer (FXESO) is designed to estimate unknown hydrodynamic parameters and environmental disturbances with bounded convergence time. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

title: A Multimodal Stochastic Planning Approach for Navigation and Multi-Robot Coordination
authors: M. Gonzales; E. Oh; J. Moore
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: In this paper, we present a receding-horizon, sampling-based planner capable of reasoning over multimodal policy distributions. By using the cross-entropy method to optimize a multimodal policy under a common cost function, our approach increases robustness against local minima and promotes effective exploration of the solution space. We show that our approach naturally extends to multi-robot collision-free planning, enables agents to share diverse candidate policies to avoid deadlocks, and allows teams to minimize a global objective without incurring the computational complexity of centralized optimization. Numerical simulations demonstrate that employing multiple modes significantly improves success rates in trap environments and in multi-robot collision avoidance. Hardware experiments further validate the approach’s real-time feasibility and practical performance.

title: When Not to Write Memory: Governing False Promotion from Correlated Agent Traces
authors: Y. Qi; X. Xu; Y. Li
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Machine Learning and Intelligent Systems Engineering (MLISE)
abstract: Long-lived language agents increasingly write reusable memories from their own execution traces. The key safety question is not only what agents should remember, but when they should refuse to write memory at all. Repeated observations across agents are not necessarily independent evidence: the same claim may be copied from a shared source, induced by a shared prompt, stale under a new environment, or valid only in a narrower scope. We study this failure mode as a memory writepath governance problem. We introduce GovMem as a conservative diagnostic reference policy that estimates dependency-aware support, retrieves counterevidence, assigns scope, and outputs one of three decisions: promote, reject, or needs-review. In controlled synthetic stress tests, GovMem reduces false promotion from 0.597 to 0.040 in the default setting while preserving 0.960 recall, at an explicit review burden. In a project-internal 120candidate human-labeled real-trace subset spanning 79 recorded traces and project reports, dependency-aware promotion reduces false promotion from 0.371 for source+scope to 0.032 overall, but held-out false promotion remains 0.111 and the method is highly conservative, with 0.692 review burden and 0.448 direct recall. A final human adjudication of 133 high-impact external codingagent candidates is more severe: none are safe for automatic promotion, and all 11 verification-gate positives are rejected as boilerplate, shared-tool artifacts, file dumps, or non-reusable debugging traces. These results support GovMem primarily as a diagnostic governance design point, not as a generally validated or efficient automatic memory writer: agent memory write paths should be evaluated as risk-controlled evidence-governance systems, while broader external coverage and downstream harm evidence are still needed before stronger claims.

title: Dynamic Communication and Global Guidance for Multi-Agent Path Finding
authors: Y. Ma; X. Lu; N. Ning; P. Zhu; L. Shi; W. Li; N. H. Trung; Y. Zhou
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Transportation Systems (RAITS)
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots are deployed in transport and logistics for large-scale handling and distribution tasks. However, real-time collaboration in such dynamic settings faces two primary challenges: effective collision avoidance and efficient communication. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Dynamic Communication with Global Guidance for Multi-Agent Path Finding (DCGGM), which integrates a Latent Representation Dynamic Communication (LRDC) module reducing redundant messaging and a early waiting policy to anticipate conflicts. It significantly enhances multi-agent cooperation without compromising real-time performance. Experimental results show that DCGGM matches the performance of coupled centralized expert algorithms. Ablation studies and comparisons across various agent densities confirm the effectiveness of our communication mechanism. The framework generalizes to potential problem instances and surpasses state-of-the-art learningbased approaches in success rate, path efficiency, and collision minimization.

title: An Ensemble MARL Approach for Heterogeneous UAV Swarm Target Search in 3D Space
authors: X. Zhang; C. Wei; Z. Wang; Y. Zhang; W. Ding; X. -P. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
abstract: In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly pivotal in cooperative searches.However, the performance of using a homogeneous UAV swarm for search is often limited because a single class of UAVs cannot guarantee accuracy and coverage simultaneously. This work tackles the challenge of target search in a large-scale three-dimensional (3D) environment using a heterogeneous UAV swarm. Specifically, we design a novel search scheme that leverages the complementary strengths of two UAV types: fixed-wing UAVs, which enable swift area coverage at high altitudes, and multi-rotor UAVs, which provide high-precision detection at low altitudes. To address the stochastic optimization problem posed by unknown targets, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) scheme—where multiple agents learn to optimize their strategies through interactions with each other and the environment—for efficient target search. To ensure the safety of UAVs, an action masking scheme is integrated into the MARL framework to avoid collisions. Moreover, to further enhance decision robustness and search efficiency, we propose an Ensemble MARL framework that aggregates multiple independently trained networks via a majority voting mechanism, and further present our Ensemble QMIX (E-QMIX) algorithm. Furthermore, we provide a mathematical analysis showing that E-QMIX increases the probability that each agent selects its optimal action, thereby strengthening the robustness of joint decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that our E-QMIX outperforms classic single-network MARL benchmarks in both search efficiency and coverage rate.

title: Governed Agentic AI for Software Platforms: A Reference Architecture for Safe Autonomy at Scale
authors: S. Karuppuchamy
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have accelerated the emergence of agentic AI systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting across software platforms [1], [9]. While such systems promise significant productivity and operational gains, unconstrained autonomy introduces substantial risks related to safety, reliability, security, regulatory compliance, and organizational trust-particularly in large, distributed enterprise environments [3], [11], [12]. These concerns are further amplified by emerging regulatory frameworks such as the European Union's Digital Services Act [5], which impose stricter requirements on transparency, accountability, and human oversight. This paper introduces a governance control plane for agentic AI systems in software platforms and empirically characterizes the trade-offs between autonomy, safety enforcement, and human oversight. The proposed architecture balances autonomous decision-making with deterministic policy enforcement and structured human control. The proposed architecture decomposes agent behavior into four controlled layers: (1) intent interpretation using LLMs [1], (2) policy-aware planning and decision logic informed by enterprise rules and risk constraints [6]–[8], (3) guarded execution over platform APIs inspired by tool-augmented LLM paradigms [9], [10], and (4) continuous telemetry, auditing, and rollback mechanisms to ensure operational safety and accountability. Central to the architecture is the concept of bounded autonomy, where agents automate routine and low-risk decisions while remaining constrained by declarative policies, approval gates, runtime validation, and execution allow-lists. We demonstrate the applicability of this approach through representative enterprise scenarios, including AI-assisted feature rollout and automated issue triage, building on established software engineering and DevOps principles [2], [4]. Beyond qualitative analysis, we report prototype-based measurements of governance overhead and safety effectiveness, including policy-evaluation latency, invalid-action blocking rates, and changes in human intervention volume across autonomy tiers. We further discuss adversarial robustness considerations such as indirect prompt injection [11], [12], concurrency and state-drift management in long-running agents, and policy conflict resolution in multi-agent settings [13]. Overall, this work contributes a practical, governance-centered blueprint for deploying agentic AI systems with explicitly bounded autonomy, observable decision-making, and enforceable safety controls in large-scale software platforms.

title: Matrix Control Barrier Functions
authors: P. Ong; Y. Xu; R. M. Bena; F. Jabbari; A. D. Ames
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control
abstract: This article generalizes the control barrier function (CBF) framework by replacing scalar-valued functions with matrix-valued ones. Specifically, we develop barrier conditions for safe sets defined by matrix inequalities—both semidefinite and indefinite. Matrix inequalities provide a richer representation of safety constraints, generalizing multiple scalar CBFs and enabling nonsmooth safety constraints, including those arising from spectral conditions. The safety filters constructed from our proposed matrix CBFs via semidefinite programming are shown to be continuous. Our matrix formulation naturally provides a continuous safety filter for Boolean-based control barrier functions, notably for disjunctions, without relaxing the safe set. We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework with applications in drone network connectivity maintenance—which relies on nondiagonal matrix-valued constraints—and nonsmooth obstacle avoidance, both in simulations and hardware experiments.

title: Flexible Multi-Robot Social Navigation Using Diffusion-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: M. Y. Nishimura; K. Matsumoto; J. Tørresen; R. Kurazume
venue: 2026 IEEE 35th International Conference on Robot and Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN)
abstract: Diffusion-based reinforcement learning has recently shown strong performance in robot navigation, and prior work has demonstrated that Q-Score Matching (QSM) is effective in crowded environments. Building on this line of work, we study inference-time guidance for multi-robot social navigation using Multi-Agent Q-Score Matching (MAQSM) as the backbone policy. Rather than modifying the training objective, the proposed method steers reverse diffusion sampling of a trained MAQSM policy at evaluation time toward more coordinated multi-robot behavior. The guidance combines formation consistency and goal alignment, enabling deploymenttime control without retraining. In our implementation, robots share the same diffusion policy parameters, generate per-robot actions under this shared policy, and execute the resulting multi-robot action jointly in the simulator. Experiments first compare QSM and MAQSM to motivate the choice of MAQSM as the underlying multi-robot backbone, and then compare unguided and guided MAQSM in a more challenging bidirectional scenario. The results show that inference-time guidance improves success and safety in denser settings, at the cost of longer navigation time. These findings position post-training guidance as a practical way to improve diffusion-based multirobot policies while preserving the original learning pipeline.

title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Inspection System for Substations
authors: L. Wang; H. Wang; B. H. Zheng; B. Li; Y. Fan; W. Li; J. Xue; J. Wang
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a comprehensive intelligent inspection system for electrical substations. The system addresses the limitations of traditional manual inspections by integrating a heterogeneous fleet of robotic agents—including quadruped robots, rail-mounted robots, and fixed sensor arrays—with a centralized data analytics platform. Deployed on secure domain servers, the system architecture is built around five core functional modules: Information Overview, Inspection Task Management, Real-time Monitoring, Analysis & Decision Support, and Configuration Management. It enables fully automated, continuous inspection workflows, from task scheduling and execution to intelligent defect identification and maintenance orchestration. The paper details the system's network and functional architecture, elaborates on its key operational functionalities such as panoramic monitoring and silent patrols, and discusses its application in enhancing operational efficiency and equipment reliability. By providing a closed-loop solution from data acquisition to actionable insights, the system represents a significant advancement in substation automation, demonstrating a practical path toward unattended operations and predictive maintenance.

title: POPM: A Two-Stage Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Joint Vehicle-Application-Infrastructure Task Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing
authors: S. Pang; L. Zhao; N. Wang; C. Zhang; X. Liao
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: The rapid development of Internet of Vehicles technologies has generated a large number of latency-sensitive deep neural network task requests. Vehicular edge computing systems constitute a complex environment involving vehicles, computation application, and infrastructure components such as roadside units (RSUs). Existing studies often focus on optimizing only a subset of these elements, thereby overlooking the potential benefits of joint optimization across multiple layers. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a two-stage distributed scheduling framework, termed POPM, which enables prediction-assisted offloading optimization through joint modeling of the vehicle, task, and infrastructure layers. In the proposed framework, the first stage focuses on the vehicle and task layers, where latency-constrained visual perception tasks are modeled as directed acyclic graphs, and a multi-dimensional dynamic priority mechanism incorporating vehicle residence time is integrated with a MAPPO-based algorithm to enable fine-grained distributed local offloading. The second stage emphasizes the infrastructure layer, where RSU load prediction is performed using a TCN–FiLM model, and a MADDPG-based policy is adopted to formulate proactive cross-RSU migration strategies, thereby achieving dynamic global resource balancing and hotspot avoidance. Simulation results show that POPM improves the task success rate by approximately 18% on average compared with the baselines, while keeping the task completion latency within a competitive range. In addition, the proposed load-balancing mechanism improves fairness by approximately 14%.

title: A Novel Integrated Sensing and Communication Scheme in UAVs-Enabled Vehicular Networks With MARL-Driven Adaptive Control
authors: Z. Wang; X. -P. Zhang; W. Ding; Y. Dong; X. Chen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scheme tailored for UAVs-enabled vehicular networks, which leverages the information coverage capabilities of multiple UAVs and addresses critical challenges posed by multiple moving users. Unlike many traditional scheme, our scheme efficiently leverages ISAC signal echoes and real-time data uploads to provide communication services while achieving accurate sensing, thereby overcoming issues of resource waste and low operational efficiency. In the scheme, we aim to optimize both communication and sensing indicators, taking into account practical issues such as energy saving and collision avoidance for UAVs. However, the inherent complexity of multi-objective stochastic optimization in dynamic environments and limited communication resources render centralized UAV control inconvenient. To address the above challenges, we propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm based on local information to realize the distributed adaptive control of motion decision, power selection, and channel allocation for UAVs. The algorithm combines random network distillation (RND) and dynamic data augmentation with multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) to encourage agents to explore effectively under sparse rewards and improve MADDPG’s policy learning ability in finite data, thus approaching the global optimal solution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can improve communication and sensing performance by more than 16.71% and 68.26% compared with other baselines and satisfy the set constraints. Furthermore, by adjusting hyperparameters, we can optimize the ISAC performance while achieving different energy savings levels for UAVs, proving that the designed scheme can reduce the waste of resources and improve the ISAC operation efficiency.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Cyber–Physical Systems: A Unified Review of Methodologies for Smart Energy Systems and Intelligent Localization
authors: S. Mamun; S. Ioannou; M. Raspopoulos; S. Peng
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The transformative advancement of critical infrastructure is being driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) with cyber-physical systems (CPS). In this review, two seemingly distinct domains-Intelligent Energy Systems, including smart grids and energy communities, and Intelligent Localization and Navigation Systems for GPS-denied environments-are unified through a common methodological lens. A shared framework of AI/ML paradigms, encompassing supervised and reinforcement learning, probabilistic models, sensor fusion, and physics-informed techniques, is established. Furthermore, the adaptation of these methods is examined under domain-specific constraints, such as stochastic energy generation, power flow limitations, and real-time robotic navigation. Through the analysis of high-impact studies from 2018-2026, cross-cutting trends are identified, including the use of graph neural networks for spatial modeling and multi-agent systems for decentralized decision-making. Persistent challenges regarding data scarcity, interpretability, and edge deployment are found to remain central across CPS applications. In response to these challenges, the CPS-Bench platform-a unified, cross-domain benchmark designed to standardize evaluation across energy and localization tasks-is proposed. Four primary contributions are presented: 1) a cohesive taxonomy by which two previously isolated CPS domains are connected, 2) a comparative analysis through which transferable techniques are uncovered, 3) a thorough assessment of domain-specific adaptations, and 4) the introduction of the CPS-Bench framework alongside a practical roadmap for interdisciplinary collaboration. It is concluded that the next generation of CPS will be defined by adaptive, embodied intelligence, where AI is co-designed with physical components. By such a vision, the energy transition is expected to be accelerated and resilient, human-centric infrastructure is expected to be realized.

title: Prescribed-Time Cluster Consensus Control of HMASs Under Actuator Faults and FDI Attacks
authors: M. Li; Z. Yu; Y. Zhang
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Security and safety are crucial for the distributed coordination of heterogeneous multiagent systems (HMASs). Therefore, this article focuses on the prescribed-time cluster consensus control (PTCCC) problem for a class of HMASs composed of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs) in the presence of actuator faults and false data injection (FDI) attacks. First, to meet the prescribed-time requirement, a practical prescribed-time stability (PPTS) criterion related to a time-base generator (TBG) is established for the cluster consensus design and analysis of HMASs. Second, based on the hierarchical control framework, a prescribed-time cluster state estimator is designed for HMASs with time-varying communication topology to achieve reliable estimation of the output trajectory of the cluster leader under FDI attacks in the cyber layer, and a prescribed-time synchronization tracking controller is designed for each agent with the help of neural networks (NNs) to maintain the desired formation configuration under actuator faults in the physical layer. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Agent-Based Pricing Strategy for Fast-Charging Stations Considering Price Responsiveness of Electric Vehicles at Large Scales
authors: S. Lai; Y. Tao; Z. Y. Dong; G. Wang; X. Zhang; J. Qiu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) presents urgent demands for the efficient operation of fast-charging stations (FCSs), which must accommodate diverse user pReferences, high mobility, and spatiotemporal traffic variability. As these systems scale, one critical challenge lies in dynamically responding to the price-sensitive behavior of EV users under complex spatiotemporal conditions and pricing strategies. This paper proposes a data-driven, agent-based pricing framework for FCSs that captures both individual decision-making dynamics and collective behavior of EV fleets. Compared to conventional studies that rely on macroscopic traffic flow models (e.g., user equilibrium formulations) or regression-based charging load forecasts, this paper introduces a fine-grained, data-driven, agent-based pricing framework that captures both the microscopic decision-making dynamics of EVs and the emergent collective behaviors across large fleets. We first formulate a graph-embedded Markov Decision Process to simulate EV drivers’ route and charging choices, incorporating transportation and charging network features. A scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MA-DRL) algorithm with count-based abstraction is then proposed to jointly learn decentralized EV policies and enable collective coordination. To bridge behavioral modeling and demand forecasting, a deep Graph Attention Network (GAT) is trained to approximate the nonlinear, high-dimensional mapping between FCS attributes. Finally, an agent-based pricing model is designed to optimize FCS profits while accounting for users’ price sensitivity and electricity market constraints, with nodal prices obtained from a lower-level power distribution network optimization. Simulation results validate the framework’s effectiveness in modeling price-responsive EV charging behaviors and achieving economically efficient station operation under dynamic conditions.

title: Trust-Adaptive Explainable Consensus and Permissioned Governance for Collaborative Embodied AI in Smart-Hospital IIoT Networks
authors: S. U. Jamil; M. A. Rahman; N. Jamil; M. S. Hossain; S. Al-Hazzaa
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Magazine
abstract: Increasing use of embodied AI and autonomous medical devices is transforming smart hospital IIoT/IIoMT into highly connected cyber-physical ecosystems. Unlike conventional healthcare authorization systems, smart hospitals require trustworthy governance and collaborative embodied agents coordinating communication, sensing, data access, and physical actuation under strict safety, accountability, and privacy requirements. However, available techniques heavily rely on centralized decision-making and static access control policies that limit the abilities of those approaches to address privacy, safety, dynamic trust, and accountability requirements. This article proposes a trust-adaptive explainable consensus and permissioned governance framework for collaborative embodied AI in smart hospital IIoT/IIoMT networks. The proposed framework incorporates specialized governance agents responsible for policy compliance, preserving privacy, clinical validation of health conditions, risk assessment, and safety evaluation. A trust-aware explainable consensus approach aggregates the agents’ recommendations for supporting accountable and transparent decision-making, while a human oversight module handles high-risk and uncertain situations. For ensuring governance integrity and auditability, decision metadata and trust records are stored on a permissioned blockchain. An adaptive trust management engine evaluates the reliability of the participating devices and agents based on governance and operational behavior outcomes: supported by experimental evaluation and validation.

title: HMSim: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Simulator For Autonomous Vehicles
authors: H. Liu; J. Zhao; L. Zhang
