venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of developing a realistic urban-driving simulator to accurately model agent behaviors, a crucial component for self-driving car development. Most previous simulators focus on the plausibility of sensor data synthesis, whereas the plausibility of driving behaviors is poorly explored. To tackle this problem, we propose a hierarchical architecture, which comprises (i) a high-level intention simulation summarizing driving scenarios and (ii) a low-level policy trained by reinforcement algorithms to refine plans. Unlike existing simulators, our approach captures diverse behaviors, even sub-optimal ones, vital for robust policy training and evaluation. We also highlight the importance of interactive simulations over static scenarios for realistic policy development. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves long-term behavior prediction and closed-loop simulation, enhancing the realism and diversity of urban-driving simulations. The videos of this work are available in our project page: https://sites.google.com/ucsd.edu/h-sim/home.

title: A Digital Twin-Driven Improved MADDPG Multi-Robotic-Arm Cooperative Control Method
authors: Y. Liu; P. Wang; J. Huang; C. Jia
venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: To address the issues of low obstacle avoidance efficiency and slow convergence speed in multi-manipulator cooperative control in dynamic industrial environments, based on the background, a control strategy that combines Digital Twin (DT) technology with an improved version of the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is put forward. Moreover, with the use of MADDPG, an attention mechanism along with prioritized experience replay is adopted. Additionally, based on the improved MADDPG algorithm, a hierarchical collision penalty function together with an enhanced oscillation constraint mechanism is designed to improve its sensitivity to important environmental information as well as the efficiency of experience replay. The experiment results show that the improved MADDPG algorithm has strong robustness because, under the conditions of gradients with low, medium, and high densities of obstacles, the task completion ratio throughout the convergence process remains above 91.3 %.

title: VissimRL: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Traffic Signal Control Based on Vissim
authors: H. -C. Chang; S. -Y. Huang; Y. -C. Chen; I. -C. Wu
venue: 2026 IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)
abstract: Traffic congestion remains a major challenge for urban transportation, leading to significant economic and environmental impacts. Traffic Signal Control (TSC) is one of the key measures to mitigate congestion, and recent studies have increasingly applied Reinforcement Learning (RL) for its adaptive capabilities. With respect to SUMO and CityFlow, the simulator Vissim offers high-fidelity driver behavior modeling and wide industrial adoption but remains underutilized in RL research due to its complex interface and lack of standardized frameworks. To address this gap, this paper proposes VissimRL, a modular RL framework for TSC that encapsulates Vissim’s COM interface through a high-level Python API, offering standardized environments for both single- and multi-agent training. Experiments show that VissimRL significantly reduces development effort while maintaining runtime efficiency, and supports consistent improvements in traffic performance during training, as well as emergent coordination in multi-agent control. Overall, VissimRL demonstrates the feasibility of applying RL in high-fidelity simulations and serves as a bridge between academic research and practical applications in intelligent traffic signal control. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/CGI-LAB/VissimRL.

title: Output Formation Tracking for Heterogeneous MASs With Incomplete Leader Measurements: A Hybrid-Triggering Observer Approach
authors: B. Dong; L. Yan; C. Yan; Y. Xia
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper investigates the time-varying output formation tracking (TVOFT) problem for heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs) under the jointly observable condition (JOC). In practical applications, the neighboring followers of the leader often have access only to partial information due to external disturbances and occlusions, rendering existing formation control approaches ineffective. To address this challenge, we propose a set of distributed observers based on the JOC and a hybrid time-dynamic event-triggering mechanism (ETM) to estimate the leader’s state. Unlike standard ETMs, the triggering condition in the proposed hybrid triggering approach is evaluated only after a predetermined time interval, which serves as an explicit lower bound on the minimum inter-event time (MIET). This design ensures that the MIET remains positive. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed hybrid triggering approach effectively reduces redundant triggering actions while ensuring the robustness of communication performance against external disturbances. Building upon the developed distributed observer framework, we further propose a novel observer-based TVOFT scheme, which overcomes the conventional requirement that at least one follower must have full access to the leader’s state or output. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. Note to Practitioners—In dynamic and uncertain environments, such as those encountered by mobile robot teams or autonomous vehicle platoons, external disturbances, environmental occlusions, and limited communication bandwidth can significantly impair the performance of traditional formation control strategies. The existing formation control methods often rely on the strong assumption that at least one follower can access the complete state or output of the leader, which is rarely practical in real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel observer-based TVOFT scheme that operates solely on incomplete output measurements of the leader. In addition, a hybrid triggering mechanism is introduced to enable intermittent communication among agents. This design not only avoids excessive transmissions but also guarantees a strictly positive MIET, thereby improving both communication efficiency and robustness under disturbances. Numerical simulations suggest that this approach is feasible but it has not been tested in production. Future work will focus on improving formation safety performance by extending the proposed observer-based formation control approach to MASs under attack.

title: Multiagent MPC With Nash-Based Allocation for Vehicle Stability Control Under Tire Blowout
authors: Z. Li; H. Liu; X. Wang; L. Li; Y. Xu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: Tire blowouts can trigger serious vehicle instability due to the sudden loss of tire force, posing a critical threat to road safety. Conventional electronic stability control (ESC) based on differential braking may be insufficient under severe blowout conditions. Based on a systematic analysis of vehicle motion behavior for different blowout locations and driving conditions, this article proposes a hierarchical framework that combines multi-agent model predictive control (MA-MPC) with Nash-based control allocation. A reference motion is generated to preserve the driver’s steering intention while respecting the tire-road friction limit. At the upper layer, the MA-MPC, built on a blowout-adapted vehicle model, generates the desired longitudinal force, lateral force, and yaw moment for stability regulation. The lower layer then formulates the distribution of these demands among the drive, brake, and steering actuators as a three-player game under force degradation and actuator limits. Convergence of the Nash iteration to the unique equilibrium is theoretically proven. Hardware-in-the-loop tests further verify the framework under blowout detection delays and uncooperative driver inputs. Real-vehicle experiments then validate it under representative two-tire and three-tire blowouts. The MA-MPC layer accelerates sideslip recovery and improves the residual tracking accuracy, while the Nash-based allocation improves actuator coordination and markedly reduces the steering correction demand.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Driven Nanobot Collectives for Micro-Thrombus Localization and Cardiovascular Flow Optimization
authors: S. G; S. K. Henge
venue: 2026 IEEE Global Symposium on Emerging and Communication Technologies (GSEACT)
abstract: Nanorobotic assemblies present a disruptive solution to the early-stage cardiovascular diagnostics and therapy, especially at micro-thrombus sensing in a complicated microcirculation setting, the place where standard imaging cannot resolve. This paper has included a detailed simulationbased platform that has incorporated (i) 3D patient-specific cardiovascular CFD; (ii) a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) system built upon Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs); (iii) multi-physics ultrasound and magnetic actuation models; and (iv) combined sensors of shear stress, Doppler flow, and thrombus probability. The nanobot swarms independently move around, track micro-thrombi, and improve local hemodynamics without violating vascular safety limits. Experiment evaluations on 150 simulated vascular models show that it can localize 92.4 percent, with a 39 percent reduction in pressure drop and a 61 percent reduction in recognition time compared to classical controllers. These findings have a good basis for future in vitro validation and preclinical cardiovascular nanorobotics.

title: Toward Auditable Multi-Agent AI: a Deterministic Framework for End-to-End Execution Traceability
authors: S. Mohanta; P. Apoorva; V. Jambale; A. Chakraborty; V. K; S. Natarajan
venue: 2026 IEEE Global Symposium on Emerging and Communication Technologies (GSEACT)
abstract: Multi-agent systems are being implemented in an increasing number of large language model (LLM) applications. In these systems, specialized agents are responsible for tasks such as planning, retrieval, reasoning, and generating responses. The modular design of the system renders it more adaptable and potent; however, it is also more challenging to monitor and rely on its functionality. This study introduces a traceable multiagent AI system that integrates deterministic agent orchestration with Retrieval-Augmented Generation to guarantee transparent and verifiable operation. The system neatly displays retrieval evidence, latency, token consumption, and validation results in execution traces. It fails to monitor sensitive chain-of-thought reasoning in order to ensure the safety and legality of the situation. An external write-only audit observer can witness the system's operations without altering its functionality. The experimental results imply that the proposed framework improves evidence grounding and traceability in comparison to traditional tracing methodologies. This renders it an appropriate substitute for locations that are subject to regulation and pose a significant risk.

title: The Drone Tree Network: A High-Assurance Distributed Framework for BVLOS-Compliant UAV Logistics
authors: P. Manimangalam
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: The commercialization of distributed Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) logistics, particularly Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) operations, requires addressing regulatory compliance, autonomous scalability, and system assurance. This paper presents the Drone Tree Network (DTN), a hierarchical cyberphysical framework designed to support performance-based BVLOS operations aligned with emerging Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 108 requirements. The DTN integrates a cognitive decision stack combining a Weighted Sum Model for mission prioritization with an enforced emergency dispatch threshold and a hybrid Lazy Theta and D Lite path-planning architecture for real-time rerouting. Payload release safety is ensured through a dual-authorization protocol requiring both cryptographic validation using a FIPS 140-3-compliant hardware module and physical ground verification via a convolutional neural network and PointNet-based sensor fusion model, generating a ground-stability confidence score. Command-andcontrol resilience is strengthened through frequency-hopping spread spectrum and Unscented Kalman Filter-based positioning integrity. Simulation-based validation demonstrates measurable improvements in path efficiency, command-and-control robustness under jamming conditions, and fleet scalability, providing empirical evidence toward scalable BVLOS-compliant UAV logistics.

title: Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-AAV Cooperative Pursuit With Sparse Team Rewards
authors: Y. Sun; X. Xiang; C. Yan; H. Zhou; X. Xu; J. Jiang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: With the rapid development of urban air mobility, cooperative pursuit with multiple autonomous aerial vehicles (multi-AAV) has become increasingly important for airspace security and emergency response applications. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has emerged as a mainstream paradigm for this problem. However, existing MARL methods mainly rely on dense individual rewards that encourage agents to maximize personal gains rather than team objectives, leading to suboptimal coordination. Consequently, learning effective cooperative pursuit policies under sparse team rewards remains a significant challenge, especially in obstacle-dense environments. In this article, we propose KG-MASAC, a knowledge-guided MARL approach for multi-AAV cooperative pursuit. To address this challenge, we introduce two knowledge guidance mechanisms. First, knowledge-augmented policy optimization provides coordination guidance through a cooperative force field. Second, an adaptive reward transition guides early exploration with dense auxiliary rewards, then progressively shifts to sparse team rewards as cooperative performance improves. We validate KG-MASAC through extensive simulations and physical experiments on indoor and outdoor AAV platforms. Results show that KG-MASAC achieves superior capture success, robust generalization to unseen obstacle densities and team sizes, emergent cooperative behaviors such as herding and encirclement, and successful sim-to-real transfer under environmental uncertainties. Note to Practitioners—Multi-AAV cooperative pursuit of fast-moving targets in obstacle-dense environments underpins applications from low-altitude airspace patrol to intruder interception. However, existing methods rely on hand-shaped individual rewards that demand extensive tuning but often produce selfish rather than cooperative behaviors. To address this, we present KG-MASAC, a practical approach that learns team-oriented pursuit policies from sparse task-level feedback. By leveraging force field priors and an adaptive reward curriculum that automatically transitions from dense to sparse signals, KG-MASAC reduces the need for manual reward shaping and curriculum design. Once trained, the policy transfers zero-shot to both indoor motion-capture arenas and outdoor GPS-based settings, demonstrating robust generalization across quadrotor platforms, localization modalities, and environmental disturbances. Future work will explore dynamic obstacles and multi-target pursuit to further extend this generalization.

title: Multi-robot obstacle-aware shepherding of non-cohesive target agents
authors: C. Tomaselli; S. Covone; A. Reina; M. Di Bernardo
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel control strategy for multi-agent shepherding of non-cohesive targets in obstacle-rich environments. Unlike previous approaches that assume cohesive flocking behavior, our method handles targets that interact only with nearby herders through repulsive forces and exhibit no inter-target coordination. Each herder employs a hybrid control policy that combines direct goal-oriented steering with obstacle-tangent maneuvering, enabling targets to circumnavigate obstacles while being guided toward a goal region. The herder dynamics integrate three key behaviors: return-to-goal motion when idle, target steering with adaptive directional control, and obstacle avoidance using both normal and tangential force components. Numerical simulations demonstrate superior performance compared to existing shepherding methods, achieving higher target confinement rates in cluttered environments. Experimental validation using Turtle-Bot4 herders and Osoyoo target robots in an indoor arena confirms the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Mitigation of Fragmentation Jailbreak Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems: An Architecture Based on Global Semantic Monitoring
authors: D. Romero; C. Alonso
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs) into multi-agent and embodied artificial intelligence (Embodied AI) systems has significantly expanded the attack surface of digital services. Current safetyalignment mechanisms are increasingly effective against direct jailbreak attempts on individual agents, but multi-agent architectures remain vulnerable to fragmentation jailbreak attacks. In a fragmentation jailbreak, a malicious instruction is split into seemingly innocuous subtasks that are distributed across agents and processed in isolation. In this article, we present an empirical study and an architecture proposal aimed at mitigating this phenomenon, which we term “context washing”. To validate our hypothesis, we have developed a simulation environment based on a two-phase architecture: a Planning Phase, in which an uncensored LLM running locally via Ollama generates a structured attack plan in JSON, and an Execution Phase, in which domain-specific agents with safety guardrails execute the fragmented steps in isolation. We illustrate the threat in ten safety-critical, language-level Embodied AI scenarios spanning chemistry, aviation, diving, electrical maintenance, and hospital radiology, in which the fragmented plan culminates in actions that would violate Asimov's First Law. To address this risk, we introduce a Monitor Agent that supervises the execution chain in parallel, similar to an intrusion detection system in network security. This component audits the execution chain in real time and evaluates the semantic trace globally -augmented by a domainspecific knowledge base- to identify latent fragmentation tactics. This provides preliminary evidence that global monitoring can help mitigate confused-deputy failures in the evaluated scenarios by maintaining an analytical context of the activity of all agents in the system. All attacks and defenses are validated purely at the language level: no real actuators, robots, or external APIs are involved.

title: Cooperative and Conflict-Aware Alerting Using Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning in Rural Intersections for CAVs
authors: C. Jeyaseelan; K. S. Balasubramanyam; R. Suresha; N. Manohar; G. Ajay Kumar
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) are reshaping mobility, yet rural intersections remain a persistent challenge where heterogeneous traffic, limited infrastructure, and frequent occlusions complicate safe navigation. Existing approaches using multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) show promise, but they often struggle with scalability, efficiency, and priority-aware conflict resolution. This paper presents a conflict-aware intersection alerting framework that integrates Relational Graph Convolutional Networks (RGCNs) with a Hybrid Proximal Policy Optimization (HPPO) to address these limitations. Vehicles are modelled as graph nodes enriched with spatial and kinematic features, while multi-relational edges capture proximity, geometric conflicts, and time-to-collision risks. The Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent, guided by pre-trained critic values from extensive Car Learning to Act (CARLA) simulations, generates context-specific alerts that adapt to dynamic traffic states. A safety controller with PPO, complements reinforcement learning by enforcing collision avoidance, deadlock prevention, and prioritized zone release across vehicle types and with their arrival times. Evaluation across diverse unsignalized intersection geometries demonstrates measurable improvements in safety and traffic efficiency. The proposed framework reduced collision rates from 56.75% to 2% in 3-way intersections and from 37.5% to 22.62% in 4-way intersections, while maintaining queue reductions up to 1.28% and average speeds upto 4.92 m/s. By combining relational reasoning with reinforcement learning and safety-aware control, this framework advances intersection management for CAVs in rural contexts, mitigating risks associated with occlusion, heterogeneous traffic, and limited infrastructure, and contributing to safer, more efficient, and sustainable mobility systems.

title: Agentic AI for Autonomous Decision-Making in Large-Scale Distributed Systems: Patch Orchestration for Critical Infrastructure
authors: N. Leuva; C. Patadia; U. Goyal
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Mechatronics Systems (AIMS)
abstract: Maintaining software patches is essential for the security and reliability of modern distributed systems, especially in infrastructure environments that rely on geographically dispersed endpoints. Traditional patch management approaches use static rollout policies and reactive failure handling, which can increase operational risk at scale. This paper proposes a bounded agentic AI framework for autonomous patch orchestration in large-scale distributed systems. The framework combines patch impact analysis, environment-state assessment, digital-twin-based simulation, policy-constrained multi-objective risk scoring, phased deployment, and adaptive feedback. Candidate rollout strategies are evaluated before execution, and deployment decisions are refined using telemetry from prior rollout stages. A scenario-driven simulation over 1,000–5,000 endpoints compares the proposed framework with a rule-based static rollout baseline. Under representative simulation assumptions, the results indicate potential reductions of 81% in rollout planning time from 4.0 hours to 0.75 hours, 46% in critical patch MTTR from 26 hours to 14 hours, 43% in rollback rate from 6.8% to 3.9%, and 71% in network transfer from 14.4 TB to 4.2 TB per cycle. The main contribution is a decision-oriented architecture that integrates agentic planning, digital twin validation, and closed-loop adaptation for safer patch orchestration in critical distributed infrastructure.

title: Compliance Factor-Based Artificial Potential Fields for Collision-Aware UAV Swarm Tracking
authors: T. Loctin; M. Omar; E. M. Mudassir; K. Bingi; R. B. Ibrahim
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Mechatronics Engineering (ICOM)
abstract: The deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms poses a major technical challenge for modern surveillance, search-and-rescue, and industrial inspection missions. Unlike traditional monolithic architectures that rely on a single central supercomputer, this paper proposes a fully decentralized control architecture. The system is developed using the Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) framework, leveraging its Data Distribution Service (DDS) protocol to ensure asynchronous and robust node communication without a single point of failure. The objective is to coordinate a fleet of five drones to navigate autonomously in a complex environment, avoid collisions, and track a moving target. Using a PID controller for low-level stabilization and an Artificial Potential Field (APF) approach enhanced with a dynamic compliance factor, the swarm can dynamically elect a tracker and maintain a tactical formation. The results demonstrate the proposed method’s potential for high-speed, real-time obstacle avoidance in a simulation environment while maintaining decentralized communication among the UAVs.

title: Multi-Agent Optimization for Railway Network Scheduling and Coordination
authors: S. George; R. Manassa; M. Medhat; R. Sameh; Y. Salama; S. Yacoub; J. Magdy; O. M. Shehata
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Sustainable Systems for Computer and Engineering Applications (3SCEA)
abstract: Railway station throats represent critical bottlenecks in modern transportation networks, where high traffic density and complex platform-track topologies create significant scheduling challenges. This paper addresses the multiobjective optimization problem of assigning trains to platforms and determining arrival and departure times while minimizing both total makespan and energy consumption. We systematically implement and evaluate six distinct approaches: First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) baseline, Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) on a benchmark 30-train instance. Experimental results demonstrate that metaheuristic optimization delivers substantial improvements over baseline approaches. While Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) achieved the lowest numerical makespan and energy, it failed to meet strict safety constraints, rendering it operationally infeasible. Consequently, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) emerged as the overall superior approaches, delivering the best balance of makespan reduction and energy efficiency while maintaining 100% feasibility. All metaheuristic methods significantly outperform the FCFS baseline and achieve dramatic 75% reductions compared to the single-platform worst case. The study concludes that population-based metaheuristics provide effective solutions for complex railway scheduling problems, making them promising candidates for real-world deployment in automated railway timetabling systems.

title: Theory-Grounded LLM Societies for Emergent Coordination
authors: J. de Curtò; I. de Zarzà
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Recent generative-agent frameworks demonstrate that large language models (LLMs) can produce socially plausible behavior in multi-agent simulations, yet their strategy dynamics remain ungrounded: agents update beliefs through narrative reasoning alone, without the evolutionary and game-theoretic mechanisms known to govern cooperation in structured populations. We introduce Coevolutionary Generative Societies (CGS), an architecture that fuses LLM deliberation with evolutionary cooperation theory (EC-theory) to produce stable, resilient cooperative equilibria on interaction networks. Each agent maintains episodic memory and updates its cooperation propensity through a three-component rule combining Fermi-function social learning from neighbors, sigmoid individual reinforcement normalized by network degree, and a $\beta $ -weighted advisory signal from a Solver–Critic–Aggregator deliberation pipeline, where the solver proposes an action, a critic evaluates strategic soundness, and a deterministic aggregator fuses both signals, flipping the proposed action on strong disagreement. We evaluate CGS on Watts–Strogatz, Barabási–Albert, and Erdös–Rényi networks ( $n = 40$ , $T = 50$ steps) under a standard Prisoner’s Dilemma with an adversarial shock at $t = 30$ that forces 15% of agents to defect. CGS achieves peak cooperation rates of 0.80 and recovers from adversarial shocks within 8 time steps, whereas a narrative-only ablation (pure LLM-driven updates, no EC dynamics) plateaus at 0.55 cooperation and exhibits no dynamic response to perturbation. A no-critic ablation confirms that the full deliberation pipeline contributes measurable gains over solver-only inference. Cross-topology analysis reveals that small-world networks yield the highest cooperation and lowest payoff inequality (Gini = 0.236), while scale-free networks amplify inequality through hub concentration (Gini = 0.420). Ten-seed replication establishes that the qualitative distinction between CGS and a narrative-only ablation is statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (Cohen’s $d = 4.59$ on cooperation responsiveness, $p_{\mathrm {Bonf}} \lt 0.001$ ; CGS-EC remains dynamically adaptive in 9 of 10 seeds whereas the narrative-only baseline converges to a static equilibrium in 10 of 10). Population scaling to n = 80, a four-model sweep, alternative game substrates (Snowdrift, Stag Hunt), and five non-LLM learning and imitation baselines confirm that the dynamics are preserved across initialisations, scales, LLM families, and game classes. Comparison against GNN structural baselines, which replace LLM deliberation with graph message-passing, quantifies the LLM advisory premium at + 20.2% cooperation over the best structural baseline, establishing the respective contributions of evolutionary structure and language-model advisory. An OAT sensitivity analysis confirms that the fixed architectural weights are robust (NSI < 0.1 for $\kappa $ and $w_{\ell } $ ), and temperature robustness experiments across $T_{s} \in \{0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8\}$ confirm insensitivity to LLM sampling stochasticity (CV = 0.6% on final cooperation). Our results establish that grounding LLM-agent societies in evolutionary game-theoretic update rules is essential for emergent coordination within the tested regime ( $n\le 80$ , $T=50$ , PD/Snowdrift/Stag Hunt, single shocks up to 15%), and that the topology of the interaction network significantly modulates both the level and the equity of cooperation.

title: Minimizing Costs in UAV Inspection Routing: Trade-offs Between Fleet Size and Recharging Strategies
authors: Y. Sun; G. Qi; W. Guan; R. Guo
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Transportation Systems (RAITS)
abstract: Battery powered unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed for infrastructure inspection, yet planning remains challenging due to limited endurance and the non negligible time and cost of energy replenishment. Prior UAV routing studies are largely delivery oriented or assume fixed traversal directions for inspection tasks. Moreover, charging is often represented through hard endurance constraints, while the cost impact of charging dwell time is seldom incorporated; the trade off between fleet availability and recharging behavior is also rarely quantified. This study investigates routing optimization for UAVs performing multiple inspection tasks. Given a network with depots, charging stations, and task endpoints, the problem jointly determines UAV dispatching, node visiting sequences, task execution directions, and charging actions to minimize total cost, including takeoff cost, travel time cost, and charging cost, subject to depot time windows and a minimum battery safety threshold. A mixed integer linear programming model is formulated and solved using Gurobi. A sensitivity analysis on an instance with three tasks and two charging stations evaluates available fleet sizes from one to five UAVs. Results show that increasing the available fleet size from one to three reduces total cost by $\mathbf{4 2. 2 \%} \boldsymbol{(} \mathbf{1 8 1. 7 5 0}$ to 105.125), primarily by eliminating charging operations. Allowing four or five UAVs yields no additional reduction, and the optimal solution dispatches only three UAVs, indicating a critical fleet size of three under the tested setting.

title: Linear Reciprocating RGV Inbound and Outbound Scheduling With Movable Buffer Zone
authors: T. Li; S. Lin; Y. Sun
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: In traditional Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS), shared fixed tracks for Rail Guided Vehicles (RGVs) are prone to congestion and collisions, leading to reduced efficiency. To address this, this paper proposes introducing movable buffer zone on straight tracks to physically isolate RGVs, enabling them to operate independently within their respective zones and avoid obstacles. The scheduling scheme must simultaneously consider task sequences and buffer zone location, increasing the complexity and practicality of the scheduling problem. A mathematical model is constructed with the objective of minimizing the maximum completion time of RGV tasks. An Adaptive Genetic Algorithm (AGA) is employed to solve the complex scheduling problem integrating task sequences and buffer zone location. Comparative testing across small, medium, and large task scenarios demonstrated time efficiency improvements of 15.10%, 10.27%, and 3.97%, respectively. Experimental results confirm that the scheduling scheme combining movable buffer zone with the Adaptive Genetic Algorithm significantly enhances RGV system operational efficiency. Its optimization performance surpasses traditional fixed-buffer approaches, offering an efficient and feasible new solution for resolving RGV track-sharing conflicts.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Decentralized AI in Autonomous Drone Swarms
authors: V. Pal; G. Sarraf; M. Bhende; S. Patil
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI Engineering and Innovations (AIEI)
abstract: The collaborative aspect of drone swarms endangers smooth functioning of services and security of national facilities. Multi-Agent Deep Learning (DL) Coordinating swarms of drones in dynamic systems are not simple tasks, but learning is proving to be a legitimate solution. The paper introduces a new end-to-end UAV swarm intelligence system that combines DL and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to achieve autonomous and coordinated actions of drones. The system uses a new UAV swarm intelligence system that is based on YOLOv8 detection, DeepSORT-like tracking, and multi-agent PPO reinforcement. YOLOv8n model has the following performance: 0.91 precision, 0.83 F1-score, and 6.6 ms processing time per frame. The tracker is running at 151.5 FPS, ensuring the identities of the UAVs are the same throughout the movie. A specialized DroneSwarmEnv trains drones in formation control as well as in collision avoidance and cooperative navigation thus achieving an average reward of 1,886 with minimal collisions. In order to encourage generalization, real and synthetic UAVSwarm datasets are employed, consequently, training diversity and adaptability are multiplied. An in-depth analysis and visualization have indicated that the detection, tracking, and swarm behavior performance is outstanding and proves the policy convergence and policy stability. The system is of low weight, scalable, and is applicable for real-time deployment, thus providing a huge potential for uses such as autonomous surveillance, disaster monitoring, and aerial mission planning.

title: Approximation-Free Fault-Resilient Prescribed Performance Consensus Tracking for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Q. Xu; G. Guo; C. -L. Zhang; Y. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article proposes a resilient approximation-free control architecture that enhances the robustness of prescribed performance control (PPC) for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) under inelastic actuator faults, while retaining the transient and steady-state performance achieved in nominal (fault-free) operation. During actuator faults, the applied control action may deviate from the commanded input due to unknown inelastic fault effects, which can temporarily degrade regulation performance and cause transient bound violations. To address this problem, a fault-resilient PPC architecture is developed by smoothly reconfiguring the PPC-based controller into a safety-oriented mode when the consensus tracking errors approach the prescribed performance envelopes. By allowing short-term violations of the performance bounds, the design mitigates PPC-induced instability associated with the barrier-function formulation and maintains closed-loop stability under adverse conditions. The fault onset and severity evolution are assumed unknown, and no explicit fault detection/diagnosis module is required. Simulation and experimental results corroborate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design.

title: Autonomous Agentic Edge Operating Systems: Architectural Frameworks for Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination and Real-Time Hardware Interfacing
authors: A. S B; S. P G; A. M; B. Subramani
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abstract: The issue of implementing AI agents on cloud servers is causing more issues, which the majority of people do not discuss openly. The latency is excessive, the dependability is not high enough, and in any respect of safety use it is practically unserviceable at all. Our paper is on the Agentic Edge OS-an operating system which we created ourselves based on a blank embedded board such as the Raspberry Pi 4B, to execute AI agents directly on its embedded edge hardware. To create a system that does all its thinking without the help of a cloud server, we simply created a simple Buildroot-based Linux image and coordination protocols of the Multi-Agent System. The system is based on systemd controlled Python runtime, Redis shared state and direct access to hardware via Python GPIO and PWM. Another thing that not many people have tried previously is letting agents read plain English instructions and figure out hardware wiring and GPIO mappings automatically. On our test, the edge approach is about 160 times faster than cloud configurations, as well as $1.79 \times$ faster than kernel scheduling. These figures indicate clearly that edge running intelligence is highly sensible to the robotics, industrial control, and smarter infrastructure systems.

title: SCALE-COMM: Shared, Contrastively-Aligned Latent Embeddings for MARL Communication
authors: M. Abouelyazid; E. Hammad
venue: 2026 IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)
abstract: Emergent communication enables partially observant Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to coordinate effectively in decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) settings. However, existing approaches often struggle with unstable communication protocols, ungrounded message semantics, and interference between communication learning and policy optimization, leading to degraded coordination over time. We propose SCALE-COMM (Shared, Contrastively-Aligned Latent Embeddings for COMMunication), a self-supervised framework for learning compact, stable, and policy-relevant communication representations. SCALE-COMM decouples communication learning from policy optimization by training low-dimensional latent messages that capture task-relevant planning and traffic information, while enforcing consistency across agents and time. Across standard MARL benchmarks and a realistic warehouse coordination task, SCALE-COMM consistently outperforms existing communication frameworks in both representation quality and task performance. The learned communication space yields improved stability, sample efficiency, and throughput under policy fine-tuning, demonstrating the effectiveness of representation-driven communication for scalable multi-agent coordination.

title: Quantization-Induced Robustness Collapse in EdgeDeployed Language Models: Security and Governance Frameworks for 6G IoT Ecosystems
authors: K. Pandey; N. Kyadiggeri; N. Shukla
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Emerging and Intelligent Technologies and Systems (EITS)
abstract: The rapid migration of generative foundation models from centralized cloud infrastructure to decentralized network edges marks a fundamental shift in both technical orchestration and organizational governance. To address this gap, we develop and curate a benchmark that examines the socio-technical tensions arising from the deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs) across sixth-generation (6 G) wireless infrastructure and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. Although decentralized deployment improves latency, bandwidth efficiency, and data sovereignty, it also introduces critical architectural and governance vulnerabilities driven by hardware-induced safety degradation. By combining sociotechnical systems theory with advanced cryptographic and networking formalisms, this paper proposes a unified codesign framework that balances hardware-constrained efficiency, operational safety, and task accuracy. Through fine-tuning on this benchmark, we trace the taxonomic evolution of edge-capable foundation models and identify a socio-technical phenomenon termed quantization-induced robustness collapse, demonstrating how mathematical network optimization can inadvertently undermine algorithmic policy adherence. Finally, we present an actionable research roadmap that highlights cooperative parameter alignment and holistic energy-to-token optimization as essential requirements for next-generation digital societies.

title: Self-Attention-Enhanced Multiagent Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAVs Target Search in Obstacle-Dense Environments
authors: M. Liu; L. Xie; L. Xiao; S. Guo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: In the field of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) decision-making, cooperative target search by multiple UAVs represents a central research focus. Recent advancements in neural-network-based deep reinforcement learning, coupled with improvements in UAV performance, have significantly enhanced the intelligent decision-making capabilities of UAVs in unknown and dynamic environments. However, as search scenarios grow in scale and complexity, existing UAV search methods increasingly struggle to maintain efficient search performance. To address these challenges, this study introduces a multiagent deep deterministic policy gradient integrated with a self-attention mechanism (SA-MADDPG) algorithm, which integrates a self-attention mechanism to facilitate global spatial information modeling. By effectively capturing long-range dependencies within complex, high-dimensional spatial data, such as obstacle distributions, teammate positions, and target probabilities, the algorithm overcomes the constraints of localized receptive fields inherent in conventional architectures. This enables agents to prioritize critical environmental features, thereby significantly enhancing collaborative decision-making in obstacle-dense settings. Furthermore, we develop a dual-incentive exploration mechanism that synthesizes Bayesian-updated target probability maps with Voronoi-region partitioning to enhance multi-UAV collaborative coordination and search reliability. Experimental results reveal that the proposed SA-MADDPG method significantly outperforms existing search strategies across critical metrics, including collision rate, coverage rate, and target detection rate.

title: Swarm-Steward: Scalable and Reliable Natural-Language Coordination of Autonomous Aerial and Ground Robots
authors: A. Jarabo-Peñas; J. Bravo-Arrabal; E. G. A. Rolland; A. L. Christensen
venue: 2026 International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (ICUAS)
abstract: We present Swarm-Steward, a platform-agnostic system for natural-language multi-robot control that enables a non-expert operator to coordinate many drones by creating and commanding groups, bridging high-level intent to reliable, lowlevel execution. Swarm-Steward uses a hierarchical LLM-based multi-agent design where planning and context gathering are separated from actuation: specialized agents ground requests in map features and telemetry, while a dedicated actionexecution stage composes group actions and dispatches only deterministic, schema-constrained commands through a safety gate (e.g., geofencing, altitude and separation limits), with optional operator preview before execution. To keep grounding scalable, Swarm-Steward applies dual retrieval-augmented generation over both map features (Feature RAG) and telemetry variables (State RAG), injecting only relevant candidates at each step. In scalability tests, Feature RAG remains effective with up to 10,000 features, and end-to-end sessions from 5 to 500 drones maintain near-constant LLM token cost with $\text{9 2. 9 \%}$ task success across 280 prompts. The observed failures arise from prompt-specific scaling limits at larger swarm sizes, rather than from incorrect coordinator planning. Finally, we validate sim-toreal transfer by executing the same mission script in simulation and on a real-world DJI Mini 4 Pro swarm, demonstrating consistent behavior across comparable mission phases without modifying the LLM multi-agent system layer.

title: LLM-DTS: Resilience Formation Control Via Semantic Reasoning and Adaptive Topology Switching
authors: X. Zhou; Y. Zhang; Z. Zhou; D. Xue
venue: 2026 IEEE 20th International Conference on Control and Automation (ICCA)
abstract: Achieving robust formation navigation for MultiRobot Systems (MRS) in complex and non-convex environments remains a fundamental challenge in modern robotics. Traditional Model Predictive Control (MPC) methods, which rely on fixed parameters and rigid topologies, are highly susceptible to local minima and navigation deadlocks when encountering dense obstacle traps or narrow apertures. To address these limitations, this paper proposes LLM-DTS, a hierarchical method that utilizes a Large Language Model (LLM) as a cognitive reasoner to perform environmental semantic analysis and dynamically reconfigure the underlying MPC topology and control parameters. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method increases navigation success rates across diverse scenarios and enables autonomous formation reshaping to traverse extreme spatial bottlenecks, enhancing the stability and environmental adaptability of the system.

title: Safe Coverage Control via Optimal Transport and Control Barrier Functions
authors: G. N. P. Pratama; I. Ardiyanto; A. I. Cahyadi
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper addresses multi-agent coverage control with safety requirements in environments with obstacles. The nominal Optimal Transport Coverage Control (OTCC) law derives from the Kantorovich dual of the optimal transport problem and follows the prior formulation for workload balancing through auxiliary potentials. A Lyapunov function based on the primal-dual gap establishes local exponential stability of the nominal dynamics when a gain ratio condition holds. To enforce collision avoidance, we incorporate Control Barrier Functions (CBF) through a quadratic program that modifies the nominal control. The CBF implementation uses soft constraints with slack variables to preserve feasibility when safety constraints conflict with velocity limits. For comparison, we also implement Artificial Potential Fields (APF) in simulation. We conduct ten simulation runs with random initial positions for agents and obstacles. Both methods achieve nearly identical coverage performance. OTCC with CBF keeps the minimum agent-obstacle distance at the safety threshold of 0.300 across all runs and the Lyapunov derivative negative at every time step. OTCC with APF allows the distance to drop to 0.289 and produces occasional positive Lyapunov steps. In narrow passages, OTCC with APF becomes trapped in local minima while OTCC with CBF navigates through and reaches the centroids. The CBF method requires $8.6 \times 10^{6}$ operations per step compared to $4.0 \times 10^{5}$ for APF, but provides smoother control, stronger stability guarantees, and more reliable safety enforcement. These advantages make CBF the preferred choice for safety-critical multi-agent coverage tasks when computational resources permit.

title: Agentic Service-Oriented Computing: A Manifesto for the Next Frontier of Service-Oriented Computing
authors: A. Beheshti; R. N. Chang; B. Benatallah; F. Casati; S. Dustdar; G. Fox; Q. Z. Sheng; Y. Wang; J. Yang; A. Zomaya
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
abstract: The rapid emergence of LLM-powered autonomous and semi-autonomous agents is reshaping software systems from static, request-response components into goal-directed, adaptive, and tool-using computational actors. As these agents move from isolated cognitive prototypes into complex distributed workflows, they confront challenges that the Service-Oriented Computing community has studied for more than two decades: composition, interoperability, quality of service, lifecycle management, governance, security, and trust. Yet much of today's agentic AI ecosystem is developing these foundations ad hoc, without the engineering rigour required for dependable enterprise and societal deployment. This paper introduces Agentic Service-Oriented Computing (ASOC) as a new research and practice area concerned with engineering agents as services, orchestrating services through autonomous and semi-autonomous agents, and governing ecosystems of agents and services under constraints of trust, cybersecurity, compliance, performance, and accountability. We articulate six foundational principles of ASOC (harness-ability, composability, lifecycle engineering, trustworthiness by design, goal-driven orchestration, and observability/accountability) and organise a five-dimensional research agenda spanning: (i) agentic services foundations and lifecycle engineering; (ii) composition, orchestration, and interoperability; (iii) governance, observability, and accountability; (iv) security, trust, and risk management; and (v) evaluation, certification, and Agentic QoS. We argue that the Services Computing community is especially well positioned to provide the conceptual and engineering spine for this emerging field, transforming agentic AI from fragmented demonstrations into dependable, service-based systems worthy of human and organisational trust.

title: Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Survey of Foundational Algorithms, Recent Advances, and Future Directions
authors: N. Ramshankar; D.Elangovan; S. P. K. S; J. S. A. Johnsana; F. R. A; S. K. Verma
venue: 2026 10th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged to be one of the most radical ideas in artificial intelligence since it enables the learner to learn the desired behavior through a response to the environment. The survey provides the overall picture of reinforcement learning, its development history beginning with the classical techniques up to the state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning algorithms. The paper provides a comprehensive explanation of the concepts and algorithmic structures and theoretical under-pinnings of the current RL systems. Such value-based approaches discussed in this paper include Q-Learning and Deep Q-Networks, such policy gradient techniques as REINFORCE and Actor-Critic, and such more sophisticated techniques as Trust Region Policy Optimization and Proximal Policy Optimization. This paper focuses on the more recent developments in model-based RL, multi-agent systems and hierarchical reinforcement learning and also offers commentary on the application to robotics, game playing, autonomous systems and resource management. Additionally, this methodology describes such issues as the efficiency of the sample, the conflict between exploration and exploitation, and safety issues and offers some of the prospects of future studies. As a source, it is not only an introduction to new readers, but also an independently useful resource to researchers who may wish to discover what the state of the field of reinforcement learning is.

title: Learning Cooperative Strategies for Drone Swarms using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: C. Llanes; K. A. Williams; S. W. Jensen; S. Coogan
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: In this work, we investigate cooperative strategies for an evader drone team of various sizes using multi-agent reinforcement learning in a multi-agent pursuit-evasion scenario. The objective of the evader team is to reach a goal with minimal velocity while not colliding with the pursuer team. The objective of the pursuer team is to defend the goal by catching evaders before they reach it. In this environment, we allow the pursuer to have superior control authority compared to the evader such that reaching the goal is challenging for the evader in a one-on-one scenario. The proposed strategy for an evader is to team up with an ally to lead pursuers into a collision with each other instead of intercepting the evader. We design policies using multi-agent proximal policy optimization, an actor-critic reinforcement learning method, and investigate how the learned strategy changes when we vary the size of the pursuer and evader teams. Finally, we demonstrate the learned policy’s sim-to-real capabilities through a hardware demonstration.

title: Navigating Embodied Intelligence: Enabling Technologies, Security and Privacy, and Emerging Trends
authors: Y. Wang; X. Niu; J. Ba; Z. Su; L. Du
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Driven by recent advances of large models and agents, embodied artificial intelligence (AI) emerges as a transformative paradigm for next-generation AI, endowing agents with physical forms and the ability to perceive, reason, and act within real-world environments. Unlike disembodied or virtual AI agent systems, embodied agents coevolve cognition, control, and embodiment through continuous feedback loops, enabling applications ranging from humanoid robots to autonomous vehicles. In this survey, we first introduce a dual-brain architecture of embodied AI and examine its foundational technologies and key characteristics. We then analyze the security and privacy landscape, identifying critical vulnerabilities and evaluating existing/potential countermeasures. Finally, we outline emerging trends and open research directions in this emerging field, charting a roadmap toward efficient, secure, and ethically aligned embodied AI ecosystems.

title: AI-Driven Attention and Integer Programming for Optimal Motion Planning and Control in Autonomous Vehicles
authors: Z. Wu; F. Sun; Q. Gao; J. Qiu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: AI-based motion planning in autonomous vehicles requires not only efficient path generation but also real-time adaptation under uncertainty, limited onboard resources, and stringent safety requirements. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates Transformer-based attention mechanisms with Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) to enable intelligent, constraint-aware trajectory planning and control. The attention module learns to prioritize critical waypoints and generate informed initial solutions based on real-time traffic dynamics, vehicle states, and environmental context. These solutions are then globally optimized via MIP to ensure collision-free motion, optimal resource usage, and task fulfillment within safety and stability bounds. By combining AI perception with mathematical optimization, the proposed system demonstrates strong performance in fault tolerance, real-time scheduling, and safety-critical control, offering a viable solution for next-generation autonomous driving systems and intelligent transportation networks.

title: Detour-Delta Task Assignment for Reservation-Based Online MAPD
authors: T. Hirayama; K. Yoshida; H. Sakaji; I. Noda
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Space-efficient automated warehouses often create narrow single-agent aisles, dead ends, and tree-like layouts. In such layouts, reservation-table planners that commit both task paths and safe retreat paths provide a natural way to avoid collisions and deadlocks. We propose detour-delta (Delta), a plug-in task-scoring rule that evaluates extra travel time under already committed space–time reservations beyond the spatial shortest-path baseline that ignores other agents’ reservations. Delta ranks candidate tasks by this extra planned delivery time beyond the geometric baseline, while preserving the planner’s collision/deadlock-avoidance mechanism. With Delta applied to the Safe HAven Retreat Planner (SHARP), a fixed-haven reservation-table planner for structurally constrained layouts, in 2250 structural-map runs SHARP+Delta completes every released task and improves makespan (latest delivery completion time) and service time (release-to-delivery time) in all 45 structural configuration means. On the tree map, only the SHARP-family methods complete every released task under the tested task stream. PIBT and PIBTTP-TA complete all released tasks on some structurally constrained layouts, but their makespan and service time remain higher than SHARP+Delta’s. Well-formed maps are where many MAPF/MAPD baselines can complete the task stream and structural bottlenecks are weaker; even in this less favorable setting for congestion-aware scoring, SHARP+Delta significantly improves SHARP and ranks second to LNS-wPBS in the normalized makespan/service summaries.

title: Real-Time Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization via GPU-Accelerated MPC
authors: F. Rastgar; T. Stoyanov
venue: 2026 European Control Conference (ECC)
abstract: We present a GPU-accelerated trajectory optimization framework for scalable, real-time multi-agent motion planning in both 2D and 3D environments. The proposed method refines nominal trajectories using a model predictive control (MPC) approach, incorporating collision avoidance with obstacles and neighboring agents. By formulating the problem to exploit parallel computation, the optimizer efficiently handles tens of agents simultaneously. The algorithm supports dynamic environments by allowing local updates in response to unforeseen perturbations. We validate our method through a diverse set of simulated scenarios, demonstrating smooth and feasible trajectories with low computational overhead. Comparative analysis in 2D scenarios against the RVO2 baseline highlights improvements in smoothness and path quality.

title: LLM-Enabled Human-in-the-Loop Control of Multi-UAV Teams under Communication Constraints
authors: K. G. Alamdar; F. Petric; M. Orsag
venue: 2026 International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (ICUAS)
abstract: This work presents a human-in-the-loop framework for coordinating multi-UAV teams in disaster environments, where a large language model serves as a naturallanguage interface between a human operator and a swarm of UAVs operating under short-range communication constraints. The system is demonstrated in a mission scenario in which a ground robot explores an environment while UAVs act as communication relays to maintain connectivity between the robot and a base station. The operator provides high-level guidance that complements an autonomous connectivity-andperching controller. The framework is evaluated in multiple simulated environments using connectivity and missionduration metrics, together with interaction measures such as command-to-execution delay. Experiments show that trained user interaction can outperform the fully autonomous baseline in multiple environments.

title: Toward Efficient Utilization of Low-Altitude Airspace: A Unified Approach Integrating Architecture Frameworks and Operations Research
authors: W. Chen; L. Li
venue: IEEE Intelligent Transportation Systems Magazine
abstract: This article presents a unified approach that integrates the unified architecture framework (UAF) with operations research to automate design and optimization of low-altitude airspace systems of systems. We extend the UAF domain metamodel with lightweight stereotypes within strategic, operational, service, resource, and actual resource views. An optimization bridge view generates solver-neutral mixed-integer linear programming models that minimize mission time while enforcing explicit energy budget and safety separation constraints and feeds the optimization results back into the architecture for iterative refinement. We validate the methodology on a 1,000-case urban logistics scenario by formulating a multidepot heterogeneous fleet vehicle routing problem (MDHFVRP) directly from the architecture models. The baseline architecture yields a mean operating time of 23.32 min, meeting the service target in 72.75% of cases. Introducing a moving-depot extension and solving the resulting moving MDHFVRP with a gradient-guided large-neighborhood search reduce the mean to 21.20 min, achieving the target in 96.09% of scenarios at a median solve time of 10.88 s. The coupled pipeline preserves full traceability from strategic goals to detailed optimization outputs and supports rapid tradeoff analysis and bottleneck diagnosis.

title: Quantifying Risk Propagation in Agentic AI Networks: A Simulation Framework and Singularity Index Approach
authors: S. M. Naeem; S. H. M. Raza; A. Shabbir; S. U. Hussaini
venue: 2026 International Conference on AI Innovations and Industry (ICAIII)
abstract: As agentic AI systems gain autonomy and self-optimization capabilities; they increasingly operate within complex feedback loops that can lead to unexpected emergent behaviors. Small decision errors or misaligned objectives in one agent can cascade and amplify across interconnected subsystems, pushing the overall system toward instability; a phenomenon we call risk propagation near singularity points. In this paper, we present a quantitative framework for modeling and analyzing such dynamics using a simplified multi-agent control environment. Each agent optimizes a local objective under shared global constraints, while a feedback term governs how decisions influence others. Through controlled simulations, we demonstrate how minor perturbations in agent policies can trigger nonlinear escalation of collective risk, measurable via a newly proposed Singularity Index (SI). The results provide insights into designing safety buffers, coordination mechanisms, and trust boundaries for agentic AI systems, particularly as they approach high-autonomy, high-coupling regimes reminiscent of singularity scenarios.

title: Flocking Control for Cucker–Smale Model Under Data Privacy-Preserving Constraints
authors: J. Shao; L. Shi; W. X. Zheng; Z. Sun; Q. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Flocking is an essential ability for agent clusters to complete tasks in real-world scenarios. However, the data exchanged among agents during flocking may disclose their private information. This paper aims to investigate the flocking control problem for the Cucker-Smale model under data privacy-preserving constraints. The core idea of the proposed scheme is to inject privacy-preserving factors into the states transmitted by each agent. In addition, a weight function that depends on the masked information is designed to generate the edge weights of the interaction topology, which characterize the influence degree between agents. For the privacy-preserving Cucker-Smale model, three essential features defined by Reynolds for achieving flocking are studied, i.e., velocity matching, non-collision, and aggregate motion. Algebraic conditions are established to ensure flocking without compromising the privacy of the initial states of agents, and the performance of the privacy-preserving scheme is analyzed against both malicious agents inside the network and eavesdroppers outside the network. Finally, numerical examples and a semi-physical experiment are provided to verify the theoretical results. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by the need to coordinate multiple autonomous agents, such as uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and mobile robots, when their state information has to be exchanged over wireless networks. In many practical missions, exchanged positions and velocities may reveal sensitive information that compromises agent’s privacy. This paper provides a privacy-preserving flocking control method that enables agents to achieve coordinated group motion while reducing the risk of exposing private state information. The proposed method can be implemented by injecting specially designed privacy-preserving factors into the transmitted data, without changing the basic distributed interaction structure of the flocking controller. From an engineering perspective, the results provide useful design guidelines for balancing three practical requirements: velocity coordination, collision avoidance, and data privacy. The effectiveness of the method is illustrated through numerical simulations and a semi-physical Crazyflie-based UAV experiment.

title: GPU-Accelerated Resilient Control: Experimental Validation and Performance Benchmarking for Autonomous Systems
authors: T. P. Patel; C. Kulkarni; R. Purushothaman; D. Kole; M. Parikh; R. Keshava
venue: 2026 International Conference on Current Research in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science (ICCRAIDS)
abstract: The reliable operation of autonomous systems in safety-critical domains—from unmanned aerial vehicles conducting search and rescue to intelligent e-mobility managing urban traffic—demands fault tolerance coupled with edge-deployable computational efficiency. This paper presents an experimental validation of GPU-accelerated resilient control mechanisms for robust multi-agent autonomous systems. We introduce FAROC (Fault-Aware Resilient Optimization for Control), a learning-based adaptive control framework that integrates progressive fault injection during training with neural network compression techniques to achieve performant operation under resource constraints. Through GPU-based experiments on commercial NVIDIA P4000 hardware spanning over 120 hours of compute time across multiple random seeds, we demonstrate that FAROC achieves a 27% improvement in task success rates under 20% agent failure scenarios while reducing model size by 50% with 3.2% accuracy degradation. Experiments are conducted on a cooperative navigation task; generalization to other environments warrants further study. Our progressive fault injection experiments across escalating failure rates ($0-30 \%$) reveal graceful degradation superior to the evaluated baselines, with $2.8 \times$ faster recovery times. Compressed models achieve $3 \times$ inference speedup (10.2 ms to 3.4 ms per action) while maintaining 96.1% of original control performance, enabling edge deployment on resource-constrained platforms. We provide computational benchmarks (GPU utilization profiles, memory consumption patterns, training convergence dynamics), energy efficiency analysis demonstrating 39% operational power reduction, and statistical validation with confidence intervals across five random seeds.

title: Entity-Aware Spatiotemporal MAPPO: A Multi-UAV Cooperative Navigation Framework Based on Asymmetric Artificial Potential Fields
authors: J. Yang; P. Yao
venue: 2026 International Conference on Image, Signal Processing and Pattern Recognition (ISPP)
abstract: Multi-UAV cooperative navigation in highly dynamic environments presents critical challenges in modern autonomous robotics. Traditional Artificial Potential Fields (APF) often converge to local optima, whereas standard Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) methods struggle with long-term spatiotemporal reasoning, yielding high collision rates and erratic maneuvers. This paper proposes an Entity-Aware Spatiotemporal Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) framework. To process complex kinematic histories, we introduce a Spatiotemporal Attention Mechanism integrating inverse distance physical priors and temporal positional encoding, alongside a Safe Radius Masking technique to eliminate NaN gradient explosions. Furthermore, an Asymmetric APF reward shaping scheme applies distinct repulsive forces for obstacles versus teammates, optimizing safety and efficiency. Extensive tests demonstrate that our approach achieves superior success rates and faster convergence than baseline models.

title: Connectivity Maintenance for High-Speed Communication With Adversarial Jamming
authors: T. Kaminsky; H. Izhar; D. Garces; C. Brady; J. Rottner; S. Gil
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: We consider the problem of adaptively controlling a fleet of robots to maintain a communication network in an adversarial environment. In particular, a network team of robots is tasked with maintaining a directed communication channel at some data rate γ from an independent task robot to a fixed base station, accommodating the task robot’s motion and adversarial intervention in the form of an omnidirectional jammer and network team robot removals. We utilize a physically-motivated model for directed signal strength between robots in the presence of a jammer, introducing asymmetry into communication which challenges connectivity maintenance approaches [1]. Our main contribution in this paper is the introduction of a strategy for translating this directed model into an undirected graph for which enforcing connectedness is sufficient for maintaining high-rate communication. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in simulation using a CBF-based controller, showing that our controller maintains a high-rate connection throughout diverse trajectories, even when more conservative controllers fail.

title: Agentic AI-Driven Cyber-Physical Defense Framework for Proactive Threat Anticipation in Mission-Critical Networks
authors: P. K. Pal
venue: 2026 International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Cognitive Engineering (ICIICE)
abstract: Mission-critical networks supporting defense, industrial control, and critical infrastructure are increasingly exposed to sophisticated cyber-physical attacks that cannot be effectively mitigated using traditional reactive and rule-based security mechanisms. This paper proposes an Agentic AI-driven cyber-physical defense framework that enables proactive threat anticipation and autonomous response through distributed intelligent agents. The framework integrates multi-agent reinforcement learning, agentic reasoning, and unified cyber-physical telemetry to predict attack trajectories and coordinate mitigation actions. A digital twin-based validation layer is employed to evaluate defense strategies before deployment, reducing operational risk. Experimental results demonstrate improved threat anticipation accuracy, reduced response latency, and enhanced system resilience compared to conventional approaches. The proposed framework establishes a scalable, predictive, and self-adaptive security paradigm for next-generation mission-critical networks.

title: A Systematic Review of Adversarial Attacks and Defenses for Deep Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Vehicle Applications
authors: Z. Sarayloo; S. Lohrasbi; P. Xiong; N. Lashgarian Azad
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is a significant component of autonomous vehicle (AV) systems, as it is involved in crucial aspects such as decision-making, motion planning, and control systems. Nevertheless, DRL exhibits inherent weaknesses that render it vulnerable to adversarial attacks. On the other hand, AV applications are classified as safety-critical applications. This work presents a systematic literature review of several forms of adversarial attacks and the corresponding response mechanisms developed in the literature on AVs. This study additionally examines several datasets utilized for benchmarking purposes and different evaluation factors employed to assess the resilience and efficacy of adversarial attacks. The survey adheres to the PRMA standards. Excluded from consideration are articles that failed to take into account adversarial assaults on DRL and Deep Learning (DL). A comprehensive search yielded a total of 2250 distinct peer-reviewed articles sourced from the ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer, and Elsevier databases. Upon fulfilling the predefined criteria for inclusion and exclusion, a sum of 151 articles is encompassed in the ultimate review. In the end, the paper examines the existing research gaps and proposes potential options for further investigations.

title: Global–Local Coupling Formation Cooperative Obstacle Avoidance Method for Multirobot Systems
authors: J. Wang; J. Wang; X. Lu; Q. Wang; B. Wu; S. You; Y. Qi
venue: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: Multirobot systems (MRSs) can efficiently accomplish various tasks in complex environments, requiring robots to form the specified formation and navigate through obstacles. However, when obstacles are dense and irregularly distributed, robots must frequently adjust their relative positions, which increases the difficulty of maintaining formation and reduces system flexibility. In this article, a global–local coupled formation cooperative obstacle avoidance approach (CFCOA) is introduced. The global path planning phase introduces a local discriminator that captures the positional relationship between sampling nodes and obstacles to obtain a collision-free optimal reference path. In the local collaborative optimization stage, a feasible corridor is first constructed by circles to better approximate the feasible region. Subsequently, a formation optimization method is proposed, which improves formation maintenance by optimizing the scaling factor and rotation angle. A trigger mechanism is designed to activate formation optimization by quantifying obstacle influence on the robots, enhancing coordination efficiency. Finally, the velocities of the robots under formation constraints are computed using an improved dynamic window approach. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments validate the effectiveness of CFCOA, demonstrating superior performance over state-of-the-art methods in success rate, path cost, overall distortion degree, path smoothness level, and formation maintenance rate.

title: ParkDiffusion++: Ego Intention Conditioned Joint Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction for Automated Parking using Diffusion Models
authors: J. Wei; A. Rehr; C. Feist; A. Valada
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Automated parking is a challenging operational domain for advanced driver assistance systems, requiring robust scene understanding and interaction reasoning. The key challenge is twofold: (i) predict multiple plausible ego intentions according to context and (ii) for each intention, predict the joint responses of surrounding agents, enabling effective what-if decision-making. However, existing methods often fall short, typically treating these interdependent problems in isolation. We propose ParkDiffusion++, which jointly learns a multi-modal ego intention predictor and an ego conditioned multi-agent joint trajectory predictor for automated parking. Our approach makes several key contributions. First, we introduce an ego intention tokenizer that predicts a small set of discrete endpoint intentions from agent histories and vectorized map polylines. Second, we perform ego intention conditioned joint prediction, yielding socially consistent predictions of the surrounding agents for each possible ego intention. Third, we employ a lightweight safety-guided denoiser with different constraints to refine joint scenes during training, thus improving accuracy and safety. Fourth, we propose counterfactual knowledge distillation, where an EMA teacher refined by a frozen safety-guided denoiser provides pseudo-targets that capture how agents react to alternative ego intentions. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that ParkDiffusion++ achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Dragon Lake Parking (DLP) dataset and the Intersections Drone (inD) dataset. Importantly, qualitative what-if visualizations show that other agents react appropriately to different ego intentions.

title: Lineage-Aware Memory Governance: A Derivation-Gated Framework for Privacy-Preserving Column-Level Access Control in Enterprise AI Agents
authors: V. Sangaraju; S. Vissa
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Enterprise AI agents that share a memory store face two unaddressed risks: sensitive data can leak through legitimately computed results the requester could not derive, and departments can silently compute a same-named key performance indicator (KPI) through conflicting logic. Existing agent-memory systems (e.g., MemGPT, Zep, A-MEM) gate retrieval by content, ownership, and role, not derivation, missing a cached insight that embeds a forbidden column. We introduce the Analytical Memory Unit (AMU), a memory schema that attaches a full derivation (lineage) graph to every cached result, gated by a retrieval policy that serves a hit only when the requester is authorised for every column touched. Provided lineage recording is complete, we prove by construction that the policy blocks retrieval of results derived from a sensitive column outside the requester’s permissions, at $O(n)$ worst case – a conditional design guarantee, not an empirical claim, that excludes derived features encoding sensitive information without naming their source. Eliminating measured leakage required 75–90% recorded lineage completeness, so we treat 90% as a conservative deployment target. Across six experiments, lineage-gated retrieval removes the 18.8–25.5% cross-department leakage naive content-gated memory suffers, keeping 81.5–82.6% of memory reuse at $13.8{\,}\mu $ s worst-case overhead. A real-agent proof-of-concept with LLM-generated SQL is consistent with the guarantee: zero leaks over 9 round-trips, two conflicts caught automatically – though a feasibility demonstration, not evidence of production viability. This offers a practical governance layer for shared agent memory, complementing source-layer access control and supporting EU AI Act compliance.

title: Inventory Optimization via Stochastic Modeling in Complex Supply Network
authors: H. P. Jothiswaran
venue: 2026 Contemporary Computing Innovations Conference (CCIC)
abstract: Addressing the limitations of conventional Material Requirements Planning (MRP) in contemporary supply chains, this paper introduces a novel approach centered on constrained stochastic optimization. A simulation-optimization framework is proposed to minimize inventory costs while adhering to service level targets and operational constraints. This framework determines optimal reorder parameters, essential for Material Requirements Planning (MRP) systems, to achieve cost minimization while satisfying service level constraints.

title: FOGMACHINE - Leveraging Discrete-Event Simulation and Scene Graphs for Modeling Hierarchical, Interconnected Environments Under Partial Observations from Mobile Agents
authors: L. Ohnemus; N. Hantke; M. Weisser; K. Furmans
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: Dynamic Scene Graphs (DSGs) provide a structured representation of hierarchical, interconnected environments, but current approaches struggle to capture stochastic dynamics, partial observability, and multi-agent activity. These aspects are critical for embodied AI, where agents must act under uncertainty and delayed perception.
