We introduce FOGMACHINE, an open-source framework that fuses DSGs with discrete-event simulation to model object dynamics, agent observations, and interactions at scale. This setup enables the study of uncertainty propagation, planning under limited perception, and emergent multi-agent behavior. Experiments in urban scenarios showcase realistic temporal and spatial patterns while revealing the challenges of belief estimation under sparse observations. By combining structured representations with efficient simulation, FOGMACHINE establishes an effective tool for benchmarking, model training, and advancing embodied AI in complex, uncertain environments.

title: Resilient Observation Scheduling Against Smart Intermittent DoS Attacks: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Game
authors: J. Lu; Y. Mo; C. Yang
venue: 2026 15th Asian Control Conference (ASCC)
abstract: In modern cyber-physical systems (CPSs), state estimation is increasingly threatened by intelligent intermittent Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. Unlike traditional attacks, intermittent DoS attackers with learning capabilities can dynamically infer deterministic defense patterns and preemptively block critical sensor data, which greatly threatens the accuracy and stability of estimations. To address this challenge, we formulate the resilient observation scheduling problem as a two-player, zero-sum Markov game between an adaptive defender and a smart attacker. We propose a novel game-theoretic Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework, featuring a customized Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm integrated with a curriculum-guided Fictitious Self-Play (FSP) mechanism. This approach effectively overcomes the non-stationarity and “strategy cycling” pathologies inherent in multi-agent adversarial training. Furthermore, we propose an emergent, physics-inspired “decoy” mechanism: guided by the stability threshold of system control theory, the defender autonomously learns to randomly sacrifice low-value data packets to absorb interference energy, thereby transmitting critical data packets more securely. Simulations demonstrate that our proposed framework successfully converges to a robust mixed-strategy Nash Equilibrium, significantly outperforming conventional fixed-order strategies and ensuring longterm system stability under extreme adversarial conditions.

title: Distributed Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative UAV-UGV Formation Control with Multirate Dynamics
authors: S. R. Allada; P. Palpandi; J. Gold Beulah Patturose; M. S. Shankari; K. Revathi; M. Aishwarya
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Circuit, Power & Computing Technologies (ICCPCT)
abstract: Coordinating heterogeneous aerial and ground vehicles with fundamentally different dynamic time-scales is a longstanding challenge in multi-agent robotics. This paper proposes a distributed reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for cooperative Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) formation control that explicitly accounts for multirate dynamics: UAVs execute high-frequency control at 10 Hz while UGVs operate at 2 Hz. Each agent maintains a local actor-critic network trained via a variant of MultiAgent Proximal Policy Optimisation (MAPPO) augmented with a consensus-based communication graph and a multirate synchronisation module that bridges the temporal mismatch between the two vehicle classes. A shaped reward formulation penalises formation deviation, inter-agent collisions and communication dropout simultaneously. Simulation experiments In a physicsaccurate Gazebo/ROS2 environment with two UAV leaders, two UAV followers, and two UGVs demonstrate a task success rate of 96.4%, a formation accuracy of 97.1%, and a collision rate of only 0.8%, outperforming MADDPG, MAPPO (singlerate), centralised DDPG and PID baselines by margins of up to 24.9 percentage points. The framework is further validated in a disaster-response scenario with a dynamic obstacle fields confirming its suitability for real-world heterogeneous multirobot missions.

title: Distributed Safe Secondary Voltage and Frequency Control for Isolated Microgrids With Guaranteed State and Input Constraints
authors: Y. -S. Lin; K. -Z. Liu; M. -S. Yang; F. -C. Xu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: In the secondary control of the microgrid (MG), unknown disturbances, load variations, and the plug-and-play operation of distributed generators (DGs) can result in voltage and frequency exceeding safe boundaries during transient operations, posing greater challenges for voltage and frequency restoration control. To ensure the stability and safety of the islanded MG, a safe secondary voltage and frequency control scheme based on control barrier functions (CBFs) is proposed in this paper. The secondary control problem of the MG is transformed into a multi-agent distributed consensus tracking problem. The objective of consensus tracking is determined by the control Lyapunov function, and the safe constraints on states are handled through CBFs. Meanwhile, input constraints are considered to avoid actuator saturation. Then, a quadratic programming (QP)-based voltage and frequency controller is designed to achieve the secondary control objective of the MG. Moreover, in response to disturbances and uncertainties in the system, a robust finite-time disturbance observer is designed and integrated into the proposed CBF-CLF-QP framework. This integration enables the controller to proactively compensate for disturbances and uncertainties, improving the robustness of the system. In contrast to traditional methods, the proposed method exhibits smaller voltage and frequency fluctuations under load variations, plug-and-play operations, and uncertain disturbances, thereby ensuring smoother power output and reducing regulation time. Finally, the proposed method is ultimately verified through simulations and experiments on a hardware test platform with the StarSim rapid control prototype. Note to Practitioners—This work develops a distributed secondary control framework that incorporates control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions to rigorously enforce state and input constraints. By enforcing voltage and frequency safety constraints during transients, the proposed strategy ensures safe operation while achieving consensus tracking. It addresses critical operational challenges in islanded microgrids, including voltage and frequency deviations during load changes, plug-and-play operations, and unknown disturbances. By adjusting the safety boundaries according to the DG rating, practitioners can effectively reduce voltage and frequency fluctuations, achieving shorter regulation times and satisfactory steady-state performance. This scheme is applicable to microgrid scenarios in ships, aircraft, and renewable energy stations. In addition, its practicality and effectiveness are further validated through experiments on a hardware test platform, offering a practical solution for the secondary control of microgrids.

title: An Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Based Path Planning Model Inspired by Termite Alate Behaviour for Efficient Target Coverage
authors: S. S. T; G. J. S; S. L. S; S. K
venue: 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Effective coverage of an area is a root problem in autonomous robotic systems, especially during surveillance, search and rescue, as well as environmental monitoring. The conventional approach to path coverage usually involves centralized path control or fixed path plans, thus constraining flexibility in changing conditions. In order to overcome these difficulties, the given work suggests a Bio-Inspired Q-Learning-Based Path Coverage algorithm that is to be used in discrete grid-based environments. The timbered system proposed is based on the Q-learning agent that is used to navigate and traverse the workspace, reduce redundancy and overcome obstacles. The robot modulates its Q-table on the basis of local information and reward feedback, which motivates it to cover unexplored cells effectively and discourages a collision or a revisit. Bio-inspired mechanisms are combined with the need to improve the efficiency of learning, which enables the robot to use environmental cues based on swarm intelligence. This mixed system creates a balance of both exploration and exploitation, resulting in quicker convergence and better coverage quality. The simulation outcomes confirm that the suggested solution will be more efficient in terms of coverage, less variable, and more flexible than the traditional tools. The system has been proven to be effective in different grid sizes and obstacle densities, which is why it can be applied in the real world in autonomous patrolling, agricultural surveying, disaster rescue, and other areas. In general, the Bio-Inspired Q-Learning-Based Path Coverage model offers a strong, smart and flexible way of exploring the environment efficiently. Keywords: Single-Robot Systems, Coverage Path Planning, Q-Learning, Bio-Inspired Algorithms, Swarm Intelligence.

title: A Meta-Learning Framework for Resilient UAV Swarm Networks
authors: A. Shiri; M. H. Jeridi; R. Ouersighni
venue: 2026 IEEE International conference on Advanced Systems and Emergent Technologies (IC_ASET)
abstract: Maintaining the self-healing of communication connectivity (SCC) is a primary challenge for resilient Unmanned Sensor Networks (USNETs). This document proposes an intelligent framework utilizing Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs) and meta-learning to address unpredictable external destructions (UEDs). By integrating the Communication-Relaxed Meta Graph Convolution (CR-MGC) algorithm, the system enables autonomous topology reconstruction. Simulations demonstrate that this collaborative intelligence approach significantly reduces connectivity restoration time and computational complexity compared to traditional heuristic methods.

title: Stop Means Stop: Measuring and Repairing the Enforcement Gap in Agent-Framework Control Primitives
authors: S. Khan
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Agent frameworks ship control primitives (human-in-the-loop approval, cancellation, and timeouts) that operators trust as a barrier: while a run is paused, canceled, or timed out, no gated side effect reaches the world. We measure whether the shipped primitives enforce this barrier, and in six open-source frameworks they do not. Model-free probes isolate a sibling leak: an approval gate suspends only its own branch, so a sibling’s effect executes during the pause. It appears in every framework with a pre-execution gate (four independent designs plus the Node port of one). The probes also confirm replay double-execution, cancellation orphans, and timeout zombies. The hazard is reachable. Frontier models emit the triggering plan shape in up to 14% of runs on authored multi-effect tasks, and live models driving an unmodified framework leak in 215 of 1,200 runs; a 13-incident public corpus corroborates the replay and cancellation failures. On naturalistic benchmark episodes, models mostly serialize, so the gap is latent rather than frequent. We repair it with SoundGate, an external Rust reference monitor at the tool boundary that holds gated effects until a decision, makes rejections final, deduplicates replays, and fences canceled runs, under an explicit complete-mediation contract. A model of its admission core is mechanically verified (Verus, TLA+/TLC, TLAPS) and linked to the deployed code by differential testing. SoundGate blocks every measured violation on all six frameworks while releasing approved effects, at about 1 ms per admitted write, and holds its guarantees through a 30-minute sustained-load soak with 72 crash–restart cycles.

title: Design and Development of Semi-Automated Assembly Frameworks for Enhanced Ergonomics, Precision, and Repeatability in Automotive Component Manufacturing
authors: R. Parambil; N. Khatri; H. Sharma
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: The increasing complexity of automotive components demands assembly systems that balance precision, speed, and human factors. Semi-automatic assembly machines integrate human skills with mechanized assistance, enabling efficient and accurate production while improving operator ergonomics. This paper presents a systematic approach to the design and development of semi-automated assembly frameworks, focusing on key objectives: minimizing cycle time, enhancing repeatability, reducing errors, and incorporating robotics with robust safety systems. A detailed case study on the assembly of a powered window regulator illustrates the application of these frameworks, highlighting the challenges of handling precise components and optimizing workflow. The study explores the integration of advanced technologies in semiautomation, including ergonomic workstation design, modular assembly stations, and safety-compliant robotic interfaces. Emphasis is placed on prototyping methodologies and iterative design processes to ensure consistent part quality and reduced scrap rates. Results demonstrate that thoughtful integration of human and machine elements can significantly improve production efficiency, operational safety, and repeatability. This research provides a structured framework for designing semiautomated assembly systems, offering practical insights for industrial implementation in the automotive sector and contributing to the advancement of hybrid human-machine manufacturing technologies.

title: Practical Prescribed-Time Rigid Formation Maneuvering Control Under Performance Constraints
authors: Z. Zhou; Y. Wang; D. Yang; F. Ren; Y. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article addresses the formation maneuvering control problem for multi-agent systems (MASs) by proposing a practical prescribed-time formation control scheme based on finite time-varying scaling functions. The approach employs time-scale transformation and state conversion techniques to coordinately regulate the convergence rate and precision of distance errors, ensuring specified accuracy is achieved within the prescribed time while maintaining rigidity-based formation errors within predefined performance boundaries. The developed method possesses a unique converging feature in that the distance errors first converge to a small adjustable residual set around zero within a prescribed finite time, and then asymptotically converge to zero (or to an adjustable bound). It features a dual-regulation mechanism that enables flexible configuration of formation error magnitude through coordinated parameter tuning of time-varying scaling functions and prescribed performance functions. Simultaneously, while guaranteeing convergence accuracy and transient performance, the control algorithm maintains safe inter-agent distances to achieve collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed protocol enables MASs to synchronously track time-varying velocities while preserving rigidity-based formation configurations within the prescribed time, validating its comprehensive advantages in precision, transient performance, and safety assurance.

title: Coordinated Task Allocation and Collision Avoidance in Multi-AGV Systems
authors: Y. Liu; Z. Zhang; R. Pang; L. Song; S. Zhu
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges associated with real-time dynamic heterogeneous task allocation and path conflict resolution among heterogeneous agents within largescale AGV systems in smart manufacturing environments. A distributed market-optimized task allocation algorithm is introduced alongside a multi-AGV cooperative obstacle avoidance algorithm, both founded on a two-level priority structure. To alleviate system oscillations induced by dynamic tasks, a dynamic task buffer pool mechanism has been implemented to prioritize tasks effectively. Additionally, an incremental path caching mechanism is established to minimize redundant calculations of repetitive paths in the 2-opt algorithm. The proposed two-level priority mechanism effectively addresses cooperative obstacle avoidance and path conflict issues encountered by multiple AGVs. The task allocation comparison test framework is constructed, and the performance of the proposed algorithm in the case of multiple task numbers is verified under this framework. The feasibility and effectiveness of the hybrid algorithm are verified on the simulation map based on the actual scene, which provides a feasible solution for guiding actual production and collaborative obstacle avoidance.

title: Knowledge-Informed Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction at Signalized Intersections for Infrastructure-to-Everything
authors: H. Yin; Y. Xu; J. Li; H. Zhang; G. Rigoll
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Multi-agent trajectory prediction at signalized intersections is pivotal for the safety of autonomous driving and the efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. However, conventional vehicle-centric approaches are limited by restricted perception ranges and occlusion. Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) cooperation is widely regarded as an effective approach to alleviating these limitations. Furthermore, existing cooperative systems often suffer from complex coupling and selection bias, hindering universal and real-time service. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel Infrastructure-to-Everything (I2X) collaborative prediction scheme. This scheme decouples infrastructure capabilities from vehicle requests by independently forecasting and broadcasting trajectories for all detected vehicles. Building on this scheme, we propose I2XTraj, a dedicated infrastructure-based model that leverages three core mechanisms. First, a continuous signal-informed mechanism to adaptively encode real-time traffic light information. Second, a maneuver strategy awareness mechanism that integrates intersection geometric constraints to estimate maneuver distributions. Third, a spatial-temporal-mode attention network to refine multi-agent interactions. Extensive evaluations on two real-world datasets, V2X-Seq and SinD, demonstrate the superiority of our approach. In both single-infrastructure and collaborative scenarios, I2XTraj outperforms state-of-the-art methods by over 30% and 15%, respectively, confirming its strong generalizability and robustness in complex intersection environments.

title: Towards Acceptance of Virtual Validation: The Indirect Technology Acceptance Framework
authors: C. Demuth; N. Schade; H. Lampe; T. Behrens; J. Pannek
venue: 2026 IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration (SII)
abstract: The development of autonomous and respective multi-agent systems creates both technological innovations and significant societal and regulatory challenges. Of particular note is the social acceptance of these systems once they are integrated into their usage environment. This is a critical factor that is typically limited to the end product, while the development process and the underlying technologies remain largely disregarded. However, there are indirect technologies like virtual testing, which are increasingly used in the respective product development, for which their potential effects on the acceptance among stakeholders are overlooked. To address this source of indirect skepticism, this paper introduces the Indirect Technology Acceptance Framework (iTAF) to investigate the practical applicability and acceptance dimensions using the example of virtual validation methods. The framework reveals specific implications for each framework layer: the technological layer requires procedural transparency; the institutional layer necessitates harmonized standards across jurisdictions; the societal layer highlights the influence of communication strategies and safety demonstrations; and the interactive layer emphasizes continuous stakeholder engagement throughout the development process. The model successfully integrates technical, regulatory, and societal dimensions, acknowledging the unique position of indirect users as critical stakeholders in societal legitimation and integration. It also offers a foundation to align development processes and especially system validation to the stakeholders’ needs regarding the trustworthiness of the system of interest (SOI). To illustrate the iTAF, it is applied as a demonstrative example to the social acceptance of virtual validation in the presence of legal uncertainty.

title: Research on Day-ahead Optimal Scheduling and Robustness of Large-scale Industrial and Virtual Power Plants Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: F. Gong; S. Chen; Y. Ai; T. Gong; K. Shi
venue: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: With the increasing integration of high-penetration renewable energy and diverse flexible loads into modern power systems, Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) face significant scheduling challenges arising from dual uncertainties in both supply and demand. Traditional model-based optimization methods struggle to simultaneously achieve computational efficiency for high-dimensional mixed discrete – continuous action spaces and robustness under nonlinear constraints. To address this, we propose a day-ahead optimal scheduling strategy for VPPs based on an improved Deep Q-Network (DQN). First, we construct a collaborative VPP framework comprising 8 industrial/commercial load nodes, 5 photovoltaic (PV) nodes, and a centralized energy storage system (ESS), incorporating real-world industrial load profiles and a PV output model with weather-induced fluctuations. Second, we design a multi-objective reward function that integrates time-of-use electricity price incentives/penalties, ESS degradation cost penalties, and operational safety constraints. The continuous ESS charging/discharging power is mapped into a discrete action space to enhance algorithmic convergence stability. Finally, we adopt an ε-greedy exploration decay mechanism and a soft target network update strategy to enable rapid approximation of the optimal VPP dispatch policy in high-dimensional state spaces. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges stably within 800 training episodes. Compared with random and fixed-rule strategies, it effectively tracks dynamic price signals to implement "charge low, discharge high" arbitrage, mitigates the impact of PV uncertainty, and reduces the average daily operational cost to ¥54,842.95, representing a 7.03% reduction compared to the baseline scenario.

title: Unified Global Formation Path Planning Strategy for Multi-Agent Systems Using Graph of Convex Sets
authors: M. Shen; Q. Gao; Z. -X. Yang; J. Zhao; X. Liu; Z. Liang
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: To enhance the quality and scalability of global formation path planning in multi-agent systems, this letter proposes a unified strategy based on the Graph of Convex Sets (GCS) framework. The formation path planning problem is formulated as a shortest path problem within the GCS framework. The translation-only rigid (TO) and translation-and-scaling (TS) cases yield Mixed-Integer Convex Programming (MICP) problems with tight convex relaxations, whereas the translation-scaling-rotation (TSR) case combines the relaxed GCS formulation with nonlinear refinement during rounding. This approach enables simultaneous planning of optimal paths and formation configurations using convex optimization and rounding techniques. The framework supports a wide range of formation constraints, including rigid and flexible formations, ensuring adaptability to diverse scenarios while maintaining a scalable geometric representation as the number of agents increases. By exploiting the convex hull property of formation shapes, most constraints and costs are expressed in convex form, enabling efficient computation for the convex cases. Tests and comparisons across multiple scenarios validate the method's effectiveness in computing collision-free, scalable, and high-quality global formation paths and configurations.

title: Homotopy-Guided Potential Games for Congestion-Aware Navigation
authors: M. I. I. S. Imran; L. Peters; M. Khayyat; S. Arrigoni; F. Braghin; L. Ferranti
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: We address the multi-agent motion planning problem where interactions, collisions, and congestion co-exist. Conventional game-theoretic planners capture interactions among agents but often converge to conservative, congested equilibria. Homotopy planners, on the other hand, can explore topologically distinct paths, but lack mechanisms to account for the interdependence of agents’ future actions. We propose a unified framework that leverages homotopy classes as structured strategy sets within a receding-horizon setup. At each planning stage, a deterministic homotopy planner generates topologically distinct paths for each agent, conditioned on the joint configuration. To avoid intractable growth of candidate paths, we propose a simple heuristic filtering step that selects a top-$K$ subset of the most suitable congestion-free joint strategies to ensure computational tractability. These serve as initializations for a potential game that enforces homotopy-consistent constraints and yields a generalized open-loop Nash equilibrium (OLNE), with penalties discouraging abrupt strategy shifts in a receding-horizon setting. Simulations with three agents demonstrate improved efficiency (faster completion) and enhanced safety (greater inter-agent clearance, leading to reduced congestion) compared to a local baseline and NH-ORCA that do not reason about homotopies. Hardware trials with two robots and one human demonstrate robustness to irrational behaviors, where our method adapts by switching to alternative feasible equilibria while the baseline game fails.

title: HPNA: A Hybrid PSO–NSGA-II Optimization Framework with Adaptive Diversity Preservation for Multi-Objective UAV Three-Dimensional Path Planning
authors: M. Liu
venue: 2026 IEEE 8th International Conference on Communications, Information System and Computer Engineering (CISCE)
abstract: Multi-objective UAV three-dimensional path planning demands simultaneous optimisation of path length, energy consumption, and flight safety under dense obstacle environments—a challenge that exposes three critical limitations in existing methods: (1) single-objective metaheuristics (e.g., vanilla PSO, GWO) sacrifice solution diversity for convergence speed and cannot represent Pareto-optimal trade-offs; (2) evolutionary multi-objective algorithms (e.g., NSGA-II) provide well-spread fronts yet suffer from slow convergence, limiting real-time applicability as fleet size grows; (3) static initialisation and fixed operator parameters cause premature stagnation, degrading robustness in high-density obstacle scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose HPNA (Hybrid PSO-NSGA-II Algorithm), a unified optimisation framework that integrates (1) Pareto-guided PSO velocity updates driven by crowding-distance tournament selection from an elite non-dominated archive, (2) an adaptive cosine-modulated inertia weight that dynamically balances exploration and exploitation throughout the search horizon, and (3) an entropy-monitored chaotic re-initialisation mechanism that injects structured stochasticity whenever population diversity collapses. Extensive experiments on six standard multi-objective benchmarks (ZDT1-6, DTLZ2) and a three-dimensional UAV path-planning simulator with up to 16 agents confirm that HPNA consistently outperforms PSO, NSGA-II, MOPSO, and GWO across hypervolume, IGD, success rate, and computational scalability metrics.

title: Large-Scale Autonomous Vehicle Fleet Management
authors: T. Mulumba
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: We present a hierarchical framework for city-scale autonomous ride-hailing that integrates vehicle prepositioning, request matching, charging, and facility ingress. A fine-grained mixed-integer program (MIP) coordinates prepositioning and matching on short horizons, while a coarse-grained Deployment+Summoning decomposition enforces charger/parking capacities at scale. On ride-hail traces, the method increases coverage and reduces wait relative to greedy and decoupled baselines, while keeping charger overuse near zero (≈1–2%) under rolling-horizon execution. We detail boundary-condition handling for 24/7 operations and specify a concrete RL training/validation protocol for a constraint-aware hybrid in which learned policies act tactically under a MIP-based safety shield.

title: Agentic AI Architecture for Structural Design Automation: From Regulatory Retrieval to Physics-Based Optimization
authors: A. Abbasi; M. Alves; S. Hosseini; O. Hassanshahi; R. Rodrigues
venue: 2026 IEEE 9th International Conference on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (ICPS)
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into structural engineering is currently hindered by two critical limitations: the stochastic hallucination of regulatory clauses and an inherent lack of physics-based reasoning capabilities. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces a neurosymbolic cognitive architecture that effectively couples semantic regulatory compliance with mathematical structural optimization. Our approach leverages a Graph-Retrieval Augmented Generation (Graph-RAG) framework, where the ASCE 7-22 standard is indexed into a hybrid Knowledge Graph to facilitate deep, context-aware retrieval. Reliability is enforced through a Multi-Agent Swarm utilizing GPT-4o as the underlying reasoning kernel, comprising a Designer, an Adversarial Auditor, and a Translator. These agents operate under a strict chain-ofverification protocol, debating and validating design parameters against cited dependencies prior to execution. Once validated, natural language intents are autonomously translated into structured physics payloads, triggering a Finite Element Analysis (FEM) engine driven by a Constraint-Adaptive Genetic Algorithm (CAGA). Comprehensive benchmarking across semantic faithfulness, safety, and optimality metrics demonstrates that this adversarial architecture achieves a RAGAS faithfulness score of 0.98 and a 100% recall rate in identifying ambiguous or unsafe queries. Empirically, the system successfully automated the design of a 3D Warren truss, reducing material costs by $\mathbf{5 6 \%}$ while satisfying rigorous deflection ($L / 240$) and stress (345 MPa) constraints. These findings establish a viable blueprint for autonomous, hallucination-free engineering systems capable of deriving valid physical structures directly from vague user prompts.

title: Prescribed-Time Critic-Only Consensus for Constrained Multiagent Systems Through ADP
authors: S. Liu; Y. Zhang; X. Zhao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This article investigates the optimization consensus and constraint issues of multi-agent systems within a given time. By adopting a barrier function and the improved non-negative function, a new finite-horizon cost function is constructed. Based on this cost function, a simple single-critic network framework is proposed, which avoids the complex interaction and iterative update process between the actor and critic networks, thereby reducing the computational complexity. Under this framework, the temporal differential (TD) signal generated by the integral Bellman equation and the terminal constraint (TC) error are used to jointly guide the update of the critic learning law, and a concurrent learning technique is employed to adaptively adjust the weights without requiring persistent excitation conditions. The proposed adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) control strategy does not rely on the system model information of the controlled plant, enhancing the applicability of the algorithm in unknown dynamic environments. Furthermore, by incorporating the prescribed-time (PT) criterion into the optimization design process, a collaborative control protocol with explicit time constraints is designed, which strictly ensures that the controlled system achieves consensus within the specified time. At the same time, by adjusting the parameters of the PT criterion, the convergence rate and transient performance can be flexibly controlled. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the designed control algorithm and illustrate the impact of key parameters on system performance. Note to Practitioners—Consensus control in MASs is widely employed in practical engineering applications including cooperative UAV formation and smart grid scheduling. However, in practical applications, cost and time constraints make infinite-time consensus inadequate for engineering requirements. Accordingly, a PT consensus protocol is developed and integrated with ADP to achieve system consensus within a predefined time while optimizing control inputs and system performance under a single-critic network framework. The proposed PT criterion enables both direct specification of the convergence time and flexible regulation of the consensus error convergence rate through parameter tuning. Moreover, by incorporating barrier and nonnegative functions into the finite-horizon cost function, the safety ranges of system inputs and outputs are effectively constrained, further enhancing the practicality and reliability of the algorithm.

title: Supervisory Control and Model Predictive Multi-Agent Coordination using Stochastic Consensus Strategies
authors: M. P. Loures; G. V. Raffo; P. N. Pena
venue: 2026 18th International Workshop on Discrete Event Systems (WODES)
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid stochastic planning and predictive control strategy for multi-agent coordination that enables decentralization while preserving the formal safety guarantees inherent in centralized supervisory control. The approach integrates Supervisor Localization to embed safety constraints into agent-level supervisors, Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) for local performance optimization under uncertainty, and a stochastic consensus protocol to synchronize distributed event probability with communication delays. By employing a receding-horizon MDP that updates policies online based on dynamically refined stochastic models, the strategy supports autonomous and adaptive decision-making without centralized oversight. Validation through a case study of heterogeneous autonomous robots under resource constraints demonstrates that the framework maintains safety, ensures probabilistic co-ordination, and achieves near centralized performance, thereby unifying formal discrete-event control with scalable, resilient multi-agent autonomy.

title: Predefined-Time Formation Control for Various Heterogeneous Autonomous Systems
authors: Q. Lin; Y. Liu; Z. -G. Wu; W. Gui
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: In this paper, we consider the predefined-time formation control problems subjected to various constraints for heterogeneous autonomous systems. We propose a novel distributed predefined-time formation control framework, which consists of a multi-agent system (MAS) estimator layer and a local tracking controller layer. Firstly, the MAS estimator layer is designed to tackle predefined-time distributed formation optimization problems with multiple constraints. Compared to previous approaches, our method effectively address challenges posed by cost functions that are non-strongly convex or even non-convex, while significantly reducing computation time. Subsequently, the local tracking controller layer is designed to ensure that the sailing states of the autonomous system can track the optimal signals obtained by the distributed optimization estimator. Additionally, we design a robust predefined-time tracking controller for autonomous systems capable of effectively handling unknown but bounded external disturbances. A control term is further incorporated to enable the autonomous system to achieve internal obstacle avoidance. Finally, we provide illustrative examples to demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed predefined-time distributed optimization scheme.

title: Dynamic Multi-Agent Drone Path Planning Using Conflict-Based Search with YOLOv12
authors: S. Tiwari; N. Chakraborty; M. Khatua
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Techniques in Computational Intelligence (ICETCI)
abstract: The growing deployment of autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in applications such as surveillance, logistics, and disaster response necessitates robust multi-agent navigation in dynamic environments. A critical challenge in such systems is ensuring collision-free path planning while adapting to unforeseen obstacles. This paper proposes a vision-integrated multi-agent path planning framework that combines Conflict-Based Search (CBS) with real-time object detection using YOLOv12, an attention-enhanced deep learning model. Initially, optimal paths are computed using A* and refined through CBS to resolve inter-agent conflicts. During execution, onboard vision systems detect dynamic obstacles using YOLOv12, which are incorporated into the environment model, triggering real-time replanning. The proposed approach is validated in a 3D simulation environment. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves zero collision instances, maintains near-optimal path lengths (19, 19, 14 steps for three drones), and introduces only 0.005 seconds of additional computation time compared to standard CBS, while successfully adapting to dynamically appearing obstacles.

title: TACOS: A Topology-Aware Cooperative Multiagent Framework for Power-Computing Coscheduling in Data Center Microgrids
authors: Y. Zhang; Y. Ye; J. Hu; C. Wu; T. Cui; G. Strbac
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: The rapid expansion of data center (DC) clusters has led to a significant increase in electricity consumption and carbon emissions, making power-computing coscheduling a critical enabler for sustainable DC operation. Large-scale AI services introduce massive and bursty workloads with complex task dependencies, which pose substantial challenges to minute-level scheduling in DC microgrids integrated with renewable energy and energy storage. These challenges are further aggravated by multidimensional uncertainties, including stochastic job arrivals, volatile electricity prices, and photovoltaic generation, as well as by stringent quality-of-service requirements and time-coupled computation-energy constraints. Existing analytical optimization and single-agent learning methods are often limited by poor scalability, weak topology awareness of job structures, and insufficient safety guarantees under temporally coupled constraints. To address these issues, this article proposes a topology-aware heterogeneous multiagent deep reinforcement learning framework for dynamic power-computing co-optimization in DC microgrids. Specifically, the problem is formulated as a constrained Markov Game to characterize interactions among scheduling and energy management entities. A Graphormer-based representation module is developed to encode directed acyclic graph job topologies and capture task dependencies. Moreover, constrained heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization with hybrid advantage decomposition and sequential updates is designed to handle temporal coupling constraints and improve the stability and safety of policy learning. Experimental results under realistic AI workload and energy scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reduce energy costs while satisfying task deadline constraints, and exhibits strong scalability and robustness in large-scale DC microgrids.

title: DART: Data Augmentation of Rare ATT&CK Techniques Using LLM Agents
authors: T. Ambrose; S. Valderrama; Y. Park; Á. A. Cárdenas
venue: 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy Workshops (SPW)
abstract: Machine learning for cybersecurity relies on representative datasets, yet most security datasets remain highly imbalanced across classes. This problem is particularly acute for datasets mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, where well-documented adversarial behaviors dominate while rare or complex techniques are underrepresented, creating blind spots for detection systems. We present DART, a semi-automated system for generating ATT&CK-grounded malicious commandline samples. DART combines Python-based orchestration, syntax validation through parsers and compilers, large language models (LLMs) for constrained command generation and multi-agent evaluation, and embedding-based cosine similarity to measure dataset diversity. Our four-phase pipeline defines generation scenarios, produces candidate commands through constrained prompting, validates their syntactic and semantic quality via static testing and multi-agent scoring, and applies diversity filtering to curate a balanced and representative dataset. Results demonstrate that the system generates operationally realistic and diverse samples while providing a scalable framework for improving coverage of underrepresented ATT&CK techniques.

title: Agent-Based Modular Architecture for Autonomous Driving with Shared Context and Risk-Aware Planning
authors: M. Amr; A. Elewah; K. Elgazzar
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Mobility (SM)
abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have advanced through large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models, with works such as Alpamayo-R1 demonstrating improved reasoning in long-tail scenarios. However, three structural limitations remain: (i) the action space is constrained by the trajectory decoder’s training distribution, limiting generalization to diverse edge cases; (ii) performance gains, while meaningful, remain insufficient for safety-critical deployment, leaving residual risk, and (iii) the monolithic design requires full-system retraining to improve individual components, reducing scalability. To address these limitations, we propose an agentic architecture that decomposes the driving task into eight specialized, independently deployable agents coordinated through a typed shared-state bus, the Context Manager. This design is grounded in the success of agent-based systems in applied AI, including retrieval-augmented generation and multi-agent frameworks, offering a scalable and modular foundation for autonomous driving.

title: AROSpect: A ROS 2 Timing Introspection Framework
authors: L. Dust; C. Timperley; R. Gu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: This paper introduces AROSpect, a framework for timing introspection and controlled experimentation for ROS 2-based applications. AROSpect enables developers to model system components using standardized templates, inject synthetic delays, and measure end-to-end latencies across message paths. Through instrumentation, the framework supports iterative refinement of timing parameters and identification of misconfigurations. A case study using a multi-agent turtlesim system demonstrates how AROSpect can guide developers to understand the effects of adapting timing parameters, contributing toward more predictable robotic systems.

title: Multi-agent Dynamic Surface Consensus Control of Dual-Motor Steer-by-Wire System Under Communication Faults
authors: K. Xu; J. Liu; H. Huang; C. Wang; W. Zhao; S. S. Ge
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: Intelligent driving vehicles impose higher safety requirements on steer-by-wire systems, and the dual-motor steer-by-wire (DMSBW) system with redundancy capabilities demonstrates significant advantages. However, communication faults and disturbances in the DMSBW can cause asynchrony between the two motors, thereby compromising tracking accuracy and coordination. This article proposes a multi-agent dynamic surface consensus control strategy (MADSCCS), which includes three components: a multi-agent consensus control architecture (MACA), an implicit time-delay RBF neural network observer (IDNNO), and a multi-agent adaptive dynamic surface consensus controller (MADSC). The proposed MACA designates the virtual spindle as the leader agent and the two steering motors as follower agents, using dynamic communication topology to enhance the consistency performance of the DMSBW system under disturbances. Considering the state changes caused by variable communication delays, the IDNNO is designed to estimate the system state and disturbance after implicit time-delay transformations. On this basis, the MADSC is designed by integrating implicit time-delay transformations, dynamic surface tracking and consensus errors, thereby achieving tracking and consensus control of the DMSBW vehicle under communication faults. Finally, hardware-in-the-loop experiments are conducted on the DMSBW test platform, and the experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

title: Lifelong Learning of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Roadmap
authors: J. Zheng; C. Shi; X. Cai; Q. Li; D. Zhang; C. Li; D. Yu; Q. Ma
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Lifelong learning, also known as continual or incremental learning, is a crucial component for advancing Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) by enabling systems to continuously adapt in dynamic environments. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in natural language processing, existing LLM agents are typically designed for static systems and lack the ability to adapt over time in response to new challenges. This survey is the first to systematically summarize the potential techniques for incorporating lifelong learning into LLM-based agents. We categorize the core components of these agents into three modules: the perception module for multimodal input integration, the memory module for storing and retrieving evolving knowledge, and the action module for grounded interactions with the dynamic environment. We highlight how these pillars collectively enable continuous adaptation, mitigate catastrophic forgetting, and improve long-term performance. This survey provides a roadmap for researchers and practitioners working to develop lifelong learning capabilities in LLM agents, offering insights into emerging trends, evaluation metrics, and application scenarios.

title: A Survey on LLM-Enabled AAV Digital Twins for Internet of Vehicles Systems
authors: S. Bajoria; S. Kanrar; H. Pandey; P. DE; A. Akash; V. Hassija; V. Chamola
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
abstract: Vehicular Digital Twins (VDTs) are emerging as a core enabler for real-time monitoring, simulation, and intelligent control in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems. While prior research has largely focused on ground vehicles, the integration of Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (AAVs) into vehicular digital twin ecosystems remains underexplored. This paper presents a comprehensive survey on the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in enabling AAV Digital Twins for autonomous and cooperative operations within IoV environments. By conceptualizing AAVs as cyber–physical entities continuously synchronized with their virtual counterparts, we analyze how LLMs act as cognitive engines for high-level reasoning, multimodal perception grounding, natural-language interaction, and adaptive mission planning. The survey introduces an LLM-enabled AAV Digital Twin architecture incorporating edge–cloud collaboration, real-time state mirroring, and safety-aware control. Communication workflows leveraging vehicular networking paradigms such as V2X are discussed to support low-latency synchronization and fleet-level coordination. Key application domains, including disaster response, infrastructure monitoring, and Drone-as-a-Service within IoV systems, are examined. Finally, open challenges related to real-time synchronization, computational constraints, and scalability are highlighted, along with future research directions involving TinyLLMs, federated learning, and edge-enabled digital twin platforms.

title: Network Recovery From Cascading Failures in Cyber–Service-Coupled Manufacturing Internet of Things
authors: J. Qian; X. Fu; L. Xing; R. Peng
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Tightly interdependent cyber and service networks in the Manufacturing Internet of Things (MIoT) drive cascading failures to propagate in intertwined horizontal (intralayer) and vertical (cross-layer) directions, greatly complicating post-cascading-failure recovery decisions. To address limitations of existing approaches that neglect cross-layer dependencies and struggle to simultaneously handle heterogeneous load patterns and multiple failure states, this article proposes a coordinated recovery framework for cyber–service-coupled MIoT, termed the coupled reinforcement learning (Coupled-RL) mechanism. Specifically, the Coupled-RL-based recovery (CBR) method equips two layer-specific recovery agents for the cyber and service networks and a lightweight coordinator that orchestrates cross-layer decision-making. This coordinator is designed to avoid infeasible and globally suboptimal plans; its feasibility module (FM) shares the set of repaired nodes between layers and filters out actions that violate cross-layer prerequisites, while its prediction module (PM) exchanges per-state maximal target $Q$ values across layers—these values are used to construct a coupled return and inject cross-layer foresight into the Bellman update process of the agents. A weighted coupled return function and an alternating decision procedure further enable decentralized policy coordination. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed recovery method effectively addresses the two-layer network coordination problem in MIoT during cascading failure recovery. Additionally, a comparative analysis between the proposed algorithm and existing ones is conducted to verify its superiority.

title: Fixed-Time Formation Control for Multi-Robot Systems with Actuator Faults
authors: Z. Zhao; Y. Rui; K. Yan; J. Lei; H. Wang
venue: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: This paper studies the formation control problem for nonholonomic multi-robot systems with actuator faults. A distributed fault-tolerant strategy based on fuzzy adaptive fixed-time control is proposed. A preset performance error transformation is constructed, along with a barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) with a dead-zone design. Uncertain dynamics are approximated using a fuzzy logic system (FLS), such that formation errors converge to a preset small neighborhood within a fixed time. Angle convergence is enhanced by an integral term, and safety is ensured by dynamic adjustments to collision and communication constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated by simulations, which demonstrate strong steady-state accuracy, rapid convergence, and robust fault tolerance.

title: Pass the Parcel: A Relay-Based Nonprehensile Approach to Manipulate Cargo With Multirobot Systems
authors: H. Zhi; F. Bertoncelli; A. Ferrando; C. Yang; L. Sabattini; D. Navarro-Alarcon
venue: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: This article presents a relay-based strategy for multirobot object transportation in constrained environments, where an object is passed sequentially between agents. To enable physical handovers using simple differential drive platforms, we employ nonprehensile pushing, which introduces strict kinematic and friction constraints. We propose an integrated, manipulation-aware framework that jointly optimizes the locations of relay points and their connecting pushing trajectories. Our assignment method explicitly accounts for handover pose constraints and exploits push-face switching to minimize turning effort. The connecting trajectories are generated via a decoupled approach: geometric paths are synthesized using curvature bounded primitives within safe corridors to guarantee pushing stability, followed by temporal optimization to balance robot workloads. To bridge offline planning with online execution, each robot runs a decentralized behavior tree featuring short horizon replanning and spatial–temporal coordination for smooth, collision free handovers. Extensive real world experiments and quantitative comparisons against baselines validate the effectiveness, reliability, and practical viability of the proposed approach.

title: Transformer–based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Sequential Decision–Making in Swarm Confrontation
authors: R. Sun; Q. Wu; L. Chen
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) is a potent paradigm for addressing long–horizon sequential decision–making in swarm confrontation. However, its strategic capabilities are often bottlenecked by high–level policies that struggle to reason over the dynamic, variable–sized observations of other agents. To address this, we introduce a novel decentralized HRL framework featuring a Transformer–based strategic policy. The Transformer’s self–attention mechanism is uniquely suited to capture complex spatio–temporal relationships among a varying number of entities, enabling robust long–horizon task allocation. This high–level strategy is then translated by a low–level policy into collision–free navigation. In complex swarm confrontation scenarios, our method significantly outperforms established baselines, achieving win rates of up to 81%. Beyond this performance, the learned policies exhibit strong zero–shot generalization to larger swarms, offer decision–making interpretability via the attention mechanism, and foster the autonomous emergence of complex cooperative tactics. This work provides a blueprint for scalable, strategically sophisticated, and interpretable multi–agent systems.

title: A New Curriculum-Enhanced Replay Balancing Framework for Cooperative Multi-AUV Target Collection in Sparse-Reward Underwater Environments
authors: Z. Tan; E. Karaköse; N. Özbey
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Cooperative target collection in underwater environments is a challenging sparse-reward multi-agent reinforcement learning problem due to delayed task feedback, continuous navigation dynamics, replay imbalance, and coordination requirements among autonomous underwater vehicles. This study introduces Success-Balanced Dynamic Sampling (SBDS), a task-semantic replay-balancing mechanism that constructs secondary critic updates from controlled proportions of successful target-acquisition, progress-oriented, and uniformly sampled transitions and activates replay enhancement according to training-stability conditions. SBDS is integrated into a MADDPG-based curriculum framework incorporating heading-aware reward shaping and curriculum-compatible observation masking and padding. The primary ablation study compared six algorithmic variants across ten random seeds. CE-SBDS-FR-MADDPG achieved the highest average reward, $5319.56\pm 152.64$ , while maintaining a target-collection rate of $0.9890\pm 0.0202$ , and improved energy efficiency and episode length relative to FR-MADDPG. To evaluate scalability and environmental robustness, an additional 120 training runs were conducted across eight configurations involving 2–5 AUVs and targets, operating regions from $75\times 75$ to $150\times 150$ , obstacle densities up to approximately 5.94%, and ocean-current strengths from 0.00 to 0.12. Under the highest obstacle density, CE-SBDS-FR-MADDPG achieved a collection rate of $0.981\pm 0.010$ , while under the strongest current it maintained $0.977\pm 0.022$ . In the largest five-AUV/five-target configuration, CE-DS-FR-MADDPG achieved the highest mean collection rate, whereas SBDS exhibited lower seed-to-seed variability. FR-MADDPG retained lower collision and obstacle-contact penalties in several conditions. Overall, the results indicate that SBDS does not uniformly dominate every operating condition, but provides a robust replay-management strategy that maintains strong task performance and reduced variability under increasingly challenging cooperative underwater environments.

title: Dual-Stage Coordinated Landing Control for Cross-Domain UAV-USV Fleets
authors: J. Ding; H. -T. Zhang; B. -B. Hu; B. Liu; J. Huang; Y. Zhang; H. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article addresses the challenging issue of coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to land on appropriate unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in a distributed cross-domain setting. Although substantial progresses have been made for single UAV-single USV coordination, achieving seamless experimental cooperative landing of multiple UAVs on multiple USVs remains a dilemma. To this end, we establish a dual-stage coordinated landing control framework. In the first stage, a consensus-based auction algorithm (CBAA) is proposed together with a constrained minimum-energy task-execution strategy to enable pairwise UAV-USV matching and tracking. In the second stage, a visual navigation-based landing controller ensures smooth UAV landings onto designated USVs. Afterwards, sufficient conditions are derived to guarantee the finite-time stability of the associated closed-loop systems. Finally, both the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme are validated through real lake-based experiments conducted on a self-established platform consisting of three DJI M100 UAVs and three HUSTER-37 catamaran USVs, along with simulations demonstrating its robustness to increased fleet sizes.

title: QUARE: Quality-Aware Requirements Analysis Through Multi-Agent Dialectical Negotiation
authors: H. Cheng; M. Kim; F. Khomh; T. Racharak; N. Yoshioka; N. Ubayashi; H. Washizaki
venue: 2026 IEEE 34th International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE)
abstract: Automating requirements quality analysis remains challenging because multiple, often conflicting quality attributes must be balanced while preserving stakeholder intent. Existing Large-Language-Model (LLM) approaches predominantly rely on task-oriented decomposition or implicit aggregation, limiting their ability to systematically surface and resolve cross-quality conflicts. We present QUARE (QUality-Aware REquirements Analysis), a multi-agent framework that takes a project description as input and formulates requirements quality analysis as structured negotiation among five quality-specialized agents (Safety, Efficiency, Green, Trustworthiness, and Responsibility), coordinated by a dedicated orchestrator. QUARE introduces a dialectical negotiation protocol that explicitly exposes interquality conflicts and resolves them through iterative proposal, critique, and synthesis. Negotiated outcomes are transformed into structurally sound KAOS goal models via topology validation and verified against industry standards through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). We evaluate QUARE on five benchmark systems drawn from established RE benchmarks (MARE, iReDev) and an industrial autonomous-driving specification, spanning safety-critical, financial, and information-system domains. Results show that QUARE achieves 98.2% compliance coverage (+105% over both baselines), 94.9% semantic preservation (+2.3 percentage points over the best baseline), and high verifiability (4.96/5.0), while generating 25-43% more requirements than existing multi-agent RE frameworks. These findings suggest that, when using capable instruction-tuned models, architectural choices such as quality-dimension decomposition, explicit negotiation, and automated verification may contribute more to output quality than model scale alone.

title: BudgetSRE: Budget-Aware Multi-Agent Incident Response for Backend Operations
authors: Q. Yang; G. Feng; Y. Wang; J. Chen; Z. Luo
venue: 2026 3rd International Conference on Image Processing, Multimedia Technology and Machine Learning (IPMML)
abstract: Modern cloud incident response increasingly relies on large language model (LLM) powered agents, yet operational deployments face a critical and often overlooked constraint: cost. Unconstrained agents can consume thousands of tokens and dozens of tool calls per incident, incurring non-trivial monetary and latency overhead while occasionally issuing unsafe remediation actions. We present BudgetSRE, a multi-agent framework that treats budget—tokens, tool calls, and action depth—as a first-class design parameter alongside response quality and safety. BudgetSRE comprises a lightweight Scout Agent for cheap triage, a Specialist Agent invoked only when diagnostic uncertainty is high, an Action Planner that orders remediations by risk-to-benefit ratio, and a Budget Controller that dynamically reallocates quotas across agents. We formulate budget allocation as a constrained optimization problem and derive a greedy Pareto-style policy. Experiments on the AIOpsLab benchmark show that BudgetSRE achieves a success rate within 4–6 percentage points of an unconstrained oracle at medium budget, outperforms single-agent ReAct by up to 17.9 points at low budget, and reduces unsafe-action incidence by up to 53% compared with naive multi-agent baselines.

title: Imitation and Exploration: Learning for Vision-Based Communication-Free Multi-UAV Coordination in Cluttered Environments
authors: Y. Wan; X. Chen; Z. Zhao; K. Wang; J. Tang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: Multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (Multi-UAV) autonomous navigation in complex environments presents significant challenges, particularly in communication-denied scenarios where traditional coordination methods fail. Vision-based approaches offer a promising alternative by enabling operation with only onboard sensors, but face fundamental limitations: modular approaches separating perception, mapping, and planning introduce compounding errors across stages, while end-to-end learning methods struggle with sample inefficiency and poor generalization to different environments. We present imitation and exploration learning (IEL), a framework that enables robust communication-free multi-UAV coordination in cluttered environments. Unlike previous methods that treat imitation learning and reinforcement learning as separate paradigms, IEL integrates them through a unified objective function that dynamically balances expert guidance with reinforcement-based exploration. Our implementation combines Dagger’s iterative expert supervision with soft actor–critic’s maximum-entropy reinforcement learning within a centralized training with decentralized execution architecture. Extensive experimental validation demonstrates that IEL achieves 95.5% of the performance of privileged-information models while operating solely with onboard visual sensors. Most significantly, IEL maintains 85.4% performance in challenging environments where conventional imitation learning approaches degrade substantially, confirming its effectiveness in bridging the efficiency-generalization gap. Our approach consistently outperforms both pure imitation learning and reinforcement learning baselines across multiple metrics, including collision avoidance, formation maintenance, and adaptive navigation. The principles established in this work extend beyond UAVs to broader multiagent systems requiring coordination without communication infrastructure. By successfully integrating complementary learning paradigms, IEL contributes to the understanding of robust learning approaches in autonomous systems and establishes a promising direction for resilient multiagent technologies.

title: Bearing-Only Formation Control of Nonholonomic Unicycles: A Conditional Disturbance Utilization Method
authors: Q. Wang; H. Yin; Y. Zhang; Y. Yi; W. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers
abstract: Maintaining a stable formation among nonholonomic unicycles presents a significant challenge, particularly when subjected to real-world disturbances such as wheel slipping and motor noise. To tackle this issue, we propose a conditional disturbance utilization (CDU) framework that selectively uses favorable disturbances rather than simply rejecting all. First, the disturbance observer (DO) is employed to establish the informational foundation for subsequent conditional utilization decisions. And, the CDU mechanism dynamically decides whether the disturbance aligns with the desired control objective. Moreover, incorporating bearing rigidity achieves global stability with fast convergence. Specifically, the proposed potential function, constructed from bearing information, mitigates disturbance driven collision risks and ensures safety. Finally, simulations and experiments validate the proposed CDU-based formation control. The results demonstrate substantial improvements in responsiveness, and efficiency when compared to disturbance suppression method, highlighting the superiority of the proposed framework.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-based Optimization Framework for Smart Energy and Resource Management in Cyber-Physical Smart Grid Systems
authors: A. Thakur; A. Chaurasiya; K.Roopatharshini; A. Sarraf; T.Hemalatha; S. P
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
abstract: The transformation of smart grids calls for scalable, autonomous, and adaptive optimisation approaches to manage energy and resources in complex, dynamic, and distributed systems. Traditional centralized methods are not scalable, have slow response times, and are prone to single-point failures. To overcome these challenges, this research introduces a Hierarchical Federated Graph-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (HFG-MARL) approach that combines distributed intelligence, real-time coordination, and adaptive learning to effectively manage diverse energy resources. The hierarchical structure employs graph-based learning to model spatial–temporal correlations between distributed grid nodes to efficiently optimize energy dispatch, load balancing, demand response, renewable integration, and energy storage. Moreover, safe and explainable reinforcement learning approaches are integrated to guarantee system safety, reliability and regulatory adherence, and federated learning improves scalability and data privacy by allowing local model training without data exchange. Blockchain-based verification also enhances security by thwarting malicious model training and aggregations. The experimental results show substantial improvement in performance including 28.90% reduction in operational cost, 24.70% power loss and 86.50% renewable energy absorption over traditional optimization and reinforcement learning approaches. The model converges faster (640 episodes) than centralized RL (950) and independent MARL (820), demonstrating enhanced learning capability. Scalability analysis shows lower communication costs (55-65%), increased cumulative reward (up to 0.91) with improved stability. Additionally, the security and privacy analysis reveals 99.2% attack detection, 0.8% false acceptance rate, 100% tamper detection and 0% data leakage, ensuring secure and reliable distributed learning. In summary, the proposed approach offers a scalable, efficient, and secure solution to next-generation cyber-physical smart grids in line with sustainable energy and Industry 5.0 goals.

title: Agile Flight Emerges from Multi-Agent Competitive Racing
authors: V. Pasumarti; L. Bianchi; A. Loquercio
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Through multi-agent competition and the sparse high-level objective of winning a race, we find that both agile flight (e.g., high-speed motion pushing the platform to its physical limits) and strategy (e.g., overtaking or blocking) emerge from agents trained with reinforcement learning. We provide evidence in both simulation and the real world that this approach outperforms the common paradigm of training agents in isolation with rewards that prescribe behavior, e.g., progress on the raceline, in particular when the complexity of the environment increases, e.g., in the presence of obstacles. Moreover, we find that multi-agent competition yields policies that transfer more reliably to the real world than policies trained with a single-agent progress-based reward, despite the two methods using the same simulation environment, randomization strategy, and hardware. In addition to improved sim-to-real transfer, the multi-agent policies also exhibit some degree of generalization to opponents unseen at training time. Overall, our work, following in the tradition of multi-agent competitive game-play in digital domains, shows that sparse task-level rewards are sufficient for training agents capable of advanced low-level control in the physical world. title: A Path Evolution Model and Velocity Field Cooperative Optimization Method for Multi-Node Rigid System
authors: S. Qu; J. Ma; D. Wang; X. Li; Y. Yang
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Algorithm, Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision (AAICV)
abstract: In the complex curved path environment, the modeling of multi-node rigid connection system and the dynamic behavior control are the core challenges in automatic control and computer simulation. In the complex curved path environment, the modeling of multi-node rigid connection system and the dynamic behavior control are the core challenges in automatic control and computer simulation. The global path guidance field is constructed based on the helical space curve, and the continuous modeling of the rigid connection relationship is realized by the recursive strategy from the head node to the tail node. Meanwhile, the differential velocity estimation and dynamic correction mechanism are introduced to effectively buffer the nonlinear velocity disturbance caused by the path curvature. Furthermore, the integration of a lightweight collision prediction module significantly enhances the system's stability and physical consistency under high-density simulations. The simulation results show that the proposed method has good speed smoothness and system stability while keeping the geometric structure of the node queue, and is suitable for typical engineering scenarios such as multi-robot path planning, flexible chain system simulation, traffic formation scheduling, etc. This paper provides theoretical support and practical solutions for modeling and path collaborative control of chain systems in complex geometric environments.

title: Machine Learning Methods for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance in Autonomous Systems
authors: I. Kazazic; D. Music; E. Babovic
venue: 2026 25th International Symposium INFOTEH-JAHORINA (INFOTEH)
abstract: With the continuous evolution of technology, autonomous systems have become increasingly capable of operating effectively in complex and dynamic environments. Traditional collision avoidance methods, though effective in static or controlled conditions, struggle to adapt to real-world scenarios characterized by uncertainty and change. The integration of machine learning enables autonomous systems to perceive their surroundings, learn behavioral patterns, and predict the trajectories of dynamic obstacles. By leveraging large-scale sensory and visual data, these systems can distinguish between static and moving objects and plan safe, proactive paths. Trajectory prediction and reinforcement learning (RL) further enhance adaptability by allowing systems to anticipate future states and learn optimal decision-making strategies through interaction with the environment. These advancements mark a transition from reactive to proactive behavior, forming the foundation for safe, intelligent, and fully autonomous operation in real-world dynamic contexts.

title: A Privacy-Preserving On-Device Multi-Agent Architecture for AI PC (POMA) Workflow Automation
authors: S. Begum; M. Rosenzweig
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI and Data Analytics (ICAD)
abstract: AI agents that automate desktop workflows can reduce time spent on repetitive knowledge work, but enterprise deployment raises acute privacy and trust challenges. Computer-use agents (CUAs) observe sensitive on-screen content and execute high-impact actions in open-world environments, making them vulnerable to prompt injection and unsafe tool use. Meanwhile, recent model evolution has significantly improved the capabilities of small language and compact multimodal models, enabling specialized low-latency inference that can run fully on-device. This paper presents AIPC-POMA, a privacy-preserving on-device multi-agent architecture for personal and enterprise AI PC workflow automation. AIPC POMA composes a set of carefully crafted, task-specialized small agents including an SLM for drafting, a compact VLM+OCR stack for document and screen understanding, and a sandboxed CUA for GUI interaction coordinated by a local Orchestrator and enforced by a Policy Verifier. POMA is designed around two principles: privacy by minimized data flow and trust by controlled action execution, achieved through least-privilege action primitives, risk-aware gating, and auditable execution traces. We describe a hardware aware implementation optimized for heterogeneous AI acceleration on AI PCs such as Panther Lake-class system, and we introduce an evaluation task suite and adversarial safety battery targeting indirect prompt injection and real-world agent threats. We define metrics spanning utility, latency, privacy leakage, and action safety, demonstrating that POMA enables practical low-cost automation while reducing exposure to untrusted inputs.

title: Actuator Fault-Tolerance Control of Nonlinear Fully Actuated Systems
authors: D. -W. Zhang; Z. Lei
venue: 2026 Joint International Conference on Automation-Intelligence-Safety (ICAIS) & International Symposium on Autonomous Systems (ISAS)
abstract: This paper considers a fault-tolerance control problem against actuator failures by means of a fully actuated system (FAS) approach. A fault observer-based dynamic compensator is established to deal with the proposed problem. Concretely, a FAS model of discrete-time nonlinear systems under actuator failures is firstly constructed as a foundation for the FAS approach-based control. Then, a fault observer is developed to implement the accurate fault estimation of the unknown but bounded actuator failures. Based on the FAS approach, a dynamic compensator is generated to achieve the tracking control with eliminating the originally open-loop nonlinearities. To investigate the bounded stability and tracking performance of the closed-loop FASs, a sufficient condition is derived in the following discussion. The proposed approach provides a solution to a spacecraft rendezvous trajectory tracking problem for verifying the feasibility.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Distributed Control for Cooperative Manipulator With Output Constraints
authors: C. -H. Zhang; Z. -Y. Hu; Y. -J. Li; H. -B. Yan; Y. Zhang; Z. -Y. Qin; C. -C. Hua
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Existing joint constraint formulations typically ensure hardware safety and task feasibility by imposing limits on position, velocity, and torque. While effective in joint space, such approaches can sometimes be conservative with respect to operational performance and may not fully align with the needs of high-level task planning. In this article, a novel universal time-varying asymmetric barrier function (UTABF) for coordinate constraints is proposed, which intuitively captures desired task performance. Specifically, the Hadamard product is employed to construct the UTABF that directly handles vector-type coordinate constraints and transforms them into boundedness problems within a reconstructed system. The reconstructed system retains the skew-symmetric property of the system matrix, which is essential for stability analysis. Based on this framework, an online learning module and a distributed cooperative controller are co-designed to achieve unified online estimation of unknown dynamic parameters and uniformly ultimately bounded performance under task-oriented constraints, while a robust term in the controller handles external disturbances. Finally, the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed strategy are validated through both simulations and physical experiments.

title: Behavioral Gateways of the AI Revolution: An Agent-Based Analysis of Human Decision Rules and Emergent Reliance
authors: Y. Turgut; A. Gürbüz
venue: 2026 10th International Artificial Intelligence and Data Processing Symposium (IDAP)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is often described as a productivity shock, but this shock reaches people through behavioral filters. Workers interpret AI through trust, perceived risk, loss aversion, social cues, and their own confidence in a task. This paper develops a transparent agent-based model that connects seven behavioral decision mechanisms–expected utility, satisficing, prospect-theoretic loss aversion, heuristic cue following, algorithm aversion, automation bias, and social learning–to three AI-use modes: non-use, assisted use, and delegated use. The model is illustrated through a stylized knowledge-work organization with synthetic team, advice-seeking, and weak cross-team network layers. The first six scenarios keep the AI frontier approximately fixed and vary organizational or behavioral conditions; the high-capability scenario is treated separately as a technology-frontier stress test. Across Monte Carlo runs and run-level robustness checks, the model generates clustered adoption, local non-adoption lock-in, trust polarization, aversion-driven sensitivity, and a productivity-risk trade-off under delegation pressure. Because the model is uncalibrated, the results should be read as mechanism demonstrations rather than empirical forecasts. They suggest that organizations should evaluate AI deployment not only by adoption rates, but also by calibrated reliance, verification behavior, delegation intensity, visible failures, and distributional effects across behavioral types.

title: Global Predefined-Time Neural Network-Based Performance Control for UAV Safe Formation With Input Saturation and Disturbance Estimation
authors: M. Wu; X. Zhuang; Z. Hou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This study presents a global predefined-time adaptive control method with prescribed performance for quadrotor UAV safe formation subject to external disturbances. The dynamic models of quadrotor UAVs are first transformed into position and attitude subsystems. Then, a global neural network-robust control strategy with switching functions is proposed by introducing an $n$ -th-order continuously differentiable function. On this basis, a global predefined time-prescribed performance controller is developed by utilizing a performance function, which ensures both position and attitude subsystems converge globally to specified accuracy within a given time. During flight, obstacle effects are also considered, and an obstacle avoidance strategy is designed using Barrier Lyapunov Functions (BLFs) to guarantee the safety for the UAV formation.
