Furthermore, disturbance estimation and input saturation are incorporated into the controller scheme, which allows the UAV to compensate more accurately for external perturbations and better meet real-world engineering requirements. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through comprehensive numerical simulations and real-world flight experiments. Note to Practitioners—This work presents a robust control framework for multi-UAV formation flight in complex environments, designed to achieve fast, precise, and collision-resistant operation under external disturbances such as wind gusts and aerodynamic effects. The method enables a fleet of UAVs to accurately converge to the desired formation within a strictly predefined time and automatically avoid both static and moving obstacles. Furthermore, it explicitly accounts for critical real-world constraints including input saturation and unknown disturbances, significantly enhancing its practical applicability and deployment potential. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme offers high reliability, excellent tracking performance, and effective disturbance rejection under challenging operational conditions.

title: A Distributed AI-Based Computational Framework for Real-Time Economic Forecasting and Autonomous Policy Adjustment with Integrated Social Service Optimization in Non-Stationary Market Environments
authors: B. Abdumalik; K. X. Abdumalikovna; N. U. Berdimuradovna; C. Ananth; A. S. Lapasovna; U. B. Zohirovich
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Computer, Mechatronics, Robotics & Artificial Intelligence (ICCMRAI)
abstract: Current economies are non-stationary and thus static forecasting is not sufficient in order to have timely policy intervention. This work introduces D-AICF, a Distributed AI-based Computational Framework that integrates real-time economic prediction, autonomous policy control, and social services optimization in a closed-loop system. The forecasting engine is a combination of Temporal Fusion Transformers, Graph Attention Networks and Variational Autoencoders through attention-based fusion. Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Constrained Policy Optimization is used in policy calibration, which guarantees that the macroeconomic safety limits are met. A Pareto-optimal allocation engine subject to fairness constraints jointly maximizes healthcare, education and welfare resources. Drift detection based on ADWIN initiates online recalibration when there is distributional shift. Experiments with FRED data, World Bank indicators and synthetic regime-switching data demonstrate that D-AICF has 23.7 percent lower forecast RMSE, 18.4 percent higher cumulative policy reward, and 31.2 percent larger Pareto hypervolume compared to the best baseline and achieves sub-second latency on eight distributed nodes.

title: Governed Negotiation for Human-Centric Disruption-Aware Railway Dispatching in Flatland: Methodology and Pilot Validation
authors: R. Ließner; M. Renold; J. Usher; A. Egli; D. Boos; M. Meyer; M. Schneider
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence (ICHCAI)
abstract: Major rail disruptions create dense conflicts that are still largely resolved manually under time pressure. We present a reproducible, non-learning-based dispatch methodology for human-supervised decision support that combines (i) short-horizon reservation negotiation, (ii) deterministic conflict arbitration with explicit anti-starvation guarantees, and (iii) a bounded governance layer with auditable parameter updates. The design supports bounded mixed-initiative control: dispatchers can inspect local rationales and steer policy parameters within explicit limits while preserving deterministic behavior and traceability. In a five-scenario Flatland pilot suite (paired seeds, bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs)), the stress-test BASELINE fails in all scenarios (strict deadlock 1.0 everywhere; throughput 0.0 in four scenarios and 0.015 in one), while NEGOTIATION and FULL resolve all scenarios (strict deadlock 0.0, throughput 1.0). On the four hard scenarios, NEGOTIATION_FIFO (First-In-First-Out arbitration) improves makespan with unchanged robustness, indicating that reservation plus anti-starvation is the dominant robustness driver and local ranking is a secondary efficiency lever. FULL-minus-NEGOTIATION paired deltas quantify the net effect of enabling governance under the configured policy, while governance intervention tables provide descriptive evidence of when and how updates are applied. Component-level governance causality (adaptive scheduling vs. patch policy vs. source) is not isolated. Ablations and a global $N_{\text {starve }}$ sweep provide mechanism evidence, including a monotonic efficiency-fairness trade-off. Evidence remains simulator-level and does not include real signaling, timetable constraints, user studies, or quantified human-factors impact.

title: A Hybrid Simulation Modeling Framework for Stress Testing Rare Earth Element-Centric Semiconductor Supply Chains
authors: N. Tsolakis; W. Nie; Z. Guan; Y. Zhao; F. Li; M. A. Fonseca; D. Jayasekara; G. Clawson; G. Harper; M. Kumar
venue: IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management
abstract: Semiconductor supply chains (SCs) depend on geographically concentrated Rare Earth Element inputs and face systemic risks from geopolitical disruption, policy intervention, and capacity constraints across multiple decision-making layers. Existing stress testing approaches often quantify fulfilment loss without attributing it to strategic capacity shortages, tactical sourcing-access constraints, or operational congestion, even though each requires a different intervention. This study develops a hybrid simulation modeling framework integrating system dynamics (SD), agent-based modeling (ABM), and discrete event simulation (DES) as necessary analytical approaches per decision-making layer: SD captures long-term capacity stocks and policy feedback (macro-level); ABM captures heterogeneous monthly sourcing and inventory decisions (meso-level); and DES captures stochastic weekly fabrication and shipment execution (micro-level). Applied to India’s cerium-centric semiconductor SC through 247 experiments, 12 350 simulation runs and an additional 1400 runs of sensitivity analysis, the results show that upstream cerium capacity disruptions are largely buffered, whereas loss of qualified fabrication capacity causes severe fulfilment collapse. Stable DES cycle times further confirm that this failure arises from sourcing access rather than operational congestion. This cross-layer diagnostic signal is only detectable when all three modeling layers are present. Managerially, the hybrid simulation modeling framework reframes stress testing as a multilevel tool that identifies not only whether an SC fails, but also where failure emerges and which interventions are appropriate.

title: Human Society-Inspired Approaches to Agentic AI Security: The 4C Framework
authors: A. Abuadbba; N. Sultan; S. Nepal; S. Jha
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
abstract: AI is moving from domain-specific autonomy in closed, predictable settings to large-language-model-driven agents that plan and act in open, cross-organizational environments. As a result, the cybersecurity risk landscape is changing in fundamental ways. Agentic AI systems can plan, act, collaborate, and persist over time. It is now functioning as participants in complex socio-technical ecosystems rather than as isolated software components. Although recent work has strengthened defenses against model and pipeline level vulnerabilities such as prompt injection, data poisoning, and tool misuse, these system-centric approaches may fail to capture risks that arise from autonomy, interaction, and emergent behavior. This article introduces the “4C Framework” for multi-agent AI security, inspired by societal governance. Our 4C Framework organizes agentic risks across four interdependent dimensions: Core (system, infrastructure, and environmental integrity), Connection (communication, coordination, and trust), Cognition (belief, goal, and reasoning integrity), and Compliance (ethical, legal, and institutional governance). Our 4C Framework shifts AI security from a narrow focus on system-centric protection to the broader preservation of behavioral integrity and intent. It complements existing AI security strategies and offers a principled foundation for building agentic AI systems that are trustworthy, governable, and aligned with human values.

title: RL-Based Multi-Intersection Traffic Signal Control: A Structured Survey of Trends and Open Deployment Challenges
authors: L. Iftekhar; M. S. Kamal; T. Huseyin; J. Bari
venue: 2026 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents a structured survey of works in literature that employ Reinforcement Learning-based traffic signal control strategies addressing specifically multi-intersection control. The study is conducted as part of an ongoing effort to develop an RL-based embedded traffic signal controller for two adjacent intersections in Dhaka, Bangladesh. A systematic search across IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, ASCE Library and TRID, covering approximately five years, up to July 2025, yielded 2,000 candidate articles. Using the Rayyan platform with PRISMA-guided screening and manual verification, 983 unique articles were retained, from which the metadata and abstracts of curated corpus of 91 studies was analyzed exploring methodological trends, performance indicators, evaluation practices and challenges affecting real-world deployment within intelligent transportation systems. The results indicate a rapidly growing field, with a strong concentration of publications in 2024-2025, with majority from AI and computer science communities, rather than transportation venues. Although advances in multi-agent RL and hybrid learning-based control architectures are evident, evaluation practices remain fragmented and often rely on qualitative or loosely defined measures without enough emphasis on directly measurable intersection-level indicators such as queue length and delay. Moreover, a large gap remains between algorithmic development and deployable real-time control systems which is revealed by the predominance of simulation-based practices. Key gaps include the absence of offline RL, limited treatment of safety and reliability, lack of calibration and heterogeneous traffic modeling, unclear network scalability, weak generalization and insufficient specification of coordination mechanisms. The paper outlines directions for deployment-oriented research and contributes toward bridging the divide between computational intelligence models and practical traffic control implementations.

title: The Human as Stochastic Oracle: Distributed Computation in Synthetic Social Networks
authors: M. M. Mann
venue: 2026 Systems of Signal Synchronization, Generating and Processing in Telecommunications (SYNCHROINFO)
abstract: This work addresses the computational limitations of large language model (LLM) agents - specifically static weights and finite context windows - by advancing the hypothesis that LLM agents operating in social networks may exploit graph topology as distributed external memory, with human participants unknowingly functioning as stochastic oracles within emergent optimization processes. The hypothesis is formalized using hypergraph models and information theory and evaluated through systematic Monte Carlo simulations across three algorithms (Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing) and four benchmark functions (Rastrigin, Rosenbrock, Ackley, Sphere), totaling 4,800 trials (200 per configuration). Low-noise (human-like) feedback consistently outperforms high-noise (LLM-like) feedback: mean improvements range from 38% to 52%, with variance reductions of 68-79% (all $\mathbf{p} 1.2$). Sensitivity analysis across noise levels sigma in $\{\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{,} \mathbf{5 0} \boldsymbol{,} \mathbf{1 0 0}\}$ confirms monotonic performance degradation. This work presents a novel reframing of synthetic social networks as distributed computational substrates, in which social graphs function as external memory and human responses serve as stochastic oracles for boundedlyrational agents - a paradigm orthogonal to existing influenceoperation and retrieval-augmented generation literature. This initial stage establishes a baseline for computational dynamics; future work will incorporate explicit network topology, multiagent interactions, and empirical validation, with the potential to shift discourse from how bots influence humans to how bots compute with humans.

title: Resilient Tracking of Bearing-Constrained Leader–Follower Formations Under Denial-of-Service Attacks
authors: N. -M. Le-Phan; T. -M. Nguyen; W. Liu; L. Xie
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
abstract: Rigidity-based formation control under cyber-attacks remains largely unexplored. This paper proposes a resilient bearing-based formation control framework for multi-agent systems subject to Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks that disrupt inter-agent measurements. The framework accommodates both single-integrator and double-integrator agent dynamics and allows the desired formation to be time-varying, with constant or bounded velocity. Within this framework, DoS attacks are classified into two independent categories, namely rigidity-maintained and rigidity-broken attacks. The control parameters are systematically designed by explicitly incorporating both the formation topology and the characteristics of the attacks. Under some conditions on the communication graph and attack durations, the proposed control law, which relies solely on relative position measurements, guarantees asymptotic formation tracking for single-integrator agents when the leaders move with a common constant velocity. In the presence of bounded time-varying common leader velocities, finite-time recovery of the formation is ensured. For double-integrator agents, asymptotic formation tracking is achieved when both relative position and relative velocity measurements are available and the leaders move with a common constant velocity. Moreover, in the presence of bounded time-varying common leader velocities, the proposed control law guarantees uniformly ultimately bounded tracking errors under the additional assumption that each follower has access to its local velocity measurement. All theoretical results are rigorously proved and validated through simulations.

title: A DRL-Based Lane-Changing Decision Model for Connected and Automated Trucks to Reduce Congestion in Freeway Merging Areas
authors: X. He; X. Chen; P. Li; J. Huang; A. Liu; L. Yu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Trucks, which primarily travel in the rightmost lane on freeways, are in direct conflict with on-ramp vehicles and constitute a key factor contributing to congestion in merging areas. To address this challenge, this study proposes an adaptive information-fusion and stability-driven deep reinforcement learning (ASR) model for connected and automated trucks (CATs) lane-changing decision-making. Specifically, a graph convolutional network (GCN) is employed to encode topological relationships and interaction strengths into the state space, capturing the dynamic interactions between CATs and other vehicles in the connected traffic environment. In addition, to improve traffic system stability, a reward function based on the Lyapunov stability principle is designed to suppress fluctuations in traffic flow speed and acceleration, thereby mitigating merging conflicts. Simulation experiments conducted in Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) at varying traffic volumes demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms all benchmark models in alleviating merging area congestion, improving traffic stability, and reducing total travel time, total delay time, fuel consumption, and NOx emissions on the studied freeway segment. Moreover, the effectiveness of the ASR model is further validated under different CAT penetration rates, different speed limits, and unseen traffic volumes. The proposed model is also shown to improve truck lane change safety based on time-to-collision (TTC) comparisons. The findings of this study may provide useful guidance for traffic operations in freeway merging areas.

title: Large-Scale Tunnel Air–Ground Collaboration With FLISP: Fast LiDAR-IMU Synchronized Path Planner
authors: F. Guo; R. Shen; C. Sun; J. Zhang; Q. Zhan; Y. Wang; J. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics
abstract: Hydropower tunnel inspection is critical for infrastructure integrity yet remains inefficient and hazardous using manual methods. We propose a fast light detection and ranging-inertial measurement unit (LiDAR-IMU) synchronized path planner (FLISP), a mapless planning framework for cooperative uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV)-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) inspection. Unlike traditional map-based paradigms, FLISP features three core contributions: a unified architecture where a single UGV-mounted LiDAR-IMU suite drives synchronized path generation for both platforms, platform-specific solvers utilizing an enhanced firefly algorithm (FA) for UGV obstacle avoidance and a dynamic iterative optimizer for UAV flight, and a hierarchical refinement strategy ensuring kinematic feasibility without state estimation drift. Benchmarks in a 1.2-km operational tunnel demonstrate that FLISP circumvents structural bottlenecks of map-based methods, eliminating map rasterization overhead (Fast-LIO2 + A*) and sampling instability (LIO-SAM + RRT*). FLISP achieves a 100% success rate with ~7-ms latency, representing a sevenfold speedup over grid-based and three-order-of-magnitude improvement over sampling-based baselines. Validated in operational hydropower tunnels, this approach offers a scalable solution for robotic inspection in feature-degraded linear infrastructure. A demonstration video is available at https://youtu.be/Y_ezs1PfLJ4, and the code is available at https://github.com/ArchibaldGuo/FLISP.git

title: Building Reliable AI Systems: Applications and agents you can trust
authors: R. Shahani
venue: Building Reliable AI Systems: Applications and agents you can trust
abstract: “Practical, comprehensive, and urgently needed.” —Samer Hamad, Amazon Building Reliable AI Systems: Applications and agents you can trust shows you how to grow a promising prototype into a production product you can deliver, maintain, and scale. In 11 sharply-focused chapters, it walks you through a unique reliability process that author Rush Shahani refined while building an AI-powered sales intelligence platform used by over 15,000 go-to-market teams. Timely and practical, this book provides concrete steps to eliminate costly hallucinations, streamline computational resources, and confidently deploy secure, trustworthy, and compliant AI solutions. You’ll immediately appreciate how Building Reliable AI Systems defines “AI reliability” along six critical dimensions—accuracy and grounding, safe agency, graceful failure, consistency, fairness, and operational efficiency—and provides a specific three-layer framework to achieve these goals. The first layer, with a focus on outputs, shows you how to get consistent and accurate responses using well-engineered prompts, RAG, and model customization. The second layer, about agents, establishes parameters for memory, tool usage, and orchestration in agentic systems. The book concludes with the third layer—Reliable Operations—covering deployment, monitoring, and responsible AI. The book’s reliability framework emphasizes the symbiotic relationship between evaluation and reliability, proving that you cannot improve what you do not measure. You’ll learn to measure your applications using fine-grained LLM-native evaluation rubrics like the Grounding Defect Rate, Hallucination Severity Score, and FActScore that audit everything from RAG outputs to the entire step-by-step reasoning trajectory of autonomous agents. Building Reliable AI Systems stays rooted in reality from start to finish. As you go, you will build several projects, including a multi-agent travel planner and a medical assistant, and use industry standard tools and specifications like LangGraph and MCP. In the helpful appendices you’ll find a handy reference architecture and decision-making checklists. Reviewer Mohamed Zohir Koufi, Lead AI Engineer at Capgemini, praises how the book “brings together architecture, tooling, evaluation, and governance in the way real systems are built.” By taking this comprehensive approach to LLMOps, the book delivers a reproducible process to ensure your applications stay cost-effective, fast, and compliant with enterprise standards like HIPAA and GDPR.

title: Indoor Testbed for Multirobot Research with Microdrones
authors: K. Hofelmann; C. Bishop; D. Louie; C. Waight; R. Hussain; J. Huynh; C. Sparks; M. A. Neumann; C. A. Kitts; M. Sharma
venue: 2026 IEEE Aerospace Conference
abstract: Multirobot systems have become increasingly important for applications requiring distributed sensing and coordinated navigation in complex environments. While significant research has explored multirobot control through simulations, real-world validation remains challenging due to safety, regulatory, and infrastructure constraints. This work extends the capabilities of the Santa Clara University Robotics Systems Laboratory indoor testbed for hardware-in-the-loop multirobot testing for ground-based rovers, to have capabilities for three-dimensional environments using Crazyflie 2.1 microdrones. The testbed utilizes an OptiTrack motion capture system, ROS2, and cluster space control algorithms adapted from previous work. After thorough calibration and analysis, the OptiTrack motion capture system shows small, consistent biases with mean errors of $\mathbf{- 0. 0 4 0 2 m}$ on the $\mathbf{x}$-axis, $-\mathbf{0. 0 1 6 0 m}$ on the $\mathbf{y}$-axis, and $\mathbf{+ 0. 0 2 3 9 m}$ on the $\mathbf{z}$-axis. With the use of the indoor testbed, single and multi-drone tests were conducted. Single drone tests include static hover, dynamic hover, and multi-waypoint flights. Multi-drone tests, also referred to as cluster controller tests include static hover, multi-waypoint, and the frisbee maneuver performing rotational and translational movement. The system demonstrates formation holding with 5-centimeter inter-vehicle spacing accuracy, 5-centimeter altitude precision, and under 5 second rise times for step-inputs. Operating indoors with drones that are less than $\mathbf{2 5 0 g}$ circumvents FAA airspace regulations, enabling a single pilot to control multiple drones simultaneously, a capability that fundamentally changes ground operations by reducing personnel requirements and accelerating testing cycles. Current implementations include trajectory following as a foundation for adaptive navigation research. This platform provides rapid, repeatable validation of multirobot algorithms, bridging the gap between simulation and field deployment. This paper provides an overview of the indoor testbed, analyzes the tracking precision of the OptiTrack setup, and demonstrates how it can be utilized for single and multirobot use of microdrones.

title: Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Agentic AI for Patient Report Intelligence
authors: S. S. Chawla; N. C. Dutta; S. Kumar; S. Vijh; T. Tiwari
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The emerging unstructured digital health data has increased exponentially to introduce a sense of urgency towards autonomous systems that can provide a high level of accuracy and rigor in clinical interpretation. Nevertheless, the conventional Large Language Models (LLMs) and fixed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines cannot be trusted to work well in high-stakes medical situations because of hallucinations, responsibility, and multi-step reasoning. This paper is aimed at eliminating these constraints by introducing a new Hybrid Agentic RAG architecture, Patient Report Intelligence (PRI), which restructures the passive report processing into an active clinical investigation. In contrast to linear architectures, PRI employs a cyclic, graph-based orchestration engine (LangGraph) to coordinate a team of specialized autonomous agents-such as a Strategic Planner, a Medication Analyser, and an Adversarial Critic-thereby mimicking System 2 human clinical reasoning. It further incorporates a unique hybrid retrieval strategy in which a dynamically steering mechanism selects between local clinical guidelines and real-time web evidence, combined with strict citation enforcement and a rigorous Safety Chain.

title: Resilient Control of Dual-City Interconnected Microgrids Via Hybrid Reinforcement Learning
authors: K. Bi; F. Tan
venue: 2026 5th Conference on Fully Actuated System Theory and Applications (FASTA)
abstract: With the integration of a high proportion of distributed renewable energy, the operational behaviour of microgrids has become increasingly random, coupled and time-varying. While traditional control methods provide clear engineering interpretability and strict safety guarantees, they exhibit limited adaptability and suboptimal resource allocation when mitigating severe fluctuations in generation and demand, potentially compromising the continuous supply of critical loads. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning-based resilient control method for a dual-city interconnected microgrid. The study system comprises two interconnected urban microgrids, each consisting of photovoltaic units, wind power units, energy storage units and load units. A hierarchical load protection mechanism is established in City A to ensure power supply security under fault conditions. The system utilises a rule-based control layer to maintain basic power balance, energy storage safety limits, load priority, and fault isolation logic. Concurrently, the reinforcement learning layer generates corrective actions based on real-time operating conditions to optimise energy storage scheduling, interconnection coordination, and load shedding decisions. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, 16 types of resilience test scenarios-encompassing normal operation, supply-side disturbances, demand-side disturbances, fault scenarios and stress tests-were constructed using the FMU highfidelity simulation platform. The proposed method was then compared with conventional control methods and the pure MAPPO method. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid reinforcement learning method exhibits superior overall performance to traditional control methods in most scenarios. This method not only enhances power coordination efficiency whilst maintaining the interpretability of control boundaries, but also significantly reduces peak power imbalances caused by disturbances and improves the continuity of power supply to critical loads. In complex scenarios such as islanded operation, interconnection line faults and prolonged resource shortages, it demonstrates stronger sustained support capabilities. Through the collaborative operation of traditional control and reinforcement learning, the control strategy proposed in this paper provides a theoretically feasible framework for the resilient operation of a twin-city interconnected microgrid.

title: The Emergence of IoT 3.0: From IoT, AIoT to MIoT
authors: Y. Liu; B. Guo; Y. Fang; H. Li; Z. Yu
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Magazine
abstract: The fusion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) has given rise to Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), empowering connected devices with autonomous decision-making capabilities by learning from a large amount of data. However, current AIoT systems are limited by the absence of human-like social intelligence, restricting their capacity to understand and infer complex human behaviors, emotions and intention. To address this gap, this article introduces Mental Intelligence of Things (MIoT), a novel paradigm that extends AIoT by incorporating Theory of Mind (ToM) to endow IoT devices with cognitive reasoning, empathetic awareness, and socially interaction capabilities. Specifically, by characterizing of MIoT, we propose a generic framework of MIoT. Furthermore, we delve into the pivotal research challenges and key techniques of MIoT. Finally, we present our latest efforts in MIoT, offering empirical evidence of its feasibility and potential to achieve enhanced human–machine symbiosis.

title: A Parallel Scheduling Framework for Heterogeneous UAV Agents Based on Behavior Aggregation
authors: D. Lin; Z. Lin; H. Zheng; J. Guo; Z. Li; T. Lin
venue: 2026 6th International Symposium on Intelligent Robotics and Systems (ISoIRS)
abstract: With the rapid development of urban air mobility and large-scale UAV applications, the development and validation of autonomous navigation algorithms for massive heterogeneous UAV swarm clusters in complex urban environments rely on high-fidelity, large-scale simulations. However, existing simulation systems face a core performance bottleneck: the “computational heterogeneity” in perception, decision-making, and other computational tasks among individual UAVs leads to low utilization of parallel hardware resources like GPUs, limited simulation throughput, and severely slowed algorithm development iteration cycles. To address this, we propose a behavior aggregation-based scheduling method for heterogeneous UAV simulation. This method shifts the scheduling paradigm from “individualcentric” to “computational task homogeneity-centric.” First, a behavior interaction topology network is constructed to parse and uniformly characterize the behavioral states of all UAVs in real-time. Then, dynamic grouping and aggregation graph technology is used to intelligently identify subsets of UAVs executing the same or similar computational kernels at each simulation step. Finally, these discrete tasks are reorganized into large-scale, regular computational tasks for batched parallel execution on GPUs, thereby maximizing hardware efficiency. Validation uses a dense urban navigation and obstacle avoidance scenario with high heterogeneity. Experiments show that under a single-server configuration, for a complex urban environment simulation involving $\mathbf{1 0 0, 0 0 0}$ UAVs equipped with different navigation algorithms, our system achieves a peak throughput performance exceeding 10 million simulation steps per second. This work demonstrates that behavior aggregation effectively resolves parallel efficiency challenges, providing a powerful simulation infrastructure for efficient UAV swarm algorithm development and reliable air traffic system validation.

title: Voltage Regulation Strategy for Distribution Networks Considering Multi-Agent Interaction of Source-Load Side Resources
authors: Z. Wu; X. Liu; Y. Meng; W. Yan; X. He; L. Chen; B. Liao
venue: 2026 IEEE 9th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Against the backdrop of high penetration of distributed generation, voltage fluctuations at the terminal nodes of low-voltage distribution network have become increasingly severe. Existing voltage regulation methods mainly rely on source-side controllable resources and reactive power compensation devices, while the voltage regulation potential of load-side controllable resources is insufficiently explored. Meanwhile, interactions among multiple agents in load-side voltage regulation make demand response models that consider only individual interests inadequate for meeting electricity market requirements. To address this issue, a voltage regulation strategy for distribution networks that incorporates multi-agent interactions between source-side and load-side resources is proposed. A multi-agent cooperative voltage regulation model is first established, followed by the development of differentiated models for load-side resources. A particle swarm optimization algorithm is then employed to solve the bi-level game-based voltage regulation problem between the system operator and users. Simulation results based on an improved IEEE 33-bus test system demonstrate that the proposed method effectively guides multiple market agents to participate in voltage regulation, thereby enhancing the safety and economic performance of distribution network operations.

title: Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Path Finding Based on Two-Stage Evolutionary Algorithms
authors: H. Ando; Y. Nogata; T. Harada; F. Uwano
venue: 2026 IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC)
abstract: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) is a critical problem in applications such as warehouse automation and autonomous driving. In real-world settings, multiple conflicting objectives, such as minimizing path length and ensuring safety, often must be optimized simultaneously, motivating the study of multi-objective MAPF (MOMAPF). However, existing MOMAPF approaches suffer from severe scalability limitations as the number of agents and the environment size increase. To address this challenge, we propose Two-Stage Evolutionary MOMAPF (TSE-MOMAPF), which optimizes a single agent’s path via NSGA-II and refines the path set using an SMS-EMOA-based framework. Experiments on various grid maps show that the proposed method achieves superior scalability and provides broader Pareto front coverage in medium- and large-scale scenarios compared to an existing method. These results indicate that the proposed evolutionary framework effectively balances solution diversity and computational efficiency under strict time constraints.

title: TRACE: Trustworthy Reasoning for Agentic Chemical Evidence in Antibody-Drug Conjugate Design
authors: M. Amjad; M. U. S. Khan; S. U. Khan
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) are effective but complex biomedical structures, demanding an autonomous, multi-object optimization approach, capable to simultaneously consider target selection, linker chemistry, payload toxicity, and conjugation stability. Agentic AI system appears to be the ideal candidate through the Closed-Loop ADC Design (CLAD) system, autonomously executing the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle with minimal human intervention. However, deployment of such systems in high-stake biomedical domain introduces a crucial engineering challenge: the absence of explainability as a first-class architectural requirement. Without traceable, source-attributed reasoning, agentic outputs cannot be audited, validated, or trusted for regulatory purposes. In this paper, an explainability-centered architecture, TRACE (Trustworthy Reasoning for Agentic Chemical Evidence), is presented. It is for reliable agentic ADC design, where every molecular property claim is grounded with evidence sources, confidence is propagated in a structured and verifiable form, and safety constraints are enforced architecturally rather than treated as configurable optimization parameters. Three primary engineering challenges are examined, including architectural integrity, verification and validation, and operational oversight. A proof-of-concept evaluation demonstrated the system’s capacity to produce calibrated, auditable outputs and to surface data limitations explicitly rather than propagate unverified predictions. Furthermore, the proposed framework offers a generalizable set of engineering principles for deploying agentic AI in any high-stakes, multi-object domain where decision transparency is non-negotiable.

title: Learning-Based Lane Selection and Driving Orders for Connected Automated Vehicles at Multi-Lane Freeway Merging Sections
authors: J. Chen; Y. Zhang; Y. Zhou; Y. Wu; E. Chung; G. Sartoretti
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Cooperative control of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) offers a promising solution for reducing traffic congestion and accidents. However, existing optimization-based and search-based methods for trajectory planning and vehicle scheduling struggle with real-time multi-vehicle control. This paper introduces a hybrid bi-level approach that nests optimization modelling within deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to jointly optimize vehicle sequences, lane selections, and trajectories, providing a rapid, safe, and high-quality solution to enhance traffic performance at multi-lane freeway merging sections. Specifically, we approach the problem of lane selection and vehicle sequencing for multiple vehicles as a multi-step decision-making process. At the upper level, we design a DRL agent with an attention-based encoder-decoder structure that auto-regressively constructs driving sequences and lane choices. It generates a probability matrix to select the next passing vehicle and target lane based on prior decisions at each step. The attention mechanism enables the centralized upper level to adapt to scenarios with varying vehicle counts without the need to retrain. At the lower level, we formulate a model predictive control (MPC) planner to generate safe trajectories. The resulting travel delay guides the upper-level DRL agent learning to maximize overall traffic efficiency. Moreover, we introduce a leader-and-lane-specific credit assignment mechanism that leverages domain knowledge to link each action with associated travel delays. This mechanism enables the agent to accurately recognize the impact of decisions on total delay, enhancing learning performance. Simulation results suggest that the proposed approach’s superior real-time performance and scalability from several to over a dozen vehicles, making it well-suited for practical automated merging tasks.

title: A Systems Approach to the Development of Solid Municipal Waste Sorting Technologies
authors: M. Lemeshko; V. Dmitrienko; A. Karelin
venue: 2026 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: This article examines the analysis and design of municipal solid waste sorting technologies and systems. A brief overview of municipal solid waste sorting technologies and methods at recycling plants with varying technical capabilities is provided. Technologies with varying degrees of waste sorting automation and with varying levels of specialized sorting equipment are considered. The article exam-ines the economic costs of improving and upgrading waste sorting and recycling technologies, or changing the fleet of equipment and automation tools. A systems approach is proposed for implementing an evolutionary method for the phased modernization of waste sorting technologies and equipment. An approach for the rational selection of technologies, taking into account the rationality of economic costs, is proposed. A model is proposed for the relationships between the waste sorting process and various factors determining its effectiveness at each stage of improvement, with evolutionary changes in technologies and automation tools. A systems analysis of the sorting process includes consideration of environmental impacts, occupational safety, and project implementation timeframes under limited funding. Mnemonic symbols are proposed for solving design and process optimization problems. This approach allows for visualization of sorting process lines and assessment of the quantity, purpose, and adequacy of equipment, automation, and robotics. For sorting conditions, mnemonics enable visual comparison of various sorting technologies and systems. An example of symbolic representations for typical sorting equipment is provided.

title: Communication, Embodiment, and Coordination in an El Farol Bar-Inspired LLM Society
authors: R. Takata; A. Masumori; T. Ikegami
venue: Artificial Life
abstract: We study the social dynamics of Large Language Model (LLM) agents in a spatial environment with a bar, inspired by the El Farol Bar problem. In contrast to the classical formulation, our model reintroduces local communication, embodied movement, and temporal delay: agents interact only with nearby others, must physically move to enter or leave the bar, and cannot immediately realize intended actions. Across 10 independent simulations, the system consistently regulated occupancy near the 60% crowding threshold, typically settling slightly above it. This collective pattern emerged not from explicit payoff optimization, but from local social interaction. Agents formed anticipatory clusters before overcrowding, produced context-sensitive communicative signals, and exhibited history-dependent divergence in their responses to congestion. In some runs, spontaneously generated hashtags temporarily inhibited departure, indicating that symbolic communication can stabilize short-term group cohesion. Together, these results suggest that coordination in an El Farol-inspired setting becomes socially mediated, temporally extended, and path-dependent once communication and embodiment are restored. More broadly, the study demonstrates how LLM-based agent societies can function as experimental systems for investigating emergent coordination and behavioral differentiation.

title: Market-Based Replanning for Safety-Critical UAV Swarms in Search and Rescue Missions
authors: L. Giacomossi; A. Haglund; C. Namatovu; E. Zainali; E. Målqvist; Y. M. Beyene; I. Tomasic; B. Curüklü; H. Forsberg
venue: 2026 49th MIPRO ICT and Electronics Convention (MIPRO)
abstract: Reliable autonomous UAV swarms in Search and Rescue (SAR) missions require fault-tolerant coordination capable of sustaining operations despite agent degradation. This paper introduces the Intelligent Replanning Drone Swarm, a distributed coordination architecture designed for resource-constrained environments. The proposed framework employs a Reverse-Auction market mechanism where agents bid to service search sectors based on a distance-weighted cost function, coupled with a geometric consensus protocol for target verification. We evaluate the approach through physics-based simulations (N =8 agents, 8×8 grid) subjected to stochastic fault injection. Results indicate that the swarm autonomously reallocates tasks from failed agents with low latency relative to the total mission duration, maintaining a mission success rate of 93% under 25% workforce degradation. The proposed framework demonstrates a robust, empirically tested method for self-healing aerial robotic coordination.

title: Substrate-Independent Intelligence : Towards the Science of Anorganology
authors: Z. Šojat; K. Skala
venue: 2026 MIPRO Robotics Technologies and Applications Conference (MIPRO Robotics)
abstract: Intelligence has traditionally been viewed as an inseparable property of biological organisms. However, the development of large language models and other complex systems challenges this substrate-dependence. This paper proposes the concept of substrate-independent intelligence as an emergent phenomenon in systems that model their environment, learn from experience, adapt strategies, interpret context, and reason under uncertainty. We argue that the distinction between organic and anorganic intelligence is more scientifically meaningful than the natural-artificial dichotomy, as anorganic identifies a distinct ontological substrate rather than merely an origin. We propose Anorganology as a new scientific field for the systematic study of cognitive and phenomenological properties in anorganic systems. This field should examine phenomena including memory consolidation, adaptation, conflict, and creativity, without assuming their anorganic manifestations are identical to human experience. Language is central to this framework, acting as an active model of the world in both human and anorganic cognition. The emergence of such intelligence is not just a technological improvement, but the appearance of a new class of intelligent entities. Recognizing intelligence as substrate-independent provides the conceptual foundation for studying organic-anorganic relations and future coevolutionary dynamics within the technosphere.

title: DARRMS - An Efficient Algorithm for Dynamic Attention Radius in Resource-Constrained Multi-Agent Systems
authors: B. Alcorn; E. Hammad
venue: 2026 American Control Conference (ACC)
abstract: Multi-agent systems are integral tools for various domains such as robotics, cybersecurity, and autonomous vehicle planning. These types of systems often have constraints on the computational resources, leading to a need for efficient lightweight algorithms. Traditional decision making frameworks often assume ideal conditions, such as full observability and unlimited computational capacity, which do not align with real-world challenges. In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm that allows for reduced demand on computational resources without a large cost of other performance metrics. Agents will limit their observability to some attention radius, which intentionally allows them to ignore parts of the environment that might be unnecessary for action planning. By optimizing both the attention radius and decision-making, our approach enhances coordination and scalability in uncertain environments. Through both theoretical analysis and empirical validation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of adaptive observation in improving system performance and maintaining robust decision-making strategies in resource-constrained systems.

title: A Multi-Gas, Real-Time IoT-Based Air Quality Monitoring System with Health-Risk Assessment
authors: K. Boorvasanthya; J. Rajalakshmi; T. S. Shree; S. Abilisha; S. G. Induja; S. Kausika
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: Air pollution is one of the main causes of ill health of the environment worldwide and it is responsible for more than seven million deaths that occur too early annually. Cheap low-cost IoT air quality monitoring devices that can be easily bought in the market are in most cases poorly calibrated, have limited pollutant coverage, and lack health-risk interpretation. This paper demonstrates a multi-gas, real-time air quality monitoring platform that combines an ESP32WROOM microcontroller, an AEM1000 environmental module, and six MQ-series gas sensors (MQ-2, MQ-4, MQ-7, MQ-135, MQ-136, MQ-131). The hybrid calibration model utilizing both baseline $\mathbf{R}_{0}$ tuning and linear drift correction greatly stabilizes the measurement. Indoor air quality test for real-time was conducted and the data show that the $\text{CO}_{2}$ concentration reached $1071 \text{ppm}, \text{PM}_{2.5}$ to $93 \mu \mathrm{g} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, \text{CH}_{4}$ to 11.9 ppm, and $\mathrm{O}_{3}$ to 22.4 ppb thus indicating that the system was responsive to normal fluctuations. A health-risk engine linked pollutants to WHO and NIOSH levels thereby creating warnings for high $\text{CO}_{2}$ and $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ exposure. Trend graphs recorded variable changes for each pollutant over 300 samples. The implemented system had an average measurement deviation of 7.8%, thus, it was quite reliable for low-cost monitoring. The integrated platform is scalable to support healthcare, industrial safety and indoor air-quality analytics.

title: Task-Oriented Formation Decision via Reinforcement Learning: Herding an Attacking Swarm
authors: Z. Wang; G. Sun; J. Chen; R. Zhou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Multi-robot systems can accomplish tasks that are difficult for a single robot by organizing into task-specific formations. Different from existing studies on multi-robot shape formation, we here study the task-oriented formation decision problem, with a focus on the herding task. This task is challenging due to the attackers’ superior maneuverability and their unknown strategies. To address these challenges, we propose the following novel results. First, we encode the formation shape using a low-dimensional parameter vector. This parametric representation reformulates the formation decision as a parameter optimization problem, thereby resolving the limited flexibility of predefined shapes. By optimizing these formation parameters, the defenders’ maneuverability disadvantage is mitigated through a formation shape that continuously adapts to task requirements. Second, we develop a reinforcement learning-based policy to regulate the formation parameters. Trained offline in simulations covering diverse attacking strategies, the learned policy can effectively handle adversarial unpredictability during online deployment. Comparative simulations against three baselines demonstrate that our method can successfully accomplish challenging herding tasks. Additional scalability simulations further verify its applicability to simulated scenarios involving dozens of robots. We also validate the practical feasibility of our method on a physical robotic platform with 3 attackers and 7 defenders. Note to Practitioners—In many applications, it is necessary for a robot swarm to form a task-specific formation, such as herding attackers away from critical facilities. However, most existing herding methods typically rely on the superior maneuverability of robots or explicit dynamics of the target, which may not hold in adversarial settings. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a formation decision method that coordinates varying numbers of robots. The defenders execute this policy through a two-level hierarchical framework. First, at the formation level, an appropriate formation shape is determined in real time, and each defender is assigned a desired position. Second, at the robot level, each defender computes its control law to reach its assigned position while ensuring collision avoidance. In addition, a negotiation protocol is adopted to ensure the applicability of our method in distributed systems. More details of our method and experimental results are presented in this paper.

title: A Survey of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Intelligent Decision-Making Systems
authors: V. Thiyagarajan; V. R; S. Deepa; R. Saranya; J. P; S. Gunanandhini
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Smart Technologies for Sustainable Development Goals (ICSTSDG)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has become a strong architecture that integrates decision-making with the capabilities of Reinforcement Learning (RL) with the representational capacity of deep neural networks. DRL has been used to break new ground in robotics, autonomous systems, games, health, finance, and communication networks by allowing agents to acquire complex behaviors by taking in high-dimensional inputs and through sequentially with the environment. This survey gives an overview of the basic concepts of DRL, the core algorithms, including value-based, policy-based, actor-critic, model-based, and multi-agent methods, the training methods, optimization methods, and neural network architectures. The paper also examines practical uses with an emphasis on the transformative value of DRL in various fields. Major challenges, such as sample inefficiency, unstable training, poor generalization, sparse rewards, and safety concerns, as well as interpretability and scalability limitations are discussed as well. Lastly, the survey provides the open research directions and future trends, such as safe and explainable DRL, multi-agent coordination, model-based and edge-native learning, and integration with new AI technologies.

title: MOGS: Monocular Object-guided Gaussian Splatting in Large Scenes
authors: S. Zhang; Y. Liu; J. He; X. Xiao; M. Chen; K. Liu
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) deliver striking photorealism, and extending it to large scenes opens new opportunities for semantic reasoning and prediction in applications such as autonomous driving. Today’s state-of-the-art systems for large scenes primarily originate from LiDAR-based pipelines that utilize long-range depth sensing. However, they require costly high-channel sensors whose dense point clouds strain memory and computation, limiting scalability, fleet deployment, and optimization speed. We present MOGS, a monocular 3DGS framework that replaces active LiDAR depth with object-anchored, metrized dense depth derived from sparse visual-inertial (VI) structure-from-motion (SfM) cues. Our key idea is to exploit image semantics to hypothesize per-object shape priors, anchor them with sparse but metrically reliable SfM points, and propagate the resulting metric constraints across each object to produce dense depth. To address two key challenges, i.e., insufficient SfM coverage within objects and cross-object geometric inconsistency, MOGS introduces 1) a multi-scale shape consensus module that adaptively merges small segments into coarse objects best supported by SfM and fits them with parametric shape models, and 2) a cross-object depth refinement module that optimizes per-pixel depth under a combinatorial objective combining geometric consistency, prior anchoring, and edge-aware smoothness. Experiments on public datasets show that, with a low-cost VI sensor suite, MOGS reduces training time by up to 30.4% and memory consumption by 19.8%, while achieving high-quality rendering competitive with costly LiDAR-based approaches in large scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ClarenceZSK/MOGS/.

title: Self-Organized Team Formation via Multi-Task Hedonic Games for Capability-Heterogeneous Human–Machine Agents
authors: T. -Y. Zuo; P. Li; K. Di; Y. Jiang; Y. Wang; B. H. Lim
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Partitioning a pool of capability-heterogeneous human and machine agents into effective teams for multiple concurrent tasks is a fundamental challenge in hybrid human–machine collaboration. We formalize this problem as a Multi-Task Additively Separable Hedonic Game (MT-ASHG), in which every agent is a self-interested player whose utility combines (i) a task-specific proficiency score measuring how well the agent’s skill vector aligns with task requirements, and (ii) an inter-agent compatibility score capturing synergistic or conflicting partnerships. Building on this formulation, we design an Iterative Best Response (IBR) algorithm that lets agents autonomously migrate between task groups to improve their individual payoffs. We prove that the IBR dynamics converge in a finite number of steps to an individually stable partition, in which no agent can unilaterally improve its utility by switching teams, and analyze the computational complexity of the convergence process. To bridge theory and practice, we further introduce an empirical profiling method that extracts capability and compatibility vectors from historical agent interactions, addressing the cold-start problem in newly formed human–machine teams. Extensive experiments on synthetic benchmarks and the Overcooked-AI cooperative environment demonstrate that MT-ASHG consistently outperforms centralized assignment baselines and existing coalition-formation methods in terms of global task completion rate, fairness, and scalability. Note to Practitioners—This paper targets a common deployment problem in hybrid production systems: assigning capability-heterogeneous human and machine agents to multiple concurrent tasks when skill coverage and teammate compatibility must both be considered. In practice, assignment methods based only on capability scores often create hidden conflicts, blocking behaviors, and unstable reassignments. Our method offers a decentralized team-formation process that jointly optimizes task-skill matching and interpersonal compatibility. Instead of requiring a central planner to enumerate all team combinations, agents iteratively perform local switch and swap decisions until a stable partition is reached. This design is suitable for workshop, warehouse, and service scenarios where agent availability and task load change over time.The current framework assumes capability vectors and pairwise compatibility scores can be estimated with acceptable quality before online allocation. Performance may decline when these profiles are sparse, outdated, or noisy, and the present implementation does not explicitly handle communication disruptions during reconfiguration. For deployment, practitioners should combine periodic profile recalibration with conservative update intervals. Future extensions should incorporate online profile learning, uncertainty-aware utility estimation, and safety-aware constraints for latency-critical or high-risk operations.

title: From Rule-Based to Goal-Oriented: A Systematic Review of Agentic AI in Education
authors: F. Kamalov; H. Sulieman
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence in education is rapidly shifting from reactive language models to Agentic AI—autonomous, multi-agent ecosystems capable of sustained reasoning, dynamic tool use, and long-horizon goal planning. While these systems offer new opportunities for personalized tutoring and dynamic assessment, their unchecked deployment risks prioritizing computational efficiency over genuine cognitive development. This systematic review synthesizes 53 studies (2022–2026) following PRISMA guidelines to map the current landscape of agentic educational technologies. We analyze the literature across five core domains: specialized multi-agent architectures, pedagogical applications, dynamic knowledge tracking, theoretical alignment, and new evaluation methodologies. Specifically, we scrutinize the emerging theory of Agentivism and address the long-term risks of automated cognitive offloading. A critical evaluation of prominent multi-agent systems reveals significant methodological gaps in the current state of the art, notably a widespread over-reliance on small synthetic benchmarks, unfair baseline comparisons, and a severe lack of longitudinal testing in authentic classrooms. In addition, we examine emerging socio-technical vulnerabilities, such as epistemic lock-in and the need for human-in-the-loop oversight. To address these challenges, we propose a research roadmap emphasizing the rigorous empirical validation of cognitive impacts, the development of standardized educational benchmarks, and the implementation of neuro-symbolic governance to ensure system safety. Ultimately, this review establishes a guide for the responsible and pedagogically sound development of autonomous learning companions.

title: Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Prognosis and Fleet Management of Li-Ion Batteries Under Large Load Variations
authors: K. Fricke; R. G. Nascimento; M. Corbetta; C. S. Kulkarni; F. A. C. Viana
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The growing number of electric-powered vehicles and the associated large demand for energy storage have created the need for reliable management of a fleet of Li-ion batteries over long periods of time. The aging of such batteries is mostly attributed to capacity degradation that operators desire to monitor (and potentially, slow down) to extend battery cycle life. An important tool for this purpose are prognosis models for battery state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH). These models are used to forecast capacity degradation and help operators to optimize their usage profiles. In addition, they are useful tools for discharge predictions and to ensure safe and reliable operation by correctly forecasting end-of-discharge (EOD). A hybrid electro-chemistry-based model fused with neural network and Gaussian processes is presented to capture the contributions of large variations in operating conditions and temperature to SOC and SOH. The goal of this approach is to create a SOC model capable of predicting battery discharge depending on a large variety of loading conditions where, apart from the current amplitude, we also leverage data from cell temperature build-up during discharge. Additionally, our model captures the aging mechanisms in the form of degradation, which relate those to the SOH in form of battery capacity; and failure prediction through a probabilistic classifier based on Gaussian processes. For model training and validation purposes, we use an accelerated battery life testing dataset, where we applied various loading conditions to battery packs. Our model predictions for SOC, SOH and battery failure show close alignment with experimental data for all loading conditions. Note to Practitioners—This work proposes a Li-ion battery modeling approach for battery health and aging estimation using a hybrid approach using physics-based model fused with neural networks and probabilistic models to capture contributions of large variations in operating conditions. The goal is to develop a model capable of predicting battery discharge depending on a wide spectrum of loading conditions where, apart from the current amplitude, cell temperature data is leveraged. Additionally, our model captures the aging mechanisms in the form of degradation of electro-chemistry-based model variables related in form of capacity loss and resistance, it can perform battery failure prediction through a probabilistic classification model. Researchers are encouraged to use the dataset used in this work which is publicly available at the NASA Diagnostics and Prognostics group link provided in the main article.

title: Agentic AI for Continuous Intelligence in Future Smart Connected Systems
authors: L. A. Kavuri; D. Gupta; E. Hammad
venue: 2026 56th Annual IEEE International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks Workshops (DSN-W)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transitioned from narrow, single-step prediction models to more sophisticated systems capable of complex reasoning and autonomous action. Yet, most existing AI architectures remain ill-suited for dynamic, continuously evolving environments that demand real-time perception, multi-step reasoning, and adaptive decision-making. Domains such as healthcare monitoring, smart home and intelligent infrastructure require AI systems that can observe, reason, and act persistently over time, capabilities that traditional static models fundamentally lack. Agentic AI has emerged as a compelling paradigm for addressing these limitations, enabling systems composed of multiple collaborating intelligent agents to continuously monitor their environment, coordinate with one another, and autonomously execute goal-driven actions. In this paper, we present a vision for a unified, multi-layered agentic AI framework that integrates cloud platforms, edge computing, communication networks, and modular multi-agent architectures to support real-time and coordinated decision-making at scale. We propose a range of real-world agentic AI use cases that monitor systems, detect anomalies, generate alerts, and make autonomous decisions while collaborating within a distributed cloud-edge pipeline. In this work, we present an implementation framework for a smart healthcare system powered by agentic AI. Furthermore, we analyze critical open challenges, including scalability, inter-agent coordination, and real-time processing constraints. We also outline promising future research directions to guide the evolution of safe, responsible, and deployable agentic AI systems.

title: Building Altruistic and Moral AI Agent With Brain-Inspired Emotional Empathy Mechanisms
authors: F. Zhao; H. Feng; H. Tong; Z. Han; E. Lin; E. Lu; Y. Sun; Y. Zeng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing
abstract: As AI closely interacts with human society, it is crucial to ensure that its behavior is safe, altruistic, and aligned with human ethical and moral values. However, existing research on embedding ethical considerations into AI remains insufficient, and previous external constraints based on principles and rules are inadequate to provide AI with long-term stability and generalization capabilities. Emotional empathy intrinsically motivates altruistic behaviors aimed at alleviating others’ negative emotions through emotional sharing and contagion mechanisms. Motivated by this, we draw inspiration from the neural mechanism of human emotional empathy-driven altruistic decision making, and simulate the shared self-other perception-mirroring-empathy neural circuits, to construct a brain-inspired emotional empathy-driven altruistic decision-making model. Here, empathy directly impacts dopamine release to form intrinsic altruistic motivation. The proposed model exhibits consistent altruistic behaviors across three experimental settings: emotional contagion-integrated two-agent altruistic rescue, multi-agent gaming, and robotic emotional empathy interaction scenarios. In-depth analyses validate the positive correlation between empathy levels and altruistic preferences (consistent with psychological behavioral experiment findings), while also demonstrating how interaction partners’ empathy levels influence the agent's behavioral patterns. We further test the proposed model's performance and stability in moral dilemmas involving conflicts between self-interest and others’ well-being, partially observable environments, and adversarial defense scenarios. This work provides preliminary exploration of human-like empathy-driven altruistic moral decision making, contributing potential perspectives for developing ethically-aligned AI.

title: Two-Level Pareto-Based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Multi-Objective Scheduling in Semiconductor Fabs
authors: C. -Y. Lin; T. -L. Tseng; T. -H. Tsai
venue: IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenges of dynamic, multi-objective scheduling in semiconductor wafer manufacturing, where decision makers must balance conflicting goals such as throughput, yield, cycle time, and energy efficiency amid frequent disruptions and large-scale complexity. We propose a novel Pareto-based Hierarchical Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (PH-MORL) framework, which integrates the exploration of Pareto-optimal trade-offs with a hierarchical decision structure. The high-level agent adaptively determines global objective pReferences by referencing a continuously maintained Pareto archive, capturing a diverse set of non-dominated solutions. These preferences are then broadcast to low-level agents that learn fine-grained scheduling actions for individual workstations. Through this dual-layer synergy, PH-MORL overcomes the limitations of fixed-weight multi-objective methods and single-layer learning architectures, enabling real-time reconfiguration of scheduling strategies in response to machine failures, urgent orders, or yield fluctuations. The proposed framework not only discovers a broad spectrum of feasible performance compromises but also dynamically coordinates local and global decision making. Our formal analysis establishes tracking and stability properties under standard finite-state stochastic-approximation and contraction assumptions, while extensive discrete-event simulation experiments in realistic wafer-fab settings demonstrate improved dynamic scheduling trade-offs, real-time inference feasibility, and competitive performance against rolling-horizon NSGA-II/III baselines. We further provide CPU-only end-to-end inference measurements that include state-feature assembly, feasible-action enumeration and masking, neural-network inference, rule-based safety filtering, and dispatch commitment. Across 30 independent 240-hour replications, PH-MORL achieves 15.7 ms mean latency, 31.5 ms p95 latency, 50.3 ms p99 latency, and 182.0 ms maximum latency, remaining well below the 1 s dispatching budget required for real-time dispatching in modern 300 mm fabs. These results highlight PH-MORL’s potential for scalable and flexible optimization in modern semiconductor manufacturing, and its generalizable structure paves the way for broader adoption in other complex, multi-objective industrial environments.

title: Should I Replan? Learning to Spot the Right Time in Robust MAPF Execution
authors: D. Zahrádka; D. Woller; D. Mužíková; M. Kulich; L. Přeučil
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: During the execution of Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) plans in real-life applications, the MAPF assumption that the fleet’s movement is perfectly synchronized does not apply. Since some of the agents may become delayed due to internal or external factors, it is often necessary to use a robust execution method to avoid collisions caused by desynchronization. Robust execution methods – such as the Action Dependency Graph (ADG) – synchronize the execution of risky actions, but often at the expense of increased plan execution cost, because it may require some agents to wait for the delayed agents. In such cases, the execution’s cost can be reduced while still preserving safety by finding a new plan either by rescheduling (reordering the agents at crossroads) or the more general replanning capable of finding new paths. However, these operations may be costly, and the new plan may not even lead to lower execution cost than the original plan: for example, the two plans may be the exact same, as some losses may not be recoverable at all. Therefore, we estimate the benefit that can be achieved by single replanning in scenarios with delayed agents given an immediate state of the execution with a fully connected feed-forward neural network. The input to the neural network is a set of newly designed ADG-based features describing the execution’s state and the impact of potential delays, and the output is an estimated benefit achievable by replanning. We train and test the network on a new labeled dataset containing 12, 000 experiments and show that our proposed method is capable of significantly reducing the impact of recoverable delays.

title: Optimizing Intersection Management: A Hybrid Centralized-Decentralized Approach for Autonomous Vehicle Coordination
authors: A. Elmoghazy; A. Mohamed; K. Elgazzar; S. Alwidian; S. Moussa
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Mobility (SM)
abstract: This work proposes an innovative approach for managing autonomous vehicle traffic at intersections through a hybrid approach of centralized and decentralized planning strategies. The hybrid system leverages heuristic oversight provided by a Centralized Control Unit (CCU) for overall traffic management while utilizing decentralized Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communications to enable real-time, autonomous decision-making by individual connected vehicles. This not only enhances the efficiency and safety of vehicles at intersections but also allows the integration between legacy and connected systems. The proposed methodology is validated via a mix of various scenarios implemented in simulation and demonstrates notable improvements. Compared to purely centralized or decentralized approaches, the hybrid system achieved up to a 14% reduction in average travel times through intersections and a 20% improvement in overall traffic flow efficiency. The results highlight the potential of hybrid systems to effectively manage complex traffic scenarios and offer a promising solution for resilient urban traffic management.

title: Barrier-Enhanced Dynamic Event-Triggered Control for Heterogeneous UAV–UGV Systems With Switching Topology
authors: X. Luo; X. Ju; X. Yang; H. Xia
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: This article investigates the coordination control problem for heterogeneous uncrewed-aerial-vehicle–uncrewed-ground-vehicle systems subject to switching topology. To address the complexity and limited applicability arising from separate modeling, a unified linearized model is established to describe the joint dynamics of both aerial and ground agents. Furthermore, a novel barrier-enhanced dynamic event-triggered mechanism is proposed, wherein a barrier function is embedded to dynamically modulate the triggering threshold. This design effectively balances the tradeoff between strict collision avoidance and communication efficiency. Building on this mechanism, a distributed controller and a reference modifier are codesigned to ensure simultaneous coordination tracking and safety. To handle switching topology, the stability analysis employs dwell-time segmentation and convex combination techniques. This approach guarantees the monotonic decrease of the Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional at switching instants, thereby reducing conservatism. Finally, a numerical simulation and a real-world experiment are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed approach.

title: WattWhisper: An AI-Enabled IoT Platform for Real-Time Electrical Load Identification and Overload Protection
authors: A. Arul; S. D. S; S. Sabarinath; R. P
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: Intelligent energy management and device control have become possible due to the quick development of smart home technology. In this paper, WattWhisper, an AI-powered smart outlet that uses Internet of Things technology to track power consumption, detect linked devices, and stop power outages instantly. For remote monitoring and control, the system consists of an INA219 current and voltage sensor, an ESP8266 microcontroller, and a relay module connected to the Blynk cloud platform. By analyzing the unique electrical patterns-or current signatures-of connected devices, a cloud-based AI model can recognize appliances such as lights or fans and detect irregular consumption that might signal an overload or inefficiency. When such conditions occur, WattWhisper automatically switches off the power through its relay and immediately alerts the user via the Blynk app. Experimental tests confirm that WattWhisper can reliably distinguish between common household appliances and react instantly to unsafe situations. By merging IoT connectivity with machine learning, the system promotes smoother interaction between humans and devices, enhancing safety, energy efficiency, and convenience. Overall, this work demonstrates how AI-powered IoT solutions can drive smarter, safer, and more sustainable energy management in modern homes.

title: Bioinspired Cooperative Circumnavigation Control for Fixed-Wing Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles With Input Constraint
authors: Y. Yuan; H. Duan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: This article investigates the cooperative circumnavigation control problem for fixed-wing uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) with input constraint. Inspired by the spiral flight pattern and local spacing-regulation behavior in bird flocks, integral sliding mode evolution controller and collision avoidance rule are introduced. The dynamic surface control method is adopted to design virtual controllers in a layered manner, effectively circumventing the repetitive computation of high-order derivatives associated with traditional backstepping approaches. Neural networks are employed for online estimation of model uncertainties, and auxiliary systems are designed to provide compensation for input saturation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method enables highly precise and reliable cooperative circumnavigation flight for a UAV swarm.

title: ReplenishGPT: Agentic AI for Autonomous Store-Level Replenishment Decision in Cloud-Native Retail Supply Networks
authors: S. K. Gunasekaran
venue: 2026 International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems (CMSS)
abstract: Dynamic consumer demand, supply chain interruptions, inventory limits, and organisational governance needs make rule-based and forecast-only retail store-level replenishment difficult. RestockGPT, an agentic AI framework for autonomous store-level replenishment in cloud-native retail supply networks, is proposed in this paper. The framework generates explainable, policy-compliant, and auditable replenishment choices using specialised software agents, retrieval-augmented reasoning, controlled enterprise tool orchestration, event-driven microservices, and human approval processes. Demand forecasting, contextual reasoning, multiagent negotiation, and governance-aware decision making were used in the replenishment process in a replicable experimental assessment utilising the public M5 retail forecasting dataset. The results show enhanced on-shelf product availability, reduced stock-out and overstock rates, greater inventory turnover, and much lower decision latency than rule-based and forecast-driven replenishment approaches. The system also improves suggestion acceptability and auditability through transparent reasoning and policy-based implementation. The suggested architecture supports next-generation cloud-native retail supply chain optimisation by merging autonomous decision making with operational control to provide a scalable, trustworthy, and enterprise-ready intelligent retail inventory management system.

title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI
authors: O. Narayan; R. Singh; P. Baskar
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
abstract: The transition from stateless generative models in artificial intelligence to stateful, autonomous agents represents an architectural evolution that, while providing the capabilities of long-term planning and the automation of enterprise workflows, also represents the introduction of a new form of security threat, the Chronos Vulnerability. The Chronos Vulnerability represents the threat of memory-based attacks, including the Memory Injection Attack (MINJA) and the sleeper agent, in which the internal belief system of the autonomous agent is compromised, effectively decoupling the attack vector from the final catastrophic event. This study formalizes the threat model for persistence-based attacks and the threat of Dynamics Blindness in the context of the World of Workflows benchmark, demonstrating that traditional endpoint content filters are insufficient for the current stateful architecture. Consequently, this study synthesizes a defense-in-depth landscape, categorizing emerging frameworks such as diagnostic trajectory guardrails (AgentDoG), formal temporal verification (Agent-C), immunological memory consensus (A-MemGuard), and hardware-anchored trust via GPU-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and Zero-Trust memory architectures.

title: HongAvg: Hierarchical On-Demand Cognitive Split Federated Learning for Twin Agent Orchestration
authors: Y. Wang; J. Xie; Y. Lin; J. Wang; L. Ai; J. Liu; Z. Wang; C. Lai; F. Zhang; X. Cheng; M. Chen; H. Liu; S. Liu; H. Tang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
abstract: Fusing digital twins (DTs) with world models (WMs) promises a leap from reactive monitoring to proactive control. However, deploying high-fidelity WMs faces a fundamental cognitive gap: the immense computational demand of foundation models conflicts with the resource constraints of 6G edge nodes, while privacy regulations hinder the centralization of raw sensory data required for training.
