To bridge this gap, this paper presents HongAvg, a hierarchical on-demand cognitive split federated learning framework designed as cognitive infrastructure for next-generation DTs. By establishing a national-basin-edge three-tier architecture, HongAvg introduces foundation models to resource-constrained edges via split computing, offloading heavy cognitive reasoning while preserving data privacy. We propose a dual-stream semantic consistency mechanism to align edge interactions with the foundation model's cognition, ensuring that distributed cognitive primitives serve as valid inputs for global state estimation. Validated on a heterogeneous benchmark, HongAvg serves as a prototype for industrial cognitive computing, improving accuracy in visual monitoring by up to 8.9% and reducing edge memory usage by approximately 75%. This work provides the scalable architectural prerequisite necessary for evolving static DTs into proactive WM-driven multi-agent orchestrated intelligent systems.

title: Quantized-Observer-Based Event-Triggered Secure Consensus for NMASs Under DoS Attacks
authors: D. Yao; Y. Wang; H. Wei; Y. Shi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: In order to study the safety control of linear cyber-physical systems, under constrained network communication burden, this article conducts research on the event-triggered cooperative stabilization problem of networked multiagent systems (NMASs) with unavailable states and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. First, we construct a state observer to estimate unavailable internal system state. Second, a quantization control policy is proposed between the encoder and the decoder for reducing the data transmission. Third, we develop an event-triggered mechanism (ETM) with quantized state estimation to cut down the occupation of network communication bandwidth. To make up for the influence of DoS attacks launched between the observer and the controller channel, we establish an event-triggered hybrid controller based on quantized state observer to carry out secure consensus of NMASs, and deduce the secure consensus conditions via multiple Lyapunov functions. Moreover, the Zeno behavior is effectually eliminated due to the fact that each network node has a lower positive bound. In the end, the effectiveness of the developed safety control strategy via quantized observer is revealed through an example.

title: Fixed-Time Fault-Tolerant Consensus of MASs Against Power Faults via Multi-Signal Quantization and Fuzzy Graph With Application to DC Microgrid
authors: Y. Yang; Q. Shen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The practical fixed-time quantized fault-tolerant control of multi-agent systems (MASs) under power faults and fuzzy graph is addressed in this article. Firstly, a state-dependent fuzzy graph is introduced to describe information exchange between agents. Specifically, the topology weight is considered as an unknown state-dependent function, which is more practical than the common fixed topology. Secondly, the novel actuator and sensor power faults are proposed in this paper. Unlike gain and bias faults, power faults cause the input powers of sensors and actuators to become unknown time-varying functions. The impact of power faults is handled by designing compensation signals. In addition, the state constraints are realized by conducting coordinate transformations, thereby ensuring the system’s safety. To reduce resource depletion, this article employs a quantizer to quantize all states and inputs, and designs the needed controller based on the discontinuous quantized states. The relationship between quantized signals and unquantized signals is established to compensate for the discontinuity caused by quantization. Under the developed quantized controller, the boundedness of all closed-loop signals and the practical fixed-time stability of the system can be guaranteed. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed control strategy is validated by simulating an actual circuit system. Note to Practitioners—In practical applications, many industrial systems can be modeled as MASs, making the distributed research of MASs hold significant industrial value. Considering the complexity of the system’s actual operating environment, the information exchange between agents may become uncertain. A state-dependent fuzzy graph is introduced in to describe the network topology. After prolonged operation, the system’s internal structure may change in unanticipated ways. Therefore, new sensor and actuator power faults are proposed to ensure the control result better align with reality. In addition, reducing resource consumption is also a critical metric in industrial production. To reduce the frequency of parameter updates, a quantizer is introduced to quantize all subsystem states and inputs, thereby designing a suitable quantized control scheme. The presented control scheme holds broad research significance and application prospects in the field of intelligent manufacturing.

title: The AGI-Powered Metaverse: A Decentralized Task-Based Cognitive Architecture
authors: A. Nechesov; J. Ruponen
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: The pursuit of Strong Artificial Intelligence (AGI) is hindered by the fundamental limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs), such as hallucinations, static knowledge, and a lack of verifiable reasoning. This paper proposes a hybrid, decentralized cognitive architecture for an AGI-powered Metaverse that addresses these challenges. The framework with Task-Based Cognitive Architecture (TBCA) establishes a closed cognitive loop integrating three core components: an LLM for creative hypothesis generation (“System 1”), a symbolic logic engine for rigorous verification (“System 2”), and a decentralized multi-blockchain knowledge base serving as a secure long-term memory for collective intelligence. We demonstrate within a simulated Metaverse environment that this architecture supports cumulative learning and solves complex tasks, such as legal reasoning, which are intractable for isolated LLMs. The key innovations include a probabilistic knowledge hierarchy for explainable reasoning and a multi-blockchain structure that ensures tamper-proof knowledge sharing among multiple AI agents. This approach provides a foundational framework for verifiable and cumulative learning in dynamic multi-agent environments, paving the way for transparent, robust, and continuously evolving AI systems within the Metaverse.

title: Distributed Control Lyapunov and Control Barrier Certificates for Reactive Formation
authors: D. Liu; M. Li; W. Fang; L. Zhu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control
abstract: In this article, we study reactive formation control for multirobot systems, where robots maintain safety while achieving formation objectives. In complex environments, preserving formation shape often conflicts with safety requirements. Therefore, we allow temporary formation deviations to avoid hazards (e.g., obstacles) and automatic recovery afterward. To address this, we propose a distributed control Lyapunov function–control barrier function (CLF-CBF)-based quadratic program controller, where formation goals are encoded as distributed CLF conditions and safety constraints as CBF conditions. Sufficient distributed CLF and CBF conditions are derived to guarantee controller feasibility, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation studies.

title: Resilient Coordination of Swarm Systems Against Cyberattacks: A Delay Feedback and Global Optimization Framework
authors: C. Wei; H. Fan; Y. -H. Chen; T. Chai
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
abstract: This article investigates the resilient coordination problem for swarm systems under cyberattacks, with particular emphasis on challenges induced by information feedback delays. Each agent in the swarm is modeled as an Euler–Lagrange system. A novel constraint-following-based resilient coordination framework is developed, which unifies constraint modeling, resilient coordination, and delay compensation under cyberattacks. Specifically, collision avoidance and formation maintenance are systematically formulated as ideal constraints and transformed into an equivalent constraint-following control problem, providing a unified systems-level framework for coordinated swarm operation. To explicitly compensate for delayed information, a delayed feedback control mechanism is designed, ensuring uniform boundedness and uniform ultimate boundedness of the closed-loop system. Furthermore, a global optimization scheme is embedded into the proposed framework to enhance control performance and robustness. Simulation results on four-vehicle, eight-vehicle, and multiquadrotor formation scenarios validate the effectiveness, scalability, and practical applicability of the proposed approach. In particular, quantitative comparisons with the preoptimization case demonstrate that the proposed global optimization scheme achieves at least 11.94%, 11.95%, and 13.78% reductions in accumulated collision-avoidance errors, formation errors, and control effort, respectively.

title: Automatic Alignment Control Strategy for GIL Flanges Based on Laser-Vision Fusion
authors: Y. Zhou; X. Xu; Y. Li; Z. Shen
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Manufacturing and Automation (IMA)
abstract: To address the efficiency and safety challenges of manual Gas-Insulated Line (GIL) flange assembly in confined spaces, particularly under strong optical interference, this paper proposes a robust automatic alignment control strategy utilizing a hierarchical laser-vision fusion framework. First, a geometric constraint-based laser algorithm is employed for coarse alignment to overcome Field-of-View (FOV) limitations caused by large initial deviations. Subsequently, an anti-interference visual servoing method integrates adaptive morphological filtering with least-squares circle fitting to achieve robust, high-precision pose estimation despite metal reflections. A hierarchical state machine ensures smooth switching between coarse and fine control modes. Experiments on $300-\text{kg}$ pipe sections demonstrate that the system achieves an alignment error within 0.5 mm, a success rate exceeding 95%, and an average docking time of 10 seconds. This multi-agent collaborative approach offers a robust solution for intelligent power facility construction.

title: Obstacle Avoidance-Driven Formation Scaling Maneuver Based on Distributed Optimization
authors: G. Li; X. Wang; G. Wang; D. Zhang; J. Lü
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article investigates a novel distributed optimization-based method of formation scaling maneuver control with obstacle avoidance. The agents track the formation center in a geometric configuration and perform collective scaling maneuvers to avoid convex obstacles. To handle such a problem, we propose a method consisting of a bearing controller and a distributed optimizer. Combined with the bearing controller, not only does the optimizer under consensus constraint controls the generation of the expected geometric configuration, but it also maneuvers the scale of the configuration to avoid convex obstacles by optimizing a specialized cost function. In particular, the optimizer adopts an adaptive dynamic average consensus observer to estimate the summation of the local gradients, partial derivatives, and Hessian matrices. A simulation is conducted to distinguish the proposed method from existing obstacle-avoiding formation controllers. An experiment on unmanned ground vehicles is performed to verify the practicability of the proposed method.

title: Editorial: Advancing Innovation Ecosystem Research: Measurement Dynamics and Contextual Intelligence
authors: D. Cetindamar; M. Bliemel; N. Acur; A. Ates; A. McNabola
venue: IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management
abstract: This integrative editorial introduces the Special Issue (SI) on the evaluation of innovation ecosystem (IE) performance. While ecosystem perspectives have gained prominence across innovation, entrepreneurship, and strategy research, the systematic measurement of ecosystem performance remains theoretically fragmented and methodologically underdeveloped. Drawing on 11 SI articles, this editorial provides an integrative synthesis that advances understanding of how ecosystem performance can be conceptualized, operationalized, and evaluated across dynamic and contextual settings. We aim to identify cross-cutting patterns, unresolved challenges, and emerging research trajectories by synthesizing the SI papers. The article concludes with suggestions for future research aimed at fostering a richer conceptualization of IE performance.

title: Distributed Battery Prognostics via Quantized Edge Encoding and Cloud-Based Feature Decoding
authors: L. Manoj; P. Wang
venue: 2026 Annual Reliability and Maintainability Symposium (RAMS)
abstract: SUMMARY & CONCLUSIONSBattery health management is a critical component in ensuring the safety, longevity, and performance of electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems. Traditional Battery Management Systems (BMS) face limitations in onboard computing, memory, and communication bandwidth, making them suboptimal for high-resolution diagnostics or fleet-scale analytics. To address these constraints, we propose a distributed battery prognostics framework that leverages quantized edge inference and cloud-based refinement. The edge device performs real-time feature extraction and transmits compact 8-bit vectors to the cloud, where a learned Feature-Aware Decoder (FAD) reconstructs full-precision representations for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction and fault diagnosis.We evaluate multiple decoder architectures and find that Mamba-based decoders provide the best trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Our results show that the FAD can recover nearly all of the performance lost through quantization, reducing RUL prediction error by up to 20% compared to fixed inverse-scaling baselines. The system achieves over 75% reduction in transmission bandwidth while maintaining high predictive accuracy, enabling scalable, secure, privacy-preserving, and energy-efficient health monitoring across edge– cloud environments. This work provides a deployable architecture that advances the practicality of cloud-integrated BMS for modern EV and IoT applications.

title: Agentic Cybersecurity: Autonomous Threat Detection Defense Against Adversarial Metamorphic Malware Attacks
authors: V. M. González-Gorrín; J. Prieto-Blázquez
venue: 2026 International Symposium on Networks, Computers and Communications (ISNCC)
abstract: Adversarial malware evolves faster than traditional defenses can adapt. With the average breach costing $4.88 million in 2024 [1] and metamorphic malware exceeding 95% mutation rates, organizations need new approaches to detection and response. This paper presents a framework for applying agentic AI to security operations, introducing a multi-agent architecture for metamorphic malware detection that reaches 94.2% accuracy on known families against 8.7% recall for signaturebased systems. We report a pilot on 2,847 samples across five families, and a leave-one-family-out evaluation in which recall falls to 76.2% on unseen families-a bound we state explicitly, since the higher figure does not characterise performance against novel threats. Our implementation uses the ReAct paradigm with cryptographically secured agent communication (Ed25519 signatures, AES-256-GCM encryption). Grounded in Markov Decision Processes, we discuss practical deployment of agentic AI in enterprise security. Industry benchmarks report 80-87% response-time improvements; our framework has not yet been validated in a production SOC.

title: ARIA: An Agentic Release Intelligence Architecture for Autonomous End-to-End Mobile DevOps - From Build Prediction to Incident Resolution
authors: S. Gudimetla; S. Gangula; R. Adinarayana; C. Challa; S. Vunnam; S. Buhyavarapu
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Systems, and Emerging Technologies (ICAISET)
abstract: Enterprise mobile delivery pipelines remain fragmented: build, CI, release, deployment, and incident response operate as disconnected stages, with post-deployment learning rarely propagating upstream. We present ARIA (Agentic Release Intelligence Architecture), a multi-agent architecture whose central contribution is the ARIA Feedback Protocol (AFP)—a confidence-gated, time-decayed mechanism providing two complementary benefit pathways: (i) per-incident observability acceleration that enriches diagnosis context for every incident, and (ii) multi-incident feedback accumulation that improves upstream test selection over time. ARIA coordinates five specialized agents through a shared provenance substrate and a graduated autonomy model whose governance components are mapped to NIST AI Risk Management Framework practices. A controlled simulation study parameterized from the public CI/CD histories of Signal Android, Firefox for Android (Fenix), and Wikipedia Android reports baseline, ablation, and sensitivity analyses over 30 stochastic replications. The per-incident mechanism yields a statistically significant MTTR reduction from 51.0 to 44.6 minutes (−12.6%, p<0.001, d=0.86) and governance improvement from 8.3 to 9.1 (+10.1%, p<0.001, d=1.30). The multi-incident mechanism (DDR +1.0%, RIR −5.8%) shows favorable trends; a post-hoc power analysis determines that ≈670 observations (≈22 applications) are needed for 80% statistical power, providing a concrete sample-size target for future production studies. An offline replay against 30 held-out CI failure events yields 83.3% prediction accuracy (vs. 60.0% baseline), supporting simulation fidelity.

title: Integrated Deep Reinforcement Learning Agent Approach for Multi-Lane Cooperative Variable Speed Limit Control
authors: D. Xiao; Y. Wang; L. Xing; Z. Han; T. Li; C. Wang; S. Chen
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Given the advancements in intelligent highway management systems and connected and autonomous vehicles, precise traffic flow control via highway gantries has become feasible. Bottleneck zones caused by construction or accidents, as a primary source of highway congestion and crashes, have emerged as a key focus in proactive traffic flow management. To address the issue of conflicting gantry decisions in the context of sparse gantries, multi-lane highways, and mixed traffic flows within bottleneck zones, a coordinated speed limit control model utilizing the gantry system is proposed. This model aims to enhance safety and efficiency while maintaining energy consumption levels. Building upon this coordinated control framework, an improved neural network-based Proximal Policy Optimization integrated-agent algorithm is introduced for centralized training and decision-making. The algorithm incorporates elite experience replay, enhanced exploration, entropy regularization, and gradient clipping to improve deep reinforcement learning performance and avoid local optima. Finally, simulation via SUMO and PyTorch demonstrates that the proposed control strategy improves safety metrics by 11.6%, increases space-mean speed by 6.7%, and achieves a 1.02% reduction in energy consumption compared to real-world control strategies. The effectiveness of the proposed coordinated speed limit control model and the integrated-agent training and decision-making framework is validated against traditional models and multi-agent distributed control approaches.

title: Dynamic Spectrum Aggregation and Access for Rescue Cognitive Networks Using Multi-Agent Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning
authors: W. Zhang; W. Ding; C. -X. Wang; Y. Chen; G. T. F. d. Abreu; Z. Liu; J. Sun; Z. Han
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) based emergency communication is gaining more attention for disaster rescue, where the UAV can work as an aerial base station to provide spectrum access in areas with power outages or network interruptions. However, UAVs can only provide limited spectrum access for a short period of time due to limited battery energy. Aiming to providing spectrum access to more users under spectrum and energy limitations, a new dynamic spectrum aggregation and access scheme is proposed for rescue cognitive networks (RCNs), in which different kinds of users are modeled as primary users (PUs) and secondary users (SUs). In each time slot, SUs with different spectrum sensing capabilities, spectrum aggregation capabilities, and bandwidth demands need to sense and aggregate multiple spectrum slots that are not occupied by PUs for data transmission. Based on selected channel states, the reward is designed as a function of transmission rates and is fed back to SUs. A maximum entropy based multi-agent actor-critic (ME-MAAC) algorithm is proposed to optimize the action selection policy for SUs. Simulation results show that the proposed ME-MAAC algorithm can effectively achieve higher achievable rate, lower mean collision rate and lower power consumption, than state-of-the-art methods based on Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm. The proposed RCNs provide a novel spectrum usage paradigm for emergency communication and rescue networks.

title: High-Precision UAV Swarm Control: Evaluating Fractional-Order Methods for Close-Proximity Operations
authors: G. E. M. Abro; J. M. Alsayegh; H. Mustafa
venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Industrial Electronics
abstract: Maintaining stable close-proximity flight in multirotor swarms is challenging because of complex aerodynamic interactions, particularly the downwash effects from higher to lower vehicles. Many conventional managers neglect these interactions, resulting in excessively high safety distances. This complicates the swarm's capacity to construct and manoeuvre additional multiagent. This study rigorously evaluates fractional-order PID with fractional-order linear quadratic regulator (FOLQR), and integral state-feedback control—to identify the most stable and precise method for managing clusters of proximate uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). Our approach integrates a straightforward dynamics model with robust control mechanisms to ensure accurate stabilization of high-order multivehicle interactions. The FOLQR controller reduces maximum altitude tracking error by four times compared to the typical nonlinear tracking controller, according to experiments. We additionally evaluate our approach in practical settings to ensure its efficacy with larger swarms. This ensures its use on a broader scale and in practical settings. These findings demonstrate the efficacy and utility of fractional-order control in multirotor swarm coordination, offering a more stable and precise method for aerial robot control. The proposed architecture facilitates denser, safer, and more efficient utilization of UAV swarms for urban air mobility, self-inspection, and formation flying.

title: MAC and Routing Protocols Design in Multi-Hop Terahertz Networks
authors: S. Cavallero; L. M. Amorosa; G. Cuozzo; A. Pumilia; C. Buratti
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Communication at Terahertz (THz) frequencies is strongly affected by high path loss and blockage, making multi-hop strategies essential, especially in obstacle-dense scenarios such as Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. We propose a joint Medium Access Control (MAC) and Network (NET) layer design, centered on a distributed Table-Based (TB) routing protocol that removes control-plane signaling by leveraging only user-plane data transmissions for route discovery and maintenance. The MAC layer employs a simple contention-based unslotted Aloha protocol, whose fully distributed nature makes it well-suited to THz IIoT multi-hop networks while avoiding the overhead of more complex contention-free schemes. The performance of TB is evaluated against two well-established NET-layer benchmarks: a Table-Less (TL) broadcast-forwarding scheme and the reactive Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) protocol. Results show that AODV suffers from fairness degradation due to high control overhead and asynchronous route discovery, while TL can achieve higher throughput under congestion, but incurs higher latency due to suboptimal path selection. Overall, TB provides the best trade-off between fairness, throughput and latency. To further minimize the necessity of hyperparameter tuning, we also extend TB with a decentralized Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) mechanism that enables autonomous MAC-layer parameter adaptation. Simulations in a realistic IIoT scenario demonstrate that MADRL-TB delivers competitive performance compared to optimal static configurations while ensuring high robustness against parameter variations.

title: Graph Neural Network with Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Joint V2V Resource Allocation for String Stability in Dynamic Platoons
authors: A. Bari; P. S; S. Srinath; B. Akhil; D. M
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Computational Networks (ICISCN)
abstract: Vehicular platooning needs reliable communication and effective allocation of resources to maintain string stability and safety in dynamic networks. Current techniques such as static Maximum Allowable Transmission Interval (MATI), results in time-domain wireless resource allocation process which leads to communication delay, and deterioration in dynamic channels. In this paper, we introduce a Graph Neural Network with Deep Reinforcement Learning (GNN-DRL) framework for joint resource allocation which overcomes these issues by modeling interactions among vehicles through graph and optimizing parameters such as transmit power, bandwidth, and transmission rates. The unique closed-loop approach embeds frequency-domain string stability into a time-domain DRL reward function, prioritizing physical safety over communication performance. The GNN-DRL framework helps to improve adaptability in decision-making process, minimize delays and improve reliability depending on traffic and channel conditions. According to experimental results, the proposed approach performs better in terms of the fairness index (0.935), minimized outage probability (0.082), increased stability margin (0.947), and minimized average delay (18.6 ms).

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Exploration in UAVs
authors: O. Elbagory; E. Uslu
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Recent Advances in Air and Space Technologies (RAST)
abstract: Recent advances in autonomous systems have accelerated the deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for unknown-environment exploration and search-and-rescue missions. Despite sustained progress in this domain, many existing algorithms rely on computationally intensive predefined heuristics, which often require global map knowledge and introduce single points of failure. This paper offers a Reinforcement Learning (RL) approach capable of exploring environments without intensive computations and prior knowledge of the environment. For implementation, the system was designed on the Q-Learning algorithm utilizing discrete states and a policy dependent on local Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) and Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU) sensor data. The experiment was carried out using a combination of a Python virtual environment for training and the Robot Operating System (ROS2) Humble, and Gazebo Harmonic stack for testing to be in line with the industry standard at the time of the paper. Results showed the Q-Learning agent was able to provide comparable results to traditional exploration baselines, with Q-Learning standing at a map coverage ratio of 92.4% and a collision rate of 7.5%. This provides us with a lightweight, resource efficient baseline suitable for resource constrained environments that is a potentially decentralized solution for environmental exploration, and providing a foundation for future multi-UAV reinforcement learning work.

title: Swarm Exploration and Navigation of Uncertain Environments Utilizing Affine-Transformation-Based Elliptical Virtual Navigation Region
authors: L. Wu; H. Duan; C. Wei; B. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: This article addresses swarm exploration and navigation in uncertain environments by utilizing an affine-transformation-based elliptical virtual navigation region. The framework comprises three key techniques: (1) a tight elliptical formation strategy that dynamically adjusts the swarm shape based on environmental constraints and group size, reducing energy consumption through the 2-opt algorithm, which optimizes the assignment sequence of agents to virtual navigation points on the elliptical formation by minimizing the total Euclidean path length; (2) a virtual navigation region generation method leveraging uncertain target information to enhance multipath exploration; and (3) an obstacle avoidance approach that tracks obstacles as dynamic trajectories and employs a constrained nonlinear receding-horizon predictor for safe navigation in dynamic environments. The proposed solution significantly improves formation compactness, efficiency, and safety, particularly in narrow corridors and dynamic scenarios.

title: Donato: An AI-Driven Food Donation and Redistribution Platform for Reducing Waste and Hunger
authors: A. Gnanabaskaran; R. Sakthi; T. Nithesh
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: Food waste and hunger are still side by side in the world today, and tons of unused food are thrown away, meanwhile, many people do not have access to healthy food reliably. The classic systems of donations still rely on the manual inspection, unstructured communication, and weak logistics that tends to result in delays and spoilage as well as, lack of transparency. In this paper, Donato is an AI-based food donation and redistribution platform that will combine automated freshness prediction, traceability supported by blockchain, and intelligent route optimization. The system uses a trained ResNet50 to classify donated food into freshness categories, keep donation and delivery records on an authorized blockchain to be tracked tamper-proofly and create dynamic delivery plans to increase urgency to minimize spoilage changes. It has been experimentally shown that Donato is better in classification accuracy, trust, because of immutable records, and pickup latency is lower than that of a manual process. These findings indicate the promising opportunities of deep learning, distributed ledger technologies, and optimization of logistics integration to enhance efficiency, safety, and scalability of the redistribution network of food.

title: Adaptive Control with Prescribed Performance for Uncertain WMR Dynamics under Multiplicative Sensor Faults
authors: J. Fan; X. Huang; B. Liao
venue: 2026 Joint International Conference on Automation-Intelligence-Safety (ICAIS) & International Symposium on Autonomous Systems (ISAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the stabilization problem for uncertain EL dynamic systems of wheeled mobile robots (WMR) with multiplicative sensor faults in both unconstrained and constrained scenarios. Through coordinate transformation, the original WMR system is converted changed into a state-space form suitable for controller design, and a low-complexity, strongly robust adaptive state feedback control scheme is developed by introducing a filtered variable. For the unconstrained system, strict proofs based on Lyapunov analysis and Barbalat’s lemma demonstrate that all closed-loop signals remain bounded and the system states asymptotically converge to zero. For the constrained system, prescribed performance bounds are incorporated via error transformation, achieving performance mapping from the filtered variable to the system states. Numerical simulations proof the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed control scheme.

title: Agent-Based Reinforcement Learning for Automated Pipe Routing in Modular Water Electrolyzer Plants
authors: S. Krieger; N. Niedernostheide; P. Adler; B. Kuhlenkötter
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
abstract: Automated pipe routing in large-scale modular water electrolyzer plants is challenging because dense three-dimensional layouts, fixed interfaces, and sequentially accumulating constraints strongly restrict the feasible routing space. Existing algorithmic and reinforcement-learning-based approaches have demonstrated the general potential of automated routing. Still, they typically address more narrowly scoped scenarios and do not capture the growing geometric coupling caused by previously routed pipes. This paper proposes an agent-based reinforcement-learning framework for automated pipe routing in a Unity simulation derived from the HyPLANT100 plant concept. The routing task is formulated as a discrete 3D decision problem in which one constrained port-to-target connection is generated per episode under explicit geometric and rule-based constraints. To learn robust routing behavior under increasing congestion, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy is trained in Unity ML-Agents, while successfully generated routes are retained in the simulation as collision obstacles for subsequent episodes. The evaluation shows that this approach is suitable for automated pipe routing in modular electrolyzer layouts and can support feasible and efficient connection planning under progressive congestion.

title: A Review on Multi-Scenario Decision-Making for Urban Autonomous Driving
authors: A. H. Reyna; I. P. Gomes; L. A. Rosero; V. Grassi Junior; D. F. Wolf
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Autonomous vehicles depend on decision-making systems capable of interpreting environmental data and vehicle states to operate safely and efficiently. Single-scenario methods perform well in limited conditions but lack adaptability for diverse scenarios. Generalized approaches address these challenges but face issues with efficiency and safety. This systematic review compares single-scenario and multi-scenario decision-making techniques, categorized as rule-based, optimization, learning, and hybrid methods. It highlights gaps and advances needed to enhance flexibility and reliability for handling complex driving scenarios. Analyses show that hybrid methods tend to offer greater adaptability and security by combining explicit rules and constraints with the flexibility of learning. System evaluation uses databases, simulation, and closed-track and open-road testing, but the focus varies depending on the approach: in single-scenario, the aim is to diagnose and correct specific behaviors under controlled conditions; in multiple scenarios, the objective is to measure the system’s robustness and generalizability within the operational domain. Despite advances, gaps persist in the ability to deal with unknown and critical situations, demanding future investigations into generalization strategies, incremental learning and integration of contextual representations of the environment.

title: Virtual–Real Hybrid Game Approach for Virtual Power Plants Based on Continual Learning With Forward-Feedback Knowledge Replay
authors: W. Zhou; J. Lai; Z. Zeng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: This article proposes a multiagent collaborative game evolution strategy to address issues of distributed resource sharing among virtual power plants, which is based on multicriteria matching and continuous learning. First, a peer matching mechanism is designed considering heterogeneous factor fusion and reasoning, which can enhance the adaptability and effectiveness of matching work. Then, a virtual–real hybrid game evolution framework is proposed based on continuous learning, in which a data-driven SE estimation method is developed to transform the traditional iterative response process into an efficient strategy estimation, thereby improving the efficiency of multiagent games. Furthermore, to further mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continuous learning, a multitimescale forward-feedback knowledge replay method is proposed to dynamically adjust replay timing and content, which can achieve knowledge consolidation through a combination of preventive maintenance and targeted repair, enhancing model evolution capabilities. Case studies validate that the proposed strategy exhibits superior performance in matching rationality, game convergence speed, and resistance to knowledge forgetting.

title: Hybrid Metaheuristic-Based Decision Support Framework for Employee Transportation Optimization
authors: N. Mlika; H. Khlif
venue: 2026 IEEE International conference on Advanced Systems and Emergent Technologies (IC_ASET)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid metaheuristic framework for optimizing large-scale employee transportation systems in industrial settings. The proposed approach integrates a modified Sweep Algorithm for initial geographic clustering, a direction-aware Weighted Nearest Neighbor rule to minimize backtracking, 2-opt intra-route refinement, an inter-route relocation operator for load balancing, and a Multi-Start Local Search metaheuristic to avoid local optima. The method is specifically designed to address the characteristic constraints of industrial shuttle routing, including fixed station locations, known demand, heterogeneous vehicle capacities, and the need for geographically coherent, non-overlapping service sectors. Validation using realworld operational data from a Tunisian multinational automotive company demonstrates substantial improvements in fleet efficiency, travel distance reduction, and vehicle occupancy increase, while completely eliminating route overlaps. This resolution approach has been integrated into a Decision Support System (DSS) featuring an interactive interface and geographical visualization of optimized routes. The results confirm that the framework provides a scalable, practical, and efficient solution for daily transportation planning in industrial logistics.

title: Learning Rollout from Sampling: An R1-Style Tokenized Traffic Simulation Model
authors: Z. Wang; P. Chen; D. Li; C. Li; Q. Zhang; Z. Xia; G. Yu
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Learning diverse and high-fidelity traffic simulations from human driving demonstrations is crucial for autonomous driving evaluation. The recent next-token prediction (NTP) paradigm, widely adopted in large language models (LLMs), has been applied to traffic simulation and achieves iterative improvements via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). However, such methods limit active exploration of potentially valuable motion tokens, particularly in suboptimal regions. Entropy patterns provide a promising perspective for enabling exploration driven by motion token uncertainty. Motivated by this insight, we propose a novel tokenized traffic simulation policy, R1Sim, which represents an initial attempt to explore reinforcement learning based on motion token entropy patterns, and systematically analyzes the impact of different motion tokens on simulation outcomes. Specifically, we introduce an entropy-guided adaptive sampling mechanism that focuses on previously overlooked motion tokens with high uncertainty yet high potential. We further optimize motion behaviors using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), guided by a safety-aware reward design. Overall, these components enable a balanced exploration–exploitation trade-off through diverse high-uncertainty sampling and group-wise comparative estimation, resulting in realistic, safe, and diverse multi-agent behaviors. Extensive experiments on the Waymo Sim Agent benchmark demonstrate that R1Sim achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: Hallucination-Aware Hierarchical LLM for Autonomous UAV Mobility Control: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
authors: H. Ahn; S. Oh; G. S. Kim; S. Park; S. Jung; J. Kim
venue: IEEE Transactions on Networking
abstract: This paper proposes SafeGPT, a hierarchical framework that integrates generative pretrained transformer (GPT)-based large language models (LLM) with safe reinforcement learning (safe-RL). SafeGPT addresses the large-scale random multi-point tour problem (RMPT) for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The target platforms are large electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) class rotary-wing UAVs. Such platforms suit wide-area logistics and infrastructure inspection rather than small drones. The hierarchical architecture enables scalable UAV coordination by centralizing strategic planning and distributing local route computation, mitigating the complexity issues of conventional methods. To mitigate LLM hallucination risks, i.e., the generation of plausible routes that violate physical constraints, a safe-RL method is implemented as a constrained Markov decision process (MDP) with Lagrangian actor-critic optimization, which promotes constraints on energy consumption, communication efficiency, and duplicate visits. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate SafeGPT’s performance advantages in battery efficiency, communication reliability, and travel distance across problem scales from 500 to 2000 waypoints. Even in demanding scenarios, constraint violation rates remain below specified thresholds. These results establish SafeGPT as an effective solution for large-scale UAV route planning, respecting operational constraints without compromising efficiency.

title: Bridging the Simulation-to-Emulation Gap in Autonomous Cyber Defence: A Hybrid PPO and LLM-Based Framework
authors: L. K. S. Kumar; M. Yaseen; R. Uyyala; J. Ravichandarreddy
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
abstract: Autonomous cyber defense has become an important research area as modern networks increase in complexity, size, and vulnerability to rapid multi-stage attacks. Although reinforcement learning shows potential for making defensive decisions, many current studies focus only on simulations. This leaves questions about how well trained policies work in more realistic settings. Practical autonomous defence systems also require not only adaptive action selection but enforcement of safety constraints and operator-facing explainability. This paper presents a hybrid framework bridging simulation and emulation. We train a Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) defender in the CybORG CAGE Challenge 2 and evaluate it within a Dockerbased network emulation using a custom telemetry bridge. The system integrates the PPO policy with a rule-based guard layer to prevent unsafe actions and a Large Language Model (LLM) to provide real-time natural language explainability to operators. Experimental results show that the trained policy successfully transfers to the Docker environment, though its strategic behaviour adapts noticeably to live emulation conditions. Overall, this work demonstrates that combining reinforcement learning with rule-based logic and LLM explainability enables autonomous defenders to successfully transition into live environments.

title: A Planning-Oriented Autonomous Driving Framework: From Image to Trajectory With Intent-Aware Prediction
authors: H. -Y. Kang; J. -G. Lu; M. Wei; Q. -H. Zhang; Z. Zhu; Y. Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Autonomous driving requires accurate prediction of surrounding agents and reliable planning of ego-vehicle trajectories, yet integrating these components into a coherent pipeline remains challenging. This paper proposes a planning-oriented framework that maps bird’s-eye-view images directly into executable ego-vehicle trajectories, balancing an end-to-end formulation with modular components. The system operates in three sequential stages: multi-agent intent-aware prediction, where intent embeddings are injected into agent encodings together with static environment structures to enhance joint feature fusion, followed by a trajectory decoding stage that further exploits intent to guide sequential prediction; goal-conditioned trajectory generation via an imitation-learning planner with cross-attention and a transformer decoder; and geometric post-processing to enforce obstacle clearance and trajectory smoothness. Throughout the framework, road structure features can be obtained from coarse semantic layers in the bird’s-eye-view domain, which provides sufficient abstraction for prediction and planning while preserving flexibility and avoiding reliance on high-definition maps. Evaluations on the nuPlan benchmark show that the proposed method achieves strong and well-balanced performance across standard non-reactive and reactive planning metrics, while maintaining real-time efficiency with an average overall pipeline latency of $164{\,}\mathrm {ms}$ . In addition, a preliminary deployment on an Intelligent Guided Vehicle in a mixed-traffic container terminal demonstrates the practical deployability of the proposed framework in real-world industrial scenarios. Although not fully differentiable, the design intentionally balances end-to-end learning with structural modularity to ensure interpretability, flexibility, and robustness, ensuring both practical feasibility and strong closed-loop performance.

title: Cooperative Multi-UAV Task Allocation and Smoke Deployment for Simulation-Based Line-of-Sight Screening
authors: Z. Tan; D. Wu; Y. Peng; J. Deng; Y. An
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This study examines how multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) should allocate tasks and coordinate smoke deployment to interrupt line of sight under fast, spatially dispersed incoming threats. A three-dimensional simulation framework is developed that couples proportional-navigation-like reference threat motion, aerodynamic drag, overload saturation, field-of-view break-lock and reacquisition, smoke-puff advection–diffusion–settling, and infrared/electro-optical attenuation through the Beer–Lambert law. Under the same five-UAV physical model and search budget, we compare a non-optimized greedy estimated-time-of-arrival heuristic (M0) with three genetic-algorithm-coupled task-organization structures: round-robin balancing (M1), spatiotemporal clustering and matching (M2), and capacity-constrained global preallocation (M3). Four topologies are evaluated with 30 independent runs per topology and 20 threat tracks per run. The aggregate successful-screening rates are 0.00%, 34.96%, 65.83%, and 81.25% for M0–M3, respectively; in the most dispersed omnidirectional topology, the corresponding rates are 0.00%, 41.50%, 29.83%, and 66.50%. Run-level tests confirm the overall M2–M3 separation (Welch p = 0.0004603; Mann–Whitney p = 0.006083). Component checks, threshold scans, optimal-transport-invariance tests, one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analysis, and runtime benchmarks indicate that M2 is limited by structural coverage loss in dispersed settings, whereas M3 preserves task admission more stably. The study is positioned as a simulation-based mechanism comparison rather than field validation.

title: From Generative to Agentic: A Survey of Autonomous AI Systems and Their Evolving Capabilities
authors: K. K. Sushmitha; N. Shanthi; M. Muthuraja; J. Gowthami; S. Jahaganapathi; V. K. Kishore
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Electronic Devices and Intelligent Systems (ICSEDIS)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has progressed from traditional rule-based systems that were generally not very intelligent to current advanced generative models and most recently to an even newer generation of AI called Agentic AI (or autonomous AI). Unlike traditional AI that uses pre-defined prompts to perform operations, agentic AI systems have the ability to sense their surroundings, think about their objectives, create multi-step plans and take action with very little help from people. The purpose of this paper is to provide an overview of Agentic AI; focusing on how it is structured and operates, including the types of core technologies (such as large language models (LLM), reasoning systems, memory systems, and technologies that allow agentic systems to use tools) that provide the foundation for agentic AI. In addition, important applications of agentic AI are reviewed, including, but not limited to, health care, software development, education, finance and gaming. Furthermore, the paper identifies current research issues concerning reliability, safety, governance, and ethical alignment for developing trustworthy autonomous AI systems. Finally, this paper discusses future avenues of research in developing trustworthy autonomous AI systems.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of the Transformative Path of AI: From AI Agents to Agentic AI
authors: Q. Sun; J. Koteska; J. Prodanova; J. Xu; G. Zhai; Y. Tang; L. Kocarev
venue: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has catalyzed a transition from reactive, task-specific agents toward Agentic AI – autonomous systems capable of independent reasoning, goal-setting, and recursive planning. Despite extensive research and application, existing literature remains fragmented, often conflating individual autonomy with collective agency. This paper provides a comprehensive systematic review that delineates the transition from individual artificial agency (I-AA) to social artificial agency (S-AA). We introduce a unified architectural framework based on a continuous six-component cognitive loop: perception, reasoning, planning, memory, action, and learning. Our taxonomy categorizes agents into four foundational paradigms: traditional, large language model (LLM)-based, embodied, and human digital twin (HDT)-based, while further defining three advanced Agentic AI configurations: agentic LLM-based, agentic LLM+embodied, and agentic LLM+HDT systems. By distinguishing between localized agency in I-AA and emergent agency in S-AA, we explore the complexities of a macro-scale society of heterogeneous agentic ecosystems.

title: Toward Robust Agents: A Survey of Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: A. Mohan; T. Schön
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated remarkable success in autonomous decision-making across diverse domains, including robotics, autonomous driving, and game playing. However, recent studies have uncovered a critical vulnerability: DRL agents are highly susceptible to adversarial attacks that can significantly degrade their performance or lead to catastrophic failure. These attacks exploit different components of the learning pipeline observations, actions, rewards, and policies exposing new challenges unique to DRL compared to supervised learning. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of adversarial threats and corresponding defense mechanisms within the DRL paradigm. This also aims to serve as a foundational reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to understand and mitigate adversarial vulnerabilities in DRL.

title: Policy-Prior-Guided Generative Coordination for Resilient Energy Management in Cyber-Physical Distributed Systems
authors: M. Zhou; X. Che
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The dynamic network of heterogeneous and mobile energy nodes, such as drones, electric vehicles, and ground energy stations, forms the basis of air–ground collaborative cyber-physical energy systems. It is difficult to optimize system energy efficiency and economic operation while maintaining resilience under information and physical disturbances. The problem becomes more complex under strong spatiotemporal coupling, limited local information, and non-ideal communication. This paper proposes a strategy-prior-guided generative collaborative energy management framework, named PG-TSCD. The framework adopts a two-stage structure-aware decision process. At the system level, a spatiotemporal graph-based conditional diffusion model captures the dynamic coupling among nodes and global safety constraints. It describes the feasible scheduling space under complex constraints and generates a coordinated discharge and recharge power prior sequence. At the node level, each agent combines the global prior with incomplete local observations through a lightweight adaptive reconstruction module. It then produces executable scheduling actions that remain robust under disturbances. In this way, distributed agents achieve system objectives through coordinated decision making. Theoretical analysis shows that PG-TSCD approximates centralized optimal scheduling with a bounded performance gap and ensures stable distributed learning. Experiments show that the model converges in about 85 training rounds, reaches a peak energy efficiency of 3.5, and maintains a task completion rate above 93% under high load. The performance remains stable under 300 ms communication delay and 12% packet loss.

title: Constructing Generalized Singularity-Free Controllers for Distance-Based Formations
authors: Z. Liu; Z. Sun; J. Chen; M. Cao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
abstract: This article provides a general method of constructing distributed controllers for achieving distance-based multiagent formations. We first extend the definition of the distance error into a general function of the interagent distance, delivering more general controller functions than the standard distance-error-based controllers. We further develop methods of constructing formation controllers that guarantee asymptotic or exponential stability of the closed-loop system. We then discuss singularities, i.e., singular states where gradient controllers fail to operate, caused by colocated agents. Gaps in the literature regarding the relationship between collision avoidance properties and the infinite gradient of potential functions have been bridged. These enable us to propose formation control methods for constructing singularity-free stabilizing controllers.

title: Real-Time Scheduling of CPU/GPU Heterogeneous Tasks in Dynamic IoT Systems: Enhancing GPU and Memory Efficiency
authors: X. He; S. Pang; S. Qiao; H. Gui; S. Yu; J. J. P. C. Rodrigues; S. Mumtaz; Z. Lyu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing
abstract: The real-time processing of large-scale, heterogeneous tasks—including CPU-only, general-purpose GPU, and specialized GPU tasks—poses significant challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) systems, driven by severe GPU resource fragmentation, inefficient CPU and memory resource utilization on edge servers. These issues often compromise system processing performance and server stability. To address these issues, we formulate a multi-stage mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model, to jointly optimize GPU fragmentation rate and system processing capability. We then introduce a novel deviation-based Lyapunov optimization framework that explicitly maintains memory utilization around a predefined optimal threshold, effectively balancing resource usage and system stability. Finally, to achieve real-time decision-making for massive tasks in dynamic systems with randomly arriving tasks, we propose the MA-LHTO algorithm, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach that incorporates a multi-head architecture, entropy-based exploration, and a parameter reset mechanism. Experimental results confirm that our algorithm significantly improves resource utilization, and exhibits good performance under various working conditions.

title: Bidirectional Search-Based Optimization of AGV Transportation Paths in Automated Container Terminals
authors: Y. Chen; J. Pu; L. Liang
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems (ICICACS)
abstract: Optimizing the routing and coordination of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) is essential for maximizing productivity at automated container terminals. Existing methods based on reinforcement learning typically encounter difficulties with high computational complexity, slow convergence rates, and no guarantee of achieving a deterministic optimum, which restricts their use in actual time-critical environments. In response to this issue, this paper presents a novel optimization approach to path planning for AGVs used for transporting containers in port container terminals, which is based on a bidirectional search process. Initially, the port environment is represented as a graph where spatial and temporal restrictions are imposed upon the graph. The formulation of an AGV transportation path planning multi-objective optimization problem is described where the objectives are to minimize travel distance, waiting time, and conflict costs. The main contribution of this work is the development of a bidirectional search algorithm to identify optimal transportation paths with fewer than half as many attempts at finding optimal transportation paths by searching both the initial node and the end node at the same time. The use of a conflict aware path refinement method employing time window reservation and node occupancy restrictions ensures that AGVs operate safely by avoiding collisions during navigation. Additionally, to manage the uncertainty associated with real-time operations, a multi-AGV coordination strategy based on priority scheduling and dynamic re-routing has been developed. The proposed framework achieves faster convergence, guaranteed shortest path generation, and improved scalability compared to conventional methods. Experimental evaluation demonstrates significant reductions in terms of Path Length of 1004m, Travel Time of 405s, Waiting Time of 70s respectively.

title: Evaluation of Graph- and Sampling-Based Path Planners for Multi-Agent Deployment in Known Urban Environments
authors: D. C. García; J. Izquierdo-Reyes; I. L. Villegas; R. Bustamante-Bello
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become key tools in emergency missions in urban environments, due to their rapid deployment and ability to operate in hazardous conditions. Path planning is crucial in these disasters, as it determines the safety and efficiency of the mission. This study compares graph-based algorithms, such as A-Star (A) and D-Star Lite (D Lite), as well as sampling-based methods, including Probabilistic Roadmaps (PRM), Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star (RRT), and Batch Informed Trees (BIT), along with spline-based post-processing applied to the trajectories produced by the sampling-based planners. To evaluate the performance of path planning algorithms, a framework developed in Python generates known three-dimensional urban environments with static obstacles. The benchmark considered 50 scenes, each with 15 obstacles, 5 UAVs, and 5 seed trials, resulting in 10,000 runs across eight different path planners. This study used a strict success criterion and analyzed planning time metrics, path length, minimum safety margin, and geometric smoothness. D* Lite achieved the highest success rate (98.8%) and the highest obstacle clearance, but at the cost of longer planning times. RRT* and RRT* with splines were the fastest methods (median $\approx ~4.9$ ms), although with lower success rates. In contrast, BIT* and BIT* with splines offered the best value, second only to D* Lite, combining high success rates with shorter paths, better path quality, and moderate computational demand. The benchmark provides a quantitative basis for planner selection in non-cooperative multi-agent deployment scenarios, without accounting for flight dynamics, sensor uncertainty, or dynamic obstacles.

title: Deadlocks in Dense Lifelong MAPF: A Journey from Why to Adaptive Density Control
authors: T. A. Teli; A. J. Bhat; M. N. Asgar; D. Ellahi; U. M. Mir
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
abstract: Collaborative robots share a workspace and must coordinate their movements continuously to avoid collisions. Such fleets operate within automated warehouses and guided-vehicle systems that assign transport tasks to the robots without interruption. Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) computes collision-free routes for these teams, and its lifelong variant assigns each robot a new goal on arrival so that operation never halts. Performance is measured by throughput, the number of goals a team completes per timestep, yet throughput alone shows only that a system has stalled and not the reason behind it. This work examines the effect of deadlocks through a three-stage pipeline wrapped around a fixed decentralized learned policy. The first stage measures deadlock through a per-agent stuck signal with rate, recovery time, and a spatial heatmap. The second characterizes the operating regime through a betweenness-lift order parameter, which finds deadlock concentrated at a few bottlenecks below saturation and dispersed across the workspace once it saturates. A direct test confirms that in this dispersed regime both local repair and congestion-aware routing fail, leaving a reduction in the active-agent count as the only effective control. The third stage controls density online by metering the active-agent count from the same signal. The resulting Adaptive Density Controller raises throughput by 18% under a static cap and by 8% online without prior knowledge of the optimum, and it remains the only intervention effective where centralized search becomes intractable.

title: Distributed Affine Formation Maneuver Control for Heterogeneous USV-UAV Systems with Obstacle Avoidance
authors: N. Wei; R. Changhe; S. Jun
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Intelligent Robotics and Control Engineering (IRCE)
abstract: Heterogeneous unmanned surface vehicle-unmanned aerial vehicle (USV-UAV) systems enable sea-air collaborative missions including marine monitoring, search and rescue, and coastal patrol, with rapidly growing demand in complex ocean environments. Existing formation control methods face critical challenges in unified formation description for heterogeneous dynamics, flexible maneuvering in constrained spaces, obstacle avoidance integration, and dependence on global velocity information. This paper proposes a distributed affine formation maneuver control scheme for heterogeneous USV-UAV systems. A hierarchical control architecture is established with a virtual leader layer for affine trajectory planning and a heterogeneous execution layer for distributed tracking. A stress-matrix-based dynamic affine adjustment mechanism is designed to realize formation maneuvering for obstacle avoidance. A distributed observer is developed to estimate unknown target velocity using only local position measurements. Rigorous theoretical analysis proves the global uniformly ultimately bounded stability of the closed-loop system. Simulation results under multiple complex scenarios verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. The proposed scheme provides a practical and flexible solution for sea-air heterogeneous collaborative missions in constrained marine environments.

title: Agentic AI vs Non-Agentic AI: Motivation, Security Implications, and Research Foundations
authors: S. Gupta; B. Arief; R. de Lemos
venue: 2026 21st European Dependable Computing Conference Companion Proceedings (EDCC-C)
abstract: A significant change in the development and application of artificial intelligence (AI) systems is the transition from non-agentic to agentic AI. Non-agentic AI systems, such as prompt-based language models and classical machine learning models, operate reactively, producing outputs only in response to inputs. They lack long-term memory, long-term goals, or the capacity to act independently. Agentic AI systems, on the other hand, are made to act more autonomously through goalsetting, multi-step planning, tool use, memory storage, and action execution in physical or virtual environments. This paper aims to explain the emergence of agentic AI, distinguish it from non-agentic AI, and examine the new security and governance challenges arising from this novel mode of operation. The approach used in this paper includes research about intelligent agents, large language models (LLMs) based agents, AI security, and governance frameworks. The paper also highlights how autonomous behaviour increases AI attack surface, shifts security concerns, and focuses from isolated model errors to risks involving decision-making logic, persistent memory, delegated permissions, and long-running agent behaviour. Finally, the paper argues that although agentic AI may increase the threat surface, it can be deployed responsibly provided that appropriate systemlevel safeguards are in place. This highlights the need for new or extended security and authorisation frameworks focusing specifically on agentic AI.

title: A Fuzzy-Theoretic Cooperative Game Framework for Adaptive Robust Control of Air–Ground Vehicle Systems
authors: X. Zhao; B. Dang; Y. -H. Chen; F. Dong; J. Huang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
abstract: To enhance the efficiency and safety of transportation, low-altitude economy has garnered increasing attention. In this study, we consider air–ground systems composed of both uncrewed ground vehicles and uncrewed aerial vehicles. A novel integrated framework for modeling, control, and optimization is proposed, which creatively unifies kinematics, dynamics, and control into a structured setting for approximate constraint following. The framework consists of three key phases. First, in the modeling phase, desired system behaviors, such as collision avoidance, compact formation, and trajectory tracking, are formulated into a unified performance metric. This metric is then treated as a constraint, and the system’s dynamics for approximate constraint following are derived using the Udwadia–Kalaba approach. Second, in the control phase, an adaptive robust control scheme is developed to compensate for system uncertainties. Notably, the method does not require prior knowledge of the uncertainty bounds, while still guaranteeing consistent system performance in uncertain environments. Third, in the optimization phase, the fuzzy nature of the uncertainty bounds is considered. The uncertainty bound is modeled as a fuzzy set characterized by a membership function, which is incorporated into a fuzzy-theoretic performance index. The Pareto-optimal game theory is then employed to determine the optimal control parameters. The proposed framework enables the air–ground logistics system to follow constraints with reduced error, as validated through simulation results.

title: Distributed Practical Prescribed-Time Formation Control for Multi-UGVs With Unified Irregular State Constraints
authors: Y. Chen; H. Liang; Y. Cheng; H. Zhang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed practical prescribed-time formation control problem for uncertain uncrewedground vehicle (UGV) systems via an improved state constraints approach. First, an adaptive formation controller with a prescribed-time gain is developed to guarantee UGVs achieve exact desired formations within user-defined time intervals. Unlike conventional methods requiring infinite gain, the proposed approach ensures bounded control inputs while maintaining rigorous convergence guarantees. Second, a unified framework for irregular state constraints is proposed to address heterogeneous operational requirements in multi-scenario UGV formations. This framework incorporates a boundary-adaptive dynamic scaling function coupled with a transformation-based decision mechanism to establish configurable constraint domains, where state constraints are rigorously enforced through systematically designed logarithmic barrier functions, thereby ensuring guaranteed constraint compliance in all operational scenarios. Third, the adaptive robust control term is designed to eliminate the the fuzzy approximation errors ensuring that all formation errors asymptotically converge to zero. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is rigorously verified through numerical simulation studies.

title: Behaviour Modelling of Self-Learning UAVs using Agent-Based Simulation for Understanding Battery Depletion Rates and Operational Lifespan
authors: V. G. T; Y. M. C; S. S. R; S. D. C. R
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Autonomous self-learning Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) embody the future of swarm intelligence and energy-conscious mission planning. Previous research work in UAV optimization is mostly dependent on control-theoretic or reinforcementlearning approaches with minimum real-time adaptability to evolving behavior. This paper introduces an Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) approach in $\mathbf{R}$ that models emergent learning, energy usage, and endurance behavior of self-learning UAVs. The virtual data were created with ten control parameters and were utilized to simulate $\mathbf{1 0 0}$ UAV agents across 200 mission steps. Three self-organizing UAV types emerged from the unsupervised k -means clustering of the identified behavioral archetypes. Statistical analysis by linear mixed-effects model and KaplanMeier survival analysis demonstrated substantial variance in battery depletion rates and operation lifetime between behavior clusters. The “BalancedStrategist” UAVs showed better energy efficiency and mission endurance, whereas high-aggression agents showed fast battery degradation and reduced survival time. The proposed model effectively combined behavioral, physical, and energy dynamics within a single simulated environment. Results provide a measurable connection between learning rate, endurance and aggression in autonomous UAVs and provide predictive understanding for optimizing swarm coordination and battery-conscious control approaches in industrial, defense, and environmental monitoring scenarios.

title: Consensus-Based Distributed Reinforcement Learning With Primal–Dual Update for Networked Microgrids On-Line Coordination
authors: G. Cui; Q. -S. Jia; X. Guan; Q. Zhai; X. Guo; Q. Guo
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper develops a distributed reinforcement learning (RL) method to coordinate cooperative microgrids (MGs). The high uncertainty of power loads and renewable energy sources motivate the operator to perform real-time dispatch. On the one hand, the existing online methods usually utilize approximate models that result in intractable constraint violation. A common method is to relax it as a chance constraint, while it is still hard to ensure its satisfaction in practice. On the other hand, some MGs may hope to preserve the private information on their local costs and states. To address these problems, we make the following contributions. First, the coordination problem is reformulated as a constrained multi-agent Markov decision process. Second, the distributed RL algorithm with a theoretical convergence guarantee is developed. Third, to further preserve the local private information and improve the performance, this algorithm is modified by adding a local feature extraction module for each agent. This module could also be regarded as an encryption module for the local state information. Fourth, numerical experiments are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the modified algorithm. Note to Practitioners—In multi-MG systems, voltage security is significant to energy reliability. However, the MGs are controlled by different owners who are concerned about privacy. The conventional model-based methods require detailed information to construct the closed model. And the inaccurate model induces intractable abnormal voltage problems. To address these issues, we propose to restrict the off-limit frequencies by chance constraint since the low-frequency off-limits could be adjusted by tertiary control. Additionally, we develop a distributed RL algorithm to optimize the coordination problem while preserving the private information. This algorithm is equipped with a primal-dual update to ensure that the learned policies satisfy the chance constraint. With our method, the MGs can operate in a cooperative mode to dispatch energy without exposing their sensitive information. The developed RL method can also be applied to other fields where different individuals cooperatively work on global objectives while concerning privacy. To further accelerate deployment, the offline RL techniques are compatible with our algorithm to initialize the policies with prior experience. Our algorithm considers the chance constraints instead of the hard ones. If the environment includes inviolable constraint, such as collisions, this algorithm alone cannot guarantee absolute safety. In this case, the practitioner may consider adding safety-certificates.

title: Joint Task Allocation and Charging Scheduling for UAVs: Managing Corridor Congestion and Non-Linear Hovering Penalties
authors: M. Zhang; N. Pan; S. Zhang; Y. Zhang; W. Liang
venue: 2026 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The rapid development of low-altitude corridors and complex industrial collaborative inspections imposes stringent requirements on the automated online scheduling of the UAV fleet. Existing path planning studies based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) often lack practical physical constraints, neglecting the severe nonlinear hovering energy consumption induced by microscopic collision avoidance in 3D corridors and queuing at terminal base stations. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Joint UAV Task Allocation and Charging Scheduling Model (JUTACS) formulated for 3D constrained corridors. Developed within a Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP) framework, the proposed JUTACS systematically characterizes heterogeneous inspection tasks, the dynamic congestion of charging base stations, and the asynchronous spatio-temporal transitions of the UAV fleet. Furthermore, a Dual-Layer Kinematics-Driven Neural Combinatorial Optimization Solving Framework (CAMT-RH) is introduced. In this hierarchical architecture, the upper layer employs a Congestion-Aware Mask Transformer (CAMT-PPO) as the global scheduling hub, while the lower layer embeds a Priority-based Spatio-Temporal Reservation (P-STR) mechanism as a physical feasibility evaluator, thereby achieving the collaborative optimization of inspection task allocation and path planning. Comparative evaluations against greedy dispatching, MAPPO, rolling-horizon MILP, ALNS, and neural scheduling baselines demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves the best reward, task completion, hovering control, and online inference efficiency. In addition, ablation studies, congestion sensitivity analyses, and zero-shot generalization experiments reveal how the congestion-aware encoder, dynamic feasibility mask, P-STR feedback, and nonlinear hovering penalty jointly improve robustness under varying UAV fleet sizes and chargingstation bottlenecks.

title: Prescribed Performance-Based Distributed Adaptive Predefined-Time Consensus Control for BESSs
authors: C. Yan; X. Sun; X. Zhang; T. Cheng; J. Gu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This work investigates distributed state-of-charge (SOC) balancing for battery energy storage systems (BESSs). Existing predefined-time consensus designs, despite their explicit convergence-time guarantees, may exhibit singularity, induce transient overcurrents under large initial SOC mismatches, and rely on continuous communication. To overcome these limitations, a distributed adaptive predefined-time robust control framework with prescribed performance constraints is developed. Within this framework, a dynamic error envelope is constructed to shape the convergence profile under prescribed performance bounds. In this manner, the convergence time is prescribed a priori, whereas initial transients and the associated current peaks are limited to improve the safety margins of power electronic devices. To enforce the prescribed error evolution under disturbances, an event-triggered (ET)-based distributed predefined-time sliding mode controller is designed, in which a predefined-time adaptive law is incorporated to track mismatched disturbances, thereby mitigating high-frequency chattering while ensuring nonsingular dynamics. In addition, an ET-based model-free state observer with input-to-state stability is developed to support distributed implementation without continuous communication. Predefined-time stability is rigorously established via Lyapunov analysis. Multi-scenario simulations validate the proposed method and confirm reduced communication overhead, prescribed convergence time, and improved transient safety. Note to Practitioners—SOC balancing among BESS submodules is challenging in practice because large initial imbalances may cause transient current surges, whereas communication-intensive coordination limits scalability and deployability. This work develops a distributed control framework that shapes the balancing error within a prescribed performance envelope, so that the balancing process can be explicitly regulated, transient current stress can be reduced during the initial stage, and the balancing time can be selected in advance to match scheduling requirements. The control law is designed to guarantee predefined-time convergence while avoiding undesirable singular behavior and reducing implementation-induced oscillations, which is beneficial for power electronic devices. The method further replaces continuous communication with event-triggered information exchange, thereby reducing bandwidth demand while preserving distributed operation. It is particularly relevant to modular BESS applications where transient safety, communication efficiency, and practical deployability must be considered simultaneously.

title: Privacy Protection-Enhanced Vertical-Horizontal Federated Learning Secure Sharing for Multisource Heterogeneous Data
authors: W. Deng; X. Li; Y. Sun; H. Zhao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
abstract: Flight operation relies on multientity collaboration, generating inherently multi-source and heterogeneous data. Privacy and security concerns hinder direct data sharing, while conventional federated learning (FL) cannot fully accommodate such complex data distributions. To address this, a novel privacy protection-enhanced vertical-horizontal FL (PEVHFL) framework with dual differential mechanism and sharpness aware minimization optimizer, namely PEVHFL is developed to achieve multisource heterogeneous flight operation data (FOD) secure sharing. First, a new dual differential privacy protection mechanism is designed to simultaneously protect against privacy leakage both within and across different types of clients (e.g., airlines, airports, air traffic control). Furthermore, a sharpness aware minimization optimizer is integrated to mitigate performance degradation caused by privacy noise, thereby balancing model utility with robust privacy guarantees. Finally, theoretical analysis demonstrates the privacy and convergence properties of the PEVHFL. The experiments on real-world FOD show that the PEVHFL achieves higher accuracy than individual silo-based training under strict privacy constraints, which offer a promising direction for privacy-preserving multi-agent data sharing.
