title: Adaptive Neural Network-Based Event-Triggered Consensus Tracking for Multiple Euler–Lagrange Systems With Actuator Failures
authors: D. Yao; H. Ma; H. Li; Q. Zhou; Y. Shi
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This article investigates the event-triggered adaptive fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for multiple Euler–Lagrange systems (MELSs) suffered from parameter uncertainties, actuator failures, unknown perturbations, and limited network bandwidth. The parameter uncertainties are modeled by unknown nonlinear dynamics, which are approximated by an estimation approach based on neural networks (NNs). Thereupon a nonlinear disturbance observer is devised to cope with the whole perturbations composed of unknown external disturbances, approximation errors, and actuator bias faults. Then, we establish an event triggering mechanism on control signals to dispatch triggering moments, guaranteeing that control commands are only activated when certain specially appointed events occur. After that, an event-triggered FTC algorithm based on adaptive NNs is put forward, which makes all closed-loop signals bounded and eventually allows all followers’ states to track the leader’s state. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed event-triggered adaptive NN FTC policy is verified through an example on multiple manipulators and a comparative experiment. Note to Practitioners—For MELSs such as multi-manipulator platforms and autonomous formations, guaranteeing reliable cooperative tracking while solving actuator failures and resource constraints is essential to system safety and operational efficiency. Existing adaptive FTC methods can handle actuator failures, but they are often affected by continuous signal transmission and cannot simultaneously compensate for lumped disturbances and actuator failures under limited network bandwidth. To address these challenges, this paper develops a novel event-triggered adaptive NN FTC strategy within a cohesive framework, where a nonlinear disturbance observer is inherently integrated into the event-based adaptive control architecture. This control framework provides practitioners with intuitive parameter tuning predicated on analytically derived boundedness conditions, facilitating straightforward practical implementation. Furthermore, it can be extended to other industrial nonlinear systems, such as autonomous aerial vehicles and autonomous ground vehicles, offering reliable dynamic performance across diverse practical application scenarios.

title: Agent Voyager: An Intelligent Travel Architect using AI Agents
authors: G. Sowmya; P. Reddy; S. Dileep; M. Reddy; S. Mishra; G. Annapurna
venue: 2026 International Conference on Advancements in Smart, Secure and Intelligent Computing (ASSIC)
abstract: Modern destination planning is often seen to be overwhelming based on the overload of information, fragmented services, and language barrier that essentially hinder the ability of travellers to come up with an action plan in the form of a oneto-one, systematic planned travel. As a solution to these obstacles, the current project proposes a new application, Agent Voyager, a smart and multi-lingual travel advisor that is based on an advanced AI-based multi-agent framework. To provide a simplified experience of the entire travel-planning process, Agent Voyager tries to avoid the human touch in all that it does, including finding out the destination and recommending activities to do, as well as building an adaptive day-by-day itinerary based on personal preferences. Its architecture uses a team of dedicated agents, each endowed with specific tasks such as natural language understanding, new travel information reception, user preference modelling, integration of meteorological variables, among other distinct tasks so that Agent Voyager is capable of understanding the subtextual, multiphasic queries presented by its user and is able to generate scientifically optimized, contextually aware itineraries. The main element will be the Orchestration Agent, as it would coordinate the heterogeneous agents via the implementation of Large Language Models (LLMs), thus, guaranteeing smooth teamwork and informed decision-making across the platform. Together, Agent Voyager aims to provide a convenient and interactive travel-planning experience, resembling the effectiveness of a one-on-one travel-planner, consequent to the ability of their users to save time, and attain an enhanced degree of satisfaction with their forthcoming journey.

title: Toward Optimal Multi-Vehicle Path Planning With Hybrid Roadmaps
authors: M. Turrà; S. Proia; A. Bonetti; L. Sabattini
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Effective path planning for multi-vehicle autonomous systems is essential to guarantee safe and efficient operation in industrial environments composed of both structured and unstructured settings. In the proposed framework, the overall environment is explicitly modeled as the integration of static and dynamic areas, each exhibiting distinct spatial and temporal properties. Static areas correspond to structured zones, such as corridors or production lines, and are represented by roadmaps with fixed topology. Dynamic areas, instead, represent unstructured portions of the environment and are modeled as gridmaps to enable adaptive navigation under changing occupancy conditions. Building upon this representation, a hybrid roadmap unifying static and dynamic areas is proposed, with a hierarchical control architecture for coordinated multi-vehicle navigation. The high-layer planner determines the optimal sequence of areas to traverse by solving a multi-objective optimization (MOO) problem that balances efficiency, safety, and traffic-related factors. On the other hand, the low-layer planner generates feasible paths within each area according to its structural constraints. The MOO formulation is embedded in a bi-level optimization framework, where the outer-level employs a quasi-adaptive self-tuning process for objective weights, addressing the limitations of subjective or suboptimal weight selection. Experimental validation across two realistic industrial layouts demonstrates improved mission efficiency, reduced travel-time variability, and scalability with fleet size, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed method for Industry 4.0 applications.

title: Neuro-Causal Resilience (NCR): A Certified Multimodal Intrusion Detection and Autonomous Defense Framework
authors: T. P. Balakrishnan; S. Sriram
venue: 2026 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: Sophisticated exploit evolution necessitates defensive architectures capable of synthesizing multimodal telemetry into automated, safety-critical responses. This research paper introduces Neuro-Causal Resilience (NCR), which is a multiphase framework aimed at harmonizing heterogeneous security telemetry into certified mitigation measures. The architecture consists of a hybrid statistical-semantic branch in the analysis of host-level logs through a Semantic-Sequential (LSTM) encoder and a structural network traffic analysis branch with a Graph Neural Network (GNN). A Structural Causal Model (SCM) is embraced to control multimodal fusion by way of interventional reasoning in an attempt to eliminate sensor contradictions and behavioral concept drift. This causality layer allows the system to distinguish between malicious intrusion and the benign system variations traditionally wrongly classified by deep learning models. Moreover, a reinforcement learning agent, based on a Deep Q-Network, is trained to implement safety-mindful defense against the integrated causal state. Empirical analysis of ToNIoT and UNSW-NB15 shows that the framework has a host-level detection rate of $\mathbf{9 3. 2 \%}$ and network accuracy of $\mathbf{8 1. 3 \%}$. The resulting multimodal combination platform attains a combined accuracy of $79 \%$ with an $\mathbf{F 1}$-score of 0.88, and the autonomous defense component attains a $73.1 \%$ decrease in cumulative system penalties via an $86.4 \%$ accuracy in action selection. It shows that the framework is able to offer consistent, explainable, and realtime security in dynamic enterprise settings.

title: Satellite-Enabled Edge Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Emergency Mobility: A Survey of On-Orbit Edge Computing
authors: P. Zong; Z. Ou; R. An; Q. Zhao; G. Zhang; K. Xue; Z. Tian; S. Lyu; Y. Shen; S. He; Y. Zhu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, which can rapidly disrupt road capacity, public transit operations, and logistics corridors. Reliable emergency mobility and low-carbon recovery therefore require timely, trustworthy, and spatially comprehensive situational awareness as well as resilient decision-making under intermittent connectivity. Earth-observation satellites and emerging LEO constellations provide global coverage for hazard monitoring (e.g., floods, wildfires, landslides) and infrastructure assessment, yet the resulting data volumes and limited contact windows make purely ground-centric processing increasingly insufficient for real-time transportation response. This paper surveys on-orbit edge computing (OEC) as a spaceborne edge layer that can close the sensing–analysis–action loop for climate-resilient transportation systems. We organize the literature into three evolutionary stages: 1) single-satellite on-orbit processing for event triggering and data triage, 2) satellite–ground collaboration for split inference, task offloading, and end-to-end orchestration, and 3) inter-satellite distributed computing for constellation-scale learning and inference under dynamic topology. Beyond summarizing methods, datasets, and platforms, we discuss how these OEC capabilities can be integrated with transportation digital twins and emergency operations to enable faster disruption detection, evacuation planning support, and bandwidth- and carbon-aware information delivery. Finally, we outline open challenges and future directions, including robust benchmarking under climate stressors, trustworthy autonomy, and LLM-assisted decision support across satellite–ground workflows.

title: H3CPP: Boundary-Safe Coverage Path Planning for Multi-USV Operations in Irregular Coastal Environments
authors: G. Spiliopoulos; E. Xidias; D. Zissis
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: As the need for persistent ocean monitoring grows, fleets of Uncrewed Surface Vessels (USVs) are a promising way to survey large marine protected areas with low operational cost. Their effectiveness, however, depends on solving a challenging multi-robot Coverage Path Planning (CPP) problem over complex coastal geometries while strictly respecting safety boundaries. This paper presents H3CPP, a CPP framework that leverages the H3 hierarchical hexagonal grid to discretize arbitrarily shaped marine areas, cluster them into connected subregions, and construct boundary-aware graphs on which Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) tours are computed. Each H3 cell is sized to match the nominal sensing footprint of a USV, and edges that intersect land or forbidden zones are exponentially penalized, encouraging safe paths that remain within the operational polygon. We evaluate H3CPP on seven benchmark polygonal maps and on a real-world coastal marina using 1–10 USVs. For a single USV in complex, non-convex environments, H3CPP achieves near-complete coverage (coverage ratio $\approx 1.0$ of the target area) while avoiding boundary violations that occur with swath and spiral baselines, and reduces path length by up to 10% compared to these methods in the most irregular shapes. In the Syros marina scenario, multi-USV experiments show that H3CPP decreases the total traveled distance by 4–34% ( $\approx 20\%$ on average) relative to a decomposition-plus-swaths baseline, while maintaining similar coverage and systematically reducing mission makespan as the fleet size increases from 1 to 10 USVs. The proposed framework therefore combines geodesic hexagonal indexing, connectivity-aware clustering, and penalized graph-based TSP planning into a practical CPP solution for USV swarms operating in realistic coastal environments.

title: Eventually Optimal and Scalable Multi-Agent Planning for Block Cave Mining
authors: C. Leet; P. Forte; U. Köckemann; H. Andreasson; S. Koenig
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Automation in underground mining has the potential to significantly enhance safety, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, effectively coordinating fleets of autonomous vehicles in dynamic mine environments introduces substantial challenges in both optimization and motion planning. To address these challenges, we introduce and formalize the Block Cave Mining (BCM) problem, which focuses on computing a transport plan that maximizes ore throughput while satisfying draw ratio constraints. To solve this problem, we propose SAMM, an eventually optimal anytime solver that jointly integrates task assignment, scheduling, and path planning via a mixed-integer linear programming formulation. To improve scalability, we also introduce SAMMS, a variant of SAMM that trades optimality guarantees for efficiency by decomposing the problem into shorter planning subcycles. Experimental evaluations using realistic industrial mine scenarios demonstrate that SAMMS achieves near-optimal throughput and scales effectively to larger fleets and mine layouts.

title: Stage-Based OPF–DTLR–RL Framework for Wind Curtailment Mitigation Using Shared Autonomous Electric Vehicles
authors: Z. Zhang; J. Teh; Y. Su
venue: 2026 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a stage-based framework for reducing wind curtailment in a transmission corridor with limited export capacity. The method combines weather-driven dynamic thermal line rating (DTLR) with coordinated charging and discharging control of a shared autonomous electric vehicle (SAEV) fleet. A modified IEEE RTS-24 test system with a dominant export bottleneck is used to compare four operating stages, from a static line rating (SLR) baseline to an intelligent fleet controller. The first three stages are evaluated with direct-current optimal power flow (DC-OPF), while the final stage uses a safety-aware reinforcement learning (RL) controller that projects each command to a feasible charging or discharging range. Yearlong simulation results show a substantial reduction in annual curtailed wind energy while maintaining zero simulated thermal-limit violations in the OPF replay validation. The results confirm that weather-aware line ratings and coordinated fleet control provide complementary benefits for wind integration. Annual curtailed wind energy is reduced from 239.7 GWh in the static baseline to 62.9 GWh in the final stage, corresponding to a 73.8% reduction.

title: An Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-Guided Hybrid Planner for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Path Planning in Complex Environments
authors: M. Z. Chaudhary; A. Ahmed; A. Ahmed; M. A. Shaikh; A. Sherif; R. Abdelfattah
venue: SoutheastCon 2026
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are currently essential for disaster response, environmental monitoring, logistics, precision agriculture, and surveillance. UAVs must plan paths that are globally efficient, locally responsive, and kinematically smooth in cluttered, dynamic spaces. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods, especially deep reinforcement learning (DRL), have shown promise in reducing brittle hand-tuning while complementing classical planners such as A*, which remains a reliable global backbone. We introduce a DRL-guided hybrid that supervises an A* global planner and a dynamic window approach (DWA) local navigator by reweighting the A* heuristic, managing waypoint sub-goals, and adaptively tuning DWA's scoring terms from real-time risk features; this learned meta-control replaces fixed gains and outperforms prior A* + DWA fusions and end-to-end DRL by retaining deterministic guarantees while adding context-aware adaptability. Our performance evaluations show that our DRL-guided planner reduces pathfinding runtime by over 55% and total mission time by 24% while preserving safety. Trajectories are markedly smoother, showing a 24.2% reduction in total corner degree, which better matches UAV kinematic constraints. Additionally, we observe consistent improvements in obstacle clearance and fewer evasive dead-ends than a tuned A* + DWA baseline. Replanning latency is lower across all dynamic scenarios, yielding faster recovery from environmental changes.

title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Agentic Artificial Intelligence Framework for Predictive Platform Operations and DevOps Orchestration
authors: S. R. Nimmathi
venue: 2026 7th International Conference On Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing (ICCVBIC)
abstract: Operational Intelligence increasingly needs to be autonomous to deal with scale, complexity, and failure modes that are hard to predict in modern software platforms within a distributed infrastructure. In this paper, we introduce a Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Agentic Artificial Intelligence framework for predictive platform operations and DevOps orchestration that combines model-based and model-free reinforcement learning (Deep Q-Network and Proximal Policy Optimization) with autonomous multi-agent decision making for proactive, self-optimizing IT operations. The framework was tested on a simulated hybrid cloud environment that included 500 virtual nodes for a 90-day period of time and handled about 1.2 million telemetry events. The experimental results prove that the Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) was reduced by 31.6% from an average of 42.6 minutes to 29.1 minutes while the system uptime was slightly improved to 99.61% from 99.21% for conventional automation. Overall, the predictive anomaly detection module enabled a 47.8% decrease in manual interventions and a 18.4% decrease in over-provisioning of resources while forecasting failures up to 15 minutes ahead with a precision of 89.6% and a recall level of 86.3%. Cumulative reward for a hybrid DQN-PPO policy was observed to be around 1.4x higher than the best single-algorithm baseline (DQN) in 1,450 training episodes. The results of this quantitative analysis prove that the synergy of reinforcement learning and agentic AI can have a positive impact on operational efficiency, reliability, and autonomy, paving the way for self-healing and intelligent platform ecosystems for the next generation of enterprise infrastructure.

title: Long-Term Security of Sustainable Infrastructure Under Quantum Threats
authors: A. Gupta; V. K. Polurouthu; S. Mittal; G. Hossain
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
abstract: Sustainable infrastructure increasingly depends on cryptographic trust: distributed energy resources authenticate fleet commands, water utilities protect remote maintenance, transport systems rely on certificate ecosystems, and buildings participate in grid-edge energy services. These systems also have long physical and institutional lifecycles. Assets, supplier relationships, software signing chains, and archived evidence can remain in service for decades, while the public-key assumptions embedded in them may become unsafe once cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers arrive. This paper presents Q-CLAIM, a lifecycle exposure model and prioritization method for post-quantum migration in long-lived sustainable infrastructure. The model extends the usual harvest-now-decrypt-later test by adding the residence time of quantum-vulnerable trust dependencies, migration lead time, safety constraints, and a replaceability factor. We then evaluate the model on a reproducible 28-archetype decision dataset covering electricity, water, transport, buildings, and cross-cutting supplier trust services. The scenario analysis shows that a lifecycle-agility-first strategy reduces the weighted exposure score by 93.7% while avoiding premature replacement of otherwise serviceable assets; a replacement-first strategy reduces exposure slightly further but requires twelve early replacements. The contribution is not a survey or a speculative benchmark. It is a concrete engineering method, a reproducible dataset, and a migration pattern that links post-quantum security with sustainability goals by preserving useful asset life while retiring vulnerable cryptographic dependencies.

title: Deep Multi-AI Agents-Assisted Efficient Telesurgery Framework for Healthcare Communication Systems
authors: D. Singh; M. S. Obaidat; A. Goyal; T. Singh; B. Datt; R. Datt; R. Guptal; S. Tanwar
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computer, Information and Telecommunication Systems (CITS)
abstract: Real-time control, data security, and ultimately patient safety pose significant challenges for telesurgery, especially in the context of remote and underprivileged environments. To address all these challenges, we proposed a multi-agent AI framework. The Visual Monitoring Agent analyzes surgical scenes using CNN-ADAM in real-time, the Cardiac Monitoring Agent detects anomalies based on ECG signals using ViT-RMSProp, and the Instruction Processing Agent interprets commands in natural language using LSTM-Adagrad. Performance evaluation shows an overall accuracy of 96.8% with a response time of about 11.7 milliseconds, that is, 18.5% higher in accuracy and 74% faster in response when compared to existing competing telesurgery systems. The ROC-AUC analysis confirmed the discriminative power of the framework with values higher than 0.98 for all agents. Hence, this framework indicates signigicant advancement in current existing telesurgery systems.

title: Evaluating Agentic AI Systems in Manufacturing: A Review of Taxonomy, Challenges and Future Directions
authors: N. M. Farid; S. Shafiee
venue: 2026 International Conference on Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AAIML)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are rapidly transforming the landscape of intelligent automation by enabling autonomous decision-making, planning, and interaction with complex environments. As these systems grow in capability and complexity, evaluating their performance becomes increasingly critical, yet remains a substantial challenge. In manufacturing, where agentic AI is increasingly applied to tasks such as predictive maintenance and quality control, standardized evaluation frameworks are still lacking. Prior research has proposed structured categories for this purpose in general scope, such as analyzing submodules like tool use, reasoning, memory, and self-learning, or evaluating overall high-level performance. In this paper, we aim to review the evaluation approaches of agentic AI systems, with a specific focus on applications in manufacturing and studies released between 2024-2025 and proposes a three-dimensional taxonomy spanning scope, methodology, and analysis. Reviewing 31 studies, we find evaluations are mostly small-scale proofs of concept with limited metrics, while reliability, safety, and large-scale benchmarking are overlooked. We propose a manufacturing-oriented taxonomy and reporting checklist that synthesize existing evaluation practices into a standardized framework for reproducibility and transparency. Our synthesis highlights gaps and offers guidelines for future industrial pilots.

authors: E. Sojo

abstract: Build, deploy, and monitor AI applications using Microsoft Foundry's unified portal, combining models, workflows, agents, and responsible AI practices into a single development experience. title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A 20-Year Survey of Attacks, Defenses, and Standards
authors: B. Tekeste; K. Al-Hussaeni; B. C. M. Fung; I. Alawadhi; C. Fachkha
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) presents a significant barrier to the large-scale deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in safety-critical environments. While early research focused on algorithmic robustness, the field has evolved into a complex intersection of security, assurance, and policy. This paper presents a comprehensive, multidisciplinary survey of the AML landscape, covering over 250 peer-reviewed contributions. We implement a lifecycle-oriented taxonomy that maps attack vectors and defense mechanisms to specific stages of the AI pipeline from data collection to deployment, expanding the traditional Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) triad to include Governance and Regulation. We identify critical research gaps, including certified robustness for Natural Language Processing (NLP), and emerging threats in Generative AI. To ground these theoretical insights in practice, we analyze five domain-specific case studies: Autonomous Vehicles, Medical AI, Financial Systems, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and the Internet of Things (IoT). Uniquely, this survey bridges the gap between academic literature and industrial practice by mapping technical AML findings to emerging standards, including the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (RMF), MITRE ATLAS, and ISO/IEC 42001. We conclude by providing a roadmap for researchers, practitioners, and regulators to build verifiable, trustworthy, and compliant AI systems.

title: Digital Twin-Assisted Boiler Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance
authors: V. M.S; L. S; H. R; V. S
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: High-performance boilers are indispensable elements of power production and heavy manufacturing. Where efficiency, safety, and reliability are the main factors, industrial boilers come in. The traditional boiler control systems mostly utilized the slow and inaccurate oxygen sensors of the PID-based control mechanism leading to slow response, uneconomical burning, and hence, increased fuel consumption. To overcome these challenges, the project proposes a fault diagnosis system and maintenance of industrial boilers assisted by digital twins. This system encompasses sensor data of real time along with a virtual simulation model using PIC16F877A microcontroller as a data processor and ESP8266 module for cloud connectivity. The digital twin created using Unity3D continues to monitor the boiler's physical condition that helps in spotting faults at their earliest time and provides analysis of predicting without needing to induce any faults in the real world. Therefore, the process will be made safer, more efficient, and less vulnerable to Big Data-enabled, automatic controls. The proposed solution demonstrates the way in which digital twin technology may improve the smart maintenance process in industrial sectors, as well as ecofriendly manufacturing methods.

title: AAS-Driven Architecture for Semantic Interoperability in UAV Communication Networks
authors: M. D. Bampi; P. H. Morgan Pereira; E. P. de Freitas
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence, and Communications Technology (IAICT)
abstract: The increasing deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in collaborative applications, such as precision agriculture and logistics, creates a critical need for reliable, high-quality communication. This is often hindered in heterogeneous fleets by a lack of semantic interoperability, where disparate data models and proprietary protocols hinder safety-critical, coordinated tasks. This paper proposes an Industry 4.0-based Digital Twin-driven architecture using the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) to establish a standardized semantic layer for multi-UAV systems, enabling reliable, protocol-agnostic interoperability. This proposal introduces a multi-UAV architecture that establishes four key communication layers, explicitly modeling the interactions among UAVs, their digital twins, and the Ground Control Station (GCS) to enable standardized, interoperable data exchange across all system domains. A core contribution is the design of a formal UAV Submodel, which acts as a "common language" by standardizing critical data elements, units, identifiers, and semantic references for flight performance, navigation, system health, and communication QoS. The model integrates a semantic gateway concept to bridge common UAV protocols (e.g., MAVLink, ROS) to the AAS. The model and discussion illustrate that the AAS-driven approach provides a feasible semantic layer for runtime multi-UAV systems, while the final communication quality remains dependent on the underlying wireless network. Numerical validation on edge hardware demonstrates the architecture’s feasibility, achieving an average internal translation latency of 0.006 ms and a total end-to-end latency of 8.34 ms with minimal CPU overhead (< 0.8%). The architecture is presented as a robust framework for supporting key application challenges, including decentralized collision avoidance, adaptive QoS-aware networking, and dynamic plug-and-operate fleet management.

title: Power System Restoration Assessment with Restoration Response Disturbance Factors and Social Feedback Coupling
authors: X. Zhang; Y. Yin; G. Zhang; T. Liu; X. Kang
venue: 2026 International Conference on Electrical, Control and Information Technology (ECITech)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that strategy formulation and effect evaluation are separated and the influence of social feedback is ignored in the post-disaster restoration assessment of power systems, this paper proposes a full-process restoration assessment method with the introduction of restoration response disturbance factors. Taking the power grid in restoration and restoration plan as the core assessment objects, the method constructs a three-layer multi-dimensional assessment index system to quantify the restoration service benefits, operation risks, equipment availability, as well as process characteristics such as restoration speed and smoothness. Social feedback is formalized as restoration response disturbance factors; evolutionary game theory is adopted to depict the multi-agent interaction among the government, power grid enterprises, industrial enterprises and residents, and a dynamic satisfaction mechanism driven by social feedback pressure is constructed combined with the SEIR-based emotional communication model, revealing the influence mechanism of social feedback on restoration trajectory. Simulation verification is carried out on the IEEE 39-bus system, and the results show that restoration response disturbance factors will cause a systematic shift in the time and slope of the system's restoration acceleration stage, and the improvement of governance intensity can effectively suppress public opinion pressure and improve restoration performance. The assessment framework constructed in this paper realizes the coupling analysis of social feedback and the physical restoration process of power systems, and provides a quantifiable assessment tool and mechanism support for the formulation of post-disaster restoration strategies.

title: Reasoning-Native Agentic Communication for 6G
authors: H. Seo; J. Seon; J. Young Kim; M. Bennis; W. Choi; D. I. Kim
venue: IEEE Network
abstract: Future 6G networks will interconnect not only devices but autonomous machines that continuously sense, reason, and act. In such settings, communication can no longer be understood solely as delivering bits or preserving semantic meaning: even when two agents interpret the same information correctly, they may behave inconsistently if their internal reasoning processes evolve differently. We call this emerging challenge belief divergence. This article introduces reasoning-native agentic communication, a paradigm in which transmissions are triggered not by channel conditions or data relevance but by predicted misalignment in agents’ internal belief states. We present an architecture that augments the conventional communication stack with a coordination plane grounded in a shared ontology and bounded recursive belief modeling. We further give an operational definition of agentic belief, analyze how its complexity scales with the number of agents and the recursion depth, layer the cognitive plane on top of standardized deterministic safety primitives, and outline a security model addressing cryptographically valid but semantically misleading signals. Through enabling mechanisms and representative multi-agent scenarios, we show how this approach prevents coordination drift across heterogeneous systems and reframes the network as an active harmonizer of distributed autonomous intelligence.

title: Interactive Perception Multimodal Trajectory Prediction for Road Navigation
authors: N. Zhang; Z. Zhang
venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: Accurate pedestrian trajectory prediction is critical for ensuring the safety of autonomous driving and robotic navigation in complex urban environments. However, existing methods often struggle to jointly model environmental context, motion dynamics, and multi-agent interactions, which limits their ability to infer pedestrians' latent movement intentions in highly dynamic scenes. In this paper, we propose Interactive and Intent-aware Multimodal Trajectory Prediction (I2MTP), a unified framework that incorporates neighborhood encoding, interaction-aware heterogeneous graphs, and gaze-driven attention to jointly model pedestrian interactions and motion intentions in a spatiotemporal manner. A hierarchical attention mechanism is employed to capture both local neighborhood dependencies and long-range temporal dynamics, and the model is trained end-to-end using a multi-level loss. Extensive experiments on the CREATTIVE3D dataset demonstrate that I2MTP outperforms existing methods in terms of ADE and FDE, achieving particularly significant improvements in challenging, interaction-rich environments.

title: SwarmRaft: Leveraging Consensus for Robust Drone Swarm Coordination in GNSS-Degraded Environments
authors: K. Dev; Y. Madhwal; S. Shevelo; P. Osinenko; Y. Yanovich
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms are increasingly used in critical applications such as aerial mapping, environmental monitoring, and autonomous delivery. However, the reliability of these systems is highly dependent on uninterrupted access to the Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) signals, which can be disrupted in real-world scenarios due to interference, environmental conditions, or adversarial attacks, causing disorientation, collision risks, and mission failure. This article proposes SwarmRaft, a blockchain-inspired positioning and consensus framework for maintaining coordination and data integrity in UAV swarms operating under GNSS-denied conditions. SwarmRaft leverages the Raft consensus algorithm to enable distributed drones (nodes) to agree on state updates such as location and heading, even in the absence of GNSS signals for one or more nodes. In our prototype, each node uses GNSS and local sensing, and communicates over WiFi in a simulated swarm. Upon signal loss, consensus is used to reconstruct or verify the position of the failed node based on its last known state and trajectory. Our system demonstrates robustness in maintaining swarm coherence and fault tolerance through a lightweight, scalable communication model. This work provides a practical and secure approach for decentralized drone operation in unpredictable environments.

title: On the Stochastic Flocking Dynamics of the Random Discrete Thermodynamic Cucker–Smale Model
authors: S. -Y. Ha; S. Lee; F. Zeng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
abstract: We study the emergent dynamics of the discrete thermodynamic Cucker-Smale (in short, DTCS) model with randomly switching network topologies. The thermodynamic Cucker-Smale (TCS) model corresponds to a generalized CS model with extra internal observables called “temperature”. For isothermal case in which all temperatures are the same constant, it exactly coincides with the CS model for flocking. Motivated by the work of discrete CS model in (Dong et al., 2021), we use a change of variables and reformulate the nonlinear coupling part of the DTCS model to rewrite the transformed system into a matrix form, and then we use an ergodicity coefficient to derive the exponential decay of state diameter functionals. At random switching instants, we choose one of network topologies randomly from the finite universe of network topologies whose union graph contains a spanning tree. Under some sufficient framework formulated in terms of system parameters and coupling weight functions, we show that the DTCS model exhibits a stochastic flocking with a probability one.

title: Asymptotic Tracking for Full-State Coupled Polyhedral Constrained MIMO Nonlinear Systems
authors: B. Li; T. Guan; X. Guan; Y. Song
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Practical safety restrictions in real-world control systems are generally formulated as polyhedral constraints, whereas existing barrier Lyapunov function (BLF)-based control methods only accommodate box-type state limits with decoupled state intervals. Since polyhedral constraint ranges rely on multiple coupled states, conventional BLF schemes cannot handle such complex constraints. This article proposes a novel BLF-based control framework for MIMO nonlinear systems subject to polyhedral full-state restrictions. A dedicated transformation function is first developed to convert the restricted system into an unconstrained counterpart. Combined with a novel coordinate transformation and an adaptive nonlinear filter, the proposed approach eliminates feasibility prerequisites for virtual controllers and relaxes rigid demands on reference signals. Moreover, asymptotic convergence of both tracking and filter errors is strictly guaranteed. Note to Practitioners—This work is motivated by practical control systems whose safety requirements are described by coupled state constraints, such as polyhedral operating regions, rather than simple independent upper and lower bounds on each state. Conventional BLF-based methods are difficult to apply in such cases because they mainly handle box-type constraints and often require restrictive feasibility conditions in the controller design. The proposed method provides an optimization-free tracking control framework for MIMO nonlinear systems with polyhedral full-state safety constraints by transforming the constrained control problem into an unconstrained one, while additional coordinate transformation and adaptive filtering techniques reduce the requirements on virtual controllers and reference signals. Future research will address the control of networked multi-agent systems with polyhedral full-state safety constraints.

title: Key Stability Challenges in Large-Scale TimeDelay Systems and Cloud Control Systems
authors: A. Khalil
venue: 2026 8th Global Power, Energy and Communication Conference (GPECOM)
abstract: The time delay remains one of the main concerns for the stability of control systems. With the recent advances in communication networks and their widespread applications in industry, these issues still require further research. Time-delay systems are control systems in which the rate of change of the system states depends on the previous states. Control via a communication network is becoming increasingly popular. The widespread adoption of low-cost and adaptable communication technologies is the key driving force. Time-delay systems have evolved from conventional large-delay systems, such as ecosystems and biological systems, to networked control systems, and we are now in the era of cloud control systems. These systems are characterised by induced time delays and vulnerability to cyberattacks. Failing to account for them during the design stage can lead to catastrophic consequences. Cloud control systems emerged as a new paradigm for networked control systems and have numerous promising applications. However, because they can be considered large-scale time-delay systems, they pose new challenges. The paper reviews the most common challenges in modelling, stability, and security of timedelay systems, with a focus on cloud control systems.

title: Power Circuit AI: Designing Power Electronic Circuits for Motor Drives with Generative Artificial Intelligence
authors: M. Hetrich; C. K. Sahu; S. Narasimhan; P. K. Chilukuri
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Design and Control of Automation and Drive Systems (IDCD)
abstract: The design of power electronic converters is a multi-physics optimization challenge that has traditionally resisted the high levels of automation seen in digital VLSI. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising interface for capturing high-level design intent, they inherently lack the domain understanding required to generate manufacturing-ready hardware, often resulting in hallucinations and invalid netlists. This paper presents a novel, autonomous multi-agent framework that orchestrates the end-to-end design of power electronic circuits from natural language specifications to clean Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) without fine-tuning the underlying LLMs. The proposed methodology utilizes a constrained environment to bridge the stochastic gap between generative AI and rigid Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. The logical validity of the circuit is ensured by deploying specialized agents for device specification, component selection, SKiDL-based netlist generation, and layout completion. The framework is validated through the autonomous generation of a 400V 3-phase converter for a variable frequency drive. Results demonstrate that while the system achieves 100% logical connectivity and automated routing, transitioning from logical correctness to physics-aware layout optimization and adhering to creepage and clearance requirements remains a critical frontier. The study concludes that pairing LLM agents with deterministic auto routers solves the connectivity problem but requires further integration of physics-based feedback loops to meet the requirements of commutation loop inductance, thermal management, creepage, and clearance requirements. Additionally, it also details the placement limitations within the schematic and flags any components that have not been included.

title: A Foundation Model for Automotive-Grade EV Charging Anomaly Detection via Snippet-Level Attention Learning
authors: J. Chan; H. Pan; Z. Chen; E. Pan
venue: IEEE Transactions on Transportation Electrification
abstract: With the rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), ensuring the safety and reliability of onboard lithium-ion batteries has become a prerequisite for large-scale deployment. Battery anomaly detection, particularly during charging operations, plays a critical role in early warning and risk mitigation. Most existing studies either optimize detection accuracy under narrowly controlled conditions or rely on transfer strategies to adapt a model to a specific new scenario, which limits scalability across fleets and evolving battery ecosystems. Motivated by the growing availability of large-scale EV battery telemetry, we present an automotive-grade, scalable framework that follows a foundation-model-style pretraining paradigm for EV battery anomaly detection. Specifically, we integrate and harmonize two of the largest publicly available vehicle battery telemetry datasets, constructing a large-scale corpus consisting of approximately 1,525,008 charge–discharge snippets from 811 vehicles. On this unified snippet corpus, we develop a foundation model for EV battery anomaly detection that learns transferable normality representations from charge–discharge segments and can be deployed to unseen vehicles and operating conditions. Extensive experiments show that, without any additional fine-tuning, the pretrained model achieves performance comparable to, and in many cases exceeding, strong baselines that are trained specifically for the target domain under unknown conditions. Moreover, lightweight fine-tuning on a new domain consistently yields further improvements while preserving performance on previously seen domains, demonstrating robust extensibility for future battery scenarios. Beyond accuracy, we provide practical interpretability for deployment: by visualizing prediction maps and feature-response patterns, we show that the proposed model can produce heterogeneous, condition-aware outputs and quantify feature contributions under different operating regimes. Overall, this work introduces a scalable cross-domain framework for automotive lithium-ion battery anomaly detection and provides a practical step toward fleet-level monitoring under distribution shifts.

title: Agentic AI Security: Threats, Defenses, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
authors: A. Chhabra; S. Datta; S. K. Nahin; P. Mohapatra
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Agentic AI systems powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) and endowed with planning, tool use, memory, and autonomy are emerging as powerful and flexible platforms for automation. Their ability to autonomously execute tasks across web, software, and physical environments creates new and amplified security risks, distinct from both traditional AI safety and conventional software security. This survey outlines a taxonomy of threats specific to agentic AI, reviews recent benchmarks and evaluation methodologies, and discusses defense strategies from both technical and governance perspectives. We synthesize current research and highlight open challenges, aiming to support the development of secure-by-design agent systems.

title: Hierarchical Pairwise and Group-Wise Interaction Modeling for Efficient Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
authors: J. Zhang; Y. Fan; F. Hui; E. Tan; X. Zhou
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Accurate trajectory prediction in multi-agent environments is fundamental to understanding and forecasting collective motion in complex scenes. However, existing methods often struggle to capture the dynamic nature of interactions and higher-order group relationships. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework that seamlessly integrates pairwise and group-wise interaction modeling. Our approach introduces a Step-wise Pairwise Interaction Modeling (SPIM) module to effectively capture dynamic interaction features over time, and a Hypergraph-based Global Interaction Modeling (HGIM) module to effectively model higher-order group relationships using adaptive hypergraph structures. Through the integration of these complementary modules within a unified multimodal decoder architecture, our method achieves competitive performance on the SDD and ETH-UCY datasets while significantly reducing model complexity. These results highlight the superior efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed approach.

title: Minimizing Acoustic Risk for Endangered Species through Optimized Maritime Patrol Planning in Atlantic Canada
authors: N. Hmid; M. Asghari; H. Afshari
venue: 2026 IEEE Canadian Atlantic Ocean Symposium (CAOS)
abstract: Maritime patrols for search and rescue in the Atlantic region of Canada are critical for the safety of maritime transportation; however, such operations generate underwater noise that causes acoustic masking for cetaceans. In particular, such concerns are critical for the North Atlantic Right Whale which has a high risk of extinction. We propose a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model to resolve this issue, by optimizing dynamic fleet surveillance coverage while strictly limiting noise exposure for sensitive marine mammals. By integrating time-varying accident probabilities with species-specific noise thresholds, the model redistributes vessel traffic to maintain high operational readiness while respecting the life of underwater species. This framework offers a quantitative approach to balancing national security requirements with the preservation of the marine ecosystem. The results show that structured round-trips balance day and night safety, whereas other strategies, such as roaming, leave the ocean unprotected at night. Additionally, innovative solutions such as agile vessel assignment provide the same coverage as heavy ships with significantly less noise pollution.

title: An Intelligent Surveillance System for Smokingrelated Risk Detection in Campus Zones
authors: P. R; S. S; D. K. K; R. K. K; R. R; A. A
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Current fire and smoking detection systems are mostly industrial or generic and rely on the constant surveillance by CCTV or simple smoke detectors, which lead to excessive storage conditions, ineffectiveness, and human surveillance. This paper suggests a smart surveillance system that operates on AI-based video analytics and works in a campus setting. The system can identify smoking behavior live with its analysis of human actions and smoke peculiarities along with a multipletime verification system to reduce false alarms. Only Case approved incident clips are stored which minimizes storage overhead. The system also categorizes the incidents on the Low, Medium, and High risks level depending on sensitivity of location and frequency of detecting behavior. Python sound modules are used to raise audio alerts immediately on high-risk cases and thus open security intervention. The suggested solution will increase the security of the campus, increase the efficiency of monitoring, and provide a scalable and lowcost alternative based on the existing CCTV.

title: Throughput Maximizing Takeoff Scheduling for eVTOL Vehicles in On-Demand Urban Air Mobility Systems
authors: M. Pooladsanj; K. Savla; P. A. Ioannou
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) offers a solution to current traffic congestion by using electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) vehicles to provide on-demand air mobility in urban areas. Effective traffic management is crucial for efficient operation of UAM systems, especially for high-demand scenarios. In this paper, we present a centralized framework for conflict-free takeoff scheduling of eVTOLs in on-demand UAM systems. Specifically, we provide a scheduling policy, called VertiSync, which jointly schedules UAM vehicles for servicing trip requests and rebalancing, subject to safety margins and energy requirements. We characterize the system-level throughput of VertiSync, which determines the demand threshold at which the average waiting time transitions from being stable to being increasing over time. We show that the proposed policy maximizes throughput for sufficiently large fleet size and if the UAM network has a certain symmetry property. We demonstrate the performance of VertiSync through a case study for the city of Los Angeles, and show that it significantly reduces average passenger waiting time compared to a first-come first-serve scheduling policy.

title: A Human-in-the-Loop and Explainable AI Framework for Decision Support in Battery Lifecycle Management Using Digital Battery Passports
authors: T. D. Welage; K. D. D. S. Jayasekara; U. A. D. P. Gunawardena; L. S. W. Samarathunga
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence (ICHCAI)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are central to electrified transport and renewable energy systems, yet evaluating their sustainability under real operating conditions remains challenging. Conventional life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches rely on static assumptions, generic datasets, and nominal performance values, limiting their ability to support timely and contextaware decision-making across battery use, second-life deployment, remanufacturing, and end-of-life management. These limitations are particularly critical in industrial settings where human actors must make safety-, sustainability-, and valuesensitive decisions under uncertainty. This paper proposes a human-centric Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for dynamic LCA based on a Digital Battery Passport (DBP) architecture that integrates real-time operational data into environmental assessment and decision support. The system treats the passport as a continuously evolving digital entity that ingests telemetry from the Battery Management System (BMS), interfaces with enterprise systems, and updates environmental indicators through a Digital Twin (DT) environment. AI-enabled analytics interpret degradation behavior, estimate State of Health (SoH), detect anomalies, and generate explainable recommendations for human stakeholders such as fleet operators, sustainability managers, remanufacturing engineers, and recyclers. A dynamic functional unit based on cumulative delivered energy is introduced to replace static capacity-based metrics, enabling a more realistic representation of battery performance over time. The framework supports continuous recalculation of carbon footprint and related environmental indicators, while preserving human oversight through transparent indicators, role-based access, and auditable event logging. Use cases are demonstrated for firstlife operation, second-life classification, and end-of-life pathway selection. The results show that integrating DBP, DT infrastructure, and explainable AI establishes a scalable foundation for human-centered environmental intelligence in the circular battery economy. The challenges include trust, interpretability, data governance, interoperability, SME adoption barriers, and uncertainty in battery health estimation. The proposed approach positions dynamic LCA not only as an automation tool, but as a human-in-the-loop AI system for critical sustainability decisionmaking.

title: Real-Time Fault Detection for Power Inverter
authors: T. S. Kumar; M. N. Kumar; R. Naveenkumar; N. Naveen
venue: 2026 Second International Conference on Multi-Agent Systems for Collaborative Intelligence (ICMSCI)
abstract: This paper showcases an IoT-enabled monitoring and real-time fault detection system for the safety, reliability, and remote supervision of power inverters. The design and implementation of this system are provided. The system consists of a T-Bridge PWM 4027 inverter circuit, which is controlled by an Arduino Nano microcontroller; an ESP8266 Wi-Fi module to allow for connectivity to the cloud; and a DHT11 temperature sensor for continuously monitoring the temperature of the inverter. The inverter is used to convert direct current from a 12V battery to alternating current (AC) to supply a 50W load. The charging circuit for recharging the battery from the AC mains is comprised of a D15XB bridge rectifier. If there is a power outage, the inverter will supply AC power to the load from the stored DC power in the battery. In this way, the load is guaranteed to continue functioning without interruption. The Arduino Nano continuously monitors various parameters (conditions), including temperature, current, voltage, and energy consumed, and will trigger an immediate alarm by flashing a red LED installed on the inverter board if any of these parameters fall outside of their normal range. Additionally, all real-time parameters that the Arduino Nano monitors are displayed locally on a 16 × 2 LCD and sent to the cloud-based industrial IoT Dashboard through the ESP8266 module. The cloud-based IoT Dashboard allows the user to view real-time data on voltage, current, temperature, humidity, power, and a timestamp in a visually comprehensive format and can be accessed from anywhere.

title: Ai SecureDataGuard: A Big Data Security, Privacy-Preserving and Visualization System for LLM-Powered Smart Homes
authors: J. Zhou; H. Li; F. Wang
venue: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering (ICBDSE)
abstract: Now large language models and that multi-agent frameworks are widely used, platforms like MOSS can let users talk to smart homes naturally and link up all kinds of household devices. But there’s a slew of tough issues hindering these products from practical commercial application IoT data from every device, constant user privacy leaks, intentional prompt injection and safety guardrail evasion attacks, plus no tool to monitor all risks instantly.For the resolution of all aforementioned drawbacks, I built a complete big data security framework named SecureDataGuard. It packs malicious input screening, differential privacy, federated lightweight anomaly tracking and real-time data visual monitoring into one set of tools. I built the whole system on top of MOSS AI’s multi-agent structure, and also adopted mature industrial AI security tools from Anquan Data Intelligence.First, I made a two-step intent recognition algorithm to block prompt injection and jailbreak attempts. Second, I put together a mixed privacy protection scheme, so we can use data normally without exposing raw user information. I also developed a slimmed-down Transformer model called LADT to catch abnormal device behaviors the second they happen. On top of that, I built a monitoring panel with StarRocks and ECharts, so administrators can track every risk across bird’s-eye view of the whole system.A large set of empirical experiments was implemented with real-world smart home operation records to corroborate the system’s performance.. Encouraging results are observed in our experiments. The system accurately recognizes user commands with an accuracy rate of 97.8%.Identifies anomalous activity within 18 ms and lowers privacy leakage probability by 92%. All 18 key security metrics on the dashboard update within milliseconds. This work delivers a practical, deployable technical solution to handle smart home data safety, privacy risks, Anomalous Event Detection and Visual Risk Control

title: Mathematical Modeling of Combined Vessel Loading-Unloading Operations by a Group of Quay Cranes in a Stochastic Environment
authors: V. Shchyrba; T. Pylypiuk; M. Shynkaryk
venue: 2026 16th International Conference on Advanced Computer Information Technologies (ACIT)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of integrated resource management at a container terminal under conditions of high vessel handling intensity. A multifactor mathematical model for synchronizing a group of quay cranes operating on shared rails is developed and theoretically substantiated. Unlike existing solutions, the model integrates dynamic nonintersection constraints and ground transport fleet capacity with real-time vessel hydrostatics and stability parameters within a single multi-stream architecture. This optimization ensures that high-intensity combined loading and unloading operations strictly adhere to safety margins for the vessel's vertical center of gravity, heel, and trim. Special attention is paid to the concept of “vertical slot”, where optimizing the order of access to the vessel's cells minimizes idle movements of the crane trolley. The model's study based on three cranes confirmed the possibility of reducing the total vessel handling time and minimizing ballast water pumping requirements. This is achieved by eliminating mutual locking of equipment, preventing violations of the vessel's stability and equalizing the load on the terminal's logistics network. The proposed approach improves coordination efficiency of quay crane operations, reduces idle time, and enhances overall terminal throughput, demonstrating its practical applicability for decision support in container terminal management under uncertainty.

title: Flexible Prescribed-Time Optimal Control With Adaptive State--Input Constraint Bounds via Actor--Critic Learning
authors: J. Tan; S. Xue; H. Cao; B. Chen
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
abstract: This article develops a prescribed-time (PT) optimal tracking framework for nonlinear systems with concurrent state and input constraints. The main focus is a flexible PT constraint-handling mechanism that is introduced first in the design: a time-varying auxiliary function performs PT error transformation, while a state-triggered adaptation law adjusts state/input performance envelopes online. Specifically, the envelopes are relaxed only when constraint violation risk is detected and are otherwise kept tight, which reduces the conservatism of fixed-boundary designs, enlarges feasible operation regions, and preserves safety margins. Based on the resulting unconstrained error dynamics, to achieve optimality within this framework, an actor–critic adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) scheme is constructed to solve the nonautonomous Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation online, guaranteeing user-assigned convergence accuracy and time independently of initial conditions. Rigorous analysis proves uniform ultimate boundedness of all closed-loop signals and PT convergence of the tracking error. Simulations on a general nonlinear system and a fault-tolerance tracking scenario, with comparisons to representative baselines under different initial conditions, verify the proposed method’s superior transient tracking and reliable convergence-time performance.

title: The First Step — Building an Artificial Society
authors: X. Xue; F. -Y. Wang
venue: Computational Experiments: A Bridge between Artificial Intelligence and Social Sciences
abstract: Summary This chapter analyzes the model characteristics of artificial societies, including agent heterogeneity, bounded rationality, learning and evolution, and interactive behaviors. It proposes a hierarchical modeling framework for artificial societies, including four layers: autonomous characteristics, evolutionary characteristics, interactive characteristics, and emergent characteristics. The agent model is the core of artificial society modeling and also a container for different intelligent knowledge to function. The heterogeneity of agents includes two aspects: attribute heterogeneity and behavioral heterogeneity. Agent interaction is the fundamental mechanism leading to “emergence.” Social network analysis uses formally defined graph‐theoretic methods to rigorously quantify relational patterns among social entities, aiding the understanding of various social phenomena. The integration of agent‐based model and machine learning is primarily reflected in two layers: policy agent and role agent. The chapter also presents a case study on intelligent logistics system. The intelligent logistics system can provide personalized solutions for complex transportation demands.

title: AMOVFLY: Enabling Advanced UAV Modeling With the Comprehensive Flight Status Dataset
authors: M. Lee; Y. Hu; Y. Zhu; F. Han; Y. Liu; C. Ran; X. Zhou; Z. Li; Y. Pan; J. Chen; Y. Yao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed as mobile nodes in intelligent transportation systems (ITS), facilitating traffic monitoring, emergency response, and urban air mobility. These applications demand precise modeling of UAV behavior and energy efficiency under diverse real-world traffic and environmental conditions. However, existing datasets often overlook crucial aspects such as UAV flight dynamics and multi-UAV collaboration in complex airspace. To bridge this gap, we introduce AMOVFLY, a comprehensive UAV flight status dataset captured from multiple AMOVLAB UAV platforms. AMOVFLY offers substantial improvements over existing datasets: agile heterogeneous devices, comprehensive and extended flight records, diverse flight conditions (including fixed and dynamic altitude/speed profiles), and synchronized multi-UAV flight data under uniform environmental conditions. These features provide a rich foundation for developing predictive models such as Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) to support energy consumption forecasting, multi-agent coordination, and adaptive flight control—key challenges in transportation-oriented UAV deployments, such as aerial logistics and traffic surveillance. Our evaluation further quantifies the fragility of static models against real-world dynamics. This finding underscores the critical need for online updates and robust trajectory planning to ensure reliable energy prediction and mission safety in dynamic ITS environments. AMOVFLY thus opens new avenues for improving UAV mission planning, energy prediction, and time-series forecasting in complex, real-world transportation environments. Dataset page can be found at https://github.com/YujiaoHu/AMOVFLY-Dataset

title: Lifelong Learner: Discovering Versatile Neural Solvers for Vehicle Routing Problems
authors: S. Feng; Z. Lin; J. Zhou; C. Zhang; J. Li; K. -W. Chen; S. Jayavelu; Y. -S. Ong
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Deep learning has been increasingly adopted in intelligent transportation systems (ITS) to address vehicle routing problems (VRPs) that arise in real-world operations such as fleet management, urban logistics, and dynamic dispatching. However, most neural solvers are trained to tackle VRP instances in a relatively monotonous context, e.g., simplifying VRPs by using Euclidean distance between nodes and adhering to a single problem size, which harms their off-the-shelf application in different scenarios. To enhance their versatility, this paper presents a novel lifelong learning framework that incrementally trains a neural solver to manage VRPs in distinct contexts. Specifically, we propose a lifelong learner (LL), exploiting a Transformer network as the backbone, to solve a series of VRPs. The inter-context self-attention mechanism is proposed within LL to transfer the knowledge obtained from solving preceding VRPs into the succeeding ones. On top of that, we develop a dynamic context scheduler (DCS), employing the cross-context experience replay to further facilitate LL looking back on the attained policies of solving preceding VRPs. Extensive results on synthetic and benchmark instances (problem sizes up to 18k) show that our LL is capable of discovering effective policies for tackling generic VRPs in varying contexts. The source code is available: https://github.com/fsdfsd123/Lifelong-Learner-Discovering-More-Versatile-Neural-Solvers-for-Routing-Problems.

title: Boundary Adjustment-Based Global State Constraints Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems with Novel Event-Triggered Input
authors: B. Wang; C. Hua; H. Li; R. Cui
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The arbitrary specification of constraint boundaries in existing full-state constraints control methodologies may render the constrained states not capable of covering the uncertain terms, which leads to the state constraint incompatibility. Besides, these approaches can only obtain semiglobal stability results due to the initial value limitations and the utilization of the filter. To surmount the above challenges, this paper develops a global and low complexity state constraints control algorithm for uncertain nonlinear systems via boundary adjustment. First, we constrain the state variables directly by integrating two time-varying functions, i.e., dynamic tuning function (DTF) and prescribed-time funnel function (PTFF), into the state transformation function. Then, a monitoring signal is designed to assess whether the system is at risk of divergence owing to the constraint incompatibility. Specifically, the DTF aims to tune the constraint boundaries of state variables when the monitoring signal detects that the system enters the collision avoidance zone to guarantee the fundamental system stability and tracking performance. While the PTFF serves to remove the initial value restriction conditions of the tracking error and state variables. Moreover, a new periodic coded event-triggered mechanism (PCETM) is proposed, which transmits l-bit digital numbers over the network channel to save communication bit resources, and avoids the excessive system energy consumption due to continuous monitoring of the triggering condition. Finally, the simulation results substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

title: Dual-Axis Benchmark and Preventive Scaffold: Surfacing and Mitigating Silent Risks in LLM Data Preparation
authors: M. Chen; S. Arifuzzaman
venue: 2026 25th International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications (ICMLA)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents working on raw, heterogeneous data may fail silently when they act on upstream assumptions that turn out to be wrong. Existing evaluations rarely surface this risk, benchmarking on clean, pre-identified inputs; agentic frameworks respond by layering self-critique or multi-agent debate above the executor. We introduce DiscRun-Bench, a benchmark whose family/variant design decomposes hazard discovery from hazard-aware execution and scores data correctness separately from caveat-surfacing diligence. We then treat PRVR (Plan-Run-Verify-Resolve), a scaffold imitating industry-standard plan-execute-verify scaffold, as a measurement probe. Structuring Claude Haiku 4.5’s operating loop to ask about hazards lifts its caveat-surfacing rate from around 0.74 to 0.90 and its mean task score by roughly 25%, both significant under paired permutation tests. Attribution assigns the gain to the preventive Plan stage and to delivery-layer robustness, not to the reactive self-critique retry. PRVR-Haiku meets or exceeds a bare Sonnet 4.6 reference at roughly 4× lower per-task list-price cost, decomposing into a 3× per-token price ratio and a roughly 1.35× grid-mean token ratio driven by a few high-token cells. Silent failure in LLM data preparation is thus substantially an elicitation problem rather than only a capability problem.

title: Lightweight Defense Against Data Consistency Attacks in Distributed DC Optimal Power Flow
authors: M. M. Islam; M. Ismail; H. Kurban; X. Huo; E. Serpedin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Distributed DC optimal power flow (DC-OPF) is increasingly adopted in multi-region power systems to scale power-flow optimization across regions while preserving local data privacy. However, this multi-agent architecture also creates new attack surfaces, where Byzantine or data-consistency adversaries can tamper with exchanged messages and quietly steer the system toward unfair and inefficient operating points. Fully distributed DC-OPF mitigates such threats with blockchain, but its peer-to-peer (P2P) messaging incurs $O(n^{2})$ communication complexity and prohibitive consensus latency, making it unsuitable for iterative optimization. Coordinator-based DC-OPF avoids blockchain but typically relies on P2P cross-verification for data consistency, which again results in quadratic overhead. To ensure data integrity, freshness, and consistency in distributed DC-OPF while retaining $O(n)$ communication complexity for normal operations, this paper proposes a lightweight security framework that can perfectly detect Byzantine manipulation without any P2P cross-checking. The method integrates a modified Schnorr protocol over elliptic curve cryptography into a coordinator-based architecture, enabling secure and efficient consensus at each iteration. Simulations on the IEEE 118-bus system show that, for a 10-region power system, the proposed secure DC-OPF converges in only 45 iterations and 21 s, whereas the blockchain-based alternative requires 439 iterations and 36.6 min. By combining robust security with low computational and bandwidth overhead, the framework provides a scalable and practical solution for real-time secure distributed DC-OPF. Note to Practitioners—Modern cyber-physical power systems increasingly rely on distributed DC optimal power flow (DC-OPF) to coordinate multiple control areas and clear electricity markets in real time. In these settings, economic efficiency and fairness depend on the integrity of the iterative messages that determine generator dispatch and locational marginal prices (LMPs). A compromised insider or man-in-the-middle adversary can quietly send inconsistent signals to different regions, pushing the system away from cost-minimizing dispatch, distorting LMPs, and shifting profits between market participants, even though the optimization appears to converge and all physical constraints are met. This work proposes a lightweight security layer that can be integrated on top of an existing coordinator-based DC-OPF or market-clearing system. Using digital signature aggregation, agents collectively verify at each iteration that they have received the same global update and that messages are fresh and authentic. When a discrepancy is detected, the framework triggers a simple recovery phase based on majority voting over received updates. From a market economics perspective, this helps preserve socially optimal dispatch and prices, mitigates unfair profit reallocation, and reduces the risk that subtle cyber manipulation leads to inefficient global variables. The protocol is implemented as middleware between the optimization engine and the communication layer, requiring no changes to the underlying DC-OPF formulation or pricing rules. One limitation of the proposed framework is its reliance on a single coordinator; future work will explore designs with multiple coordinators.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Control Systems With Time Delays: A Comprehensive Survey
authors: A. Alves Neto
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: In the last decade, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in the control and decision-making of complex dynamical systems. However, most RL algorithms rely on the Markov Decision Process assumption, which is violated in practical cyber-physical systems affected by sensing delays, actuation latencies, and communication constraints. Such time delays introduce memory effects that can significantly degrade performance and compromise stability, particularly in networked and multi-agent environments. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of RL methods designed to address time delays in control systems. We first formalize the main classes of delays and analyze their impact on the Markov property. We then systematically categorize existing approaches into five major families: state augmentation and history-based representations, recurrent policies with learned memory, predictor-based and model-aware methods, robust and domain-randomized training strategies, and safe RL frameworks with explicit constraint handling. For each family, we discuss underlying principles, practical advantages, and inherent limitations. A comparative analysis highlights key trade-offs among these approaches and provides practical guidelines for selecting suitable methods under different delay characteristics and safety requirements. Finally, we identify open challenges and promising research directions, including stability certification, large-delay learning, multi-agent communication co-design, and standardized benchmarking. This survey aims to serve as a unified reference for researchers and practitioners developing reliable RL-based controllers in delay-affected cyber-physical systems.

title: Architectural Resilience in AI-Driven Decision Systems under Adversarial Conditions
authors: V. Ragupathy
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on AI in Cybersecurity (ICAIC)
abstract: The Self-Healing AI Architecture shows that resilient cognitive layers improve multi-agent AI systems' stability, autonomy and dependability. The method decreases recovery latency, cross-agent failure propagation and accuracy retention across failure scenarios with minimal operating overhead. Structured recovery patterns such as Semantic Checkpointing, Cognitive Rollback, Quarantine Isolation and Adaptive Consensus Reset enable systematic reasoning-level degradations, and empirical validation across 20 cooperative agents proves the architecture's scalability and enterprise suitability. These findings emphasise cognitive-layer robustness for reliable agentic AI. Several architectural upgrades are planned. In predictive fault models, time-series analysis and anomaly detection may enable proactive recovery before reasoning fails. Reinforcement learning–based optimisation may choose experience-based recovery approaches under changing situations. Vision, reinforcement learning, and symbolic agents enhance application beyond LLM-based agents. Cognitive-layer, infrastructure-level resilience, and formal verification may improve large-scale deployment accuracy and safety.

title: Networked Functional Interval Observation With Output Compensation and Event-Triggered Updates
authors: M. Zhang; J. Huang; X. Zhao; X. Liu
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper proposes a resource-aware networked output-compensation–based event-triggered functional interval observer for uncertain nonlinear systems. Unlike conventional event-triggered interval-observer schemes that rely on periodic or continuously available measurements, we consider energy-limited sensing, where outputs are transmitted only at triggering instants. To mitigate the loss of output information over inter-event intervals, a dynamic weighting parameter is constructed from the estimated state bounds and the available output information, which effectively enhances interval tightness under sparse updates. In addition, compensation residuals are explicitly embedded into the event-triggered rule, ensuring the compensator remains effective despite intermittent transmissions and avoiding performance degradation caused by outdated compensation signals. Moreover, the proposed functional interval observer is developed within an ${H}_{\infty } /{L}_{\infty } $ framework to estimate functional state bounds while attenuating the impact of external disturbances in networked operation. Finally, simulation studies including a benchmark numerical example and two practical engineering examples demonstrate that the proposed method achieves tighter interval estimation and more accurate output reconstruction than existing event-triggered interval-observer schemes under reduced communication load. Note to Practitioners—In many automation and cyber–physical platforms, measurements are transmitted over energy-limited channels and are therefore intermittent rather than continuously available. This paper presents a practical interval estimation method that combines an output compensator with an event-triggered functional interval observer, enabling reliable state monitoring with reduced communication load. The main idea is to transmit updates only when a trigger condition is violated, while a dynamic weighting mechanism uses the latest transmitted output together with current bound estimates to reduce information loss between events. Practitioners can tune the triggering threshold to balance communication rate and estimation tightness. In addition, the compensator residual term in the triggering condition helps avoid performance degradation caused by outdated compensation signals. The method is well suited to safety monitoring, fault detection, and constraint handling, where guaranteed bounds are preferred to point estimates. The design is developed for bounded-disturbance settings and is most effective when such bounds are available for tuning and verification.
