title: CoPlanner: An Interactive Motion Planner with Contingency-Aware Diffusion for Autonomous Driving
authors: R. Zhong; R. Yao; P. Liu; X. Chen; R. Yang; J. Ma
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Accurate trajectory prediction and motion planning are crucial for autonomous driving systems to navigate safely in complex, interactive environments characterized by multimodal uncertainties. However, current generation-then-evaluation frameworks typically construct multiple plausible trajectory hypotheses but ultimately adopt a single most likely outcome, leading to overconfident decisions and a lack of fallback strategies that are vital for safety in rare but critical scenarios. Moreover, the usual decoupling of prediction and planning modules could result in socially inconsistent or unrealistic joint trajectories, especially in highly interactive traffic. To address these challenges, we propose a contingency-aware diffusion planner (CoPlanner), a unified framework that jointly models multi-agent interactive trajectory generation and contingency-aware motion planning. Specifically, the pivot-conditioned diffusion mechanism anchors trajectory sampling on a validated, shared short-term segment to preserve temporal consistency, while stochastically generating diverse long-horizon branches that capture multimodal motion evolutions. In parallel, we design a contingency-aware multi-scenario scoring strategy that evaluates candidate ego trajectories across multiple plausible long-horizon evolution scenarios, balancing safety, progress, and comfort. This integrated design preserves feasible fallback options and enhances robustness under uncertainty, leading to more realistic interaction-aware planning. Extensive closed-loop experiments on the nuPlan benchmark demonstrate that CoPlanner consistently surpasses state-of-the-art methods on both Val14 and Test14 datasets, achieving significant improvements in safety and comfort under both reactive and nonreactive settings. The source code is available on GitHub1.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Unmanned Control Systems: A Concise Review from a Control-Loop-Centered Perspective
authors: J. Wang
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Unmanned Systems and Technology (UST)
abstract: Unmanned control systems, such as unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles, unmanned surface vehicles, and related robotic platforms, increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to improve autonomy in dynamic and uncertain environments. However, existing survey literature is often organized around specific platforms, tasks, or model families, making it difficult to obtain a compact system-level understanding of how AI contributes to different stages of the autonomy loop of unmanned systems. In this paper, we provide a concise review of AI-enabled unmanned control systems from a control-loop-centered perspective. Specifically, we organize the literature into four tightly connected aspects: perception and scene understanding; estimation, prediction, and planning; learning-enhanced control and collaboration; and safety and trustworthiness. Rather than aiming for exhaustive coverage, this review highlights the functional role of AI across the autonomy pipeline and summarizes key design trade-offs under practical constraints such as real-time computation, domain shift, and deployment reliability. We further discuss major challenges and promising research directions, including hybrid AI-control integration, trustworthy autonomy, and scalable multi-agent intelligence. This paper provides a compact reference for understanding how AI is reshaping unmanned control systems from isolated intelligent modules to integrated autonomous decision-making loops.

title: BIND-USBL: Bounding IMU Navigation Drift Using USBL in Heterogeneous ASV-AUV Teams
authors: P. Kedia; R. Makam; H. Hamann; S. Sundaram
venue: OCEANS 2026 Sanya
abstract: Accurate and continuous localization of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in GPS-denied environments is a persistent challenge in marine robotics. In the absence of external position fixes, AUVs rely on inertial dead-reckoning, which accumulates unbounded drift due to sensor bias and noise. This paper presents BIND-USBL, a cooperative localization framework in which a fleet of Autonomous Surface Vessels (ASVs) equipped with Ultra-Short Baseline (USBL) acoustic positioning systems provides intermittent fixes to bound AUV dead-reckoning error. The key insight is that long-duration navigation failure is driven not by the accuracy of individual USBL measurements, but by the temporal sparsity and geometric availability of those fixes. BIND-USBL combines a multi-ASV formation model linking survey scale and anchor placement to acoustic coverage, a conflict-graph-based TDMA uplink scheduler for shared-channel servicing, and delayed fusion of received USBL updates with drift-prone dead reckoning. The framework is evaluated in the HoloOcean simulator using heterogeneous ASV-AUV teams executing lawnmower coverage missions. The results show that localization performance is shaped by the interaction of survey scale, acoustic coverage, team composition, and ASV-formation geometry. Further, The spatial-reuse scheduler improves perAUV fix delivery rate without violating the no-collision constraint, while maintaining low end-to-end fix latency.

title: Autonomous Driving at Unsignalized Intersections: A Review of Decision-Making Challenges and Reinforcement Learning-Based Solutions
authors: M. Al-Sharman; L. Edes; B. Sun; V. Jayakumar; H. Tahir; M. A. Daoud; B. J. Emran; D. Rayside; W. Melek
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Autonomous driving at unsignalized intersections is still considered a challenging application for machine learning due to the complications associated with handling complex multi-agent scenarios characterized by a high degree of uncertainty. Automating the decision-making process in these safety-critical environments involves comprehending multiple levels of abstraction associated with learning robust driving behaviors to enable the vehicle to navigate efficiently. In this survey, we aim at exploring the state-of-the-art techniques implemented for decision-making applications, with a focus on algorithms that combine Reinforcement Learning (RL) and deep learning for learning traversing policies at unsignalized intersections. The reviewed schemes vary in the proposed driving scenario, in the assumptions made for the used intersection model, in the tackled challenges, and in the learning algorithms that are used. We have presented comparisons for these techniques to highlight their limitations and strengths. Based on our in-depth investigation, it can be discerned that a robust decision-making scheme for navigating real-world unsignalized intersection has yet to be developed. Along with our analysis and discussion, we recommend potential research directions encouraging the interested players to tackle the highlighted challenges. By adhering to our recommendations, decision-making architectures that are both non-overcautious and safe, yet feasible, can be trained and validated in real-world unsignalized intersections environments. Note to Practitioners—Navigating unsignalized intersections is one of the most challenging aspects of urban autonomous driving, directly linked to high accident rates and inefficiencies in road traffic. This paper surveys decision-making strategies for autonomous vehicles at such intersections, aiming to bridge the gap between theoretical advancements and real-world applications. Traditional rule-based decision-making and optimization techniques can be effective in predictable scenarios but often fail in environments with high uncertainty and dynamic multi-agent interactions. Reinforcement learning (RL)-based methods, while promising in their ability to learn from experience and adapt to complex environments, still face significant challenges. These include ensuring safety-critical behavior, achieving real-time performance, and bridging the simulation-to-reality gap. For practitioners in the autonomous driving and robotics industries, this survey provides a practical guide to evaluating existing decision-making approaches, their potential for deployment, and their limitations. It highlights key considerations such as computational efficiency, scalability, and robustness required for urban driving scenarios. The discussion also emphasizes the importance of integrating diverse data sources and testing solutions in real-world environments to ensure reliability. By leveraging the insights presented in this survey, practitioners can better assess and refine algorithms to tackle the nuanced challenges of unsignalized intersections. This work serves as a foundational step towards developing more robust, adaptable, and safe decision-making systems for autonomous vehicles in such complex urban environments.

title: Adaptive Control and Optimization Strategies for Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems in Dynamic Environments
authors: S. Raj; A. Jain; H. Singh Pokhariya; V. Roy; S. D. K. A; P. Ediga
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Big Data & Machine Learning (ICBDML)
abstract: The Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are increasingly found to be working in dynamic, unknown environment which old statical control policies cannot achieve real-time performance and safety expectations. In this paper, a conceptual framework that combines adaptive control, online optimization, and predictive intelligence as a measure to enhance the autonomy and robustness of CPS is provided. The suggested framework uses state estimation that is dynamic, feedback loops that are context-dependent as well as the multi-objective optimization aiming to maintain system behavior under different environmental and operational bottlenecks. The hybrid learning mechanism, that is the combination of the model-based controllers with data-driven policy adaptation, allows the rapid convergence, resistance to the disturbances, and decreased computational load. Also, it is decentralized and has a coordination layer that allows scalable decision-making during multi-agent CPS deployments. The technology uses adaptation that is aware of anomalies to ensure continued activity of missions in the face of cascading failures. This research gives the technical basis of developing CPS with the type of self-configuration, real-time optimization and dependable performance under changing environments, a route towards future generations of intelligent and resilient autonomous infrastructures.

title: LeJOT-AutoML: LLM-Driven Feature Engineering for Job Execution Time Prediction in Databricks Cost Optimization
authors: L. Ma; Y. -X. Hu; Y. Ren; F. Wu; X. -Y. Li
venue: IEEE INFOCOM 2026 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications
abstract: Databricks job orchestration systems (e.g., LeJOT) reduce cloud costs by selecting low-priced compute configurations while meeting latency and dependency constraints. Accurate execution-time prediction under heterogeneous instance types and non-stationary runtime conditions is therefore critical. Existing pipelines rely on static, manually engineered features that under-capture runtime effects (e.g., partition pruning, data skew, and shuffle amplification), and predictive signals are scattered across logs, metadata, and job scripts—lengthening update cycles and increasing engineering overhead. We present LeJOT-AutoML, an agent-driven AutoML framework that embeds large language model agents throughout the ML lifecycle. LeJOT-AutoML combines retrieval-augmented generation over a domain knowledge base with a Model Context Protocol toolchain (log parsers, metadata queries, and a read-only SQL sandbox) to analyze job artifacts, synthesize and validate feature-extraction code via safety gates, and train/select predictors. This design materializes runtime-derived features that are difficult to obtain through static analysis alone. On enterprise Databricks workloads, LeJOT-AutoML generates over 200 features and reduces the feature-engineering and evaluation loop from weeks to 20–30 minutes, while maintaining competitive prediction accuracy. Integrated into the LeJOT pipeline, it enables automated continuous model updates and achieves 19.01% cost savings in our deployment setting through improved orchestration.

title: DADTP: An Autonomous Driving Trajectory Planning Model Based On A Large-scale Language Model
authors: G. Jiang; Z. Li; H. Yang; J. Sang; P. Shi
venue: 2026 International Conference on Robotics, Automation and Intelligent Transportation Systems (RAITS)
abstract: Existing end-to-end planning faces insufficient semantic-geometric alignment, poor adaptability to adverse environments, and inadequate modeling of safety-critical risks and dynamic interactions under linguistic conditions, leading to instability in complex scenarios. To address these issues, we propose DADTP, an end-to-end trajectory planning visual language model built upon an open-source large-scale language model backbone. DADTP generates safe and accurate trajectories by integrating camera-LiDAR fused 3D data, egovehicle state cues, and natural language driving instructions. We introduce a task-oriented hierarchical cross-modal alignment strategy: extracting scenario-specific tokens (hazardous scene, road structure, dynamic interaction) via dedicated perception modules, then projecting these structured 3D representations onto a shared latent semantic space. Additionally, we embed a traffic agent-scene-self interaction mechanism and an auxiliary agent trajectory prediction task into the autoregressive decoder, enabling explicit modeling of geometric dependencies and multiagent interactions. Evaluation results from nuScenes indicate that DADTP attains competitive performance across planning and driving VQA benchmarks, supporting the feasibility of scaling open-source large language model-empowered vision-language systems to end-to-end autonomous driving scenarios.

title: Privacy-Preserving Road Condition Classification from Wheel-Hub Inertial Sensing using Federated Deep Learning
authors: M. N. A. Ramadan; H. Saygin; M. Alkhedher
venue: 2026 10th International Artificial Intelligence and Data Processing Symposium (IDAP)
abstract: Timely knowledge of pavement condition is central to road maintenance planning and to the comfort and safety functions of modern vehicles. Most data-driven approaches pool trips from many vehicles into one model, forcing drivers to surrender raw motion and location traces that are both privacy-sensitive and commercially valuable. We present a wheel-hub inertial sensing platform and a federated learning pipeline that lets a small fleet jointly train a road-roughness classifier while every vehicle keeps its raw data on board. The sensor, a low-cost 9-axis IMU with GNSS, bolts to the wheel hub and records tri-axial acceleration during normal driving. Three vehicles each drove their own route through the same urban district (25,893 logged samples), giving 2,503 two-second windows with weakly-supervised roughness labels (Smooth/Moderate/Rough) from a speed-normalised vibration index. Statistical testing on non-overlapping windows confirms that the classes separate on spectral evidence the labelling index never saw. A compact one-dimensional convolutional network trained with Federated Averaging reaches 85.1% accuracy, within 3.8 points of the privacy-blind centralised model and clearly above the 79.5% obtained when a single vehicle's model is asked to serve the rest of the fleet. Under matched conditions this plain averaging proves as accurate as the heterogeneity-aware optimisers FedProx, SCAFFOLD and FedNova. Collaborative, privacy-preserving road assessment is thus feasible with inexpensive hardware.

title: Dynamic Programming-Based Fractional-Order Compound Steering Control for Lateral Stabilization of DDEVs With Closed-Loop Game
authors: X. Wang; T. Liu; P. K. Wong; W. Li; Z. Xie; J. Zhao
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: This work proposes a fractional-order compound steering control for lateral stabilization of dual motor drive electric vehicles (DDEVs) subject to multi-agent coupled game. Firstly, given that the compound steering involves the interactions between the active steering and differential torque, a closed-loop control framework-based multi-agent coupled game theory is proposed to coordinate the dynamic interaction information. Secondly, accounting for the complexity of nonlinear systems, a piecewise affine method is described to segmentally linearize the system and reduce the computational burden. Furthermore, the coupled game optimization problem for DDEVs with fuzzy nonlinearities is solved by integrating the dynamic programming strategy. Thirdly, considering that integer-order differential equations have limitations in describing complex characteristics of the vehicle dynamics, a fractional-order differential equation-based control strategy is developed to guarantee the stability of the control system by addressing the coupled game optimization problem of the vehicle dynamics. Finally, experimental results are performed to examine the effectiveness and merits of the proposed dynamic programming-based fractional-order compound steering control method in enhancing the lateral stabilization of DDEVs. Note to Practitioners—This work aims to solve the compound steering problem with the proposed dynamic programming-based fractional-order control for the lateral stabilization of the DDEVs. With the advantages of handling the system nonlinearities, reducing the computational burden, and enhancing the system robustness, the proposed method shows its potential in guaranteeing the active safety and stability of the DDEVs under complex driving conditions. A piecewise affine strategy is designed to simplify the complex vehicle dynamics and convert nonlinear optimization problems into a form suitable for real-time solutions. Through this method, the main system characteristics are maintained and the computational feasibility of the controller is guaranteed for standard automotive electronic control units. Moreover, a closed-loop game-theoretic strategy is introduced to coordinate the multi-agent interactions in the vehicle system. This strategy enables the vehicle to maintain the lateral stability with high computational efficiency. Therefore, the proposed controller holds significant importance for the development of autonomous driving. In future work, the tuning of key parameters (e.g., the fractional-order operators and game coefficient matrices) can be further optimized to satisfy the calibration requirements of different vehicle platforms.

title: From Naïve RAG to Deep Agentic Retrieval: An Evolving Context Engineering Pipeline for Regulatory Compliance
authors: M. de Costa; M. S. Anwar; D. Mercier; I. Hammad
venue: 2026 IEEE 14th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is the dominant paradigm for applying large language models (LLMs) to enterprise document corpora, yet naïve implementations encounter hard limits as corpus scale and query complexity grow. This paper traces the evolution of a production retrieval pipeline at Ontario Power Generation (OPG) for regulatory compliance and rate case analysis under Ontario Energy Board (OEB) reporting requirements. We examine successive stages—naïve RAG, hybrid retrieval with re-ranking, agentic function-calling retrieval, and a deep multi-agent architecture with code-based tool synthesis and explicit planning—and identify the failure modes and tradeoffs that motivated each transition. We formalize the mature architecture as Progressive Evidence Acquisition with Cost-Aware Escalation (PEA-CAE): begin with low-cost, high-precision retrieval and escalate to full-document reads only when the expected evidence gain justifies latency and cost. Our findings show that context engineering is a more tractable and economically viable path than domain-specific fine-tuning for large, evolving regulatory corpora. More broadly, the progression toward deep agentic retrieval mirrors classical information-retrieval ideas, introducing adaptive query reformulation, progressive document discovery, and hierarchical subagent summarization as practical system primitives. Operational traces further support the search-first, escalate-later pattern central to the final architecture.

title: A Polyglot OpenTelemetry Framework for Cloud-Native Reliability and Performance Engineering in Connected-Vehicle Platforms
authors: G. Saxena; N. B. Mohanty
venue: 2026 56th Annual IEEE International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks - Supplemental Volume (DSN-S)
abstract: The automotive industry's shift to software-defined connected vehicles has created enterprise-scale distributed systems where reliability directly impacts customer safety. Large automotive engineering organizations run dozens of cloud microservices-built by independent teams in Java, Go, and Python-that must jointly serve safety-sensitive commands, fleet-wide over-the-air (OTA) updates, and millions of simultaneous user journeys. We present a polyglot observability framework built on the Open-Telemetry (OTel) standard that unifies distributed tracing, custom metrics, and structured logging across heterogeneous microservices on a shared Kubernetes platform. The framework eliminates per-team instrumentation overhead through opinionated SDK wrappers, W3C context propagation, and an in-process mock collector for CI signal verification, while a Crossplane CRD layer auto-provisions dashboards, alerts, and incident-routing from a team-authored YAML, reducing time-to-observability from days to a single code review. Evaluated through concrete automotive use cases, the framework demonstrates less than 2 ms median added latency from instrumentation, a 63% reduction in mean time to detect (MTTD), and continuous DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) metric collection via Apache DevLake complemented by CI/CD pipeline traces for span-level root-cause diagnosis.

title: Hybrid Energy-Time Efficient Reinforcement Learning for UAV Coverage Path Planning Under Wind Disturbance
authors: T. L. Tran; T. Q. A. Mai; C. Lee; T. Thu Huong; C. -H. Youn
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: UAV coverage in real environments is challenging because onboard energy limits and spatially varying wind jointly affect motion, safety, and propulsion costs. This paper proposes ETA-PPO, or Energy and Time Aware Prior Guided PPO, within a framework that separates wind aware flight execution from fleet level coverage coordination. At the execution layer, ETA-PPO augments PPO with a deterministic state conditional VAE action prior and a bounded residual policy for closed loop point to point flight under wind disturbed dynamics. At the coordination layer, Heuristic JointETA-PPO-H assigns target, return to base, and hold macro actions above the frozen low level executor. Experiments are conducted in a shared 3D urban simulator with CFD derived time varying wind fields. Across point-to-point navigation, ETA-PPO achieves a 100% success rate on all evaluated tracks while maintaining a practical balance between energy use and flight time against actor-critic baselines. The same executor also completes all four long-horizon single-UAV ROI tours, demonstrating reliable transfer from individual legs to chained coverage execution. In the scaled multi-target, multi-UAV case study, Heuristic JointETA-PPO-H reaches 100% coverage in every tested fleet and launch configuration. The fleet-level results are therefore treated as deterministic systems evidence.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Wireless Communication Protocols for Battery Management Systems in Electric Vehicles
authors: C. K. Rao; S. K. Sahoo; G. D. Rani; I. Jahnavi; K. Lahari; B. Manikantha; B. M. Kumar; B. Srinivasarao; V. V. A. Menda
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning in Communication and Power Systems (AIMLCPS)
abstract: Recent studies identify BLE and ZigBee as promising candidates for low power, short range multi node architectures, while Wi-Fi and UWB can deliver higher through put and lower latency with careful electromagnetic and reliability optimization. NFC based and hybrid approaches are also gaining interest for secure data readout, second life battery applications, and maintenance without continuous wireless connectivity. Beyond telemetry, next generation WBMS platforms are integrating cloud connectivity, digital twins, and machine learning algorithms to enable predictive diagnostics, remaining useful life estimation, and over the air (OTA) parameter optimization. These capabilities improve state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH) estimation accuracy while enabling fleet level monitoring and continuous, software defined performance enhancement throughout the battery lifecycle. However, the deployment of wireless BMS introduces new design challenges concerning cyber security, functional safety, synchronization, and coexistence with other in vehicle wireless systems, along with the need for standardized, automotive qualified communication protocols and certification frameworks. This paper surveys the state-of-the-art developments in wireless communication for EV BMS, encompassing industrial implementations, experimental demonstrators, and research proposals up to 2025. It provides a comparative analysis of BLE, ZigBee, Wi-Fi, UWB, LoRa, and NFC technologies in terms of performance, scalability, cost, and safety implications. On this basis, the study identifies application oriented technology choices and highlights promising hybrid and cloud integrated architectures that are shaping the future evolution of BMS in electric vehicles.

title: Scalable Rigidity Maintenance Strategies for Networked Multirobot Systems: Overcoming Decentralized Coordination Challenges
authors: J. Francisco Presenza; E. Pecker‐Marcosig; I. Mas; J. Ignacio Alvarez‐Hamelin; J. I. Giribet
venue: Resilient Complex Adaptive Systems: Modeling, Simulation, Visualization and Engineering Approaches
abstract: Multirobot systems (MRSs)—an active area of research in recent decades—can be viewed as a subclass of resilient complex adaptive systems (CASs), where each robot functions as an autonomous agent in a bottom‐up architecture. Fundamental challenges arise when only relative information is available. This chapter addresses the control and localization of multirobot networks in which agents rely solely on relative distance measurements to their neighbors. Since sensing and communication ranges are limited, the network experiences changes in its topology as robots move. This can result in the loss of rigidity—the structural condition that allows position estimation through distance measurements—thereby causing the control schemes to fail. Different approaches to rigidity maintenance in networks with dynamic topologies are discussed, highlighting their respective advantages and limitations in terms of scalability and communication requirements. To illustrate the use of the proposed approach, a distributed control law is presented, where each agent exchanges local information with its near neighbors to achieve collaborative objectives. This decentralized, interaction‐driven adaptation exemplifies CAS principles, with global resilience emerging from local behaviors. Through the exploration of rigidity maintenance in networked systems, this chapter offers insights and methodologies that promise to advance the state‐of‐the‐art in resilient MRSs design and deployment.
